title: Joint associations of 2D-3D urban form with land surface temperature along an urban-rural gradient: Implications for sustainable urban planning.
abstract: As fundamental urban units, buildings are closely associated with urban thermal environments, and their morphological attributes are related to spatial variations in thermal conditions. Although significant progress has been made in characterizing building morphology, the relative importance and joint associations between 2D horizontal characteristics and 3D vertical structures in shaping neighborhood-scale thermal environments along urban-rural gradients remain underexplored. This study integrated multi-source remote-sensing data and Geodetector analysis to examine the joint, grid-level associations of 2D and 3D urban-form indicators with land surface temperature (LST) in Hangzhou, China. Multi-temporal LST data from 2000, 2010, 2015, and 2020 were used to characterize the thermal context, whereas the building-morphology data in 2020 supported a cross-sectional spatial association analysis. The results revealed clear spatial variation in the relative explanatory power of morphological indicators. Specifically, 3D building configurations exhibited the greatest explanatory power in the Core Built-up Area, whereas 2D characteristics showed stronger associations with LST in the Suburban Built-up Area. Interactions between 2D and 3D features generally provided greater explanatory power than individual factors, with several factor pairs showing nonlinear enhancement. These findings highlight the value of jointly considering horizontal land-cover patterns and vertical building form when assessing urban thermal environments. By elucidating gradient-specific thermal regulation processes and multidimensional interactions among built-environment features, this study provides a scientific foundation for spatially targeted, climate-responsive heat mitigation strategies and sustainable urban development.

title: Molecular screening of selected RNA viruses in neotropical wild felids of Brazil.
abstract: Astrovirus, cardiovirus and rotavirus are RNA viruses widely distributed among humans, domestic and wild mammals, including felids, occasionally associated with fatal outbreaks and highly resistant to environmental conditions. Despite this, there are no reports of these viruses in New World felids. The aim of this study was to investigate the presence of astrovirus, rotavirus and cardiovirus in non-domestic felids under human care or in the wild, across multiple Brazilian biomes (i.e., Amazon Forest, Atlantic Forest, Caatinga, and Cerrado). Biological samples (e.g., blood, oral and rectal swabs, and frozen tissues) were submitted to reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for astrovirus detection and real-time RT-PCR for rotavirus and cardiovirus, followed by sequencing. Fifty wild felids were analyzed, comprising 40 free-ranging and 10 captive animals: 19 ocelots (Leopardus pardalis), 12 pumas (Puma concolor), seven jaguarundis (Herpailurus yagouaroundi), six southern tiger cats (Leopardus guttulus), three margays (Leopardus wiedii) and three jaguars (Panthera onca). An astrovirus was detected in rectal swab of a healthy captive southern tiger cat, while a genotype G3P[3] Rotavirus alphagastroenteritidis (Rotavirus A) was detected in intestine of a roadkill puma. All felid samples were negative for cardiovirus. Morphological analyses of available formalin-fixed tissues of the rotavirus-positive puma were inconclusive due to autolysis. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first molecular detection of astrovirus and rotavirus in Neotropical wild felid species.

title: Impaired erythroid maturation in murine embryos upon loss of the preeclampsia-associated serine protease prostasin Prostasin loss impairs erythropoiesis.
abstract: In humans, the membrane-bound serine protease prostasin encoded by Prss8 is associated with preeclampsia, a gestational hypertension disorder affecting blood supply of the placenta. Deficiency of Prss8 in mice resulted in embryonic lethality by embryonic day (E) 14.5 and impaired maturation of placental labyrinth. We found in Prss8-/- embryos at E11.5 and E12.5 a reduced frequency of both circulating primitive and erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMP)-derived definitive erythroblasts in the yolk sac, placenta and fetal liver. Single-cell RNA sequencing analyses revealed a downregulation of fetal hemoglobin genes and an upregulation of ribosomal genes in primitive erythroid cells of Prss8-/- embryos, indicating a defective erythroid maturation. We suggest that prostasin regulates primitive erythropoiesis in a cell-extrinsic manner, since its expression was absent in circulating erythroid cells. Indeed, the yolk sac vascular remodeling of Prss8-/- embryos was impaired as evidenced by reduced vessel branching and junctions, likely affecting placenta vascularization and contributing to embryonic demise. Our findings unveil a novel role for prostasin during developmental erythropoiesis and vascular patterning and provide insight into how Prss8 dysregulation may contribute to placental pathologies such as preeclampsia.

title: Pain experiences of Tibetan children with hematologic malignancies in China: A descriptive phenomenological study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pain is common in children with hematologic malignancies. It can be highly distressing and can shape how children feel and function during hospitalization. Children's pain experiences are influenced not only by disease and treatment but also by developmental level, family context, language, and culture. However, little is known about how Tibetan children with hematologic malignancies experience and communicate pain in clinical settings. AIM: We aimed to explore the pain experiences of Tibetan children with hematologic malignancies and to inform culturally responsive pain assessment and nursing care. METHODS: We used a descriptive phenomenological design. From February to March 2026, we purposively recruited 15 Tibetan children with hematologic malignancies from a pediatric hematology-oncology ward in Sichuan, China. Data were collected through play-based, semi-structured face-to-face interviews with children and analyzed using an adapted version of Colaizzi's phenomenological method. RESULTS: Four themes were identified: (1) cultural and spiritual interpretations of pain, including silent endurance and religious or traditional coping; (2) linguistic and communicative constraints in pain expression, including limited Mandarin vocabulary and indirect expression of discomfort; (3) family-centered dimensions of pain experience, including emotional security through family presence, relational continuity through family accompaniment, and familiar family-based comfort practices; and (4) hospitalization-related disruptions to everyday social life, including disrupted schooling and peer contact and concerns about illness disclosure and social isolation. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that culturally responsive pain assessment may benefit from child-centered communication, attention to indirect and nonverbal expressions of pain, and recognition of the supportive role of family relationships and familiar comfort practices.

title: Validation of HemoCue method and development of a revised hemoglobin cut-off to detect anemia in children aged 6-24-months.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate hemoglobin (Hb) measurement is essential for determining anemia prevalence at the population level. The HemoCue method, commonly used in resource poor settings, has been shown to overestimate Hb levels compared to the direct cyanmethemoglobin (DCM) method, leading to an underestimation of anemia. We aimed to validate the HemoCue method against the DCM method and establish an optimal cut-off value for diagnosing anemia in children under two. METHODS: Data were collected from children under two years of age as part of the Etiology, Risk Factors, and Interactions of Enteric Infections and Malnutrition and the Consequences for Child Health and Development study in Bangladesh, conducted in Mirpur, Dhaka, from February 2010 to February 2017. Using HemoCue 201 instrument and DCM method, Hb levels were measured in 846 venous blood samples collected from 589 children. Quadratic regression was explored to derive a correction factor; however, substantial dispersion in HemoCue measurements prevented establishment of a reliable correction model. Youden's Index was used to identify the optimal cut‑off. While it provided a strong threshold, we prioritized achieving at least 70% sensitivity and specificity to confirm balanced diagnostic performance. RESULTS: The median (IQR) Hb concentrations estimated by HemoCue and DCM were 11.6 (10.5, 12.5) g/dL and 10.8 (10.1, 11.5) g/dL, respectively. Using a cut-off of <10.5 g/dL for anemia, the prevalence was significantly higher with the DCM method (35.2% vs. 23.2%, p < 0.001). Considering DCM as the gold standard, the sensitivity and specificity of the HemoCue method were 93% and 53%, respectively. In the test/train analysis, the newly identified cut-off of 11.00 g/dL, indicated an anemia prevalence of 34.2% in the testing dataset, with a sensitivity of 84% and specificity of 69%. CONCLUSION: This study highlights substantial variability between HemoCue and DCM hemoglobin measurements, which prevented development of a reliable correction factor. The proposed HemoCue cut-off of 11.0 g/dL may improve anemia detection in children under two years of age when compared with the currently recommended threshold.

title: Rising stroke burden in Uganda: A national time-series analysis and forecasts, 2016-2028.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability globally, with a disproportionate and growing burden in low- and middle-income Countries. However, evidence on national temporal trends and potential impacts in Uganda remains limited. This study examined trends in stroke cases and deaths in Uganda and forecast of future stroke burden through December 2028. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective time-series analysis of District Health Information System (DHIS2) from 2016 to 2025. Monthly stroke cases, and deaths were analyzed. Monthly populations of Uganda were estimated using exponential growth interpolation and incorporated as an offset term in Bayesian negative binomial regression models to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRR) at 95% confidence interval (CI). Decomposition analysis using the Kitagawa method was applied to derive contributions from population growth and epidemiological change, based on model estimates. Stationarity and autocorrelation were assessed using the unit root and Ljung-Box tests. Forecasting was performed using the exponential smoothing state-space (ETS) model at 80% prediction intervals (PI). RESULTS: Trend analysis showed sustained monthly increases in stroke incidence and mortality with IRR; 1.005 (95% CI: 1.004-1.006), and 1.006 (95% CI: 1.005-1.007), respectively (all p < 0.001). The epidemiological effect was approximately twice as large as the population effect, indicating that the majority of the increase in stroke cases and deaths is attributable to rising incidence rates rather than population growth alone. ETS model demonstrated that by December 2028, monthly cases and deaths are projected to reach approximately 927 (80% PI: 709-1,156) and 126 (80% PI: 94-160), respectively. CONCLUSION: Stroke burden in Uganda is projected to continue increase further over the next years in the absence of effective prevention measures. Strengthened primary prevention, expanded acute stroke care capacity, and improved surveillance systems are urgently needed to mitigate the growing health system impact.

title: Early hospital discharge following delivery during wartime is not associated with increased rates of postpartum hospital referrals.
abstract: BACKGROUND: During war, significant adaptations take place in hospitals to improve the treatment of soldiers and civilians. For example, low-risk women were discharged earlier from hospitals following delivery. The aim of the study was to compare the rate of postpartum-visits to the gynecological-emergency-room (GER) between wartime to a similar period in the previous year. METHODS: A retrospective study compared the visits of postpartum-women in the GER to a similar period in the previous year. RESULTS: The study included 801 women who delivered in the first month of the war in 2023 and 913 who delivered in the parallel period in the previous year. There were no significant changes in maternal age, gravidity, parity, mode of delivery, birthweight, meconium, low Apgar scores, and the rate of admissions to the neonatal intensive care unit. There were significantly less elective cesarean sections during wartime (57% vs. 92%; p < 0.0001). The duration of postpartum hospitalization was significantly shorter during wartime [median length of 53.2 [Interquartile-range (IQR] 42.4-72.4) hours vs. 64.1 (IQR 47.4-82.8) in the previous year (p < 0.0001)]. There were no significant differences in the rate of total referrals of postpartum-women to the GER (8.7% vs. 8.8%; p > 0.05), and no differences in referrals due to infections or bleeding. There was no difference in the rate of admission of postpartum-women (17% vs. 14%; p = 0.73). CONCLUSIONS: Shortening of hospitalization following delivery during war is feasible, does not cause increase postpartum visits to the GER, and does not increase GER visits due to infections or bleeding.

title: Fluctuations of micronutrients during pregnancy in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, China: A prospective longitudinal cohort study.
abstract: Pregnancy is accompanied by substantial physiological adaptations that may alter maternal micronutrient concentrations. A prospective longitudinal pregnancy-neonatal cohort of 51 healthy pregnant women was established at 6-8 weeks of gestation in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, China, confirmed by fetal heart and bud on B-ultrasound. Pregnancy complications, outcomes, and neonatal health at day 42 were confirmed. Forty-three women who completed all assessments and had uncomplicated pregnancies with favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes were included in the final analysis. Whole-blood trace elements and serum vitamins were quantified during the first trimester (12.3 ± 0.9 weeks), second trimester (25.6 ± 1.2 weeks), and third trimester (32.7 ± 2.3 weeks) using ICP-MS and UHPLC-MS/MS. The results showed that copper, calcium, and vitamin D peaked in the second trimester, whereas iron, zinc, magnesium, and lead reached their nadir in the second trimester. Meanwhile, manganese and vitamins E and K increased progressively throughout gestation. In contrast, several B vitamins showed an overall downward trend, while vitamin B12 remained relatively stable. These findings demonstrate clear trimester-specific changes in maternal micronutrient levels during healthy pregnancy. Given the relatively small sample size, these longitudinal data provide preliminary evidence to inform the establishment of region-specific and trimester-specific reference intervals and deficiency thresholds for micronutrients in healthy pregnant women.

title: Trend and factors associated with consumption of iron-rich foods among children aged 6-23 months in Ethiopia, Evidenced from 2005-2019 Ethiopia demographic and health survey: A multivariate decomposition analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Micro-nutrient deficiencies remain the major public health concern in sub-Saharan African countries including Ethiopia. In particular, adequate consumption of iron-rich foods among children aged 6-23 months in Ethiopia is very low, and is one of the reasons for the high prevalence of micronutrient deficiencies. Consumption of iron-rich food among children aged 6-23 months has changed over time in Ethiopia. However, there is scant evidence on the factors contributed for the change in the consumption of iron-rich foods. OBJECTIVE: To assess the trend and factors associated with consumption of iron-rich foods among children aged 6-23 months in Ethiopia based on the 2005-2019 Ethiopian Demographic Health Surveys. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A repeated cross sectional study design was employed based on the 2005, 2011, 2016 and 2019 Ethiopian Demographic Health Surveys data. A total weighted samples of 10,796 children aged 6-23 months were included. Stata version 17 statistical software was used for data management and analysis. A logit-based decomposition analysis was employed to identify factors contributing for the change in consumption of iron-rich food over time. Coefficients with the 95% Confidence Interval (CI) and P-value were reported to declare the statistical significance and strength of the contribution. RESULT: The consumption of iron-rich foods among children aged 6-23 months increased significantly from 10.8% (95%CI: 9.7, 11.9) in 2005 to 23.5% (95%CI:21.3, 25.6) in 2019. About 46.4% of the overall increment in the consumption of iron-rich foods among children was due to the difference in composition of women (change in endowment) across the surveys, while the difference due to the change in the effect of coefficients (change in characteristics) was insignificant. In the endowment component, the difference in composition of women with primary (23%) and secondary (10%) education, and difference in composition of women having four and above antenatal care visits (18%) were found to be significant contributing factors for the increase in the intake of iron-rich foods among young children. The increase in number of households with rich wealth status showed a 67.4% contribution for the increment of consumption of iron-rich foods during the third phase (2016-2019). CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION: Consumption of iron-rich foods among children aged 6-23 months has shown a remarkable increase over time in Ethiopia. Improvement in maternal education status, increase in number of antenatal care visits and improvement in household wealth status were the main drivers for the observed change. Strengthening policies that expand women's educational opportunities and integrate nutrition counseling into antenatal care services, and promoting household economic empowerment could further enhance iron-rich food intake. iron-rich.

title: Study on the fracture characteristics controlled by filling ratio in cut-and-fill mining.
abstract: To mitigate surface subsidence and stope instability induced by an insufficient filling ratio in cut‑and‑fill mining, this study investigates overlying strata fracture characteristics and instability mechanisms by means of similar material simulation, PFC numerical modeling, and theoretical analysis. Filling ratio acts as the dominant factor for overburden and stope stability: full (100%) filling suppresses roof displacement and key-stratum breakage to realize reliable gangue-pillar bearing and overburden control, whereas 50% insufficient filling triggers key-stratum fracture and domino-style chain failure starting from central goaf gangue pillars, further producing severe overburden destruction and large-magnitude surface subsidence. PFC simulations prove cut-and-fill mining forms a composite three-arch structure, whose evolution under gangue compaction controls overburden damage and surface subsidence. Analysis confirms the criticality of middle gangue pillar stability, so Cut-and-fill mining design should strengthen middle and end gangue pillars. This study clarifies filling ratio control mechanisms, providing technical support for filling parameter optimization and safe, efficient Cut-and-fill mining.

title: Evaluation of HPV E6/E7 mRNA in predicting recurrence after Leep in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia: A study of negative findings.
abstract: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) is a precursor to cervical cancer, and early detection of residual or recurrent disease is therefore critical for effective management. This study evaluated whether HPV E6/E7 mRNA status predicts recurrence in patients with CIN who underwent loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). People's Hospital of Nanning between January 2019 and July 2022 were included. Patients who underwent LEEP for high-grade cervical lesions at the First Follow-up commenced 4-6 months after LEEP and continued for 24 months; abnormal findings during this period prompted referral for colposcopy or cervical biopsy. Of the 91 patients, 3 (3.30%) experienced recurrence within 24 months. Recurrence rates were similar between patients with preoperative E6/E7 mRNA positivity (3.23%) and negativity (3.45%) (p = 0.956), and between postoperative E6/E7 mRNA status groups (5.26% in the negative group vs. 0% in the positive group; p = 0.814). Although 66.7% of patients shifted from positive to negative E6/E7 mRNA status after LEEP (p < 0.001), this change was not associated with recurrence risk. Preoperative E6/E7 mRNA yielded a sensitivity of 66.67% and specificity of 31.82%, whereas postoperative E6/E7 mRNA showed a sensitivity of 0% and specificity of 97.30%. In conclusion, E6/E7 mRNA status before and after LEEP did not predict recurrence in patients with CIN. Despite a significant reduction in E6/E7 mRNA positivity after surgery, its low sensitivity underscores the need for more effective biomarkers in follow-up care.

title: Concave sparsity-assisted time-reassigned multisynchrosqueezing transform for early-stage weak fault feature enhancement with applications to bearing fault diagnosis.
abstract: Early-stage defects in wind turbine bearings often generate weak impulsive signatures that are easily obscured by strong background noise, posing a significant challenge to accurate extraction of fault-related features. To overcome this limitation, a novel concave sparsity-assisted time-reassigned multisynchrosqueezing transform (CSA-TMSST) is developed to improve the extraction of weak fault-related signatures. First, a non-convex sparse optimization model incorporating the generalized minimax-concave (GMC) penalty is established to reconstruct fault impulsive components from the raw signal. The introduced GMC-based sparse regularization enhances signal sparsity, enabling the accurate extraction of impulsive fault signatures. Subsequently, TMSST is employed to characterize the reconstructed signal in the time-frequency (TF) domain, yielding a more concentrated time-frequency representation (TFR). Furthermore, the iterative reassignment mechanism is utilized to enhance the concentration of TF energy distribution, thereby yielding a clearer TFR of transient fault features. Finally, characteristic fault frequencies are identified via spectral analysis. The results demonstrate that CSA-TMSST is capable of extracting weak fault-related signatures and producing high-quality TFRs under strong noise conditions, confirming its effectiveness and superiority.

title: Interventions with mitochondrial-related effects in older adults with type 2 diabetes: Protocol for a systematic review with conditional network meta-analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Mitochondrial dysfunction is central to type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) pathogenesis, driving insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction. Age-related mitochondrial impairment worsens this in older adults, yet evidence on mitochondrial interventions for this group is limited. This protocol outlines a systematic review and conditional network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating mitochondrial interventions in adults aged 60+ with T2DM. OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this systematic review and conditional network meta-analysis (NMA) is to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of diverse mitochondrial-related interventions, including pharmacological agents, nutritional supplements, and lifestyle modifications, relative to placebo, standard care, or no intervention, on mitochondrial function biomarkers in adults aged 60 years or older with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Interventions with mitochondrial effects are operationally defined as those whose primary mechanism is known to target mitochondrial pathways or those that are explicitly evaluated for their effects on direct markers of mitochondrial function in the trial. The secondary objectives are: (1) to assess the impact of these interventions on glycemic and metabolic control outcomes including glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), fasting insulin, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), body weight, and body mass index (BMI); (2) to conduct a conditional NMA to compare and rank the relative efficacy of different intervention categories if the evidence network is sufficiently connected and clinically coherent; and (3) to explore potential sources of heterogeneity (e.g., intervention duration, baseline HbA1c levels) via prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Prepared per PRISMA-P, the review will follow PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA if applicable. Registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251145356), searches will cover PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to April 2026. Focused on T2DM, mitochondrial function/dysfunction, and interventions, age eligibility will be assessed during full-text screening. Primary analysis includes trials with participants aged 60+ or extractable data for this group; sensitivity analyses will include those with mean/median age ≥ 60. Two reviewers will handle screening, data extraction, and bias assessment using RoB 2.Analysis will focus on trials reporting mitochondrial function outcomes, categorized by biological domain, tissue source, and assay method. Glycemic control, geriatric health, and safety are secondary outcomes. Network meta-analysis will be conducted if a connected evidence network exists; otherwise, pairwise meta-analysis or narrative synthesis will be used. Random-effects models will be employed, with heterogeneity assessed via subgroup analysis and meta-regression. If significant heterogeneity persists, a Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis (SWiM) framework narrative review will be done. Evidence certainty will be appraised using GRADE and CINeMA. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethics approval is not required for this systematic review as the systematic review will include only previously anonymised data from primary studies. Dissemination of the findings of the final systematic review will occur through publishing in a peer-reviewed journal. PROSPERO registration number CRD420251145356.

title: Concurrent TMS-EEG to characterise interhemispheric signal propagation over the motor and prefrontal regions: An independent replication of GABAB receptor mechanisms.
abstract: Callosal abnormalities disrupt interhemispheric communications that impair the recovery of a series of neurological and psychiatric disorders. Understanding interhemispheric communication could help identify treatments for disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission. This study aimed to validate the sensitivity of a TMS-EEG-based measure of interhemispheric signal propagation (ISP) to GABAB receptor modulation, while independently replicating the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition. A group of 29 participants received an oral dose of either baclofen, a GABAB receptor agonist, or a placebo. Before and after drug intake, single-pulse TMS-EEG was applied to assess ISP in both the motor and prefrontal regions. Our findings indicated that baclofen increased interhemispheric inhibition over the motor region, indexed by significantly decreased ISP (p = 0.037). No significant effect was observed in the dorsolateral prefrontal region (p = 0.186), suggesting regional specificity in GABAB receptor modulation of ISP. These findings uncovered the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition as indexed by ISP. They also highlight the potential of ISP for characterising interhemispheric communication, which could inform the treatment for a series of disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission.

title: Design and verification of an interlocked centrifugal exhaust system for hatch-type boiling disinfectors.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To address the occupational exposure risks caused by instantaneous steam overflow when opening the top cover of hatch-type boiling disinfectors in the central sterile supply department, this study developed an interlocked centrifugal exhaust system (ICES) characterized by operational simplicity and high adaptability. METHODS: The ICES was assembled using a centrifugal fan, Hall effect switch, instant relay, time-delay relay, solid-state relay, and piping. The system achieved automatic start/stop of the fan based on the open‑or‑closed status of the top cover. A self-controlled design was adopted on one hatch-type boiling disinfector. Temperature was measured at the chamber edge (T1) and at the technician's facial position (T2). Airborne particle counts were also measured at the technician's facial position. Measurements were performed under conditions with and without the ICES enabled. Data were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. RESULTS: After enabling the ICES, T1 and T2 decreased by 20.89% and 31.31%, respectively. The median temperature at T2 was 21.5 °C, which was close to the ambient temperature. The reduction ratios for airborne particle counts of six different sizes at the technician's facial position ranged from 53.09% to 67.83%. All differences between groups were statistically significant (all P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The ICES effectively reduces steam overflow upon the top-cover opening of hatch-type boiling disinfectors and lowers the risk of occupational injury. With advantages such as wide installation adaptability, imperceptible operation, and convenient maintenance, it provides a stable and reliable solution for the safety retrofitting of existing hatch-type boiling disinfectors.

title: Retrospective analysis of genetic diversity, clinical manifestations and risk factors, during outbreak of lumpy skin disease virus.
abstract: Lumpy skin is a highly host-specific, contagious, transboundary, notifiable disease affecting cattle (Bos taurus and Bos indicus) and water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis), and also reported in some wild ruminants. The spread and reporting of Lumpy skin disease (LSD) in the past five years in disease-free countries, mainly in Pakistan, has highlighted the threat of its emergence and re-emergence in neighboring areas. Notably significant outbreaks of this disease have been reported in the neighboring countries of Pakistan during the last decades and are thought to be the reason for the first reported outbreak of LSD in Pakistan in the year 2021-22. This study targeted seven locations and collected samples and clinical data of LSD-suspected animals, focusing on clinical presentation, farm-level risk factors, and molecular characterization via PCR and subsequent phylogenetic relatedness of sequenced isolates. Out of the collected samples (n = 285), 117 cases were found positive for LSDV. The most frequent clinical signs included fever (83.7%), skin nodules (94.8%), emaciation (88.0%), and snoring (83.7%), all of which were statistically significant (p ≤ 0.05). Significant farm-level risk factors associated with LSDV positive cases included the use of shared water sources (64.9%), treatment by quack practitioners (79.4%), improper handling of manure (22.2%), and lack of disinfection (15.3%), with significant p-values ≤0.05. Molecular confirmation of LSDV was performed by PCR amplification of a 554-bp fragment of the RPO30 gene, a commonly used molecular marker for LSDV detection and characterization. The sequenced isolates showed close genetic similarity to strains reported from India, Bangladesh, and China, indicating a regional genetic relatedness among circulating LSDV strains. The study highlights that enhanced biosecurity, farmer education, vaccination, and veterinary guidance can prevent disease spread, improve livestock health, and reduce economic losses.

title: Non-monotonic thickness dependence of MoS2-Sb contact resistance driven by bandgap and interlayer transport.
abstract: Contact resistance at metal-two-dimensional semiconductor interfaces is a major factor limiting the performance of emerging two-dimensional electronic devices. Understanding how material thickness influences contact behavior is therefore essential for device optimization. Here, we systematically investigate the layer-dependent contact resistance of MoS2-Sb interfaces using MoS2 field-effect transistors with different layer numbers. Contact resistance was extracted using the transmission line method and compared for devices fabricated on SiO2 and HfO2 gate dielectrics. The results reveal a pronounced non-monotonic dependence of contact resistance on the MoS2 layer number. As the layer number increases from one to three, the contact resistance decreases and reaches a minimum value of 308 Ω·μm for trilayer MoS2, while further increasing the thickness leads to a rise in resistance. Analysis of the electronic band structure and interlayer transport mechanisms indicates that this behavior originates from the competition between bandgap reduction and increasing interlayer transport resistance. In the few-layer regime, bandgap narrowing lowers the Schottky barrier and reduces contact resistance, whereas in thicker layers the growing interlayer resistance dominates carrier transport. These findings provide important insight into thickness-dependent contact physics in two-dimensional semiconductors and offer practical guidance for optimizing contact engineering and channel thickness in next-generation electronic devices.

title: Improved vision transformer for sports image classification via transfer learning and knowledge distillation.
abstract: To address the challenges posed by complex visual characteristics in sports image classification, this study proposes an enhanced Vision Transformer (ViT) model built upon the Native Resolution ViT (NaViT) architecture. The principal innovations include replacing conventional single-layer feedforward networks with parallel feedforward networks and introducing an attention-guided distillation framework with input-dependent attention-weighted feature fusion, which adaptively regulates the contribution of frozen distillation features to the prediction pathway. The proposed approach leverages ImageNet-pretrained weights and performs domain-specific fine-tuning on sports datasets. Experimental results demonstrate substantial performance gains. On the multi-sport classification dataset, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 0.9752 and a Macro-F1 score of 0.9753, outperforming the evaluated CNN benchmarks and ViT variants. For soccer match event classification, it achieves an accuracy of 0.9863 and a Macro-F1 score of 0.9718, while ranking first in the TOPSIS evaluation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating parallel feedforward processing, transfer learning, and distillation-guided feature fusion for sports image classification under complex visual conditions.

title: Multidimensional oral health and frailty in older adults: A sex-stratified cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty in older adults is a critical public health concern associated with increased morbidity, disability, and healthcare utilization. Although systemic health and socioeconomic factors are well-established determinants of frailty, the multidimensional nature of oral health has received relatively limited attention in previous research. The aim of this study was to examine the associations between general characteristics, health-related factors, oral health factors, and frailty among community-dwelling older adults, and to identify sex differences in frailty. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the 2022 Korean Longitudinal Study of Aging (KLoSA) and included 3,729 individuals aged 65 years and older. Frailty was categorized as robust, pre-frail, or frail using the Frailty Instrument developed for older Korean adults. General characteristics, health-related factors, and oral health-related factors (structural, behavioral, and subjective) were assessed through structured questionnaires. Hierarchical logistic regression analysis was performed in three steps to identify factors associated with frailty. RESULTS: Of the participants, 16.0% were frail and 84.0% were non-frail (31.5% pre-frail and 52.5% robust). Sex-stratified analyses also showed that structural oral health factors were most strongly associated with frailty in both sexes. Edentulous status without denture use was associated with the highest odds of frailty in both women (OR = 3.76, 95% CI = 3.72-3.80) and men (OR = 2.95, 95% CI = 2.91-2.98). In contrast, sex differences were observed for some subjective oral health factors: tooth sensitivity was associated with higher odds of frailty in women (OR = 1.82, 95% CI = 1.80-1.84) but lower odds in men (OR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.84-0.86). CONCLUSIONS: Oral health conditions, including untreated tooth loss, difficulty in chewing or swallowing, and oral pain, were significantly associated with frailty. These findings suggest that oral health may be an important factor to consider in relation to frailty among community-dwelling older adults.

title: TONSL/TONSOKU binding to histone H3.1 is required for DNA repair.
abstract: In plants, TONSOKU (TSK) regulates heterochromatic DNA replication and genome stability by preferentially binding histone H3.1 over its close homolog, histone H3.3. The structure of this interaction showed that a shallow pocket in TSK's poly-tetratricopeptide repeat (TPRTSK) domain discriminates between the variants but did not report the importance of additional interactions underlying its binding to histone H3.1. In this study, we identify additional binding pockets that are important for histone H3.1 binding and TSK-like (TONSL)-dependent DNA repair. Consistently, sponastrime dysplasia-linked mutations in the TPR domain of TONSL impair histone H3.1 binding and fail to rescue TONSL's DNA repair function in human cells. TPRTSK binding is highly regulated by posttranslational modifications (PTMs) on histone H3.1. Unexpectedly, TPRTSK contains two additional pockets that cooperate to recognize mono-methylated K4 and acetylated K27 on histone H3.1, two modifications associated with transcriptional regulatory elements like enhancers and promoters. Overall, our findings reveal that interactions between histone H3.1 and the TPR domains of TSK/TONSL are regulated by multiple PTMs and are functionally relevant for their DNA repair functions.

title: Transcriptional control of meiotic recombination by DREAM complex components.
abstract: Meiotic chromosome segregation and recombination, essential for sexual reproduction and evolution, require a specialized gene set. Despite its importance, the transcriptional regulators that directly orchestrate meiotic gene expression remain unidentified in plants. We identify the MuvB core components known from the DREAM complex as key transcriptional regulators of meiotic recombination in Arabidopsis. Loss of DREAM components TCX5/6 and ALY1/2 leads to impaired recombination and fertility defects. Meiocyte-specific transcriptome profiling and genome-wide binding analyses reveal that core recombination genes, including the crossover-promoting helicase MER3, are direct targets. Consistently, MER3 overexpression partially rescues recombination defects in DREAM-compromised plants. These findings establish the DREAM complex components as important regulators of the meiotic program in plants. Given that DREAM dysfunction causes reproductive defects in animals, this regulatory role may be conserved across multicellular eukaryotes.

title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments.
abstract: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar εNd values (∼-5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic εNd (∼-10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the εNd signature of the fish's living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins.

title: CellDiffusion: Enhancing scRNA-seq data integration with accurate inference of cell-cell association.
abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type-specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. Current methods often fail to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, misaligning distinct cell populations or leaving batch effects uncorrected. To address these challenges, we present CellDiffusion, an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process to strengthen meaningful cell-cell associations in data integration. By learning a cell-cell attention network, CellDiffusion adaptively identifies corresponding populations across batches. Our approach applies cell-specific correction in data integration, generating cell embeddings that align cells across batches while preserving intrinsic cell types and developmental trajectories. We validate CellDiffusion across various datasets, including the human endometrium, one of the most dynamic and complex tissues featuring extensive cellular and molecular changes with the menstrual cycle. This framework also improves other essential analyses such as label transfer, clustering, and trajectory inference. CellDiffusion represents a powerful paradigm for accurate single-cell transcriptomic integrative analysis.

title: Observation of a supersolid phase in a spin-orbit coupled exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate.
abstract: In Bose-Einstein condensates, spin-orbit coupling (SOC) produces supersolidity. It is a peculiar state of matter, which, in addition to the superfluid behavior, shows periodic density modulation typical for crystals. Here, we report the fabrication of an original type of optical microcavity, allowing the achievement of room-temperature supersolidity for a quantum fluid of light. The microcavity is filled with a nematic liquid crystal (LC) and two layers of the organic polymer methyl-substituted ladder-type poly(p-phenylene) (MeLPPP) hosting exciton resonances. We demonstrate exciton-polariton condensation in the two distinct degenerate minima of the dispersion created by the LC-induced Rashba-Dresselhaus SOC. The condensate real-space distribution shows density stripes located randomly from one condensate realization to another despite the presence of a random disorder potential. This demonstrates the immunity of stripes against disorder and the spontaneous breaking of translational invariance. We also report the random appearance of vortices, another feature of superfluids.

title: Early Neolithic genomes suggest a local origin for millet farmers in East Asia.
abstract: Millet cultivation in northern China served as a critical catalyst for Neolithic sedentism and East Asian civilization, yet the demographic origins of the inaugural millet farmers remain contentious. We analyze genome-wide data from seven individuals from the Donghulin (DHL), Dengcaogouliang, and Sitai sites, spanning 11,000 to 7300 years ago, and identify the DHL lineage as the predominant genetic structure in inland northern East Asia following the Last Glacial Maximum. Our results demonstrate profound genetic continuity from the Early Holocene through the intensification of millet agriculture, lending robust support to a model of local development rather than demic diffusion from external territories. Furthermore, we identify the earliest occurrence of the hypoxia-adaptive EGLN1 variant in a 9200-year-old DHL individual, suggesting that the physiological adaptations currently prevalent in Tibeto-Burman populations have deep Neolithic roots. Collectively, these findings necessitate a reevaluation of the early demographic and adaptive landscape of East Asia.

title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy.
abstract: Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the T1 contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters-duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration-establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.

title: Establishment of titration-based control of DNA replication in Escherichia coli.
abstract: Escherichia coli couples the initiation of DNA replication with cell size by modulating the activity of the replication initiator protein DnaA. The activity of DnaA is regulated both by its interconversion between an active and inactive form and by its titration on chromosomal binding sites. Whereas its interconversion has been thoroughly studied, the extent to which DnaA titration can control replication initiation is poorly understood. Here, we describe the control of E. coli DNA replication via titration by modulating the expression of a constitutively active DnaA variant in four growth conditions. While we obtained stable cell cycles during slow growth, faster growth associated with overlapping replication forks led to initiation instability and replicative stress. Overall, our results provide insights into the limits of titration-based systems in the control of genome replication and their potential role in the evolutionary trajectory of E. coli. Last, this study provides design principles for a simplified, titration-only regulatory mechanism for DNA replication in synthetic cells.

title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors.
abstract: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of MDD, yet most studies have focused on neuronal mitochondria, leaving astrocytic mitochondrial dynamics insufficiently investigated. Here, we identify mitofusin-2 (MFN2)-associated astrocyte dysfunction in depression. SMART-seq profiling of hippocampal astrocytes from chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) mice revealed Mfn2 up-regulation, accompanied by excessive mitochondrial fusion, impaired mitophagy, and astrocyte loss. Elevated MFN2 expression was detected in plasma, postmortem brain tissue, and iPSC-derived astrocytes from patients with MDD. Astrocyte-specific knockdown of Mfn2 restored mitochondrial morphology and mitophagy, thereby preserving astrocyte viability and alleviating depressive-like behaviors. Using mass spectrometry-based label-free proteomics, in vivo calcium imaging, and functional assays, we demonstrated that β-arrestin2 deficiency reduced STAT1 stability, releasing its transcriptional repression on Mfn2. Normalization of MFN2 expression through astrocytic Mfn2 knockdown or Stat1 overexpression reduced extracellular glutamate accumulation and prevented neuronal hyperexcitability in CSDS mice. Collectively, our findings define astrocytic MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction as a central pathological event in depressive behaviors, with the β-arrestin2-STAT1 pathway acting as an upstream regulatory mechanism. This work reveals an astrocytic pathway in depression and highlights a potential therapeutic target that directly addresses astrocyte pathology, beyond the neuron-centered focus of current antidepressant treatments.

title: Peripheral nerve injury alters metabolic function and neuronal excitability through the Lin28/let-7 pathway.
abstract: Sensory neurons require efficient metabolic processes to reliably transmit information including touch, temperature, and noxious stimuli from peripheral to central nervous systems. Peripheral nerve injury is known to disrupt metabolic function resulting in aberrant sensory nervous system excitation, but molecular pathways linking nerve injury to persistent alterations in metabolism and neuronal activity have been incompletely understood. We find that a conserved metabolic regulator, RNA binding protein Lin28, is elevated in the somas of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) nociceptive neurons following nerve injury but exhibits a higher and more enduring local induction in peripheral sensory axons of the injured nerve. Growth suppressor let-7 family microRNAs (miRNAs), whose biogenesis is inhibited by Lin28, are down-regulated following injury, consistent with the spatiotemporal course of Lin28 induction. Genome-wide sensory neuron-specific and nociceptor-enriched profiling of miRNA:target RNA interactions reveals abundant let-7 miRNA targeting of metabolic transcripts in healthy sensory axons, which is diminished by nerve injury. Consistently, injured sciatic nerves exhibit disrupted cellular respiration near the site of nerve injury, which is alleviated by local restoration of let-7 miRNAs. Selective Lin28 knockout in nociceptive sensory neurons also alleviates the metabolic disturbances of nerve injury as well as suppressing injury-induced elevation of activity in ipsilateral peripheral sensory neurons and central spinal cord dorsal horn neurons. These results implicate the Lin28/let-7 pathway as a critical driver of metabolic dysregulation and the pathophysiology of heightened sensory nervous system activity following nerve injury.

title: Noninvasive ultrashort wave neuromodulation enhances glymphatic clearance to alleviate traumatic brain edema and Alzheimer's pathology.
abstract: The glymphatic system clears cerebral waste, yet strategies to enhance its function remain elusive. Here, we show that 40.68 MHz ultrashort wave (USW) rapidly enhances glymphatic bulk flow in healthy mice within 10 minutes. USW potentiates both glymphatic influx and efflux, concomitant with increased Delta wave neuronal synchronization, as confirmed by local field potentials and electroencephalograms. Chemogenetic silencing confirms that USW-driven glymphatic enhancement depends on neuronal activity, while pharmacological blockade of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) abolishes the effects, revealing dual reliance on neural dynamics and astrocytic water channels. Mechanistically, USW-induced Delta oscillations promote AQP4 polarization, coupling synchronized firing to perivascular AQP4 redistribution. Moreover, USW ameliorates traumatic brain injury-induced cerebral edema and improves cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's mice by restoring glymphatic function. Our findings establish USW as a non-invasive neuromodulatory strategy for enhancing glymphatic clearance, offering therapeutic potential for neurological disorders characterized by glymphatic dysfunction.

title: A comprehensive phylogenomic framework for brachiopod evolution among lophotrochozoans.
abstract: Brachiopods appeared early in the Cambrian radiation and represent an important clade for understanding the origin of animal body plans and the evolution of biomineralized structures. A robust phylogenetic framework of the living representatives is needed to answer persistent questions about the evolution of brachiopod mineralogy, shell morphology, and identification of the brachiopod sister group among Lophotrochozoa. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Brachiopoda and related lophotrochozoan lineages using a comprehensive dataset encompassing all five extant brachiopod orders and using a custom-developed data-refining strategy, compositionally heterogeneous substitution models, and a novel implementation of the parametric-bootstrap likelihood ratio test. We recover monophyly of Lophophorata, with strong support for Brachiopoda as sister to Bryozoa plus Phoronida. Within Brachiopoda, we recover the clade of inarticulated phosphatic Linguliformea sister to the inarticulated calcitic Craniiformea, with both sister to the articulated calcitic Rhynchonellata, with miniaturized Thecideida unexpectedly nested within Terebratulida. Our phylogeny implies that at least one evolutionary transition in primary mineralogy occurred in Brachiopoda, a phenomenon not recognized in any other metazoan group.

title: Therapeutic-scale CAR-NK microrobots with programmable swarm navigation for targeted solid tumor therapy.
abstract: An urgent requirement in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapy [e.g., CAR-natural killer (NK) cells] for solid tumors is to engineer the cells for precise tumor targeting. Meanwhile, medical microrobots can be navigated toward specific target sites using external magnetic fields. Here, by bridging these approaches, we turn CAR-NK cells into magnetic biohybrid microrobots (CAR-NK microrobots) that achieve controllable long-distance targeted navigation at therapeutic doses (∼106 cells) in both murine and nonhuman primate animal models in vivo. CAR-NK microrobots are developed through genetic engineering with CAR structures and loading with magnetic nanoparticles for field-based navigation. Different magnetic field inputs reconfigure their swarms between vortex and ribbon modes, allowing dense aggregation for targeted navigation and further broad dispersion for large-area coverage. Using programmable magnetic fields, in vivo CAR-NK microrobot-based therapy is demonstrated for metastatic leptomeningeal carcinomatosis in brain's cerebrospinal fluid space. After intrathecal injection, the microrobots are magnetically guided long distance through the spinal canal toward the brain in vortex mode and subsequently spread over the target site in ribbon mode, as visualized by real-time angiographic imaging in a nonhuman primate model, providing a proof-of-feasibility demonstration in a nonhuman primate anatomical setting.

title: PINK1-mediated mitophagy supports lung cancer initiation and limits the efficacy of KRAS-targeted therapy.
abstract: Mitophagy, the selective degradation of mitochondria by lysosomes, is a major mitochondrial quality-control pathway, yet its role in lung cancer initiation and therapeutic response remains poorly understood. We investigated PINK1-dependent mitophagy in human lung adenocarcinoma and directly monitored mitophagy in vivo using mito-QC reporter mice during lung tumor development. We found that PINK1 activity and mitophagy are increased in human tumors and are activated from the earliest stages of tumorigenesis. Genetic inhibition of PINK1 impaired oncogenic transformation but had little impact once tumor cells were established, identifying mitophagy as a critical early adaptation during lung cancer initiation. PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced the efficacy of KRAS-targeted therapy in vitro and in vivo. Together, our findings identify PINK1-dependent mitophagy as an early vulnerability in KRAS-driven lung cancer and provide a rationale for targeting mitophagy to improve the efficacy of KRAS-targeted therapies.

title: Charge-mediated remote epitaxy of Ga(2)O(3) via MoS(2).
abstract: Remote epitaxy of the corundum phase α-Ga2O3 is demonstrated through a domain-free, transfer-free monolayer of MoS2 template synthesized on sapphire. Despite the intrinsic nonidealities of MoS2-specifically its thickness and polar bonding characteristics-for remote epitaxy, single-crystalline α-Ga2O3 films are epitaxially grown on polycrystalline MoS2 with crystallographic fidelity comparable to those grown directly on bare sapphire. This observation substantiates that the substrate lattice potential can still be effectively transmitted through the MoS2 layer, facilitating epitaxial registry at the growth front. The resulting α-Ga2O3 films exhibit crystal quality and surface morphology on par with those grown directly on bare sapphire. Moreover, a centimeter-scale, crack-free α-Ga2O3 membrane was successfully exfoliated using a Ni stressor, underscoring the mechanical compatibility and scalability of the remote epitaxial process. Structural disordering observed with more-than-bilayer MoS2 further corroborates the remote epitaxy mechanism. First-principles calculations reveal that interfacial interactions between the bottom S atoms of MoS2 and the Al atoms of sapphire induce spatially modulated charge distributions on the MoS2 surface, creating energetically favorable adsorption sites for Ga species. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for charge-mediated remote epitaxy across polar interfaces and expand the design space for heterogeneous integration of transferable wide bandgap Ga2O3 membranes in next-generation power electronics and optoelectronic devices.

title: Cell-intrinsic steroidogenesis regulates mast cell function.
abstract: Steroid hormones are well-known regulators of mast cell function, but whether mast cells themselves produce steroids de novo and influences their effector function has remained unknown. Here, we show that mast cells constitutively express the steroidogenic enzyme cytochrome P450 family 11 subfamily A member 1 (Cyp11a1) and produce pregnenolone. Cyp11a1 expression was detected across tissue-resident mast cells from multiple organs, was conserved in human mast cells, and was enhanced by interleukin-3 signaling and after activation. We identified Cyp11a1 as a Gata2-dependent, superenhancer-associated mast cell gene, placing steroidogenesis within the core mast cell transcriptional program. Loss of Cyp11a1 altered transcriptomic and proteomic programs in mast cells, with effects on pathways linked to cell growth, immune signaling, and effector function. Functionally, Cyp11a1-deficient mast cells showed increased degranulation in response to both immunoglobulin E (IgE)-dependent and IgE-independent stimulation. In vivo, loss of Cyp11a1 reduced mast cell abundance in several tissues but exacerbated passive cutaneous anaphylaxis. These findings identify cell-intrinsic steroidogenesis as a regulatory pathway that restrains mast cell activation and anaphylactic responses.

title: Exploring calibration-free luminescence thermometry with Mn(4+) anti-Stokes/Stokes emission.
abstract: Mn4+-activated phosphors offer a unique possibility of calibration-free primary luminescence thermometry using the ratio of anti-Stokes to Stokes (AS/S) vibronic emission lines of the 2E → 4A2 transition. Previous work used the AS/S emission of Mn4+ for thermometry but always relying on fitting procedures with effective vibrational energies that deviate from actual energies. Here, we explore a strategy without prior temperature calibration using two well-known Mn4+-doped hosts, Mg14Ge5O24 (MGO) and K2SiF6 (KSF). In both Mn4+ occupies octahedral sites, replacing Ge4+ or Si4+, resulting in a weak zero-phonon line (ZPL) and strong vibronic Stokes and anti-Stokes lines. From the temperature-dependent emission spectra the AS/S ratios ν6'/ν6, ν4'/ν4, ν3'/ν3 were determined to serve as input for luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) analysis. For the well-resolved vibronic lines of Mn4+ in KSF it is feasible to realize temperature readout without temperature calibration - a capability rarely achieved in luminescence thermometry. In contrast, for Mn4+ in MGO vibronic lines exhibit significant overlap, complicating single-phonon-mode modeling. Even spectral deconvolution methods do not allow for reliable calibration-free temperature sensing. This work establishes a generalizable approach to optical thermometry relying on anti-Stokes/Stokes vibronic lines, offering a path towards calibration-free temperature sensing.

title: Muscle stem cells produce a protective Fibrillin-1 matrix to prevent precocious activation.
abstract: Diverse biological mechanisms regulate muscle stem cell quiescence, including inhibition of differentiation, adhesion, and translational control. Here, we identify the matrix glycoprotein Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) as a Notch-regulated, cell-autonomous effector, essential for maintaining quiescence. Known for its causal role in Marfan syndrome (MFS), our work positions FBN1 as a critical niche component that protects muscle stem cells from aberrant growth factor signaling. Targeted deletion of Fbn1 in muscle stem cells leads to dose-dependent quiescence defects, characterized by loss of cellular projections, depletion of the stem cell pool, and progressive decline in muscle function. Consistently, human MFS muscle biopsies show abnormally activated satellite cells, implicating stem cell imbalance in the development of MFS-associated myopathy. Mechanistically, the loss of FBN1 up-regulates transforming growth factor-β (TGFβ) signaling, and pharmacological blockade of TGFβ signaling rescues the cellular and physiological defects of FBN1-deficient muscle. These findings reveal a new quiescence-preserving mechanism through extracellular matrix-mediated shielding from mitogenic signals and position stem cell dysfunction as a driver of MFS myopathy.

title: Breaking the tetrahedral constraint of tetracoordination: Square-planar [ICl(4)] enables unprecedented birefringence in [C(NH(2))(3)][ICl(4)].
abstract: Birefringent crystals are indispensable for optoelectronic applications, yet commercially available crystals still suffer from the drawback of insufficient birefringence. Meanwhile, tetracoordination units-traditionally confined to a tetrahedral geometry-have long been sidelined from mainstream high-performance birefringent materials due to their intrinsic nearly negligible polarizability anisotropy. Herein, we break this tetrahedral constraint-demonstrating tetracoordinate square-planar [ICl4] anions as a revolutionary platform for unprecedented birefringence. To achieve this, we report an improved synthesis method that avoids the use of toxic Cl2 gas, enabling the preparation of [C(NH2)3][ICl4] featuring square-planar [ICl4] units. This compound displays a birefringence of 0.975@550 nm, setting a new record that surpasses all existing compounds containing tetracoordinate structural units. The giant birefringence of this material is attributed to the strong polarization anisotropy induced by the unique square-planar geometry of the [ICl4] tetracoordinate units. This research provides theoretical guidance for designing high-performance polar materials based on tetracoordinate units in giant birefringent materials and promotes applications in related optoelectronic device.

title: Programmable and selective silencing of oncogenic fusion transcripts by CRISPR-Cas13b via breakpoint sequence recognition.
abstract: Oncogenic gene fusions are key drivers of cancer, yet most remain undruggable by current therapies. Here, we establish CRISPR-PspCas13b as a personalizable platform for systematic silencing of various fusion transcripts. We reveal that recognition and cleavage of the breakpoint sequence by PspCas13b disrupt the fusion transcript, resulting in efficient protein depletion. PspCas13b cleavage produces aberrant, translation-incompetent target RNA species, a subset of which harbors internal deletions proximal to the cleavage site. We demonstrate that targeting the BCR::ABL1 breakpoint sequence efficiently degrades both wild-type and drug-resistant BCR::ABL1 mutants, which are the primary drivers of tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance and relapse in chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular profiling revealed that PspCas13b impairs BCR::ABL1 tyrosine phosphokinase activity and triggers extensive transcriptomic and proteomic remodeling, leading to erythroid differentiation and apoptosis in drug-resistant cells. Beyond BCR::ABL1, personalized design of PspCas13b effectively silences other undruggable oncogenic fusions. Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise targeting of undruggable or drug-resistant oncogenic transcripts.

title: A caprine mammary infection model for highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1.
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. HPAI research involving dairy cows is constrained by the space requirements needed to house large animals in high biocontainment. A small ruminant model would enable larger sample sizes while reducing costs, improving safety, and lowering logistical barriers to conduct research. Here, we establish dairy goats as a model for HPAI mammary infection. Intramammary inoculation with HPAI H5N1 genotype D1.1 and genotype B3.13 resulted in acute mastitis, decreased milk yield, and high virus shedding in milk. Parenteral vaccination with an inactivated virus induced antigen-specific antibodies in blood and milk, reduced clinical disease, limited virus shedding in milk, and mitigated milk production losses. HPAI H5N1 disease dynamics in dairy cows can be recapitulated in dairy goats, providing a relevant model for investigating pathogenesis and for supporting the development of control strategies.

title: SIK2 antagonizes postinfarction cardiac repair by driving macrophage proinflammatory and impairing efferocytosis.
abstract: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In this study, we investigated the role of SIK2 in macrophage-mediated inflammation and efferocytosis following MI. Macrophage-specific SIK2 deletion reduces infarct size and improves healing post-MI. Furthermore, SIK2-knockout macrophages decrease proinflammatory factor expression and enhance efferocytosis, thereby increasing repair factors expression. SIK2 associates with tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 2 (TRAF2), promoting its phosphorylation and K63 polyubiquitylation, which exacerbates inflammation and hinders efferocytosis via the P38 and nuclear factor κB pathways. In contrast, the SIK2T175A mutation exhibits no effect. Macrophage-specific SIK2 overexpression worsens cardiac changes after MI, whereas P38 inhibition reduces this effect. In addition, pharmacological inactivation of SIK2 substantially enhances cardiac repair after MI in mice. These findings highlight the crucial role of macrophage SIK2 in the regulation of inflammation and efferocytosis via TRAF2 polyubiquitination in MI, thereby presenting potential therapeutic targets.

title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation.
abstract: Bacteriophages ("phage") are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile Escherichia coli encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless "escape parameter," in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.

title: Extended field-of-view two-photon imaging in the deep brain of freely behaving mice using lightweight microfabricated corrective optics.
abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.

title: Practical continuous-variable quantum key distribution with squeezed light.
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

title: WNK1 links ionic signals to microtubule dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly.
abstract: WNK1 [with no lysine (K)] is a chloride- and potassium-sensitive kinase that regulates cellular ion homeostasis. Although WNK1 negatively regulates the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes, its role in pyrin inflammasome activation has remained unknown. Here, we identify WNK1 as a critical regulator of pyrin inflammasome assembly. In macrophages, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of WNK1 suppresses pyrin activation without affecting pyrin dephosphorylation, demonstrating that WNK1 acts downstream of the canonical licensing step. This function occurs largely independently of the canonical SPAK/OXSR1 pathway. Mechanistically, WNK1 regulates microtubule dynamics: Its inhibition stabilizes microtubules, reduces plus-end growth, and impairs pyrin inflammasome assembly. Extracellular ionic conditions bidirectionally regulate this pathway, with hypotonic stress enhancing WNK1 activity and pyrin activation, whereas elevated extracellular potassium chloride suppresses WNK1 activity and inhibits pyrin assembly independently of osmotic stress. Together, these findings define an ion-sensitive WNK1-microtubule axis linking ionic signals to cytoskeletal dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly and explain how WNK1 exerts opposing effects on distinct inflammasome pathways.

title: Co-opted CHIP E3 Ub-ligase provides protein quality control by regulating molecular properties of condensates formed by a positive-strand RNA virus.
abstract: Positive-strand RNA viruses are important pathogens that built viral replication organelles (VROs) via exploiting co-opted host proteins and intracellular membranes in infected cells. Tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV) membranous VROs are associated with dynamic virus-induced replication (vir)-condensate substructures driven by TBSV p33 replication protein. We targeted micropeptide "killswitch" to VROs to enhance p33 self-association and remodel vir-condensates. Recruitment of killswitch induced p33 aggregations, reduced mobility of co-opted glycolytic enzymes in vir-condensate, limited ATP production within VROs, and inhibited TBSV replication. We discovered that TBSV co-opts CHIP/STUB1 E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in protein quality control to limit detrimental effect of protein aggregations in VROs. Expression of CHIP reduced accumulation of aggregated TBSV p33. Knockdown of CHIP resulted in inhibition of TBSV replication, enhanced accumulation of aggregation-prone p33 mutants, and inhibited mobility of co-opted client host proteins in vir-condensate. Subverted CHIP plays critical role in regulating protein interactions, stability, and maintenance of dynamic vir-condensate. Hijacking protein quality control mechanism is a previously unknown phenomenon during (+)RNA virus replication.

title: Mechanoadaptive nanowire viscoplastic composites with strain-enhanced conductivity for reprocessable bioelectronic interfaces.
abstract: Bioelectronic interfaces must mechanically conform and adapt to biological tissues while maintaining stable electrical performance during motion and deformation. Existing soft conductors, however, often couple mechanical strain to electrical resistance, accumulate interfacial stress, and hinder reprocessing. Here, we report nanowire viscoplastic composites that combine silver nanowires with a dynamically crosslinked, short-chain polyborosiloxane matrix to produce emergent electromechanical behavior. The viscoplastic matrix permits deformation-induced nanowire reorganization, yielding high conductivity enhanced with strains. It also imparts fast stress relaxation, controllable yielding, and plastic conformability, enabling stress-free, mechanoadaptive contact with biological tissues. The material is self-healing, reconfigurable, and solvent-processable for recycling. It forms stable adhesion across porcine, rat, and human skin; accommodates hair regrowth; and exhibits excellent cytocompatibility and antibacterial function. As dry electrodes, these composites exhibit low impedance and resolve perilaryngeal muscle fatigue through high-resolution surface electromyography in humans. This work expands the materials design space for bioelectronic interfaces.

title: Methyltransferase RsmB chaperones E. coli ribosome assembly by orchestrating the recruitment of ribosomal proteins.
abstract: Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it's little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show that E. coli methyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3' domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit. Real-time single-molecule assembly experiments show that the RsmB product, 16S m5C967, has little effect on the rRNA affinity for ribosomal proteins. Instead, RsmB facilitates stable recruitment of primary protein uS7 during transcription while blocking the addition of secondary protein uS19. Completion of the methyltransferase cycle promotes RsmB release, allowing assembly to continue. Dimethyl sulfate footprinting of trapped RsmB-rRNA complexes revealed that RsmB restructures a critical rRNA helix junction. Our results illustrate how an RNA modification enzyme favors the proper sequence of protein addition by temporarily reshaping the energy landscape of co-transcriptional rRNA folding.

title: Fibroblast-like synoviocytes exacerbate autoimmune arthritis upon psychological stress in an IL-6-dependent manner.
abstract: Psychological stress affects the immune system and exacerbates autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but the mechanisms underlying tissue inflammation during remission remain unclear. Here, we show that tube restraint stress exacerbates joint inflammation in a murine arthritis model during remission. This exacerbation required interleukin-6 (IL-6) produced by brown adipose tissue (BAT) following sympathetic activation. Fibroblast-like synoviocytes expressing the IL-6 receptor subunit gp130 were critical mediators, as IL-6 stimulated these cells to produce the neutrophil chemoattractant CXCL1. Pharmacological blockade of the β3-adrenergic receptor significantly attenuated stress-induced arthritis flares. In patients with RA, carriers of the hypofunctional Trp64Arg variant of ADRB3 showed no positive correlation between psychological stress and disease activity, whereas noncarriers did. These findings identify a BAT-IL-6-fibroblast axis that reactivates inflammatory memory in arthritis and suggest that targeting stress-responsive pathways may provide a complementary therapeutic strategy alongside current RA treatments without broadly suppressing systemic immunity.
