title: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the "oxide gatekeeper" in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation.
abstract: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic "gatekeeper," regulating oxidation through a "breathing mode" of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a "rupture mode" leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Tipping point forecasting in nonstationary dynamics on function spaces.
abstract: Tipping points are abrupt, drastic, and often irreversible changes in the evolution of nonstationary and chaotic dynamical systems. For instance, increased greenhouse gas concentrations are predicted to lead to drastic decreases in low cloud cover, referred to as a climatological tipping point. In this paper, we learn the evolution of such nonstationary dynamical systems using a recurrent neural operator (RNO), which learns mappings between function spaces. After training RNO on only the pre-tipping dynamics, we employ it to detect future tipping points using an uncertainty-based approach. In particular, we propose a conformal prediction framework to forecast tipping points by monitoring deviations from physics constraints (such as conserved quantities and partial differential equations), enabling forecasting of these abrupt changes along with a rigorous measure of uncertainty. We illustrate our proposed methodology on nonstationary ordinary and partial differential equations, such as the Lorenz-63 and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equations. We also apply our methods to forecast a climate tipping point in stratocumulus cloud cover and airfoil wake and stall transitions using only limited knowledge of the governing equations. For the latter, we show that our proposed method zero-shot generalizes to forecasting multiple future tipping points under varying Reynolds numbers. In our experiments, we demonstrate that even partial or approximate physics constraints can be used to accurately forecast future tipping points.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Neuronavigated dual-target transcranial magnetic stimulation for schizophrenia negative symptoms.
abstract: Negative symptoms in schizophrenia severely impair function and quality of life, yet respond poorly to current therapies. This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial aimed to investigate the efficacy of neuronavigated dual-target repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (rDLPFC) and cerebellum for improving negative symptoms in early-stage psychosis (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04853485). Participants with first-episode schizophrenia or clinical high-risk for psychosis were enrolled from Shanghai Mental Health Center and Suzhou Guangji Hospital. Participants were randomly assigned to either a real or sham group under MRI-guided neuronavigation, targeting rDLPFC with 1Hz at 100% motor threshold(MT), cerebellar with intermittent theta burst stimulation(iTBS) at 120% MT for 20 consecutive days. Clinical assessments were conducted at baseline(T0), 10-session(T1), 20-session(T2) and one month after the intervention(T3). Cognition and MRI were evaluated at T0 and T2. The primary outcome was change of negative subscale score of the Positive and Negative Symptoms Scale(PANSS), while secondary outcomes included alterations in other PANSS subscale scores and fronto-cerebellar circuit functional connectivity. In total, 75 participants were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (36 active, 39 sham). The pre-specified primary linear mixed-effects analysis revealed a non-significant group-by-time interaction for PANSS negative subscale scores (F(3,174.6)=1.45, p=0.230). At the 4-week endpoint (T2), the nominal unadjusted between-group p-value was 0.049; after Sidak correction for multiple comparisons, the adjusted mean difference was -2.48 points (95% CI -4.99 to 0.03, adjusted p=0.150, Cohen's d=-0.51). Descriptive uncorrected t-tests indicated greater negative-symptom reductions in the active group at T1 and T2, and the 4-week negative-symptom response rate (≥50% reduction) was higher under real rTMS (χ2=9.5, p=0.002). A significant group-by-time interaction was observed for PANSS positive subscale scores (F(3,172.0)=3.26, p=0.023). Both groups exhibited substantial within-group symptom improvement. Resting-state fMRI demonstrated group-by-time interactions within cerebello-temporal, parahippocampal, caudate, and parietal networks (FWE-corrected p<0.05), and negative-symptom change correlated with cerebello-caudate connectivity (r=0.33, p=0.026). These findings suggest neuronavigated dual-target rTMS over rDLPFC and cerebellum may be associated with numerical improvements in negative symptoms in early-stage psychosis.

title: The petal identity gene PhDEF has a major binding and regulatory action in the epidermis.
abstract: In flowering plants, floral organ identity is specified by the combinatorial action of homeotic genes. While the role of these genes in the early specification of organ identity is well established, their late function throughout floral organ development and in specific cell types is much less characterized. In particular, since plant organs are structured in clonally independent cell layers, whether and how homeotic identity interacts with cell layer identity is unknown. We have previously identified cell layer-specific mutants for the petal identity gene PhDEF in petunia flowers, resulting in drastically different petal phenotypes whether PhDEF is expressed in the petal epidermis or in the mesophyll. In this study, using a combination of single-cell RNA-Seq and chromatin immunoprecipitation on phdef cell layer-specific mutants, we find that PhDEF regulates a different set of target genes in the petal epidermis and mesophyll, with a major regulatory action in the epidermis. We uncover a high diversity of binding profiles in PhDEF target genes, with a complex combination of layer-specific or non-specific binding sites, and a much more prominent binding of PhDEF in the epidermis than in the mesophyll. Our study highlights that floral homeotic genes like PhDEF can have different regulatory actions in different cell contexts, here different cell layers, demonstrating that cell layer identity indeed influences the regulatory processes underlying homeotic identity.

title: Foveated metamers of the early visual system.
abstract: The ability of humans to discriminate and identify spatial patterns varies across the visual field and is generally worse in the periphery than in the fovea. This decline in performance is revealed in many kinds of tasks, from detection to recognition. A parsimonious hypothesis is that the representation of any visual feature is blurred (spatially averaged) by an amount that differs for each feature, but that in all cases increases with eccentricity. Here, we examine models for two such features: local luminance and spectral energy. Each model averages the corresponding feature in pooling windows whose diameters scale linearly with eccentricity. We performed perceptual experiments with synthetic stimuli to determine the largest window scaling for which human and model discrimination abilities match (the 'critical' scaling). We used much larger stimuli than those of previous studies, subtending 53.6 by 42.2° of visual angle. We found that the critical scaling for the luminance model was approximately one-fourth that of the energy model and, consistent with earlier studies, that the estimated critical scaling value was smaller when discriminating a synthesized stimulus from a natural image than when discriminating two synthesized stimuli. Moreover, we found that initializing the generation of the synthesized images with natural images reduced the critical scaling value when discriminating two synthesized stimuli, but not when discriminating a synthesized from a natural image stimulus. Together, the results show that critical scaling is strongly affected by the image statistic (pooled luminance vs. spectral energy), the comparison type (synthesized vs. synthesized or synthesized vs. natural), and the initialization image for synthesis (white noise vs. natural image). We offer a coherent explanation for these results in terms of alignments and misalignments of the models with human perceptual representations.

title: What is biology research for?
abstract: In the age of generative artificial intelligence (AI), the assumption that writing a paper requires doing science no longer holds true. Before deciding how to respond to the surge of AI-generated papers, the field needs to state what biology research is actually for.

title: A broad-host-range Rhizobium rhizogenes strain enables transient expression across diverse crop species.
abstract: Agrobacterium-mediated transient expression has revolutionised plant research, enabling numerous landmark discoveries across diverse areas of plant biology. Yet this powerful approach remains largely confined to solanaceous species, leaving most economically important crop families without a comparable rapid assay platform. Here, we show that an engineered Rhizobium rhizogenes strain, AS109, mediates efficient transient expression across diverse dicot species spanning multiple taxonomic families, consistently outperforming commonly used laboratory agrobacterial strains. Leveraging the broad host range of AS109, we establish a suite of functional assays in faba bean (Vicia faba), including protein localisation, RNA interference-mediated gene silencing, cell-surface elicitor recognition screens, nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat receptor (NLR) activation, and infection cell biology at the host-pathogen interface. We further demonstrate that both singleton NLRs and sensor-helper NLR pairs from Solanaceae retain effector recognition and cell death activity when transferred into faba bean, establishing a rapid platform for evaluating cross-family transferability of disease-resistance genes. AS109 thus provides an accessible and versatile chassis for functional genomics in non-model crops, bridging the widening gap between hypothesis generation and experimental validation across diverse plant species.

title: Leveraging spatial structure to design spatially-targeted malaria interventions at the community-scale.
abstract: Progress in malaria control has stagnated since the early 21st century in many countries, requiring new approaches such as the use of spatially-targeted interventions. However, evidence on the effectiveness of spatially-targeted interventions is mixed, depending on both the setting and intervention. In addition, the potential role of community health programs in implementing spatial targeting is underexplored, with models focusing on coarser spatial scales than those needed to guide programmatic activities. We developed a two-age-class, spatially-explicit model of malaria at the community-scale for a district in southeastern Madagascar, accounting for environmental heterogeneity and spatial structure, to explore spatially-targeted community health interventions. The model was fit to field-based case notifications and malaria prevalence data and then used to simulate three interventions: indoor residual spraying (IRS), supplemental coverage of long-lasting insecticide-treated nets (LLIN), and active case detection (ACD). We compared five scenarios, one with no spatial targeting and others targeting communities (i) nearest to clinics, (ii) furthest from clinics, (iii) with highest incidence, and (iv) that are spatially central. The non-targeted intervention was generally the most effective, but the least resource efficient. The second most effective intervention was based on spatial centrality, which reached a larger population while using fewer transportation resources than the non-targeted intervention. No combination of interventions was able to eliminate malaria in the district, although detecting symptomatic cases through ACD could avert 100% of severe malaria cases at high detection rates. These results highlight the potential for targeted malaria interventions, especially in low-income settings, that take into account spatial structure in the human population and transport networks to reduce malaria burdens using fewer resources than conventional district-wide interventions. [A French language abstract is available as Text A in S1 Appendix].

title: Computation-through-Dynamics Toolkit: Simulated datasets and quality metrics for dynamical models of neural activity.
abstract: A primary goal of systems neuroscience is to discover how ensembles of neurons transform inputs into goal-directed behavior, a process known as neural computation. A powerful framework for understanding neural computation uses neural dynamics - the rules that govern how neural activity evolves over time - to explain how goal-directed input-output transformations occur. As dynamical rules are not directly observable, we need computational models that can infer neural dynamics from recorded neural activity. We typically validate such models using synthetic datasets with known ground-truth dynamics, but unfortunately existing synthetic datasets don't reflect fundamental features of neural computation and may therefore be poor proxies for neural systems. Further, the field lacks validated metrics for quantifying the accuracy of the dynamics inferred by models. The Computation-through-Dynamics Toolkit (CtDToolkit) addresses these critical gaps by providing: 1) synthetic datasets that reflect computational properties of biological neural circuits, 2) interpretable metrics for quantifying model performance, and 3) a standardized pipeline for training and evaluating models with or without known external inputs. In this manuscript, we demonstrate how CtDToolkit can help guide the development, tuning, and troubleshooting of neural dynamics models. In summary, CtDToolkit provides a necessary framework for model developers to better understand and characterize neural computation through the lens of dynamics.

title: From prompts to genomes: A constraint-first framework for AI-driven sequence design across life and viruses.
abstract: A constraint-first framework for future 'prompt-to-genome' AI across Bacteria, Archaea, Eukaryota, and viruses is proposed. Genome-scale models can now generate long DNA sequences, and experimentally viable genome-scale designs have begun to appear, but sequence generation alone does not establish biological feasibility. Constraints should not require designs to remain within natural sequence space; rather, they should define testable boundaries for function, inheritance, lifecycle coherence and safe use, including new-to-nature designs. We propose a two-part system. First, a Constraint Compiler translates natural-language prompts into machine-checkable specifications defining scope, context, objectives, assumptions and governance requirements. Second, a modular Validator Stack (C1-C6) evaluates candidate designs for sequence integrity, gene and regulatory plausibility, genome completeness, comparative coherence, systems-level feasibility, and safety and governance. Extreme prompts serve as stress tests to expose hidden assumptions, conflicting objectives, and refusal points, complemented by adversarial testing and risk assessment. A phased roadmap and community benchmarks are proposed to measure specification accuracy, biological feasibility, robustness, and governance performance. The goal is to move prompt-to-genome systems from impressive generation toward reliable, auditable, and accountable biological design.

title: Ten simple rules to build genomics capacity for routine laboratory practice in the Global South.
authors: Arabela Leal E Silva de Melo
abstract: Developing sustainable genomics capacity in the Global South requires more than technology transfer; it depends on human-centered approaches based on the workflows and existing expertise of laboratory personnel, institutional collaboration, and long-term integration into health systems. Drawing on lessons learned from regional capacity-building initiatives, this article proposes ten simple rules for implementing and sustaining genomics capacity within public health and clinical laboratory settings. These rules emphasize local context, strategic planning, continuous learning, and equitable collaboration. Together, they provide a roadmap for laboratories aiming to transform genomic technologies from research tools for diagnosis, surveillance and decision-making, into routine instruments for public health in low- and middle-income countries.

title: The hypothalamic orexin-medial prefrontal cortex pathway modulates susceptibility to depression in the learned helplessness paradigm in male mice.
abstract: Depression is a prevalent psychiatric disorder primarily characterized by behavioral despair and helplessness. The orexinergic system plays a crucial role in stress-induced depression; however, the precise mechanisms remain unclear. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), a major target of orexinergic projections, is essential for emotional regulation. This study suggests that impaired orexinergic input to the mPFC underlies depression-like behaviors in murine models. In the learned helplessness (LH) paradigm, the majority of male mice subjected to inescapable foot shocks developed depression-like behaviors (classified as LH-susceptible), whereas a subset displayed resilience (classified as LH-resilient). LH-susceptible mice exhibited a reduced number of orexin+ neuronal somata in the hypothalamus, along with decreased expression of prepro-orexin mRNA Correspondingly, the mPFC of these mice displayed decreased density of orexinergic terminals and lower Orexin A levels. In contrast, LH-resilient mice maintained stable hypothalamic orexin neuron counts, exhibited increased prepro-orexin mRNA expression, and preserved orexinergic terminal density in the mPFC. Chemogenetic activation of the hypothalamic orexin-mPFC pathway alleviated depression-like behaviors in LH-susceptible mice through Orexin A signaling. Conversely, inhibition of this pathway induced depression-like behaviors in LH-resilient mice. Additionally, LH-susceptible mice showed decreased excitatory synaptic transmission in layer V pyramidal neurons of the mPFC, which was improved by activation of hypothalamic orexinergic inputs; this improvement was attenuated by administration of an orexin receptor 1 (OX1R) antagonist. Collectively, these findings implicate the hypothalamic orexin-mPFC pathway as a pivotal regulator of excitatory synaptic transmission and suggest its involvement in modulating individual variability in susceptibility and resilience to depression.Significance statement Depression is a highly prevalent emotional disorder characterized by behavioral despair and helplessness under stress. This study demonstrates that the orexinergic system is critical for modulating resilience to aversive stimuli. Using the learned helplessness (LH) mouse model, we found that LH-susceptible mice, but not LH-resilient mice, show compromised hypothalamic orexinergic projections to the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), together with decreased excitatory synaptic transmission in layer V pyramidal neurons. Activation of the hypothalamic orexin-mPFC pathway alleviates depression-like behaviors in susceptible mice through Orexin A, while inhibition of this pathway induces depression-like phenotypes in resilient mice. These findings identify orexinergic signaling as a promising therapeutic target for depression.

title: A novel nitric oxide (NO)-dependent 'molecular switch' mediates LTP in the Octopus vulgaris brain through persistent activation of nitric oxide synthase (NOS).
abstract: Cephalopod mollusks provide a striking example of the independent evolution of advanced cognitive abilities in invertebrates. In octopuses, learning and memory are mediated by the vertical lobe (VL), whose visual input synapses undergo robust activity-dependent long-term potentiation (LTP). Here, we used Octopus vulgaris of either sex to show that persistent activation of nitric oxide synthase (NOS) mediates both LTP expression and maintenance, independently of de novo protein synthesis. Contrary to the prevailing view, NO signaling is not required for LTP induction, as LTP can still be induced in the presence of NOS inhibitors. Remarkably, however, NOS inhibitors blocked presynaptic LTP expression, while NO donors induced only short-term potentiation, together suggesting that LTP expression depends on persistently elevated NO levels. The effective NO concentrations, estimated both pharmacologically and amperometrically, were more than three orders of magnitude higher than those required for activation of the canonical sGC-cGMP pathway, suggesting that NO acts through direct covalent modification of proteins, such as S-nitrosylation. In a subset of synapses, the NOS inhibitor L-NNA rapidly and completely erased established LTP; however, following washout, full potentiation could be reinstated by renewed tetanic stimulation. We therefore propose a 'molecular switch' mechanism in which an NO-dependent positive feedback loop persistently reactivates NOS, thereby maintaining LTP. These findings reveal an unprecedented form of convergent evolution in which molecular innovations equip the octopus VL network with the computational properties required for associative learning.Significance Statement Long-term potentiation (LTP) is a central cellular mechanism of learning and memory. While extensively studied in vertebrates, its mechanisms in octopuses-animals that independently evolved sophisticated cognitive abilities-remain poorly understood. Here, we uncover a novel form of LTP involving activity-dependent activation of nitric oxide synthase (NOS) in the postsynaptic cell. The produced nitric oxide (NO) mediates LTP maintenance through persistent NO-dependent reactivation of NOS (a "molecular switch") and simultaneously mediates LTP expression by retrogradely facilitating presynaptic transmitter release. These findings reveal a striking example of convergent evolution in which distinct molecular mechanisms independently evolved to implement associative (Hebbian) learning rules within a neural network.

title: Ancient Greek votive epigraphy: Ancient religion between individual choice and cultural trends.
abstract: Ancient votive inscriptions, numbering in the tens of thousands across the Mediterranean, offer direct evidence for religious practice but have rarely been studied comprehensively across time and space due to their sheer volume. This paper presents a "distant reading" analysis of approximately 11,000 Greek dedicatory inscriptions (sixth century BCE - seventh century CE) drawn primarily from the GIST/I.PHI digital corpus. By tagging inscriptions for key features (votive/dedicatory terminology, deities, motives, gender) and analyzing their distribution chronologically and geographically while controlling for the "epigraphic habit," this study identifies large-scale trends. The results reveal a significant relative increase in the use of explicit votive terminology (forms of euche/euchomai) over time, particularly during the Roman Imperial period and Late Antiquity. This practice exhibits strong regional variation, being markedly more prevalent in Asia Minor and the East than in mainland Greece before the fourth century CE. Furthermore, the use of votive formulae correlates strongly with specific deities (e.g., Men, Meter, Hypsistos, Hosios kai Dikaios) and negatively with others (e.g., emperors, Athena). Votive terminology also appears negatively correlated with the explicit mention of other motives (like dreams or commands) and with the use of standard consecration terms. While demonstrating the potential of computational methods for identifying broad patterns of continuity and change in religious expression, the study also highlights methodological challenges (dating uncertainty, data tagging) and underscores the persistent difficulty in definitively separating shifts in epigraphic conventions from changes in underlying religious mentalities.

title: Digital twin-assisted edge-local query resolution for privacy-utility trade-off in location-based services.
abstract: Location-Based Services (LBS) generate large volumes of sensitive, location-dependent queries that must be processed under strict and often conflicting constraints of privacy and utility. Existing differential privacy (DP) mechanisms face a fundamental limitation: strong guarantees inject excessive noise and degrade utility, while utility-oriented methods under-protect users. We propose DT-ELR (Digital Twin-assisted Edge-Local Resolution), a framework that jointly optimises disclosure and retrieval utility through two tightly integrated algorithms and an on-device digital twin. Algorithm 1 (SensitivityClassifier) calibrates a monotone geo-indistinguishability budget from a data-derived sensitivity score, validated against a semantic venue-category labelling (AUC 0.81). The digital twin predicts from on-device signals alone whether releasing a query would improve its answer (AUC 0.90); self-sufficient queries are resolved against an on-device venue cache with no release and no budget spent. Algorithm 2 (ClosedFormAllocator) then distributes the remaining budget across released queries in closed form, matching the exact dynamic-programming optimum to within 1%. Experiments on three public check-in corpora - Foursquare-NYC, Gowalla and Brightkite - using an end-to-end nearest-venue retrieval task and three implemented adversaries, show that DT-ELR reduces optimal-inference localization success on sensitive queries from 61.3% to 11.4% on Foursquare-NYC at a matched mean budget, while raising end-to-end retrieval precision from 0.244 under full release to 0.559. Twin-guided release routing outperforms a tuned distance heuristic at every matched release rate, approaching an oracle ceiling of 0.565, and keeps 73% of sensitive queries entirely on the device. Component analysis confirms that each mechanism contributes independently, with edge-local resolution dominant, and the sensitivity model transfers to Gowalla and Brightkite without refitting. Against three recent location-perturbation mechanisms at a matched budget, DT-ELR attains a dominant privacy-utility frontier on all three corpora: higher utility at equal disclosure, and lower disclosure at equal utility.

title: Traffic surveillance video-based a unified road accident detection, classification, and vehicle tracking framework using an optimized spatio-temporal attention mechanism.
abstract: In recent days, vehicular accident detection has materialized because of the unique and intriguing application potential in the evolution of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). To monitor and respond to the event of a fatal accident, real-world traffic surveillance footage requires continuous analysis. In this research, the road accident from the traffic surveillance video is detected, classified, and vehicle tracked using an efficient and innovative model. The surveillance videos are gathered from the CCTV Footage dataset, which is a publicly available dataset. The gathered videos are directly applied to the Spatio-Temporal Attention-based Adaptive Yolov9 with SE-InceptionNet and Deep SORT (AYSIDSORT) model for detecting, classifying and tracking traffic accidents very effectively. The developed network allows accurate detection and tracking of vehicles in real-time, which ensures the continuous traffic flow without losing moving objects. The variables of the proposed AYSIDSORT model are tuned by the developed Generation Probability-based Equilibrium Optimizer (GP-EO) to improve the detection and classification performance. The exact location of the accident is sent to the appropriate entities using an Internet of Things (IoT) platform to provide a timely rescue for the affected individual. Here, the proposed framework acts as a computer vision-based accident detection and tracking framework with potential IoT integration to find the exact location of the accident, which helps to provide a timely rescue for the affected individual. The effectiveness of the offered approach is validated with various baseline detection models. The accuracy of the suggested AYSIDSORT reaches to 95% in the 100th epoch, whereas there is a slight variation in the accuracy values when the batch size is varied from 4 to 128. The outcomes show that the designed framework is better than existing methods.

title: Multi-feature Response Attention Network for kidney stone detection and measurement of stone size in ultrasound images.
abstract: Kidney stones are hard deposits formed in the urinary tract due to excess waste and low fluid intake, causing severe abdominal pain. Ultrasound-based kidney stone detection involves identifying and locating stones in the kidneys using high-frequency sound waves to visualize renal structures. Measuring stone size is crucial for early treatment and preventing infection. However, detection is challenging because ultrasound images suffer from noise, lower contrast, and variable quality. To overcome these limitations, the Multi-feature Response Attention Network (MFRANet) is proposed to detect kidney stones. Initially, the input image is allowed for image denoising and edge preservation using Windowed Variation Kernel Wiener Filter (WV-KWF). Further, the kidney region is segmented by the Fuzzy Clustering algorithm with Variable Multi-pixel Fitting spatial information (FCM-VMF). Moreover, descriptor computation is processed by rotated Binary Robust Independent Elementary Feature (rBRIEF) with Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT). Afterwards, the kidney stone is detected using MFRANet, wherein MFRANet is designed by combining Multi-feature Multi-Attention Network (MFMANet), along with Group Response Attention Network (GRA-Net). Next, the detected stone is segmented using Optimized DA-TransUNet (O-DAT), and lastly, the kidney stone size is measured. Performance of the proposed MFRANet is assessed with Accuracy, F1-score, Precision, and True Positive Rate (TPR) which achieved superior values of 96.64%, 96.65%, 97.44%, 95.88% Response Attention Network, Multi-feature Multi-Attention Network, Optimized DA-TransUNet.

title: Radiocarbon dating of wooden beams at Herodium palace-fortress: Modeling tree-felling events and their implications on site chronology.
abstract: The site of Herodium is best known for its impressive, well-preserved palace fortress, built by Herod the Great, towards the end of the 1st century BC. The site's conical shape, artificially created to transform it into Herod's monumental burial complex, is clearly seen from afar. The impressive preservation of wooden beams and posts at the site has allowed for a rigorous radiocarbon study of the beams' felling dates and their potential implications for the timing of construction activities at the site. A total of 24 14C measurements were performed on specific growth rings from 11 beams and posts, associated with six (sub) phases at the site. This level of detail, combined with Bayesian modeling and sensitivity testing of potential seasonal offsets, has revealed that the wood used at the site originates from four main tree-felling events. Apparently, the first event might have been as early as Alexander Jannaeus's time, in the first quarter of the 1st century BC - a period not currently identified in the archaeological record at the site. The second reflects an extensive supply of wood, felled during the period corresponding to the beginning of the main phase of Herod's massive construction activity (40-30 BC, approximately), followed by a possible third felling event towards the end of Herod's life or shortly after. The fourth felling event was identified in beams used during the Bar-Kokhba revolt in 132-136 AD. However, the beams were felled several decades earlier, around 100 AD, between the Great Revolt (66-71 AD) and the Bar-Kokhba one, in a period characterized by limited documented occupation, indicating that the wood was used several decades after the trees were felled. The origin of some of those beams is probably from the extensive gardens Herod planted at the site.

title: Policy awareness among community-dwelling older adults: The roles of cognitive status and digital access.
abstract: Policy awareness is a key prerequisite for the effective use of government programs among older adults. In increasingly digitalized information environments, access to policy information may depend not only on digital resources but also on cognitive capacity. However, limited evidence exists regarding whether the relationships between informational resources and policy awareness differ according to cognitive function. This study conducted a secondary analysis using data from the 2023 National Survey of Older Koreans, a nationally representative survey based on stratified multistage cluster sampling. The analytic sample included 9,951 community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older. Policy awareness was measured using 11 items assessing awareness of government programs for older adults (range 0-22). Cognitive status was categorized using K-MMSE-2 scores into normal cognition, mild cognitive impairment, and moderate-to-severe cognitive impairment. Complex samples general linear models were applied to examine factors associated with policy awareness and to test interaction effects between cognitive status and key predictors. The weighted mean policy awareness score was 8.34 (SE = 0.13). Policy awareness differed significantly across cognitive groups, with the lowest scores observed among those with moderate-to-severe cognitive impairment and the highest among those with normal cognition. The overall model was statistically significant (Wald F = 14.59, p < 0.001) and the model explained 12.9% of the variance in policy awareness (R2 = 0.129). Significant interaction effects were observed between cognitive status and digital access (p < 0.001) and between cognitive status and depression (p = 0.003). The association between digital access and policy awareness appeared stronger among older adults with mild cognitive impairment compared with those with normal cognition. These findings suggest that cognitive status moderates the relationship between digital access and policy awareness. Improving digital access may be associated with higher levels of policy awareness among cognitively vulnerable older adults.

title: Evaluation of a novel body temperature sensor (CORE) in dogs under general anesthesia following premedication with dexmedetomidine or acepromazine: A pilot study.
abstract: Core body temperature monitoring in anesthetized dogs is a vital part of physiological evaluation. Depending on the procedure and patient positioning, consistent core temperature measurements can be difficult to obtain. The objective of this study was to evaluate the reliability and clinical validity of a wireless, non-invasive, superficial heat flux-based thermometric device (CORE, greenTEG AG, Rümlang, Switzerland). Three healthy beagle dogs were premedicated with either dexmedetomidine or acepromazine prior to induction with intravenous propofol and isoflurane maintenance. They were monitored every five minutes with pulse oximetry, non-invasive blood pressure, electrocardiography, and capnometry. Rectal thermometry and temperatures from the CORE sensor placed on clipped and unclipped skin over the jugular veins were measured every three minutes for up to 120 minutes following induction. Based on the correlation coefficient for repeated measures (rrm) and the Shrout-Fleiss intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), in dogs administered acepromazine, there was good, statistically significant correlation and reliability between rectal and clipped CORE temperatures (rrm = 0.81, P < 0.0001; ICC = 0.78) and rectal and unclipped CORE temperatures (rrm = 0.79, P < 0.0001; ICC = 0.85). In dogs administered dexmedetomidine, although values were correlated (rrm = 0.30, P < 0.0001), there was poor reliability (ICC = 0.28) between rectal and clipped CORE temperatures which improved if dogs were unclipped (rrm = 0.48, P < 0.0001; ICC = 0.88). Clinically acceptable Bland-Altman agreements were found between rectal and unclipped CORE methods. These preliminary results suggest that the CORE sensor may provide an alternative method for assessing core body temperatures in unclipped, anesthetized dogs.

title: Lifestyle factors and clustered patterns of body shape change in Korean adults: A longitudinal observational study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major health problem driven by lifestyle habits and changes in body composition, particularly increased body fat mass and reduced skeletal muscle mass. Body mass index alone cannot fully characterize adiposity distribution or changes in muscle mass. Body-shape indicators such as waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and waist-to-height ratio predict metabolic and cardiovascular disease risk; however, few studies have assessed longitudinal changes in these measures together with lifestyle factors. In this study, we aimed to identify clusters of body-shape change using 2-year follow-up data from Korean adults and to elucidate the body-composition and lifestyle factors underlying these changes.
METHODS: K-means cluster analysis was applied to 1,404 participants in the Korean Medicine Daejeon Citizen Cohort using 2-year changes in body mass index, waist circumference, hip circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, waist-to-height ratio, and body weight. Baseline body shape, body composition, and lifestyle indicators were compared across clusters, and multinomial logistic regression was used to identify variables associated with cluster membership.
RESULTS: Three clusters were identified: Stable (48.0%), Adiposity-Increasing (31.0%), and Adiposity-Decreasing (21.0%). At baseline, cluster membership was significantly associated with body fat mass. Over follow-up, changes in body fat mass and skeletal muscle mass showed strong associations with cluster assignment. In addition, clinically meaningful worsening in sleep quality (increase of ≥2.5 points in the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index) and reduced physical activity (decrease in activity as measured by the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire) were significantly associated with the Adiposity-Increasing cluster.
CONCLUSIONS: Changes in body composition, especially body fat mass and skeletal muscle mass, were closely associated with body-shape trajectories, while worsening sleep quality and declining physical activity were associated with the Adiposity-Increasing trajectory. These findings support an integrative approach that considers body shape, body composition, and modifiable lifestyle factors when characterizing adiposity-related trajectories and designing tailored lifestyle interventions.

title: A simple method for analyzing competitive growth of multiple cell types in xenograft tumors.
abstract: Low take rates and inter-tumor variability in growth rates can limit the effectiveness of mouse xenograft models when comparing between groups. To address this problem we developed a simple method to compare multiple cell types within a single mixed xenograft. Individual cell lines or clones were transduced with a lentiviral vector that includes a unique PCR tag, allowing the use of qPCR to determine the proportion of each tagged cell type within a mixed xenograft tumor. We generated vectors with six distinct PCR tags, and two different selectable markers, and have optimized the approach for determining their relative proportions within a mix. An initial pre-amplification step is used to increase the amount of material for subsequent qPCR reactions. This also removes the bulk of the genomic DNA, increasing the specificity of the qPCR step. Samples are then used for qPCR with specific pairs of primers that distinguish between each of the individual PCR tags, and the relative proportion of each tag is determined relative to that in the starting mix. We have tested this approach for in vitro growth of mixed cell cultures and in an orthotopic cecal xenograft model using a human colon cancer cell line. Since each individual tumor is initiated with a mix of cells, multiple tumors within a single animal can be analyzed separately, and overall tumor size is not important. Similarly, multiple metastatic lesions from the same animal can be analyzed individually. Thus, each tumor provides a direct comparison between individually tagged cell lines or clones. This low throughput "bar-coding" approach is simple and cost effective and has the potential to reduce the number of animals needed for xenograft experiments.

title: Sustainable strategies to improve indoor comfort and reduce energy consumption in winter: Integration of fly ash and rice husk ash in PCM concrete.
abstract: The thermal performance of a building envelope is closely related to its energy consumption. Merging industrial by-products like fly ash (FA) and rice husk ash (RHA) with phase change material (PCM) concrete unlocks a pathway to significantly enhanced thermal insulation properties for envelopes. This study investigated the effects of two different proportions of industrial by-products (5%-15% RHA and 10%-30% FA) on PCM concrete. The test results show that, at the same dosage, RHA is superior to FA in reducing thermal conductivity, especially at an incorporation rate of 15% RHA. Adding 15% RHA and 30% FA resulted in a 2.3 °C increase in the minimum temperature of the PCM concrete. Moderate RHA and FA resulted in a more uniform pore distribution and finer pore size. With increasing RHA content, the capillary pore volume increased and the fractal dimension decreased. In comparison, a higher FA content led to a significant increase in the total pore volume, particularly in the macropore volume, accompanied by a reduction in fractal dimension. The results of the correlation analysis indicated that capillary pores have a significant impact on the thermal properties. It is shown that PCM concrete can be used to obtain available insulated concrete, which has the potential to reduce winter energy consumption.

title: Analysis of construction response for mechanized construction of metro connecting passages.
abstract: To investigate the influence of mechanized pipe jacking construction for connecting passages in weathered granite strata on the settlement and deformation of left and right shield sections of metro tunnels and ground surface, this paper takes the pipe jacking project of No.1 connecting passage in a typical weathered granite stratum as the research background. Numerical analysis software was used to model and analyze the whole construction process of the connecting passage using the mechanized pipe jacking method. The accuracy of the numerical model was verified by comparison with field monitoring data. On this basis, the influence laws of stratum cohesion, internal friction angle, clear distance between main tunnels, and burial depth on the deformation of the main tunnels and ground surface were systematically analyzed. The results show that: 1) The tunnel at the launching end experienced two sudden deformations during the portal breaking stage, with the bending moment increasing sharply first and then decreasing slowly; the deformation at the receiving end increased linearly with the pipe jacking advance, and reached the peak synchronously with the bending moment at the moment of portal breaking. 2) A centrally symmetrical settlement trough was formed on the ground surface, with a maximum settlement value of 2.3 mm; the maximum vertical and horizontal deformations of the main tunnel were 1.7 mm and 1.4 mm, respectively. 3) The improvement of stratum strength can reduce ground surface settlement but increase the horizontal deformation of the tunnel; the increase of the clear distance between main tunnels leads to the expansion of the settlement trough width; the increase of burial depth reduces ground surface settlement while increases the horizontal deformation of the tunnel.

title: Client, health care provider, and policymaker perspectives on point-of-care/near-point-of-care testing for sexually transmitted infections in community pharmacies in Uganda.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Point-of-care or near-point-of-care (POC/near-POC) tests for sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are often unavailable and unaffordable in low-resource settings, despite the World Health Organization's (WHO) recommendation that such testing be offered, leading to empiric treatment. Private community pharmacies (CPs) are often the first point of contact for people with symptoms of STIs, where pharmacists dispense treatment without diagnostic testing or prescriptions. This study evaluated clients,' providers,' and policymakers' perspectives on POC/near-POC STI testing in community pharmacies for targeted management.
METHODS: Between June and September 2022, we nested a qualitative study into a prospective cohort of clients seeking both STI and non-STI treatments in community pharmacies in Kampala and Wakiso districts in Uganda. They were tested for HIV, syphilis, trichomonas, chlamydia, and gonorrhea using POC/near-POC tests. A purposive sample of 50 participants consented to participate in in-depth and key informant interviews. Data were analyzed thematically using NVivo version 14 with an inductive approach, with results reported according to the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ).
RESULTS: Clients (n = 35), health care providers (n = 9), and policymakers (n = 6) described the benefits of POC/near-POC tests for HIV/STIs at community pharmacies, citing affordability, accessibility, and convenience. Participants noted that such testing could promote behavioral change, shorten turnaround time for results, speed access to treatment relative to conventional laboratory methods, and support sustainable antimicrobial resistance control. Reported barriers included limited awareness among clients and health workers, inadequate privacy and space, long waiting times, unclear self-sample collection instructions, stigma around HIV testing, and reluctance to test for non-HIV STIs. Participants recommended raising STI awareness, offering clearer explanations of test results, expanding test access, reducing stigma, provider training, and ensuring a sustainable supply chain for testing kits.
CONCLUSIONS: POC/near-POC testing for HIV/STIs was highly acceptable to both pharmacy clients and providers in this study. Integrating such testing into community pharmacy settings could strengthen national HIV/STI management programs, and addressing the identified barriers could improve access to HIV/STI diagnostics and strengthen linkage to care.

title: The ability of the commercial inertial measurement unit-based gait system in determining Parkinson's disease: A systematic review with meta-analysis of cross-sectional studies.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to use the meta-analytic approach to investigate the ability of Inertial Measurement Unit-based commercial system measured gait variability and asymmetry in distinguishing individuals with Parkinson's disease (PD) from healthy controls (HC). Cross-sectional studies included using commercial IMU-based systems measuring gait variability or asymmetry at any stage of PD patients and healthy adults were included. Studies were determined by searching for four electronic databases and cross-referencing. Dual selection and data abstraction of studies were conducted. Hedges' g standardized mean difference was calculated for each variable and pooled using inverse heterogeneity mode. Statistically significant was determined by two tailed z-alpha values ≤0.05 and non-overlapping 95% CI. Heterogeneity was estimated using Q and I2 with alpha values ≤0.10 for Q considered statistically significant. Small-study effects were examined using doi plots and LFK index. A total of 1,725 studies were screened. Eventually, 9 studies representing up to 571 PD patients and 470 HC met the inclusion criteria. Overall gait variability was significantly greater in individuals with PD than in HC (Hedges' g = 0.368, 95% CI 0.139-0.597). The multi-IMU subgroup also showed significantly greater gait variability (Hedges' g = 0.397, 95% CI 0.221-0.574), whereas the one-IMU subgroup did not. However, the between-subgroup difference was not statistically significant, and the multi-IMU prediction interval included null. The primary analysis detected no statistically significant overall difference in gait asymmetry (Hedges' g = 0.180, 95% CI -0.012-0.373). These findings provide preliminary evidence of an average group-level difference in gait variability but hard to establish individual-level discrimination, clinical utility, or the superiority of multi-IMU systems.

title: STCP-Net: A few-shot learning approach based on spectral-temporal convolution and an improved prototypical network for ECG classification.
abstract: To address the heavy reliance of deep learning models on manually labeled data in ECG classification, we need to tackle two major limitations. First, sample sizes are often limited in clinical settings, making data annotation costly and impractical. Second, existing few-shot learning methods still fall short in two key areas: 1) Existing strategies pay insufficient attention to rare arrhythmia types. This makes it difficult to effectively identify rare clinical cases. 2) Single feature representation fails to fully integrate the global frequency, local time-frequency, and semantic information of ECG signals. This results in incomplete feature representation. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel few-shot learning method for ECG classification. In terms of feature extraction, a spectral-temporal convolution feature extractor is designed to precisely focus on the key information of ECG by efficiently integrating the global frequency, local time-frequency features and semantic information of the signal. Furthermore, with regard to classification, an improved prototypical network based on cross-class bias diminishing is developed to enhance the recognition performance for rare arrhythmia type samples. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves significant classification performance across multiple public datasets, especially on Chapman, it attains an average accuracy exceeding 90% in the 2-way 1-shot and 2-way 5-shot tasks.

title: Optimized bilateral segmentation deep learning network for wild animal detection.
abstract: The use of Deep learning (DL) for recognition of wild animals has become an important development in wildlife monitoring. The advances will include the use of multimodal data for improved accuracy and development of lightweight models for use in edge devices. As a result, DL will help contribute to global conservation efforts as it tackles the issues. The key novelty of the proposed framework is the integration of bilateral segmentation with DL to enhance relevant animal feature extraction while reducing the influence of complex background information. The paper proposes the Optimized Bilateral Segmentation DL Network that uses Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) to improve Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) parameters for wild animal identification. The first step in the process was collecting datasets from various online sources. The image quality was improved through image processing methods such as Adaptive Histogram Equalization (AHE) as well as median filtering. The classifier was trained and validated using pre-processed images. This classifier combines the Bilateral Segmentation Deep Learning Network (BSDLN) with the HHO algorithm. CNN is utilized for detection and the weight parameter is utilized by HHO. In order to enhance model convergence also with performance, HHO dynamically adjusts the learning rate during training within the BSDLN. This balances speed and accuracy by adapting to gradients and losses behavior. By adaptively adjusting the learning rate, HHO and BSDLN optimize the CNN learning process and enhance convergence and classification performance. The suggested approach is put into practice in Python, and statistical metrics are used to assess its effectiveness. The results are compared with other approaches to verify the strategy's efficacy. With just 0.2% FPR and 0.3% FNR, the suggested BSDLN performed the best overall, achieving 99.4% precision, 99.8% accuracy, 99.6% recall, 99.5% F1-score, and 99.3% specificity. The experimental findings show that the combination of HHO and bilateral segmentation enhances the efficacy of wild animal detection, offering a strong foundation for automated wildlife monitoring.

title: MambaSeed: A lightweight Mamba-based hybrid vision network for tomato leaf disease recognition.
abstract: Crop diseases threaten agricultural productivity, creating a need for recognition models that combine accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. Existing CNN-, Transformer-, and state-space-based approaches can weaken fine-grained lesion edges and textures when emphasizing global context. We therefore propose MambaSeed, a lightweight hybrid network built on MambaVisionMixer and equipped with the Local Continuous Branch Injection mechanism, hereafter LCBI. This mechanism repeatedly introduces local feature compensation during hierarchical modeling, preserving high-frequency cues while maintaining global dependency modeling. On the Tomato, Corn, and Potato datasets, MambaSeed achieved accuracies of 98.97%, 98.06%, and 95.87%, respectively, with 1.13M parameters and 0.240G MACs. In the batch-one FP32 GPU benchmark, its latency was 3.39 ms/image on an NVIDIA RTX 4090. Without a hardware accelerator, the median CPU latency was 25.35 ms/image with one thread and 15.61 ms/image with four threads. Ablation, cross-architecture frequency analysis, and controlled perturbation tests further showed that LCBI strengthens high-frequency feature retention and maintains stable recognition under visual degradation. Together, these results show that MambaSeed provides a compact balance of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness across both accelerator-based and CPU-only inference settings.

title: Green-aware intrusion detection systems: A sustainability-driven approach to network security.
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has intensified network security challenges. Simultaneously, growing computational demands raise critical concerns about energy consumption and environmental sustainability. This paper proposes a Green-Aware Intrusion Detection System (GA-IDS) integrating sustainability metrics with machine learning to balance detection performance and energy efficiency. The framework employs a lightweight convolutional neural network optimized for resource-constrained platforms with dynamic power management and adaptive computational scaling. A novel carbon-conscious scheduling algorithm dynamically adjusts model complexity based on real-time grid carbon intensity. Experimental evaluation on CICIDS2017, NSL-KDD, and ToN-IoT datasets demonstrates 98.7% detection accuracy with 43% energy reduction compared to traditional deep learning-based IDS. The carbon-aware scheduler reduces emissions by 58.7% during high-carbon grid conditions without compromising detection quality. Comprehensive ablation studies validate component contributions, and comparative analysis against ten state-of-the-art approaches confirms GA-IDS achieves the highest Green Efficiency Score (0.0796), demonstrating superior balance between security performance and environmental responsibility.

title: Evaluation of prenatal genetic aberrations in fetuses with gallbladder abnormalities: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: With the widespread application of chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) in prenatal diagnosis, fetal gallbladder abnormalities have been found to be associated not only with chromosomal aneuploidies but also with certain syndromes caused by submicroscopic chromosomal structural variants. This study aimed to investigate the molecular etiology of fetal gallbladder abnormalities and to provide additional evidence for clinical screening and genetic counseling regarding these anomalies.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 258 fetuses diagnosed with gallbladder abnormalities through prenatal ultrasonographic screening. Among these, 167 cases underwent both karyotype analysis and CMA, 14 cases received CMA only, and 77 cases underwent karyotype analysis only. The fetuses were categorized into two groups based on the presence of additional structural anomalies: isolated gallbladder abnormalities (Group A), gallbladder abnormalities accompanied by soft markers (Group B) and gallbladder abnormalities accompanied by structural anomalies or other abnormalities (Group C). Within each of the three groups, cases were further subdivided into subgroups A1/B1/C1, A2/B2/C2, A3/B3/C3, and A4/B4/C4, corresponding to fetuses with nonvisualized gallbladder, gallbladder enlargement, small gallbladder, and other gallbladder abnormalities, respectively.
RESULTS: Among the total of 258 fetuses, karyotyping identified chromosomal abnormalities in 10 cases (4.2%, 10/240), whereas SNP-array detected abnormalities in 16 cases (8.7%, 16/184). The detection rate of SNP-array was higher than that of traditional chromosome karyotype analysis, and SNP-array identified submicroscopic abnormalities in 7 additional cases that were undetectable by karyotyping. The overall detection rates were significantly higher in gallbladder abnormalities accompanied by structural anomalies or other abnormalities group than that in the isolated gallbladder abnormalities group and gallbladder anomalies accompanied by soft ultrasound markers group(P < 0.05). The highest frequency of chromosomal abnormalities was observed in fetuses presenting with both gallbladder and facial abnormalities.
CONCLUSION: For fetuses with gallbladder abnormalities, prenatal genetic diagnosis is recommended, with chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) as the preferred testing method. It can improve the detection rate of chromosomal abnormalities associated with fetal gallbladder abnormalities and identify submicroscopic chromosomal structural variants that conventional karyotyping may miss.

title: Comprehensive Analysis of the AP2/ERF Transcription Factor Family in Schisandra chinensis and Its Implications for secondary metabolism.
abstract: The AP2/ERF transcription factor superfamily is integral to plant secondary metabolism; however, its comprehensive genomic characterization in Schisandra chinensis-a medicinal plant esteemed for its dibenzocyclooctadiene (DBCOD) lignans with a wide range of pharmacological properties-has not yet been conducted. In this study, we identified a total of 144 ScAP2/ERF genes from the high-quality, chromosome-level genome of S. chinensis. These genes were categorized into five subfamilies (ERF, DREB, AP2, RAV, and Soloist) through phylogenetic analysis with Arabidopsis thaliana. Conserved motif analysis confirmed the presence of the characteristic AP2 domain in all ScAP2/ERF proteins, with members of the AP2 subfamily containing two AP2 domains and RAV members featuring both AP2 and B3 domains. Chromosomal localization analysis revealed an uneven distribution of these genes across 14 chromosomes, with clusters identified on chromosomes 1, 2, 6, 10, 11, and 13. Cis-acting element analysis demonstrated an enrichment of light-responsive, MeJA-responsive, ABA-responsive, and anaerobic induction elements in the promoters of ScAP2/ERF genes. Synteny analysis identified 26 pairs of segmentally duplicated genes within the S. chinensis genome and 39 orthologous pairs with A. thaliana. Expression profiling across roots, stems, leaves, and fruits revealed distinct tissue-specific expression patterns. Of the 144 identified genes, 122 (84.7%) were detectably expressed in at least one tissue; among them, ten exhibited notably high expression in fruit tissues, suggesting their potential regulatory roles in the accumulation of pharmacologically active compounds in the medicinal fruit. This study represents a comprehensive genome-wide identification of the AP2/ERF family in S. chinensis, thereby establishing a foundational framework for understanding its evolutionary history and functional diversification. Furthermore, it offers candidate genes for subsequent functional validation in the regulation of their potential roles in regulating secondary metabolism.

title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) are associated with distinct clinical phenotypes two years after SARS-CoV-2 infection: A data-driven approach.
abstract: It is important to determine whether the persistent cognitive and fatigue complaints, as part of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), are associated with underlying patterns and specific symptoms clusters. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate symptom clusters and clinical phenotypes in PASC. We included n = 153 individuals (53 years old, 66% female, 2 years post SARS-CoV-2 infection) categorized into groups with (n = 88) and without (n = 65) PASC, defined by severe fatigue and concentration problems using validated cut-offs. Symptom clusters (i.e., component loadings and component scores) were identified using principal component analyses (PCA, eigenvalue[EV]>1.0), using clinical, somatic, coping and sleep factors, symptom severity, neuropsychological and physical tests (totalling 19 tests and questionnaires). We then used logistic regression techniques on (participant-level) component scores (standardized) to investigate associations with PASC. Finally, K-means clustering methods to identify clinical phenotypes. Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, education, nationality and time since infection. PCA identified 5 components, explaining 70% of the variance. We labelled these components as follows: (1) PEM, ME/CFS and sleep symptoms, coping factors (EV = 7.0, 36.9% variance), (2) information-processing speed (EV = 2.5, 13.3%), (3) executive functioning (EV = 1.5, 8.0%, (4) physical performance (EV = 1.2, 6.5%), (5) somatic comorbidities and hospital admission (EV = 1.0, 5.5%). Logistic regression showed that only the first component scores (Odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 97.1 [16.5-570.3], p < 0.001,), and none of the others (all p > 0.05), associated with PASC. Cluster analysis revealed two distinct clinical phenotypes among individuals with severe chronic fatigue: one marked by physical impairment and the other by diminished cognitive performance. Consistent with existing literature, we confirmed that PASC is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by extensive, interrelated symptoms. Notably, we identified specific cognitive and physical clinical phenotypes. These findings are important for future targeted diagnosis and treatment.

title: Lived experiences of post-traumatic growth in patients with acute type A aortic dissection: A qualitative study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute type A aortic dissection is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency characterized by sudden onset, severe pain, and high mortality, exerting profound physical and psychological burdens on affected individuals. While negative psychological sequelae predominate in most cases, a subset of patients demonstrates remarkable resilience, manifesting post-traumatic growth-a positive psychological transformation emerging in the aftermath of trauma. This qualitative study aimed to investigate the lived experiences of post-traumatic growth among Acute type A aortic dissection survivors, shedding light on this understudied dimension of their recovery trajectory.
METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted using a phenomenological approach. Twenty patients diagnosed with Acute type A aortic dissection were recruited through purposive sampling from a tertiary hospital in China. Data were collected via in-depth, face-to-face semi-structured interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step method to extract key themes and sub-themes.
RESULTS: Three overarching themes and eight sub-themes were identified, reflecting the multidimensional nature of post-traumatic growth in Acute type A aortic dissection patients: Reevaluating Life Priorities (reordering life priorities, valuing life), Behavioral Transformation (improving unhealthy habits, enhancing treatment adherence), and Enhanced Social Connections (strengthened family ties, gratitude for social support, reintegration into family and society, altruistic behavior).
CONCLUSIONS: This study elucidates three core dimensions of post-traumatic growth in survivors of acute type A aortic dissection: life priority reassessment, adoption of positive health behaviors, and enhanced social connectedness. The findings underscore the critical role of guided self-reflection, supported behavior change, and robust family-social support systems in facilitating psychological recovery. We recommend integrating interventions focused on post-traumatic growth, such as psychological counseling and structured family support, into standard cardiac rehabilitation protocols to promote holistic recovery. Together, these insights provide a theoretical and practical foundation for developing tailored psychosocial interventions for this patient population.

title: Impact of revised antral follicle count threshold on PCOS diagnosis: A comparative clinical study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical impact of the revised antral follicle count (AFC) threshold on polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) diagnosis.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional observational study including women diagnosed using the Rotterdam criteria, stratified by AFC: 12-19 (low AFC) and ≥20 (high AFC). Clinical, metabolic, and hormonal parameters were compared against controls and amongst low and high AFC group.
RESULTS: Of 336 PCOS women, 208 (62%) had an AFC between 12 and 19 and would not meet the revised ≥20 follicle threshold for the diagnosis of polycystic morphology. These women had worse metabolic and androgenic profiles than controls, and were similar to the high AFC group.
CONCLUSION: Excluding low AFC women may misclassify patients who require clinical care.

title: Why can't they "Go back"? - A multi-group comparative analysis of pre-service teachers' hometown return intention in local universities based on latent profile analysis.
abstract: The high-quality development of rural education urgently requires strengthening the supply of outstanding rural teachers. Based on Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), a survey of 6,546 teacher education students from local universities in Heilongjiang Province revealed that the willingness to teach in rural areas among three identified profiles-the Weak Foundation Profile, the Development-Oriented Profile, and the Excellence-Prepared Profile-is significantly influenced by academic year and family capital. This influence manifests differentiated patterns via the "environment-person-behaviour" transmission pathway: family support acts as a common motivating factor for rural teaching willingness across all three groups; for foundation-weak students, professional competence primarily exerts a mediating effect through the family support pathway; for development-oriented students, professional competence shows no significant mediating effect in this pathway; and for excellence-oriented students, the willingness to return to their hometowns for rural teaching is jointly driven by the dynamic interplay between environmental factors and individual professional competence. Therefore, a differentiated approach is imperative: policy orientation should strengthen the enabling role of family support, optimise the pathways for localised training and incentives for rural teachers, and establish a growth system for rural education leaders. These measures will further refine the long-term mechanisms for attracting and retaining talent in rural teaching positions.

title: Longitudinal physical-mental multimorbidity trajectories by sociodemographic factors: a cohort study using electronic health records in Scotland (2000-2021).
abstract: Multimorbidity, the co-occurrence of two or more chronic conditions, is a pressing global health challenge. However, research capturing the dynamic, longitudinal nature of health trajectories, particularly the intersection of physical and mental domains, remains scarce compared to traditional cross-sectional "snapshots." Leveraging up to 21 years of electronic health records data from 858,789 Scottish patients in the University of Dundee Health Informatics Centre, we used multistate modelling to explore how individuals transition from a disease-free baseline into multimorbidity, evaluating how age, sex, and socioeconomic status shape these pathways. Overall transition estimates were driven by the younger demographic of our baseline disease-free cohort. The findings highlight the critical role of severe, hospital-contacting mental health conditions in driving early-onset multimorbidity, particularly in young men and socioeconomically disadvantaged groups. These findings underscore the urgent need to prioritise integrated physical-mental care and address upstream structural determinants of health. This temporal approach identifies high-risk populations for targeted early interventions and informs policy initiatives aimed at reducing health disparities.

title: From skills to smart care: The mediating role of digital literacy in the relationship between digital competence and medical artificial intelligence readiness among nursing students.
abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare requires nurses to possess strong digital competence, advanced digital literacy, and readiness to engage with AI technologies. Despite this need, the ways in which digital competence influences AI readiness, and the mediating role of digital literacy, remain underexplored. This descriptive cross-sectional study examined 500 undergraduate nursing students from two Universities for Health Sciences in Saudi Arabia and Egypt using validated measures of digital competence, digital literacy, and medical AI readiness. Results indicated strong positive correlations between digital competence, digital literacy, and AI readiness, with digital literacy partially mediating the effect of digital competence on AI readiness. These findings highlight the importance of integrating ethical, reflective, and AI-focused digital literacy alongside technical skills in nursing education, ensuring that future nurses are prepared to use medical AI effectively and safely, thereby supporting clinical decision-making and improving quality of care.

title: Structure-based computational prioritization of Emodin-8-glucoside as a candidate ligand for the VEGFR1 kinase domain in the context of placenta previa.
abstract: Placenta previa is a serious obstetric condition associated with abnormal placental implantation and hemorrhagic complications, for which no targeted pharmacological therapy is established. This study applied an integrated structure-based computational workflow to explore the intracellular VEGFR1 kinase domain as a candidate molecular target. Twenty-one phytochemicals were screened using AutoDock Vina and MOE, with Emodin-8-glucoside consistently prioritized among the highest-ranked compounds. Redocking of the co-crystallized ligand 8ST reproduced its experimental pose with a heavy-atom RMSD of 1.465 Å. Comparative 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations showed persistent binding-site association of Emodin-8-glucoside and the 8ST control. End-point energy estimates were method dependent, with MM-GBSA yielding a negative mean estimate while MM-PBSA yielded a near-zero estimate with substantial variability. DFT analysis produced a HOMO-LUMO gap of 0.13204 Hartree (approximately 3.59 eV). SwissADME and ProTox 3.0 identified low gastrointestinal absorption, P-glycoprotein substrate behavior, high polarity, and several predicted toxicity liabilities. Overall, Emodin-8-glucoside represents an in-silico-prioritized exploratory candidate requiring biochemical, selectivity, placental-cell, and pregnancy-safety validation.

title: Sickle cell disease screening: Experiences of parents with positive newborns at Korle Bu TeachingHospital.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore parents experiences following receipt of positive newborn screening for sickle cell disease (SCD) test results at a teaching hospital in Ghana.
METHODS: Using purposive sampling, data were collected using semi-structured individual guides to interview parents of children attending the Paediatric SCD clinic at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital (KBTH), a major referral health facility in Ghana. Questions were categorized into 3 main areas: parents' reactions to initial positive results, parents' responses to in-clinic counselling, and parents' attitudes towards follow-up clinic care. The Socio-Ecological Model of Health was used to underpin this study. Interviews were conducted face-to-face either in English or a local dialect (Twi), after which they were transcribed verbatim. Data were analyzed using NVivo software and Microsoft Word to identify relevant codes, which were then organized into themes and sub-themes.
RESULTS: Twenty-four mothers and one father were interviewed between 2nd November 2021 and 28th January 2022. The ages of their children ranged from 7 months to 3 years 9 months. Seventeen (68%) of the parents were married, 5 (20%) had more than one child enrolled in the clinic, and 10 (40%) reported that they or their partners had SCD. The 7 themes identified were: (i) emotional response after disclosure, (ii) decision to share results, (iii) care and management of newborns at home, (iv) knowledge of genetics of SCD, (v) adherence to routine follow-up, (vi) cost, and (vii) Culture. Positive test results elicited worry, surprise, or shock in the majority, especially those with no previous knowledge of or experience with SCD. Most parents had received counselling and educational information on caring for their positive SCD children at home and the danger signs of SCD. The decision to share test results with others was influenced by fear of stigmatization. While desiring to see their children remain healthy, parents defaulted on clinic visits due to financial difficulties and the COVID-19 pandemic.
CONCLUSION: Knowledge of SCD and personal experience influenced parents' reaction to initial positive newborn screening for SCD test results. Culture and Cost were structural barriers to care. There is a need for more education about SCD among the general population and institutions, and there is a need to provide psychological and socioeconomic support for families attending the KBTH clinic.

title: Impact of structured sexual health training incorporating standardised patients on health professions students' sexual health communication competence: A single-blind randomised controlled trial in Tanzania.
abstract:
AIM: To evaluate the effect of a structured sexual health training programme incorporating standardised patients (SPs) on health professions students' sexual health communication competence, as assessed by SPs, in a Tanzanian setting.
DESIGN: Single-blind randomised controlled trial with parallel-group allocation.
SETTING: Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences, Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 312 undergraduate medical and nursing students were enrolled at the university.
INTERVENTION: Structured sexual health training incorporating didactic teaching, small-group discussions, role-play, and SP-based practice sessions.
OUTCOME MEASURES: Sexual health communication competence was assessed using SP-rated checklists at baseline and at six-month follow-up.
RESULTS: Of 310 health profession students, 73.5% were in their final year. The mean age was 24.29 years (SD = 2.51). 22.6% were female, and 60.0% reported prior sexual health training. Baseline competence scores were similar across groups. At the six-month follow-up, competence improved in both groups, with greater gains in the treatment group. Mixed ANOVA showed a significant time effect (p < .001) and a time-by-group interaction (p = .002). Exploratory item-level analyses indicated higher scores in the treatment group across most sexual health communication competencies, particularly in rapport, empathy, and information-gathering, with no significant difference observed for clear and understandable language.
CONCLUSION: Structured SP-based sexual health training incorporating SPs significantly improved sexual health communication competence during simulated consultations, particularly in patient-engagement domains. These findings support incorporating culturally adapted sexual health training into healthcare education and using SP assessments to evaluate communication competence in sensitive clinical contexts.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06428058. Registered 30 November 2023.
