title: Transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation for functional recovery in individuals with hereditary spastic paraplegia: Protocol for a pilot clinical trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) is a rare genetic neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive lower-extremity spasticity, weakness, and gait impairment resulting from corticospinal tract degeneration. With no disease-modifying therapies available, novel strategies to improve motor function are needed. Transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation (tSCS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation approach that may improve motor function but has not been prospectively evaluated in HSP. This study will assess the safety, feasibility, and preliminary efficacy of repeated tSCS in adults with HSP.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This prospective, open-label, single-arm pilot trial will enroll 15 adults with HSP. Participants will receive 16 tSCS sessions over 8 weeks targeting the lower thoracic and upper lumbar vertebral levels, followed by an 8-week follow-up. Outcomes will assess gait performance, spasticity, disease severity, mobility, walking endurance, muscle strength, 3D gait biomechanics, electromyography, and HSP-specific patient-reported measures. Exploratory blood-based neurodegenerative biomarkers and metabolomic and lipidomic profiles will investigate potential biological correlates of treatment response. Assessments will occur at baseline and weeks 4, 8, and 16. Feasibility and safety will be evaluated through recruitment, retention, adherence, and adverse events.

title: Tri-channel synergistic model for 3D human pose estimation.
abstract: 3D human pose estimation from single-view images is a fundamental and challenging task in computer vision, the key of which lies in effectively capturing the complex spatial dependencies between human joint points. Existing methods usually rely on a single computational paradigm: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) excel at capturing local physical constraints, the self-attention mechanism (Attn) is adept at modeling global dynamic correlations, and Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP) provide an efficient way for global context encoding. Although previous works have attempted to fuse these methods, they often adopt serial, simple parallel or dual-stream structures, failing to fully explore the synergistic potential among these three heterogeneous computational paradigms, which results in limited representation capability under complex or rare poses. To address the above limitations, this paper proposes a novel Tri-Channel Synergistic Model (TCSM) aiming to construct a more comprehensive and robust feature representation for single-frame pose estimation. The core idea of this model is to decouple the dependencies of different natures in human poses and perform optimal parsing in independent and functionally specific channels. Specifically, our model designs three parallel feature streams: a GCN channel for encoding structure modality based on human topology, an attention channel for capturing long-range dynamic correlation modality, and an MLP channel for efficiently extracting global context modality. To achieve deep synergy, we design a two-stage feature fusion and refinement mechanism, in which the outputs of each channel interact and are iteratively enhanced. Experiments on the Human3.6M benchmark demonstrate that TCSM achieves competitive single-frame performance. The model obtains 47.7 mm MPJPE and 37.8 mm PA-MPJPE without a pose refinement module, and the ablation results verify the contribution of the tri-channel design and the two-stage interaction mechanism.

title: Improved YOLOv26-ACearly-ASPPdeep for citrus disease and pest detection.
abstract: This study addresses early and accurate detection of citrus diseases and pests under complex orchard conditions, which is essential for timely intervention and yield protection. Existing detectors often struggle with small lesions, subtle early symptoms, and cluttered foliage backgrounds. We propose YOLOv26-ACearly-ASPPdeep, a lightweight one-stage detector that functionally decouples feature enhancement across network depth: AdaptiveConv (ACearly) is embedded in shallow C3k2 blocks to strengthen fine-grained, content-aware filtering before aggressive downsampling, while ASPP-based multi-branch context aggregation (ASPPdeep) is placed in deep backbone/neck stages to enlarge receptive-field diversity for irregular lesion morphology. SCDown modules further reduce information loss during downsampling. Experiments on a Roboflow citrus disease/pest dataset (4,358 images; blackspot, canker, greening, and healthy) show that the proposed model improves max precision from 0.75565 (baseline YOLOv26) to 0.78032 (+3.26%) and raises mean Average Precision at IoU = 0.5 (mAP@0.5) from 0.791 to 0.863. Under identical training settings, it also outperforms representative detectors including YOLOv5n, YOLOv7-tiny, YOLOv8n, and YOLOv11n in Precision, Recall, F1-score, and per-class AP, while remaining suitable for near real-time orchard monitoring (15.1 ms/image on an RTX 3090). The results indicate that depth-aware AdaptiveConv-ASPP coupling provides a practical accuracy-efficiency trade-off for smart citrus disease and pest surveillance.

title: Expert intuition vs. Algorithmic clustering: Mapping radiological subtypes in pulmonary sarcoidosis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary sarcoidosis is a heterogeneous granulomatous disease with a broad spectrum of clinical and radiological manifestations. While the traditional Scadding classification based on chest radiography remains a cornerstone of disease staging, it provides limited information regarding parenchymal involvement and poorly correlates with functional impairment. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) offers superior sensitivity in detecting subtle and early interstitial changes, yet standardized HRCT-based classification systems for sarcoidosis remain underdeveloped.
AIM: This study aimed to propose and validate a novel HRCT-based classification of pulmonary sarcoidosis grounded in expert consensus, to assess its relationship with clinical symptoms, pulmonary function, and quality of life, and to compare it with data-driven radiological groupings obtained through cluster analysis.
METHODS: The study population included patients with confirmed pulmonary sarcoidosis managed at a tertiary referral center, either as inpatients or outpatients. HRCT scans were evaluated using a modified version of the previously published questionnaire, capturing 22 radiological features per lung lobe. Based on characteristic imaging patterns, four expert-defined subtypes were proposed: (1) Lymphonodal, (2) Disseminated-Nodular, (3) Central, and (4) Fibrotic. Symptom burden was assessed using the Fatigue Assessment Scale (FAS) and the Sarcoidosis Health Questionnaire (SHQ). Spirometric and gas transfer parameters (FEV1, FVC, TL,CO) were recorded. Statistical analyses included ANOVA, Spearman's correlation, and hierarchical clustering (Ward's method with Euclidean distances), with Cohen's kappa used to evaluate concordance between classification systems.
RESULTS: Four distinct HRCT subtypes were identified through expert assessment, each reflecting varying degrees and distributions of parenchymal involvement. These subtypes differed significantly in clinical and functional presentation. The fibrotic subtype demonstrated the most severe functional impairment, with the highest prevalence of abnormal spirometry and diffusion deficits. In contrast, the lymphonodal subtype exhibited preserved lung function and minimal symptomatology. The Van den Heuvel radiological severity score showed strong correlation with radiological subtype and was significantly associated with FEV1, FVC, TL,CO, and SHQ scores. Unsupervised cluster analysis independently identified four data-driven radiological groups that partially overlapped with expert-defined subtypes, particularly in nodular and central patterns. However, the fibrotic subtype showed less distinct clustering, underscoring its radiological complexity. The agreement between expert-defined and cluster-derived classifications was limited (κ = 0.271), suggesting that the two approaches capture complementary but distinct dimensions of disease morphology.
CONCLUSIONS: HRCT-based radiological subtypes of pulmonary sarcoidosis reflect clinically meaningful differences in symptom burden, ventilatory function, and radiological severity. While expert-driven and data-driven classifications show limited concordance, both provide valuable insights into disease heterogeneity. Radiological phenotyping using HRCT may serve as a practical adjunct to traditional staging systems, offering improved risk stratification and guiding personalized treatment decisions. Further prospective validation is needed to determine its utility in routine clinical practice and to explore its integration with emerging clinical and molecular phenotyping strategies.

title: Predictive autoantibodies before the diagnosis of type I diabetes in adults.
abstract: Recent epidemiologic studies indicate that adult-onset type 1 diabetes (AOT1D) is more common than childhood-onset type 1 diabetes, yet it remains clinically underrecognized. Because little is known about the emergence of islet autoantibodies in AOT1D, we conducted a retrospective study using electronic medical records from the United States Military Health System and longitudinal serum samples from 169 individuals with AOT1D and 40 healthy controls obtained from the Department of Defense Serum Repository. Among 643 prediagnostic samples from individuals with AOT1D, IA-2 autoantibodies were the most prevalent (50%), followed by GADA (46%), IA-2β (34%), ZnT8-R (27%), and ZnT8-W (15%). Overall, 85% (144/169) of subjects were seropositive for at least one autoantibody prior to diagnosis. Analysis of the earliest available sample from all of the AOT1D cases, grouped into 5-year intervals preceding diagnosis, demonstrated a progressive increase in seropositivity over time: 38% of subjects were seropositive more than 20 years before diagnosis, increasing to 44% at 20-15 years, 59% at 15-10 years, 73% at 10-5 years, and 91% within 5 years of diagnosis. Among the 144 seropositive individuals, positivity for two or more autoantibodies was the most common pattern, occurring in 50% (72/144) of cases. Isolated GADA positivity (22%) and isolated IA-2/IA-2β positivity (24%) occurred at similar frequencies, whereas isolated ZnT8 positivity was uncommon (4%). Temporal analysis showed that isolated GADA positivity appeared earliest, with a median onset of 7.9 years before diagnosis, whereas multiple-autoantibody positivity, IA-2/IA-2β positivity, and ZnT8 positivity emerged later, with median onsets of 4.6, 4.5, and 1.9 years before diagnosis, respectively. These findings extend observations from pediatric type 1 diabetes to adults and demonstrate that AOT1D-associated autoimmunity often begins decades before clinical diagnosis, highlighting a potentially important window for risk stratification and preventive intervention.

title: Performance degradation and failure mechanisms of pultruded carbon/glass-fiber hybrid sucker rods after long-term downhole service.
abstract: Pultruded carbon/glass-fiber hybrid composite rods are increasingly used as sucker rods, yet the relationship between degradation accumulated during long-term downhole service and subsequent longitudinal splitting during retrieval and drum winding remains insufficiently understood, particularly for rods containing a carbon/glass hybrid transition region. This study compared five specimens sectioned from a pristine 22 mm-diameter parent rod with five specimens sectioned from a service-aged parent rod retrieved after 435 days of actual downhole service. Tensile, compressive, flexural, and apparent horizontal shear tests were combined with Welch's t-tests, bootstrap-assisted two-parameter Weibull analysis, scanning electron microscopy, dynamic mechanical analysis, and moisture-desorption measurements to characterize mechanical degradation and matrix/interfacial damage. After service, the mean tensile, flexural, and apparent short-beam shear strengths decreased by 10.02%, 19.92%, and 21.98%, respectively. After Holm correction, the reductions in flexural and apparent short-beam shear strength remained statistically significant, whereas the tensile-strength reduction did not (adjusted p = 0.057). The mean compressive strength decreased by only 2.25% and showed no statistically significant difference; however, its coefficient of variation increased from 2.42% to 18.88%, while the Weibull shape-parameter estimate decreased from 41.31 to 5.27, suggesting greater compressive-strength dispersion. For the carbon-fiber core, the storage modulus decreased by 34.3%, whereas the glass-transition temperature increased from 159.5 to 164.76 °C. These changes may reflect competing contributions from residual post-curing and moisture-related effects, although the underlying chemical mechanisms were not directly characterized. The greater equilibrium mass loss of the service-aged specimens during drying was consistent with greater retention of removable moisture. Scanning electron microscopy observations revealed extensive matrix fragmentation, resin loss, fiber-matrix debonding, and longitudinal interfacial cracking. Collectively, the results support a possible two-phase damage-evolution process in which prolonged fluid exposure and repeated operational loading progressively weaken the matrix and hybrid interfaces, while additional bending during retrieval and drum winding may promote the propagation and coalescence of pre-existing cracks, thereby contributing to local longitudinal splitting. These findings provide insight into the relationships among field exposure, loading-mode-dependent degradation, strength dispersion, and interfacial damage in three-region hybrid composite sucker rods.

title: Healthy lifestyle as a protective factor against the risk of gastroesophageal reflux disease: Prospective population cohort analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lifestyle modifications are recommended by American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) for managing gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), a significant health issue; but evidence is scarce. This study aims to investigate the longitudinal association between healthy lifestyle behaviors and the risk of GERD.
METHODS: We analyzed data from 306,543 participants aged between 38 and 73 years without GERD at baseline from the UK Biobank. A summarized healthy lifestyle score (range, 0-7) was calculated using seven items: never smoking, healthy sleep, moderate body mass index (BMI), regular physical exercise, moderate alcohol intake, healthy diet, and moderate tea/coffee intake. Multivariable Cox regression was performed to examine the associations.
RESULT: During a mean follow-up of 12.7 years, 27,943 (9.1%) GERD cases were identified. Each healthy lifestyle, except for moderate alcohol intake (hazard ratios [HR], 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.98-1.03) was associated with a lower risk of GERD. Relative to participants with less than 2 of summarized healthy lifestyle score, those with 2, 3, 4, and 5-7 of this score showed a significantly lower risk of GERD, with the HR of 0.94 (95% CI: 0.90-0.98), 0.83 (0.80-0.86), 0.74 (0.71-0.77), 0.63 (0.60-0.66), respectively (P for trend <0.001). Stratified analysis shows that the above associations were more pronounced among participants who were younger (< 60 years), female and employed (all P for interaction <0.05). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated similar results.
CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the importance of adherence to healthy lifestyle behaviors in reducing the prevalence of GERD in the general population.

title: Marking-based load balancing Weighted Clustering Framework for Mobile ADHOC Network.
abstract: In a mobile ad-hoc network, it has been observed that the existing weighted clustering algorithm induces high computational overhead on the mobile nodes in the cluster-head election process and distributes the load among the cluster-heads unfairly. Also, the cluster maintenance cost is very high due to the expiration or movement of the cluster-head. The purpose of this work is to mitigate the weaknesses of the existing weight-based clustering algorithm. The proposed "Marking-based Load Balancing Weighted Clustering Framework for Mobile ADHOC Network (MLWCM)" marks the weak nodes before the beginning of the election process and spares them from massive weight calculation, thus saving the scarce resources of the network. The concept of inmate affiliation reduces the maintenance cost considerably. To ensure fair load distribution among the cluster-heads, a handling factor has been computed, which is the number of nodes that a cluster-head can handle based on its available battery power. Also, to minimize the maintenance cost, a new event called inmate affiliation has been introduced. The simulation outcome reveals that the proposed framework outperforms the existing weighted clustering algorithm. MLWCM produces healthier and more stable cluster-heads. The number of members is fairly assigned to cluster-heads. Inmate affiliation allows a displaced node to get attached to an available nearby cluster silently, without inducing clustering in the complete network, which results in lower maintenance costs. Obtained results: By the simulation, it has been revealed that the MLWCM yields healthy cluster-heads in terms of battery power at a low computational cost, hence prolonging the life of the network and enabling efficient routing in the mobile ad-hoc network. For the proposed framework, MLWCM, the average battery life of the cluster-head is 73.8%, whereas for the existing WCA, the average battery life is 41.8%; hence, MLWCM enhances the stability of the network.

title: Expert consensus on the availability and consumption of herbal medicinal products in Thai pharmacies: An e-Delphi study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite the growing use of herbal medicinal products (HMPs) in Thailand, factors relevant to their availability and consumption in pharmacies remain insufficiently characterized. Pharmacies and healthcare professionals may play important roles in improving the availability and promoting their appropriate use.
METHODS: A three-round e-Delphi study was conducted among 30 multidisciplinary experts to identify and establish consensus on factors considered relevant to the availability and consumption of HMPs in pharmacies across Thailand. Experts rated the relevance and impact of each factor using a 7-point Likert scale. Consensus was defined as a Quality of the Lower Approximation (QL) score ≥ 0.75.
RESULTS: Of the 34 factors assessed, 25 reached consensus across four domains: (1) herbal medicinal products, (2) product information, (3) professional responsibilities, and (4) pharmacy operations. The National List of Essential Herbal Drugs received the highest consensus score (QL = 1.00). All nine product information factors reached consensus. Professional factors reaching consensus included product recommendation, knowledge of HMP categories, and knowledge of evidence-based efficacy and safety. Pharmacy-related factors reaching consensus included pharmacy type, business model, participation in national health programs, and location.
CONCLUSION: Expert consensus identified a set of factors considered relevant to HMP availability and consumption in Thai pharmacies. These findings provided a framework for future empirical studies and may inform policies and interventions related to product information, professional competency, and pharmacy operations.

title: Evaluation of pre-Omicron population immunity for SARS-CoV-2 in the Household Influenza Vaccine Evaluation (HIVE) cohort.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continued serosurvey for SARS-CoV-2 population immunity is critical for vaccine strain selection and identification of susceptible groups such as young children. We aim to evaluate the use of a high-throughput, low-volume assay to describe strain-specific IgG measurement in a longitudinally followed community based cohort.
METHODS: The longitudinal Household Influenza Vaccine Evaluation study has observed around 300 households annually for acute respiratory illness. SARS-CoV-2 variant-specific IgG (including original, Delta, Beta, and Omicron variants) concentrations were measured using multiplex electrochemiluminescence (ECL), pseudoviral neutralization (PN), and ACE2 inhibition assays in participants who had serum samples drawn between July 1 and December 31, 2021. Spearman's rank correlation coefficient assessed correlation within and between ECL, ACE2, and PN assays. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated the performance of ECL and ACE2 assays. Generalized additive mixed models estimated population immunity by age against SARS-CoV-2 variants.
RESULTS: A total of 156 serum samples from 117 participants were selected for this study. Most (65.8%) were from adults and a majority (77.8%) received vaccination during the analysis period. High correlations were observed within ECL IgG assays (0.95-1.00), within ACE2 inhibition assays (0.70-0.99), and between assay platforms, including ECL versus PN (0.81-0.83) and ACE2 versus PN (0.88-0.95). ROC analysis demonstrated strong discrimination of vaccination status by ECL IgG assays (AUC: 0.84-0.88; sensitivity: 0.88-0.91; specificity: 0.87-0.88). ACE2 inhibition assays showed more variable performance (AUC: 0.53-0.96; sensitivity: 0.17-0.93; specificity: 0.91-1.00), with lower performance observed for some BA.2-related antigens. SARS-CoV-2 IgG concentrations generally increased with age and appeared to plateau in early adulthood, although estimates were imprecise in younger age groups because of small sample sizes.
CONCLUSION: We found a high correlation between ECL, ACE2, and PN across variants. Age-specific IgG quantities reflected behavior and infection histories collected by active surveillance.

title: Measuring destination image dissonance: A compositional data analysis of cross-media representations in Sanya's Tourism.
abstract: This study examines Sanya's tourism image disparities across cognitive, spatial, and affective dimensions in Press Generated Content (PGC), Tourist Generated Content (TGC), and Official Generated Content (OGC) (2013-2022), comparing pre-pandemic (2013-2019) and COVID-19 (2020-2022) periods. Results show: cognitive consistency in "tourism/hotels" but TGC focusing on "coastal + food" vs. PGC/OGC emphasizing policy elements; spatial misalignment between policy-driven spaces and tourists' preferred spaces, revealing a systematic dissonance between institutional promotion and on-the-ground practices; affective dominance of "enjoyment/romance" but TGC expressing unmet needs and OGC suppressing negatives. Systematic cognitive divergence exists between official and tourist narratives. The Aitchison distance measuring this divergence jumps from 19.574 in the pre-pandemic phase (2013-2019) to 40.648 during the pandemic-impacted phase (2020-2022), demonstrating that structural gaps between the two narrative systems become more pronounced amid the public health crisis. Targeted strategies are accordingly proposed to narrow such narrative discrepancies.

title: Access, barriers, and quality of life: Student perspectives on disability support in higher education.
abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to examine students' perspectives on access to disability support services, perceived barriers to service utilization, and quality of life within public higher education contexts. By examining these dimensions within the same study design and participant sample, the study aimed to provide a broader student-centered understanding of disability support and well-being in higher education.
DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: A cross-sectional survey design was employed with 79 students with disabilities who were formally registered with disability or student support services at two public universities in the Middle East, located in Qatar and Jordan. Data were collected using a questionnaire assessing perceived access to accommodations and barriers to service utilization, alongside the World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF (WHOQOL-BREF). Nonparametric statistical analyses were conducted to examine differences in student-reported experiences across the two institutional contexts.
RESULTS: Students reported moderate overall access to disability-related accommodations and support services (Mdn = 1.95, IQR = 1.81-2.17) and moderate perceived barriers to service utilization (Mdn = 1.65, IQR = 1.47-2.00). Significant between-context differences were observed in access to selected accommodations, perceived barriers, and quality-of-life domains. Notable differences included quiet examination rooms (U = 249.00, p < .001, r = .65), physical health quality of life (U = 245.00, p < .001, r = .59), environmental quality of life (U = 251.00, p < .001, r = .58), and financial barriers to accessing services (U = 326.00, p < .001, r = .55). Overall, the findings indicate that students' experiences of disability support varied across contexts in ways that were reflected in both service access and quality-of-life outcomes.
CONCLUSION: This study contributes original evidence by examining access to disability support services, barriers to utilization, and quality of life within the same study design and participant sample. By foregrounding students' perspectives and providing contextually grounded evidence from underrepresented higher education settings, the study offers valuable baseline insights to inform inclusive policy and service development in higher education.

title: A pre-post study of self-esteem, self-concept and body image among adolescents in the context of a co-created community intervention on screen use.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Excessive screen use negatively affects adolescents' self-esteem, self-concept, and body image, largely due to social comparison on digital platforms. Educational interventions are often less effective without community involvement, highlighting the importance of an ecological and participatory approach. This study aimed to assess the changes observed following the implementation of a community co-created intervention programme on screen use, self-esteem, self-concept, and positive body image among adolescents from a rural area in Catalonia.
METHODS: The study was conducted in Bellpuig, a rural municipality in Catalonia, Spain, involving adolescents aged twelve to sixteen years enrolled at `Lo Pla d'Urgell´ institute. This was a quasi-experimental single-group study with pre and post intervention measurements. The intervention program was co-created with adolescents, families, teachers, healthcare professionals, and local community stakeholders through a participatory design process, and comprised educational and participatory activities focused on fostering digital balance and promoting self-esteem, self-concept, and positive body image. Data were collected using validated self-report measures before and after the intervention. Pre-post changes were assessed using two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Differences in individual pre-post change scores between girls and boys were assessed using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests. Rank-biserial correlations with 95% confidence intervals were reported as effect-size estimates.
RESULTS: The intervention led to a moderate improvement in positive body image, self-esteem, and self-concept among adolescents. No notable differences were found in the impact of the intervention between sex participants. However, baseline differences in self-esteem and body image were observed, with higher initial values among boys.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that a community co-created intervention program can be an effective strategy to improvement positive body image and self-esteem among adolescents. Future research should explore long-term effects and adaptation to diverse populations.
PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This study underscores the value of community co-created interventions to support adolescent well-being, especially in rural areas with limited mental health resources. The findings offer useful guidance for health professionals, educators, and policymakers to design and evaluate programs that foster healthy self-perception and digital habits, while also raising community awareness.

title: Quality of recovery after arthroscopic meniscectomy with remimazolam or propofol anesthesia: A randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anesthetic technique may influence postoperative quality of recovery (QoR). Remimazolam may offer hemodynamic stability and favorable early recovery characteristics, but its effect on patient-reported QoR compared with propofol remains unclear. This is particularly relevant in minor orthopedic surgery, where QoR is a principal outcome. This randomized controlled trial compared postoperative QoR between propofol-based and remimazolam-based total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) using the QoR-40 questionnaire.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eighty adult patients undergoing elective arthroscopic meniscectomy were randomly assigned to propofol-based or remimazolam-based TIVA; 71 patients completed the QoR-40 questionnaire and were included in the final analysis (36 in the Propofol group, 35 in the Remimazolam group). The primary outcome was the global QoR-40 score on postoperative day (POD) 1. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hemodynamic variables, anesthetic and analgesic requirements, postoperative recovery profiles, pain scores, and postoperative nausea and vomiting.
RESULTS: Global QoR-40 scores on POD 1 did not differ significantly between the Propofol and Remimazolam groups (166.1 ± 16.8 vs. 170.6 ± 13.6; mean difference -4.5, 95% CI -11.8 to 2.7; P = 0.218). In an exploratory analysis, the emotional-state domain scores were higher in the Remimazolam group (37.0 ± 4.3 vs. 39.2 ± 2.5; mean difference -2.2, 95% CI -3.9 to -0.6; P = 0.009). The Remimazolam group had a longer time to full alertness (18 [15-24] vs. 37 [31-45] min; P < 0.001) and longer post-anesthesia care unit stay (30 [30-39] vs. 38 [30-50] min; P = 0.008). Intraoperative hypotension requiring ephedrine occurred more frequently in the Propofol group (44.4% vs. 17.1%; P = 0.013).
CONCLUSIONS: Global QoR-40 scores on POD 1 did not differ significantly between propofol-based and remimazolam-based TIVA in adults undergoing elective arthroscopic meniscectomy, although remimazolam was associated with greater intraoperative hemodynamic stability at the cost of slower return to full alertness.

title: Recognition and function analysis of MKK6 in immune reaction against Vibrio Parahaemolyticus in Crassostrea hongkongensis.
abstract: MKK6 is a key protein kinase that regulates inflammatory response under pathogen infection by activating MAPK signal pathway. However, the function of MKK6 remained unclear within oysters. Our research recognized a novel KK6 gene from C. hongkongensis, which is named ChMKK6. The cDNA of ChMKK6 gene was 2,760 bp in length, containing an ORF of 1,032 bp encoding 344 amino acids, with a conserved S-TKc region and a DVD region. As illustrated by amino acid alignment and phylogenetic tree, ChMKK6 shared the maximal (99.0%) identity showing MKK6 of Crassostrea gigas. As indicated by tissue expression analysis, ChMKK6 possessed the maximal expression within hepatopancreas, and was markedly increased in all tissues following Vibrio Parahaemolyticus (V. Parahaemolyticus) challenge. As stated by the qRT-PCR analysis, ChMKK6 silencing significantly suppressed IL17 transcription, suggesting its involvement in innate immunity by regulating IL17-mediated inflammatory response. Moreover, ChMKK6 silencing led to the suppression of key immune-related enzyme activities (ACP, AKP, CAT, LZM, and SOD), while raising the MDA content in gill. In addition, the antimicrobial viability of hemolymph supernatant was markedly reduced by ChMKK6 silencing. These results collectively demonstrate that ChMKK6 is a key player in immunity defense of C. hongkongensis from V. Parahaemolyticus.

title: Change in hearing loss and its association with general health in a community-based longitudinal study of middle-aged individuals: The Busselton healthy ageing study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: With the ageing of the global population, disabling hearing loss is a major health concern. While age and sex are established determinants, the relation between general and environmental health factors and the progression of hearing loss remains incompletely understood, particularly in middle-aged adults.
METHODS: We used data from the Busselton Healthy Ageing Study (BHAS), a population-based cohort in Western Australia. Adults aged 45-70 years at baseline (2010-2015) underwent audiometric testing and health assessments with a six-year follow-up. The better-ear four-frequency Pure Tone Averages for 0.5-4kHZ (4FPTA) and for high frequencies (4 & 8 kHz) (HFPTA) were calculated. Hearing loss was classified according to WHO criteria. Demographic, ear-related, general health, and environmental factors were analysed and their association with change in hearing thresholds using linear mixed models.
RESULTS: 3596 participants with reliable audiometry at baseline and follow-up were included (mean baseline age 57.9 years, 55% female). Over 6 years follow-up, the prevalence of mild-or-greater hearing loss increased from 14% to 26% (4FPTA) and from 53% to 71% (HFPTA). Thresholds worsened across all age categories, with greater deterioration in men and at higher frequencies. In univariate models, older age, male sex, higher BMI, smoking, tinnitus, chronic ear infection, noisy workplace exposure (particularly with inconsistent or absent hearing protection), hypertension and pre-diabetes were significantly associated with faster hearing decline after adjustments for age and sex.
CONCLUSIONS: In this longitudinal population-based study of middle-aged Western Australians we demonstrated that hearing thresholds significantly declined over a six-year period with greater deterioration in men and at higher frequencies. Findings suggest that hearing loss progression in midlife is shaped not only by age and sex, but also by broader metabolic and environmental health profiles. These outcomes highlight the need for future research to further clarify the complex interplay between metabolic health, environmental exposures, and hearing outcomes.

title: Symptom clusters and help-seeking behaviours during neutropenia after autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation: A qualitative study to inform oncology nursing support.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore how adult autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation recipients experience and appraise symptom constellations during neutropenia, and how these appraisals shape help-seeking and interactions with clinicians.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted in an inpatient haematopoietic stem cell transplantation unit in Wuxi, China. Adults aged 18 years or older who had undergone autologous transplantation and were neutropenic were purposively sampled to maximise variation. Semi-structured interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Twenty-two participants were interviewed between post-transplant day + 5 and +18. Participants described symptoms as interlocking constellations rather than isolated events. They differentiated expected treatment-related toxicities from possible deterioration by attending to symptom trajectories, including worsening intensity, new symptom combinations, or symptoms that felt different from the previous day. Fever-related patterns usually prompted immediate escalation. Help-seeking ranged from prompt reporting to watchful waiting, self-management followed by reporting, or withholding. These responses were shaped by uncertainty, perceived legitimacy of concerns, and reluctance to bother staff during protective isolation.
CONCLUSIONS: Symptom constellations and symptom trajectories shaped urgency appraisal and help-seeking during inpatient neutropenia after autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Cluster-informed assessment and escalation coaching may support timelier reporting and safer supportive care in protective isolation.

title: Stage-driven mortality and clinical risk stratification among lung cancer patients in Dhaka, Bangladesh: A multi-hospital secondary analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lung cancer is a major cause of cancer mortality, and patient-level outcome data from Bangladesh remain limited. Locally relevant, interpretable risk-stratification models may help identify patients with higher recorded mortality risk using routinely available clinical variables. This study evaluated mortality-associated factors and the hospital-wise internal-external validation performance of a clinical risk-stratification model among lung cancer patients in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective secondary analysis of a publicly available, de-identified multi-hospital dataset comprising 1,782 patients. The primary endpoint was recorded binary mortality status, defined from the source variable survived (No = mortality event; Yes = no recorded mortality event). Multivariable logistic regression was used for association analysis. A hospital-agnostic logistic prediction model was evaluated using leave-one-hospital-out internal-external validation. Discrimination was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration by Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, and predicted-risk deciles, and potential clinical utility by decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: Among 1,782 patients, 770 (43.2%) were recorded as survived = No. Recorded mortality increased across cancer stages: 16.3% in Stage I, 32.5% in Stage II, 55.6% in Stage III, and 79.2% in Stage IV. Compared with Stage I, adjusted odds ratios were 2.54 (95% CI 1.86 to 3.46) for Stage II, 6.66 (95% CI 4.86 to 9.14) for Stage III, and 20.77 (95% CI 14.46 to 29.83) for Stage IV. Surgery was associated with lower adjusted odds than chemotherapy (adjusted OR 0.65, 95% CI 0.48 to 0.89). Apparent AUROC was 0.769; pooled leave-one-hospital-out AUROC was 0.753 with a Brier score of 0.198. Pooled calibration yielded an intercept of -0.031 and slope of 0.911. At the evaluated 0.05 increments, the model had greater net benefit than treat-all and treat-none strategies from approximately 0.20 to 0.75.
CONCLUSION: Recorded mortality in this multi-hospital Bangladeshi lung cancer dataset was strongly stage-driven. An interpretable logistic risk model showed moderate discrimination and reasonable calibration across hospital-wise internal-external validation. These findings support further evaluation of routinely available clinical risk stratification, but independent external and prospective validation are required before clinical implementation.

title: Smooth muscle cell mineralocorticoid receptor does not contribute to atherosclerosis in male or female ApoE-knockout mice.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Young women have a lower risk of myocardial infarction (MI) compared to age-matched men, protection that is lost with aging or obesity. There are sex differences in human plaque histopathology, where male plaques are more inflamed and female plaques have more smooth muscle cell (SMC) content. The hormone aldosterone activates the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) to regulate gene transcription. Elevated aldosterone is seen with obesity and associates with significantly increased incidence of MI. Cell-type specific knockout (KO) of MR reveals a role for endothelial cell and myeloid MR in atherogenesis and plaque inflammation in male, but not in female, mice. SMC-KO of the MR did not impact plaque phenotype in male mice, but female mice have never been studied. Thus, the role of SMC-MR in atherosclerosis was tested for the first time in female mice, directly comparing male and female littermates to identify potential sex differences.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Atheroprone male and female mice with SMC-specific MR deletion were generated by crossing ApoE-KO mice to MRflox/flox×SMA-Cre-ERT2+/- mice to generate ApoE-KO/SMC-MR-KO and ApoE-KO/SMC-MR-intact littermate controls. Significant knockdown of MR mRNA expression was confirmed in aorta from male and female littermates in this model. After 8 weeks high fat diet (HFD), SMC-MR-KO did not impact aldosterone levels, blood pressure, fasting glucose and cholesterol, or body weight, although males weighed significantly more than females. Atherosclerotic plaque size and phenotype were characterized histologically in aortic root sections. SMC-MR-KO did not significantly impact aortic root plaque area in male or female mice, although females had larger plaques than males. Analysis of Oil-Red-O-stained aortic root sections revealed no significant sex or genotype difference in the percentage of the plaque made up of necrotic core or neutral lipids. Analysis of Masson's Trichrome-stained sections showed no impact of SMC-MR-KO on the percentage of the plaque composed of fibrosis. Finally, immunofluorescent staining of aortic root sections showed no impact of SMC-MR-KO on the percentage of the plaque that was positive for smooth muscle actin or Mac2, neither of which differed significantly by sex.
CONCLUSION: In ApoE-KO mice fed HFD for 8 weeks, SMC-MR-KO does not impact traditional cardiovascular risk factors or atherosclerotic plaque size or plaque composition in early atherosclerosis in either sex.

title: Predicting lymph node metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer using clinical and PET/CT-derived morphological features: An interpretable machine-learning study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is crucial for staging and treatment planning. This study aimed to establish a standardized machine learning workflow based on routinely available clinical, serological, and PET/CT-derived parameters to enhance preoperative LNM risk stratification.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 255 patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC, all of whom underwent systematic lymph-node dissection. Patients were randomly divided, with stratification by pathological lymph-node status, into a training cohort (n = 178) and an internal held-out test test cohort (n = 77). Candidate predictors were screened using univariable and multivariable logistic regression in the training cohort. Six machine-learning algorithms were trained and optimized using repeated nested five-fold cross-validation. After model development was completed, all six models were applied without modification to the test cohort. Test-set AUCs were compared using paired DeLong tests with Holm correction. The primary model was further evaluated for calibration, clinical utility, and feature contribution using SHAP. A conventional multivariable logistic regression model using the same four predictors was added as a simple reference model, and its discrimination and calibration were compared with those of XGBoost.
RESULTS: Central tumor location, elevated carcinoembryonic antigen, elevated squamous cell carcinoma antigen, and solid nodule status were retained as predictors; none of the quantitative PET metabolic parameters remained independently associated with LNM. XGBoost achieved the highest cross-validated AUC among the six candidate machine-learning algorithms in the training cohort (0.735; 95% CI, 0.653-0.813) and was therefore designated the primary model. In the internal held-out test cohort, XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0.747 (95% CI, 0.631-0.846). The conventional logistic regression reference model achieved a test AUC of 0.733 (95% CI, 0.612-0.841), with no significant difference from XGBoost (DeLong P = 0.301). Its Brier score was 0.152, compared with 0.198 for XGBoost.
CONCLUSION: XGBoost model showed moderate discrimination and a high negative predictive value for pathological LNM in NSCLC. However, its limited positive predictive value and the absence of significant differences among the candidate algorithms support cautious interpretation. External multicenter evaluation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Circulating microRNAs as potential candidate biomarkers of left ventricular reverse remodeling after myocardial infarction: A pilot study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction (MI) induces cardiac remodeling and lead to heart failure. Some patients experience reverse remodeling, characterized by improved LV function. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression and play a crucial role in remodeling processes.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to investigate the role of miRNAs in cardiac reverse remodeling after MI and identify candidate miRNAs that could predict better response to cardiac rehabilitation.
METHODS: The study enrolled 39 patients following their first MI. For final analysis, 10 patients meeting echocardiographic criteria for LVRR at 8-week follow-up (absolute LVEF increase ≥ 10% or LVESV reduction ≥ 15%) were matched with 10 patients with stable LV status (SLVS). All patients completed a cardiac rehabilitation program. Expression of 375 circulating miRNAs was quantified - those with higher baseline accumulation in the LVRR group were identified as candidate biomarkers and their target genes were analyzed.
RESULTS: Twenty patients (mean age 57 ± 9 years) were analyzed. At baseline, the SLVS group exhibited significantly higher LVEF compared to the LVRR group (53% vs. 44%, p = 0.013). Baseline regional contractility impairment in all LVRR patients was reversed in 70% of them at follow-up. Fourteen miRNAs (-15b-5p, -24-3p, -29c-3p, -99b-5p, -127-3p, -146a-5p, -199a-3p, -361-5p, -502-5p, -625-5p, -376c-3p, -18b-5p, -342-5p, and -429) were identified as candidate LVRR biomarkers. Enrichment analysis linked their targets to PI3K-Akt, MAPK, FoxO, and HIF-1 pathways.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies 14 candidate miRNAs as LVRR biomarkers post-MI. These findings highlight the biological relevance of non-coding RNA and support the need for further research and validation in large, non-pooled cohorts.
UNSTRUCTURED ABSTRACT: Myocardial infarction triggers adverse cardiac remodeling, though some patients achieve left ventricular reverse remodeling (LVRR), marked by functional and structural recovery. This pilot study investigated 39 patients to identify circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) that predict positive responses to cardiac rehabilitation. Comparing 10 LVRR responders against 10 stable patients, we quantified 375 miRNAs via RT-qPCR. At baseline, the stable group had higher ejection fractions (53% vs. 44%, p = 0.013), but 70% of LVRR patients reversed regional contractility impairment by the 8-week follow-up. We identified 14 potential biomarkers, including novel candidates (miR-502-5p, miR-376c-3p, and miR-18b-5p), whose target genes enrich pathways like PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and FoxO. These findings bridge the gap between preclinical data and clinical settings, highlighting the therapeutic potential of non-coding RNAs in cardiac reverse remodeling and necessitating further validation in larger cohorts.

title: integrating single-cell transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility profiling to decipher the molecular landscape of Hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a prevalent and lethal liver malignancy, characterized by high recurrence rates and limited therapeutic options. Current diagnostic and treatment strategies are hindered by drug resistance and a lack of effective biomarkers for early detection.
METHODS: This study aims to elucidate the role of lactylation and fibroblast cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME) of HCC, focusing on their potential as therapeutic targets. Utilizing a comprehensive multi-omics approach, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell ATAC sequencing (scATAC-seq) data from public databases (GEO, TCGA) to explore transcriptional and epigenetic landscapes at single-cell resolution.
RESULTS: Our analysis identified fibroblast cells as key players with high lactylation-related pathway activity, and CREB1 as a central transcription factor regulating lactylation-associated genes in these cells. The CREB1 regulatory network was associated with specific immune cell infiltration patterns, drug sensitivity profiles, and enrichment in critical signaling pathways such as Chemokine, TNF, NF-κB, and EMT. These findings underscore the pivotal role of lactylation-driven epigenetic regulation in fibroblasts, influencing the HCC immune microenvironment and disease progression.

title: Insecticide resistance status predetermines behavioural responses and oviposition fitness in Anopheles coluzzii.
abstract: Behavioural resistance is one of the major public health challenges facing planned vector control strategies involving insecticides. Understanding the behaviour of mosquitoes holistically when exposed to insecticides could be key to adding up to the fight against resistance. This study evaluated the behavioural responses and oviposition fitness of male and female Anopheles coluzzii exposed to selected pyrethroids, including lambda-cyhalothrin (0.05%), permethrin (0.75%), and DDT (4%). Male and female mosquitoes, aged three to five days, were exposed in eight replicates to selected insecticides for 60 minutes. Susceptibility to insecticide exposure was assessed in a total of 2,000 mosquitoes (eight replicates of 25 per sex per insecticide, across three insecticides), while behavioural assays used resistant and unexposed cohorts of 15 mosquitoes per replicate, in triplicate, for three insecticides (lambda-cyhalothrin, permethrin, and DDT). Resistant male and female mosquitoes were separated in holding buckets, tagged, sugar-fed, and kept to acclimatize for 1 hour before further exposure for the behavioural study. Square-shaped containers connected by a pipe into an H-shape were used for the experiment. Resistant mosquitoes (n = 15) were exposed to different chambers with insecticide-treated paper (WITP) and without insecticide-treated paper (WOITP) in triplicate. A similar experiment was done for unexposed mosquitoes. The flight efficiency, resting efficiency, repellency, landing, and biting efficiency of mosquitoes were recorded. Sex crossing between exposed and unexposed mosquitoes was done, and oviposition fitness was assessed. Flight efficiency of resistant mosquitoes WITP increased (mean 3.00-30.5) whereas WOITP decreased (mean 2.00-0.50) significantly (p < 0.0001). Resting efficacy WITP decreased (mean 12.50-0.00) while WOITP increased (mean 11.50-13.50) significantly (p < 0.0001). Repellency WITP decreased (mean 14.00-0.00), while WOITP did not follow a regular pattern. Likewise, landing and biting did not follow a regular pattern. Unexposed female mosquitoes had the highest blood meal (mean of 11.5). The highest ovipositioning was recorded in unexposed males and females (mean of 0.33), but no ovipositioning was recorded in other crosses (mean of 0.00). Insecticide exposure induces both behavioural avoidance and reproductive impairment in resistant Anopheles coluzzii, emphasizing the importance of incorporating behavioural endpoints into resistance monitoring programs.

title: Trust dynamics among aquaculture producers and regulators in the midwestern United States.
abstract: This qualitative study explores the relationship between producers and regulators in aquaculture production in the midwestern United States. We use the trust ecology framework to illustrate both how different dimensions of trust are present among aquaculture producers and how the dimensions of trust might be threatened. This is the first application of the trust ecology framework in aquaculture. Our findings emphasize the importance of building stronger interpersonal relationships between regulatory agencies and aquaculture producers to promote more sustainable growth in the sector. Additionally, our research shows that producers feel a need for more vocal advocacy for the industry within the regulatory system to ensure that their needs and perspectives are considered by regulators and policymakers. These findings illustrate how trust influences the relationship between producers and regulators and how building trust might allow the industry to work together to grow production and, potentially, sustainability.

title: Ankle arthrodesis and total ankle replacement - Variations in surgical practice across England using Hospital Episode Statistics database.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: End stage ankle arthritis can be managed surgically by ankle arthrodesis or total ankle replacement. Not all surgeons perform both ankle arthrodesis and total ankle replacement. This study aims to determine the numbers of ankle arthrodesis and ankle replacements being performed throughout England and to analyse variation in provision.
METHODS: This is a retrospective study using Hospital Episode Statistics data from NHS England for the period April 2013 to March 2025 categorised geographically by Integrated Care Boards (ICB) and NHS England regions and over time by financial year.
RESULTS: A total of 26,331 procedures were performed for end stage ankle arthritis. There was variation between ICBs with regards to the proportion of ankle replacements and ankle arthrodesis being performed. Over the study period, most practices changed towards an increasing proportion of ankle replacements. Patients receiving ankle replacements travelled further for their operation compared to those receiving ankle arthrodesis.
CONCLUSION: There is variation in the proportion of ankle replacements being performed compared to ankle arthrodesis for end stage ankle arthritis in each ICB and region. Patients are traveling further to receive an ankle replacement compared to an ankle arthrodesis. Further investigation is required into the potential causes of this variation and the availability of total ankle replacements to all patients across the UK. Patients should have access to all treatment options even if both operations are not performed by the consulting surgeon.

title: Bacterial infections and antibiotic susceptibility in children with sickle-cell anemia on malaria chemoprevention using Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP) or Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) in Uganda.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Over 300,000 babies are born annually with sickle cell anemia (SCA) in sub-Saharan Africa. Despite malaria chemoprevention and early penicillin prophylaxis, these children develop febrile illnesses. The effect of malaria chemoprevention regimens on the incidence of bacterial infections and antimicrobial resistance is unclear. We assessed incidence of bacterial infections and resistance patterns in children with SCA receiving weekly DP or monthly SP.
METHODS: This study was nested in a randomized, double-blind clinical trial comparing weekly DP with monthly SP. Participants were children aged 6 months to 15 years with SCA, followed every two months for a median of 14.7 months (IQR 11.2-18.2) and evaluated at all sick visits. Blood cultures were obtained for episodes of fever (axillary temperature >38℃) and processed using the BD BACTEC automated system. Bacterial identification was by phenotypic and genotypic methods. Whole-genome sequencing was performed using Illumina DNA Prep Kit, and antimicrobial resistance genes were characterized using AMRFinderPlus. Analyses were conducted in STATA 18.0 and limited to Ugandan participants.
RESULTS: Of 725 enrolled participants, 437 were from Uganda (221 DP; 216 SP). The mean (SD) age was 7.3 (3.8) years, and 52.4% were male. Pathogenic bacteria were rarely isolated, including Escherichia coli (3), Klebsiella pneumoniae (2), Staphylococcus aureus (2), Streptococcus agalactiae. (1), and Enterococcus faecalis (1). The cumulative incidence of bacterial growth over 22 months of follow-up was 2.3% (95% CI: 1.12-4.73). Children with positive cultures tended to have higher fevers and more hospitalizations. All isolates were multidrug-resistant. Multiple resistance genes were identified, including plasmid-mediated sulfonamide resistance via sul2 in both Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli.
CONCLUSION: Pathogenic bacteria were infrequently isolated from Ugandan children with SCA receiving malaria chemoprevention. The presence of sul2 indicates the possibility of plasmid-mediated sulfonamide resistance.

title: The value of angiogenic biomarkers in determining preeclampsia-related perinatal deaths: A cross-sectional study in a high burden setting of southern Mozambique.
abstract: Estimating the contribution of preeclampsia (PE) to perinatal mortality in low-resource settings remains difficult due to limited diagnostic capacity. Lack of specific histopathologic changes in stillbirth, foetuses and/or placenta often hampers assignment of PE as cause of death. While PE angiogenic biomarkers (sFlt-1, PlGF) predict adverse pregnancy outcomes, their post-mortem diagnostic utility is unclear. We evaluated the potential role of these biomarkers in identifying PE-related perinatal deaths. This cross-sectional study was conducted among pregnant women who delivered a stillborn infant or experienced an early neonatal death at Maputo Central Hospital in Mozambique. Concentrations of sFlt-1, PlGF and their ratio (sFlt-1/PlGF) were assessed in maternal blood and post-mortem foetal/neonatal and placental blood. Causes of death were determined via minimally invasive tissue sampling (MITS) and diagnostic accuracy was assessed using ROC curves for standardized and optimal biomarker cut-offs. A total of 100 women with perinatal deaths (98 stillbirths and 2 early neonatal deaths) were included in the study between March 2021 and April 2022. Maternal sFlt-1/PlGF ratios showed the highest diagnostic accuracy for PE-related deaths (area under curve [AUC]=82%), followed by placental (AUC = 75%) and foetal blood (AUC = 61%). PlGF levels were significantly reduced in PE-associated deaths. sFlt-1/PlGF cutoffs of ≥85 and ≥110 in maternal and placental blood were reliable cut-offs for identifying PE-related foetal/neonatal deaths. Optimal ratio cut-offs were ≥50 (maternal blood), ≥ 230 (placental blood), and ≥140 (foetal blood), with maternal and placental sFlt-1/PlGF ratios showing significant associations with PE-related death (OR=10.58 and 5.98 respectively). Sensitivity and specificity in maternal and placental blood were 84% and 73%, and 67% and 78%, respectively, with a positive predictive value (PPV) of 84% in both. In conclusion, maternal and placental angiogenic biomarkers enable reliable identification of preeclampsia-related perinatal deaths and could significantly enhance cause-of-death determination in low-resource, high-burden settings. These findings underscore the potential value of biomarker measurement for both risk stratification and mortality surveillance.

title: HLA-driven variability in human cytomegalovirus immune recognition: Epitope predictions from a kidney transplant Cohort.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) infection causes life-threatening complications in transplant recipients. Despite a seroprevalence exceeding 90% in Peru, the influence of HLA diversity on HCMV immune recognition remains unexplored in the South American region. We aimed to characterize the HLA allele distribution in a Peruvian cohort and evaluate its impact on the predicted HCMV antigen-presentation landscape.
METHODS: HLA genotyping (loci A, B, C, DRB1, DQA1, DQB1) was performed in 562 kidney transplant candidates and related donors. Common allele groups (AF5%) were assigned 4-digit resolution proxies based on local prevalence. Linear T-cell epitopes from the immunodominant antigens 65 kDa phosphoprotein (pp65), Immediate early protein 1 (IE1), and Envelope glycoprotein B (gB) were predicted using high-performance algorithms. Allelic capacity to strongly bind antigenic peptides was quantified using the Predicted Strong Binder Density (PSBD).
RESULTS: We identified 16 HLA-I and 10 HLA-II common allele groups; 92% of their 4-digit proxies are widely distributed in SAM, while C*15:12 emerged as a potentially endemic variant in Peru. Screening yielded 954 HLA-I candidate epitopes, including 169 that correspond to previously reported IEDB epitopes with potential for immunotherapy. PSBD analysis revealed distinct predicted antigen-presentation profiles across the common HLA variants identified.
CONCLUSION: Our findings provide updated Peruvian HLA data and define regional HCMV antigen-presentation profiles based on predicted MHC-peptide binding affinity (PSBD). Further experimental validation of these high-confidence candidate epitopes and HLA-HCMV association studies will be necessary to determine their immunogenicity and potential utility for immune monitoring and future immunotherapeutic applications across South American populations.

title: Restless legs syndrome among third-trimester pregnant women attending ANC Clinic in public hospitals in North Wollo Zone, Ethiopia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Restless leg syndrome is uncomfortable sensations in the legs particularly while sleeping or resting at night, causing an urge to move the legs. It is a debilitating illness and has an association with quality of life and maternal and fetal outcome for pregnant women. However, RLS is underdiagnosed and poorly understood by clinicians and the general public. In Ethiopia, there was limited data on restless leg syndrome and its associated factors among pregnant women.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence of restless legs syndrome and associated factors among third-trimester pregnant women receiving ANC care in public hospital in North Wollo Zone, Ethiopia.
METHOD: An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted from November, 2023 to February, 2024. Systematic random sampling method was utilized to identify study participants. Then, an interview with a structured and pretested questionnaire and data extraction from medical charts were done for 422 women. The collected data were coded and entered using EPI DATA, and bi-variable, and multivariable logistic regression analyses were done using STATA version 16. Statistical significance was declared at a p-value less than 0.05.
RESULT: Four hundred twenty-two eligible third-trimester pregnant women (100% response rate) participated in this study, and the prevalence was identified as 11.61%. Factors such as urban residency (AOR 5.781; 95%95% CI: 1.172, 28.501), gestational age 37 weeks or more (AOR 7.789; 95% CI: 3.027, 20.039), having a history of abortion (AOR 2.381; 95% CI: 1.081, 5.246), taking iron supplementation (AOR 0.267; 95% CI: 0.094, 0.754), and alcohol drinking during pregnancy (AOR 2.289; 95% CI: 1.049, 4.995) were significantly associated with restless legs syndrome in the third trimester of pregnancy.
CONCLUSION: One out of ten third-trimester pregnant women had RLS, and living in urban areas, advanced gestational age, history of abortion, iron supplementation, and alcohol drinking have significant associations with RLS. Therefore, it is essential to give attention to RLS during pregnancy and provide support for pregnant women to get the recommended iron supplement and refrain from alcohol.

title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a complication of severe aortic stenosis. Its prevalence after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and prognostic significance are understudied, as are the post-TAVI trajectories of microvascular indices.
AIMS: The aims of this study were to determine the pooled prevalence of CMD, the influence of the diagnostic modality, the post-TAVI coronary flow reserve (CFR) and microvascular resistance changes, and the prognostic impact of baseline CMD on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI.
METHODS: Five databases were searched from January 2010 to December 2025 for studies involving adults with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI in which CMD was assessed by wire-based thermodilution, angiography-derived indices, Doppler measurements, or stress cardiac magnetic resonance. The risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and GRADE, respectively. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird) pooled CMD prevalence (stratified by modality), CFR change (mean difference; before-after design), and prognostic hazard ratios (HRs). Change in microvascular resistance was synthesized narratively. The protocol was prospectively registered (PROSPERO: CRD42025143775) and reported per the PRISMA 2020 guidance.
RESULTS: Eleven primary studies were analyzed, 10 of which (n = 1,212) contributed to the prevalence analyses. An additional study (n = 126) was included in the sensitivity analyses only. CMD prevalence was 46.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] [34.0, 59.9]; I2 = 72%) and 38.4% (95% CI [35.3, 41.7]; I2 = 0%) when assessed using wire-based thermodilution (k = 6, n = 324) and angiographic (k = 4, n = 888) indices, respectively. CFR increased post-TAVI by a pooled mean difference of +0.49 (95% CI [+0.27, + 0.71]; I2 = 72%; k = 5, n = 103 paired observations). Reductions in microvascular resistance were confined to pressure-to-velocity and reserve ratio indices, and absolute minimal microvascular resistance was unchanged (k = 4, n = 85). The HR for MACE was 3.22 (95% CI [0.98, 10.60]; I2 = 78%; k = 2, n = 585). Substantial heterogeneity reflected non-equivalent CMD definitions.
CONCLUSION: The prevalence of CMD pre-TAVI is influenced by the diagnostic method. CFR tends to improve after TAVI, likely due to reduced resting demand rather than structural repair. The CMD-MACE association should be viewed as hypothesis-generating due to limited studies, varied CMD definitions, and incompatible HR calculations. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized CMD definitions are required.

title: Network pharmacology and machine learning reveal kit as a target of roburic acid in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma: Preliminary in vitro validation.
abstract: This study aims to systematically explore the potential molecular mechanism of Roburic Acid (RBA) in the treatment of Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma (ATC) through the approaches of network pharmacology, machine learning and in vitro experiments. Public databases were used to retrieve the potential targets of RBA and disease-related targets of ATC. Intersection analysis was performed to identify the common targets, followed by the construction of a Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network for these common targets. Enrichment analyses, including GO functional and KEGG pathway analyses, were carried out for the targets. Core targets were further prioritized using SVM, LASSO and random forest machine learning algorithms. Validation of the binding affinity and stability of RBA with the core target was performed using molecular docking and dynamics simulations. Finally, in vitro experiments-including cell viability, scratch assay, apoptosis detection, and Western blot-were conducted using the ATC cell line KHM-5M to validate the therapeutic effect and underlying mechanism of RBA. A total of 401 RBA-associated targets and 2151 ATC-related targets were identified; their intersection yielded 173 shared targets. GO enrichment analysis indicated that these targets were mainly involved in responses to peptide hormones and nuclear receptor activity, among other biological functions. KEGG pathway analysis showed significant enrichment in cancer-related pathways, including the PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling pathways. Using SVM, LASSO regression, and random forest models, KIT was consistently identified as the single core target. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated strong binding between RBA and c-KIT, characterized by low binding energy and the formation of a stable protein-ligand complex. In vitro, RBA significantly reduced KHM-5M cell viability and migration; the inhibitory effect on migration became pronounced at 24 h and was comparable to that of the positive control DOX. Furthermore, RBA promoted apoptosis and dose-dependently suppressed c-KIT phosphorylation. This study integrated network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular simulations to identify KIT as a high-confidence core target of RBA in ATC. Preliminary in vitro validation demonstrated that RBA suppresses ATC cell viability and migration, induces apoptosis, and inhibits c-KIT phosphorylation in a dose-dependent manner.

title: Role of regular preventive dental visits in moderating lifestyle-related disease medical expenditures among employed adults.
abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the impact of preventive dental visits (PDVs) over a 9-year follow-up period on cumulative medical expenditures (MEs) related to lifestyle-related diseases. To this end, the study included 1,891 full-time employees (1,478 males and 413 females), aged 19-57 years, of a manufacturing company in Japan over a 9-year period. This historical cohort study was conducted from 2015 to 2023. The year 2015 served as the baseline, with the subsequent 8 years (2016-2023) used for follow-up. Based on an 8-year dental check-up follow-up survey from 2016 to 2023, participants were classified into two groups, those who reported PDVs in ≥87.5% of the years they answered the survey (regular PDVs) and those who reported PDVs in <12.5% of those years (irregular PDVs). Using 2015 as the baseline, adjustments were made for sex, age, division, Community Periodontal Index, oral health literacy, number of outpatient visits, annual MEs, annual lifestyle-related diseases medical expenditures (LDMEs), lifestyle habits, and health risks. Cumulative LDMEs per capita from 2016 onwards were examined in each group classified as with or without regular PDVs. To adjust for confounding variables between the two groups, we performed a propensity score matching. Although no significant differences in the proportion of individuals incurring LDMEs between the groups with and without regular PDVs, the LDMEs per capita among those who incurred expenditures were significantly lower in the group with regular PDVs. In sensitivity analysis, the threshold for group classification was changed. Specifically, the analysis was conducted with participants who had PDVs in ≥50% vs. those who had PDVs in <50% yielded similar findings as those obtained in the main model. Our results suggest that regular PDVs are associated with moderating LDMEs. These findings may serve as a motivation for promoting preventive dentistry in both corporate and public health initiatives.

title: Effects of microtrauma on joint structural changes in the Curdlan-injected SKG mouse model of ankylosing spondylitis.
abstract: Although microtrauma is considered a potential environmental factor in the development of ankylosing spondylitis (AS), there is a lack of experimental research regarding its precise contribution to disease pathogenesis. To induce physiological microtrauma, the right ankles of SKG mice were immobilized for a week using surgical plaster and a pipette tip to stimulate compensatory mechanical overload in the contralateral limb. Following the removal of the immobilization, the mice were intraperitoneally injected with 3 mg of Curdlan. In this model, the non-immobilized left ankle served as the microtraumatized group, while the immobilized right ankle served as the internal control. Arthritis severity was clinically scored weekly for 5 weeks. At 6 weeks, ankle, hip, and sacroiliac (SI) joint changes were evaluated using histological and micro-CT analyses. The microtraumatized (left) ankles of Curdlan-injected SKG mice exhibited exacerbated arthritis severity, synovitis, and enthesitis compared with the control ankles. Micro-CT analysis revealed a significantly elevated inflamed bone volume in the microtraumatized ankles. Immunohistochemistry showed markedly higher expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) in the synovium and enthesis of the microtraumatized ankles. Notably, distant pathological changes, including proteoglycan loss and joint space narrowing, were also observed in the left hip joints. Collectively, these findings indicate that compensatory microtrauma significantly exacerbates joint inflammation and pathological bone destruction in the Curdlan-injected SKG mouse model, highlighting mechanical stress as a critical aggravating factor in AS progression.

title: Cardiovascular risk prediction models for women: A systematic review protocol.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women. Cardiovascular risk prediction models are widely used to guide preventative management, although many do not incorporate female-specific risk factors. The aim of this review is to identify published cardiovascular risk prediction models for women or those which include female-specific predictors and to summarize the predictors and model performance.
METHODS: The protocol was developed following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA-P) guidelines. The protocol has been registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261420766). An update of the systematic review by Baart et al. will be performed by searching MEDLINE and EMBASE from July 27 2017 to May 2026 to identify primary articles reporting on the development and/or validation of models predicting incident cardiovascular disease in women. Data on model predictors, performance, validation and clinical usability will be extracted. Risk of bias will be assessed using PROBAST+AI. Findings will be synthesized descriptively although quantitative synthesis will be considered when sufficiently comparable studies are available.
CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review will provide an updated synthesis of cardiovascular risk prediction models in women and summarize how female-specific risk factors are incorporated into contemporary risk assessment.

title: Differences in treatment and outcome of patients with ST- elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI in Germany.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI (NSTEMI) are very similar regarding pathophysiology and clinical treatments, especially NSTEMI comprises a much more heterogenic group of patients and underlying diseases. We therefore aimed to assess the treatments and outcomes of both entities in a large contemporary cohort.
METHODS: Patients with STEMI and NSTEMI between 01/01/2010-31/12/2018 were identified from the largest German health insurance (AOK, ≈ 26 million members). Patient demographics, their hospital course, adherence to guideline-directed drug therapy and overall survival were assessed.
RESULTS: In total 544,529 patients (mean age 74, IQR 62-82), one third of whom had a STEMI. Chronic kidney disease, peripheral arterial disease, and heart failure were more common in patients with NSTEMI. Patients with STEMI were more likely to get coronary angiograms and percutaneous coronary interventions. Although STEMI more frequently led to cardiogenic shock, the rate of serious cardiac events was lower. Mortality was higher for STEMI only within the first 30 days, whereas long-term survival rates were better. The combination of statins, angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors/angiotensin receptor blockers, beta blockers, and oral anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents was associated with higher overall survival in patients with STEMI (hazard ratio [HR] 0.21; 95% confidence interval [95%CI] 0.20-0.23; p < 0.001) or NSTEMI (HR 0.40; 95%CI 0.38-0.42; p < 0.001). Nevertheless, the prescription rates decreased over time, particular in patients with NSTEMI.
CONCLUSION: Clear differences between STEMI and NSTEMI were observed regarding short- and long-term survival. Guideline-recommended therapy improved long-term survival, but decreased during the follow-up period.

title: Documenting Trofinetide Treatment Phenotypes in Rett Syndrome with a Dual-LLM Consensus Pipeline
abstract: Objective: Trofinetide, approved in 2023 as the first Rett syndrome treatment, lacks scalable real-world monitoring because chart review is labor-intensive. We developed a dual large language model (LLM) consensus pipeline to extract 18 treatment-response phenotypes, comprising 4 adverse effects, 13 Rett clinical features, and medication refusal, from clinical notes. Materials and Methods: We analyzed 26,763 notes from 108 patients with confirmed sustained trofinetide exposure at Texas Children's Hospital. The pipeline filters notes by keyword, classifies each through two LLMs requiring consensus, and aggregates a patient-by-timepoint matrix. Architecture and prompt were selected on a diarrhea development set, then frozen and applied to the other 17 phenotypes with the phenotype definition substituted, as an out-of-sample test. The reported prompt comparison scores 183 expert-labeled cells. Results: A prompt requiring diarrhea to be active and severe performed best (84.2 $\pm$ 0.0% accuracy; F1 = 0.674), 47 percentage points above regular-expression matching ($p < 0.0001$). Expert reviewers judged six of the pipeline's calls per phenotype, three positive and three negative, and agreed with 90.2% (92/102). The 13 Rett clinical features are manifestations of the disorder itself rather than adverse effects of trofinetide. Gross and fine motor impairment, language/communication, and stereotypy were documented present in 92-100% of patients at every visit. Discussion: In-context LLM extraction captured multi-domain treatment responses. The outcome is documented presence at each visit, not a direction-of-change judgment. Conclusion: Coupling in-context LLM reasoning with a consensus architecture offers a scalable alternative to keyword and regular-expression extraction for real-world evidence, adapting to new phenotypes and medications through configuration alone.
