title: Survival and disease burden of breast cancer (Monastir, Tunisia): A population-based cohort study (2002-2022).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population-based evidence on Breast Cancer (BC) survival and disease burden in Tunisia remains limited. This study aimed to describe BC survival and temporal trends, quantify the BC burden, and assess the impact of early diagnosis on survival and burden.
METHODS: We conducted a descriptive population-based cohort study of women diagnosed with BC in Monastir between 2002 and 2014, with follow-up through January 2022. Overall survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods, and factors associated with mortality were assessed using multivariable Cox regression. BC burden was quantified using disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), comprising years of life lost (YLLs) and years lived with disability (YLDs). Relative risks (RRs) and related measures were used to assess the association between stage at diagnosis and mortality.
RESULTS: Among 1,075 incident BC cases identified between 2002 and 2014, 21.4% were diagnosed at stage IV. By 2022, vital status information was available for 959 women. The crude and age-standardized mortality rates were 11.9 (95% CI, 8.5-15.4) and 12.5 (95% CI, 8.9-16.0) per 100,000 WY, respectively. Median survival was 187 months (95% CI, 163.7-210.2), reaching 226 months among women diagnosed at stages 0-I. Three-, five-, and ten-year survival rates were 77.0%, 70.0%, and 45.2%, respectively. Ten-year relative survival showed a significant upward trend among women aged 30-64 years, corresponding to the target population of the national BC early detection program (APC, 5.37%; 95% CI, 2.03-8.82; p = 0.005). The total BC burden was 10,665.4 DALYs, including 10,362 YLLs (97.3%). Median DALYs per patient was 28.0 years (IQR, 13.74-36.95). Diagnosis at stages 0-II was associated with a 22% reduction in ten-year mortality (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.67-0.91), with an NND of 9. Diagnosing 61 women at stages 0-II rather than III-IV would avoid one DALY.
CONCLUSION: The significant upward trend in ten-year survival among women targeted by the national BC early detection program, together with the avoidance of one DALY per 61 women diagnosed at stages 0-II rather than III-IV, supports continued investment in early detection and BC control in Tunisia.

title: Brain tumor segmentation using a combination of graph cut and optimized U-Net with genetic algorithm: An efficient hybrid framework for enhanced medical image analysis.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of low-grade gliomas (LGGs) in FLAIR MRI remains challenging due to low-contrast tumor boundaries, irregular morphology, and extreme class imbalance. This work presents a lightweight hybrid segmentation framework that integrates three complementary components: (1) a fast graph-based region refinement step using GrabCut applied during training only to enhance tumor-background contrast, (2) a compact U-Net architecture whose filter configuration is automatically selected using a small-scale genetic algorithm, and (3) an analytical evaluation of lightweight post-processing strategies studied separately from the final GA-optimized model. The method was evaluated on the LGG-MRI-Segmentation dataset using strict patient-level splits of 79 training, 19 validation, and 12 testing patients. The final model achieved strong slice-wise performance with a mean Dice of 0.9132 and a median Dice of 0.9855; the lower mean reflects the influence of more difficult, lower-performing slices and therefore provides a more conservative summary of overall performance across the evaluated test cases. Additional metrics include an IoU of 0.8851, sensitivity of 0.8954, precision of 0.9523, specificity of 0.9997, and an HD95 of 1.00 mm, indicating highly accurate boundary delineation. For contextual benchmarking, a 2D nnU-Net model was trained on the same dataset. nnU-Net achieved a mean validation Dice of 0.8450 and a best validation EMA Dice of 0.9134. Because these nnU-Net Dice values were obtained from its validation workflow rather than the exact slice-wise test procedure used for the proposed model, they are presented as contextual reference results rather than strictly matched test-set estimates. The proposed framework required substantially less training time under the evaluated implementations. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that a carefully coordinated combination of preprocessing, lightweight architectural optimization, and efficient post-processing can achieve strong segmentation performance on the evaluated dataset while remaining computationally efficient. These findings suggest that the proposed framework is promising for computationally constrained LGG segmentation workflows. However, broader clinical applicability requires validation on independent external cohorts before generalizability can be established.

title: Digital patient decision aids for cancer prevention in socially disadvantaged women: A scoping review protocol.
abstract: This scoping review aims to map and analyze the existing evidence on digital Patient Decision Aids (PtDAs) for cancer prevention targeting socially disadvantaged women. Cancer is a leading cause of premature mortality among women. Cancer prevention strategies can effectively reduce cancer incidence and mortality. Socially disadvantaged women face lower screening rates and higher mortality. Effective cancer prevention requires informed decision-making. One approach is the use of digital PtDAs. They represent a promising innovation for this population. However, their characteristics, development process, and evaluation for cancer prevention targeting this population remain underexplored. This scoping review will include digital PtDAs designed to meet the needs of socially disadvantaged women aged 18-75 in the context of cancer prevention and meeting the minimum criteria established by the International Patient Decision Aid Standards. We will include studies and sources covering quantitative and qualitative research, and gray literature. This scoping review will follow the JBI methodology for scoping reviews. A comprehensive three-step search will be conducted across MEDLINE, CINAHL, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane databases, Google Scholar and gray literature sources. All studies and sources available in any language will be considered. Citations will be imported into Rayyan for screening. Two independent reviewers will conduct study selection, data extraction, and analysis. Data will be summarized using tables and descriptive content analysis to identify characteristics, development processes, and evaluation methods of digital PtDAs. The review will be reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Findings will be submitted for publication in an international peer-reviewed journal and presented at national and international conferences focused on cancer prevention, shared decision-making, digital health or socially disadvantaged women. We will share findings with healthcare professionals, public health and cancer prevention stakeholders, and socially disadvantaged communities and their network. This protocol has been registered with the Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/f3428/).

title: Short-term subjective and EEG responses following cervical rotatory manipulation are not reproduced by simulated cracking sound: A randomized controlled study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical rotatory manipulation (CRM) is commonly used for neck-related symptoms and is often accompanied by a cracking sound. Whether a simulated cracking sound can reproduce the short-term subjective and neurophysiological responses to the complete CRM remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study compared short-term subjective and electroencephalography (EEG) responses to CRM with those following sham manipulation with or without a simulated cracking sound.
METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial with three parallel groups and a single intervention session, 54 healthy volunteers were allocated to CRM, sham manipulation, or sham + simulated sound. Positive affect, negative affect, comfort, satisfaction, and eyes closed resting state EEG were assessed before and after the intervention. Prespecified EEG derived outcomes included frontal alpha power, frontal alpha/beta ratio, occipital individual alpha frequency, and alpha band frontoparietal and frontotemporal functional connectivity.
RESULTS: CRM produced greater improvements in positive affect, comfort, and satisfaction than sham manipulation or sham + simulated cracking sound, whereas no clear difference among groups was observed for negative affect. Differences among groups were also observed in frontal alpha/beta ratio and alpha band frontoparietal and frontotemporal functional connectivity. Sham + simulated sound did not reproduce the overall pattern of subjective and EEG responses observed after CRM.
CONCLUSIONS: CRM produced greater improvements over the short-term in positive affect, comfort, and satisfaction and was accompanied by differences in selected resting state EEG outcomes compared with sham manipulation with or without simulated cracking sound. Adding simulated cracking sound to sham manipulation did not reproduce this pattern. Because CRM differed from the control conditions in several procedural components, the specific component or combination of components responsible for these differences could not be determined.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered with the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (URL: https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn; ITMCTR2025001112).

title: Using valence and arousal scoring in speech to detect depressive symptoms: A study on family caregivers.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression is a prevalent mental health condition that significantly affects individuals' well-being and daily functioning, making early depressive symptom detection crucial.
OBJECTIVES: This study explores the potential of advancing speech analytics with dimensional sentiment analysis, using valence and arousal scoring to enhance depressive symptom detection in family caregivers.
METHODS: We recruited 116 family caregivers and assessed their depression levels using the Beck Depression Inventory-II. Participants provided verbal responses to 12 open-ended questions related to family resilience. The extracted words from the responses were analyzed for sentiment using the Chinese Valence-Arousal Words dictionary to determine their valence and arousal ratings. For each participant, we computed various summary statistics (e.g., mean, variance, quantiles) and frequency-domain statistics (e.g., spectral entropy, dominant frequency components) of valence and arousal distributions. These features were then used as predictors in nine different machine learning models evaluated under repeated 5-fold nested cross-validation with cost-sensitive cutoff selection, enabling robust classification of depression levels while prioritizing the identification of true positive cases.
RESULTS: Our analysis showed that participants with higher depressive symptoms used words with more extreme valence and arousal scores than those with lower depressive symptoms. The models demonstrated strong predictive utility of these emotional dimensions: the quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA) model achieved an out-of-sample sensitivity of 0.725, a specificity of 0.563, and an AUC of 0.7. These findings support that valence and arousal analysis provides meaningful discriminative power for identifying depressive symptoms. Importantly, the high sensitivity achieved by these models ensures that individuals with elevated symptoms are more reliably detected, thereby reducing the risk of missed cases. Overall, the results suggest strong potential for automated depressive symptom detection based on emotional signal analysis, with cost-sensitive optimization reducing false negatives while maintaining clinically relevant specificity.
CONCLUSIONS: This study offers proof-of-concept evidence that emotional sentiment analysis of speech using valence and arousal scoring can capture linguistic markers associated with depressive symptoms among family caregivers. With further refinement and validation, this approach lays an important foundation for the development of more robust machine learning models and ultimately contributes to non-intrusive mental health screening tools.

title: Family SMEs as enablers or barriers to climate neutrality: A multi-level perspective on transformational management.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family firms are the dominant ownership form among European SMEs, and socioemotional wealth theory predicts their environmental behaviour in opposing directions: long-term orientation favours stewardship, capital-commitment aversion favours retrenchment. Because firm-level ownership data linked to environmental outcomes do not exist at European scale, this literature substitutes the small-firm share of a sector for the family ownership its theory concerns. We ask whether that substitution is defensible.
STUDY DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: We test four hypotheses on 3,352 sector-country-year observations, twelve sectors in twenty EU member states, 2009-2023. The dependent variable is the annual decarbonisation rate: the negative first difference of log greenhouse gas intensity per unit of value added. Data come from Eurostat air emissions accounts, business statistics, environmental tax accounts and business demography, and from ECB interest rate statistics. Models use additive country, sector and year fixed effects, with errors clustered by country-sector.
FINDINGS/CONCLUSIONS: No hypothesis is supported. The coefficient on SME concentration is negative throughout but insignificant (β1 = -0.034, p = 0.104), and the null is informative rather than inconclusive: the confidence interval [-0.074, + 0.007] excludes positive associations of consequence. Moderation by financing costs, tax exposure and enterprise maturity does not reach five per cent (p = 0.090, 0.690, 0.053). One association is robust: sectors starting from higher intensity decarbonise faster (β2 = +0.021, p < 0.001). A second, on tax exposure, proves an artefact of tax-base composition and of a shared denominator.
LIMITATIONS/FUTURE RESEARCH: Sectoral SME concentration is not a usable proxy for family-firm environmental behaviour: 58.7 per cent of its variance is sector membership, and correcting for measurement error leaves the estimate unchanged. We read this as evidence about the limits of ecological inference in family business research, not as a refutation of the theory. Progress requires linking ownership registers to environmental records.

title: Stroboscopic light stimulation safety within and beyond laboratory settings: Observational evidence and practical guidance.
abstract: Stroboscopic light stimulation (SLS) reliably evokes geometric visual hallucinations and, in some contexts, altered-state experiences. Its increasing use in research, public, recreational and exploratory clinical settings creates a need for proportionate safety guidance. The main concern is a visually triggered seizure in a susceptible individual; reported non-epileptic responses include discomfort or distress. We combined a retrospective survey of safety practices and reported events across four laboratories, provider-reported operational data from two commercial SLS platforms, and a focused review of photosensitivity and sensory intolerance. Laboratory contributors reported 20 non-serious events that interrupted or modified participation, with no reported seizures or syncopal episodes. One commercial provider reported nine medically important or otherwise notable events across approximately 3.8 million sessions. The other reported five such events across more than 400,000 sessions. Because commercial adverse-event capture was passive and the laboratory protocols and monitoring procedures were heterogeneous, these figures cannot be used to estimate incidence or establish screening effectiveness. This synthesis informed a provisional Sussex Strobe Safety Screening Questionnaire (4SQ) and a layered, context-specific risk-management approach. The resulting framework distinguishes non-serious tolerability concerns from the principal medical risk of a visually provoked seizure in a susceptible individual, and supports conservative monitored familiarisation exposure, immediate stopping procedures and systematic adverse-event surveillance. The predictive performance of the 4SQ and the effectiveness of these precautions require formal evaluation; absolute SLS risk remains uncertain.

title: Dietary and lifestyle quality and endometrial cancer: Incidence and survivorship outcomes-An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
abstract: Composite dietary and lifestyle indices capture the combined effects of multiple health-related behaviours and may better reflect real-world cancer risk and survivorship than single exposures. This umbrella review aimed to evaluate and grade the strength of evidence for associations between adherence to composite dietary and lifestyle quality indices and endometrial cancer (EC) outcomes, including risk, EC-specific survival, overall survival, disease recurrence, quality of life, and new-onset cardiometabolic diseases. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library databases were systematically searched for relevant systematic reviews. Evidence was graded using prespecified umbrella review criteria. A total of 21 systematic reviews were included. Nine investigated diet quality (7 meta-analyses) and 12 investigated lifestyle exposure or interventions (8 meta-analyses). The outcomes assessed were EC risk (N = 14), all-cause or cancer-specific mortality (N = 5), recurrence (N = 4), overall or cancer-specific survival (N = 3), QoL (N = 5), and cardiometabolic events (N = 1). Following a Mediterranean diet was associated with 29% lower odds of EC (pooled OR = 0.71, 95% CI 0.51-0.98; class IV), whereas Western dietary patterns were associated with 20% higher odds of EC (pooled OR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.03-1.39; class IV). A combined healthy diet and lifestyle approach was associated with a 46% lower hazard of EC incidence (pooled HR = 0.54, 95% CI 0.42-0.71; class III), although heterogeneity was high. No significant associations were observed between lifestyle interventions and global or domain-specific quality of life (QoL) across follow-up durations ranging from 9 weeks to 12 months, irrespective of the validated assessment instruments used. Evidence remains limited regarding the associations between diet and lifestyle factors and EC recurrence, survival, mortality, and cardiometabolic outcomes. Our umbrella review identified suggestive (class III-IV) evidence for associations between healthy dietary patterns, particularly the Mediterranean diet, and combined healthy lifestyle approaches with lower EC incidence. Evidence remains insufficient or non-significant for post-diagnosis outcomes, underscoring the need for further high-quality research.

title: Cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of the ISBAR structured handover observation tool for ICU-to-ward patient transfer in China.
abstract: The Identity, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation (ISBAR) framework is used to standardize clinical handovers. Effective ISBAR implementation requires both training and objective assessment of handover. In Chinese clinical settings, handover quality is commonly evaluated through self-reports or locally developed checklists, which provide limited information about the completeness and accuracy of information transfer. The absence of validated Chinese observational instruments restricts the identification of communication deficiencies, benchmarking of handover performance, and development of targeted workforce training and patient safety interventions. This study aimed to conduct a cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of the ISBAR Structured Handover Observation Tool and evaluate its applicability in Chinese clinical practice. The study was conducted in two phases: cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric evaluation in clinical settings. Content validity was assessed using the content validity index (CVI). Inter-rater reliability was evaluated using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) in a two-way mixed-effects model with absolute agreement. Known-groups validity was examined using the Mann-Whitney U test to compare scores across nurses with varying levels of experience. A total of 233 ICU-to-general ward handovers involving 84 nurses were observed and evaluated. The scale demonstrated good content validity, with item-level CVIs ranging from 0.86 to 1.00 and a scale-level CVI/Ave of 0.98. Based on 50 randomly selected handovers, inter-rater reliability was high, with an ICC of 0.885 for single-rater assessments and 0.939 for average-rater assessments. Known-groups validity analysis showed that nurses with more experience had significantly higher total scores than those with less experience (Z = -4.772, p < 0.001). The Chinese version tool demonstrates satisfactory validity and reliability for evaluating structured handover performance. The tool may be used to identify communication gaps, support competency-based training, monitor handover performance, and provide evidence for patient safety initiatives, facilitating its integration into nursing management and patient safety programs in Chinese clinical settings.

title: Hypoxia-inducible factor 2α does not regulate cortical brain development.
abstract: Dynamic changes in physiological oxygen levels are crucial for proper cortical brain development. In this context, oxygen is important not only for its role in energy metabolism but also as a signaling molecule. While much is already known about its most prominent signaling factor hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1α, little is known about its functionally similar isoform HIF-2α during cortical development. Therefore, we utilized HIF-2α conditional knock-out mice (Emx1 and Nestin driven), which were kept under maternal hypoxia (10% pO2), physioxia (21% pO2), or hyperoxia (75% pO2) starting at E14.5 for 48 h and analyzed their cortical development by immunohistochemistry at E16.5. The analysis of newborn neurons (BrdU+) and cortical layer IV (Tbr1+), V (Ctip2+), and upper layer neurons (Satb2+) revealed clear effects of oxygen, with hyperoxia particularly increasing the number of Ctip2+/Tbr1- layer V neurons in E16.5 fetuses. However, neither the number of newborn neurons nor the number of layer-specific neurons was affected by HIF-2α CKO. Similarly, oxygen-related effects on neural stem cells (NSCs) and neuroprogenitor cells were not mediated by HIF-2α in E16.5 fetuses. Contributing, in vitro expansion and stem cell maintenance of NSCs were accelerated by physioxia (3% pO2) compared to hyperoxia (21% pO2), without involvement of HIF-2α under either condition. In conclusion, oxygen modulates cortical development, but HIF-2α does not mediate these effects. Thus, oxygen-related changes in neurogenesis and cortical morphology appear to be regulated via HIF-2α-independent mechanisms.

title: Pulse pressure variation demonstrates dose-dependent response to volume resuscitation in pediatric craniosynostosis repair.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Restoring intravascular volume in the face of hemorrhagic blood loss is a fundamental skill critical to the practice of anesthesiology. Predictors of fluid responsiveness in pediatric patients remain a challenge. Pulse pressure variation (PPV) is a valuable predictor of volume responsiveness in adults, but the utility in pediatric resuscitation remains controversial. Surgical correction of craniosynostosis occurs early in childhood and is commonly associated with significant, rapid blood loss intraoperatively. This study examines the relationship between blood product boluses with PPV and mean arterial pressure (MAP).
METHODS: A retrospective, single center analysis of pediatric patients undergoing open cranial vault expansion over a four-year period was performed. Descriptive variables, blood product administrations, MAP, and PPV were extracted and analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model to characterize the association between blood product administration with MAP and PPV. To account for non-independence of repeated measures, the patient was modeled as a random effect with bolus events nested within the patient variable.
RESULTS: A total of 798 bolus events from 111 patients met criteria. Patient ages ranged from 1-23 months (mean 10 months, SD 4.6 months). Transfusion of blood products was associated with increase in MAP by 1.60 mmHg [95% CI: 1.14, 2.06] and reduction in PPV by 0.82 percentage points [95% CI: 0.59, 1.06] (both p < 0.001). Notably, the magnitude of PPV reduction was dose-dependent: for each additional 10 mL/kg administered, post-bolus PPV decreased by an additional 0.4 percentage points [95% CI: 0.02, 0.07] (p = 0.002). In contrast, the MAP increase was not volume-dependent (interaction p = 0.918).
CONCLUSION: This retrospective analysis of pediatric craniosynostosis repair cases at a single institution suggests that PPV is associated with a dose-dependent response to volume resuscitation, while MAP showed a fixed-magnitude response. These preliminary findings warrant further study in multicenter validity.

title: Subnational spatial co-distribution of tuberculosis and diabetes mellitus across Ghana's 16 regions following administrative reorganisation: An ecological analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: National administrative boundary reorganisations, increasingly common across sub-Saharan Africa, create discontinuities in surveillance data alignment that complicate subnational burden estimation for infectious and non-communicable diseases alike. Ghana's expansion from 10 to 16 administrative regions in 2019 provides a tractable case for demonstrating how publicly available surveillance and survey data can be used to characterise subnational co-distribution of tuberculosis and diabetes mellitus (DM) under a revised boundary structure. DM is an established risk factor for active TB, yet population-level evidence on their geographic co-distribution at the subnational level in West Africa remains scarce, and no prior study has characterised this co-distribution at the subnational level across Ghana's current 16-region structure-a gap this study addresses directly by leveraging the post-2019 administrative framework to generate region-specific evidence for programme planning.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional ecological analysis using 16 administrative regions in Ghana as the unit of analysis. TB case notification rates (per 100,000 population, 2022) were obtained from the Ghana Health Service's DHIMS2, with the Ministry of Health 2022 Holistic Assessment and WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2025 used as independent consistency checks. Regional DM prevalence estimates were drawn from the Ghana STEPS 2017 survey and published scoping literature. Sociodemographic covariates included urbanisation, a DHS-derived wealth index, mean body mass index, and smoking prevalence. Spatial autocorrelation was assessed using Moran's I with queen contiguity weights. Bivariate associations were estimated using Spearman and Pearson correlations. Negative binomial regression with log-population offset examined the adjusted association between DM prevalence and TB notification rates. A sensitivity analysis excluded the three regions created by the 2019 reorganisation.
RESULTS: TB notification rates ranged from 18.9 to 58.3 per 100,000 (mean 32.0, SD 10.1) and DM prevalence from 1.8% to 6.3% (mean 3.5%, SD 1.3). DM prevalence showed moderate positive spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = 0.40, p = 0.004); TB notification rates did not (Moran's I = -0.16, p = 0.272). Bivariate correlation between the two outcomes was moderately positive (Spearman rho = 0.638, p = 0.008; Pearson r = 0.762, p = 0.0006). In adjusted negative binomial regression, DM prevalence showed a positive but statistically imprecise point estimate (IRR = 3.62; 95% CI: 0.47 to 27.9; p = 0.217), consistent with limited power at n = 16 ecological units.
CONCLUSIONS: DM prevalence shows moderate positive spatial autocorrelation across Ghana's 16 regions, concentrated in the southern urban belt, and is moderately correlated with TB notification rates at the regional level; TB notification rates themselves did not show significant spatial clustering when tested with real-boundary contiguity weights, elevated TB notification alongside low DM prevalence, suggests that drivers other than DM dominate in that zone and that uniform national TB-DM programme approaches may be suboptimal. These methods and findings provide a reproducible template for subnational TB-DM surveillance in other post-reorganisation African programme contexts. Individual-level causal inference is not possible from this ecological design.

title: From outrage to action: Efficacy moderates the relationship between anger and prosocial political outcomes.
abstract: Politically motivated anger has surged among American adults in recent years with few signs of decline. Anger has often been associated with aggression and with violent outcomes. Here, we examined nonviolent mobilizing outcomes of anger; specifically the conditions under which anger is associated with political action and voting intentions. Informed by the Anger Activism Model (AAM; [1]), we analyzed aggregated data from a national rolling cross-sectional survey collected in the five weeks before the November 2024 U.S. presidential election (N = 1,049). We measured anger intensity, multiple forms of political efficacy (response, internal, external), commitment to social activism, and voting intention. Analyses revealed that the relationship between anger and prosocial political behavior was contingent on efficacy type and level. Among respondents with low response efficacy, very high anger was associated with greater commitment to activism but lower intention to vote. Among respondents high in these forms of efficacy, anger showed little association with either outcome. External political efficacy did not meaningfully moderate these associations. These results provide partial support for the AAM and indicate that anger's associations with political outcomes depend not only on its intensity but also on which form of efficacy is salient.

title: Maternal deaths on arrival: A 5-year retrospective study in a health district in South Africa.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Maternal deaths on arrival remain one of the blind spots in maternal death surveillance and response programs. There are no policy and guideline addressing maternal deaths on arrival in South Africa. Main objective was to analyse maternal deaths on arrival at the health facilities in a South African district. All maternal deaths on arrival at the health facilities at the Ekurhuleni district over a period of five years and nine months (July 2014 to March 2020), were retrospectively reviewed. Analysis included maternal mortality ratio, demography, gestational age at booking, delivery and deaths, newborn outcome, causes and interval between hospital discharge and presenting as dead. Descriptive statistics (proportion, mean, standard deviation, median and interquartile range) and inferential statistics (Chi-square test, Fishers exact test and Students t test) comparing the women with known and unknown causes, are presented. Twenty-eight (5.72%) women out of the 489 maternal deaths were dead on arrival. The maternal mortality ratio was 7.65 maternal deaths per 100000 live births. Causes of deaths were inconclusive in 17 (60.71%). Among the known causes, the commonest (5, 45.45%) cause was haemorrhage. Median interval between discharge from hospital and presenting as dead was 2.5 days. Information on three delay model were unavailable. Delay two was mentioned for only one year where ambulance service was disrupted due to local protests against municipal services. Comparison between the known and unknown causes showed the regional hospitals had significantly higher numbers of known causes.
CONCLUSION: Maternal deaths on arrival was an important contributor to maternal mortality in this study although poorly documented. Majority attended antenatal care and delivered at the hospitals raising a suspicion of early hospital discharge and failure to timely follow-up. A protocol and guideline, with a focus on postmortem examinations should be developed for management of maternal deaths on arrival.

title: Reservoir dynamic evolution and drainage optimization in deep saturated coalbed methane of Shenfu Block.
abstract: China possesses vast deep coalbed methane (CBM) resources, However, the dynamic evolution of reservoir pressure and permeability during the production process remains unclear, which restricts their efficient development. This study conducted to reveal the dynamic evolution of coal reservoir pressure and permeability under different production rates and its influence on the productivity of deep saturated CBM wells, so as to provide a theoretical basis for efficient development. Based on actual production data from deep saturated CBM vertical wells in the Shenfu Block, and considering positive and negative effects on coal reservoirs during drainage, this study utilizes reservoir pressure and permeability prediction models and derives from production dynamics to characterize the variations of reservoir pressure and permeability under different drainage rates, and analyzes their impacts on well productivity. The gas production curves of deep saturated CBM wells in the Shenfu Block can be classified into two types: decline type and stable type. The results show that the initial pressure drop rate is the key factor leading to productivity differentiation. Stable-type wells exhibit a lower initial pressure drop rate, a wider propagation range of reservoir pressure, and a permeability improvement of 5.4%, enabling sustained and efficient CBM production. In contrast, decline-type wells experience an excessively rapid initial pressure drop rate, resulting in slow reservoir pressure decline, limited permeability enhancement of only 0.9%, and a significant drop in productivity at later stages. To achieve high and stable production of deep saturated CBM wells, a strategy of "slow drainage and controlled pressure" should be adopted. It is recommended to control the bottomhole flowing pressure drop rate within 160 kPa/d during the initial production stage; appropriately increase the rate by 50-100 kPa/d during the gas production increase stage to promote gas desorption; and adjust it back to around 50 kPa/d during the later decline stage to maintain production.

title: Feasibility, acceptability and usability of InControl web-platform intervention for older adults with chronic musculoskeletal pain: A mixed-methods pilot study protocol.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic musculoskeletal pain is highly prevalent among older adults and is associated with disability, reduced physical activity, and decreased quality of life. Digital health interventions can improve access to care and support pain self-management. InControl is a user-centered web-based platform that combines exercise and pain science education. The aim of this pilot study is to assess the usability and acceptability of the InControl platform and the feasibility of the research methods. This will help inform methodological improvements in the design of a future randomized controlled trial.
METHODS: A randomized, parallel-group, mixed-methods pilot study will be conducted with two groups: usual care group and the InControl intervention. Thirty-four participants aged 60 years or older with chronic musculoskeletal pain will be recruited at the Local Health Unit of Aveiro Region. The InControl intervention will last 8 weeks and will combine in-person sessions with remote interventions. Feasibility will be assessed using indicators of recruitment, retention, adherence, refusal, and dropout rates. Usability will be measured using the System Usability Scale, while acceptability and appropriateness will be assessed through a questionnaire and semi-structured interviews. Secondary outcomes will include pain, physical function, psychological factors, quality of life, and cognitive function. Data will be analyzed using descriptive statistics and qualitative thematic analysis.
DISCUSSION: The findings will inform the design of a future large-scale randomized controlled trial and contribute to the development of more effective digital interventions tailored to the needs of older adults with chronic musculoskeletal pain.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study is registered on clinicaltrials.gov, NCT07774416 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07774416?tab=study), August 18, 2026.

title: A comparative study of pseudo-dipole arrays and standard arrays based on the high-density DC resistivity method.
abstract: High-density direct current resistivity surveys play a crucial role in characterizing aquifer structures and groundwater contamination. However, the necessity of using multiple electrode arrays to achieve comprehensive subsurface imaging significantly prolongs field data acquisition, posing challenges to efficient hydrological investigations. This study validates an efficient approach that employs a single pseudo-dipole array to derive comprehensive datasets equivalent to those obtained from multiple standard arrays (e.g., Wenner α, β, γ). The pseudo-dipole configuration, which utilizes fixed reference electrodes positioned at the line ends, demonstrates vertical resolution comparable to that of conventional dipole arrays, while offering superior lateral resolution in our analysis. Numerical modeling and analytical solutions for homogeneous half-space, vertical contact, and multi-anomaly models confirmed that the pseudo-dipole array exhibits enhanced sensitivity to subsurface anomalies. Numerical experiments demonstrate that high-resolution apparent resistivity pseudosections and reliable inversion models, derived from transformed pseudo-dipole data, can effectively identify hydrological units. This method provides a time-efficient solution for detailed aquifer mapping and contamination plume monitoring, thereby enhancing the utility of electrical resistivity tomography in water resource management.

title: The effects of olfactory stimulation on postural control in adults: A systematic review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Olfactory stimulation has emerged as a potential modulator of postural control, yet the evidence has not been systematically synthesized. This systematic review aimed to aggregate, critically appraise, and narratively synthesize the available literature on the effects of olfactory stimulation on postural control in adults.
METHODS: This systematic review was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 guideline and the Cochrane Handbook. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261326528). A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus was performed from inception to December 1, 2025, supplemented by grey literature searches and reference list screening. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-experimental designs, and clinical trials examining olfactory stimulation effects on any quantitative measure of postural control were eligible. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment using the Downs and Black checklist. The certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) framework. Due to substantial methodological and clinical heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was conducted following the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guidelines.
RESULTS: Ten studies (six RCTs and four Non-RCTs) involving 365 participants (mean age 47.9 ± 19.8 years) were included. Olfactory stimulation with pleasant odors (e.g., lavender, black pepper) generally enhanced postural stability, particularly in older adults and under eyes-closed conditions, while unpleasant odors consistently increased postural sway. However, inhibitory effects were observed during high-precision athletic tasks. Odor-specific effects were identified, with appetitive cues producing unique facilitatory effects. According to GRADE, the certainty of evidence was moderate for dynamic balance and functional mobility, low for fear of falling, and very low for static balance.
CONCLUSION: Olfactory stimulation can modulate postural control in adults, with effects dependent on odor valence, participant traits, and task demands. Pleasant odors generally enhance stability during sensory deprivation, while unpleasant odors increase sway; however, trigeminal stimulants like ammonia may impair high-precision tasks. Evidence certainty was low to moderate, warranting cautious interpretation. These findings lay the groundwork for future research on olfactory-motor integration and clinical applications in balance rehabilitation and fall prevention. Registration: The study was registered on the International Prospective Registry of Systematic Reviews database (CRD420261326528).

title: Does a historical catch record support a stable latent structure in catch composition across ports, taxa, and years? An assessment of cooperative-level catch statistics from Lake Biwa, Japan, 1962-1972.
abstract: Historical inland-fisheries records resolved by taxon, location, and year are rare, and whether such records support stable low-dimensional structure is an empirical question. We analyzed annual catch records from Lake Biwa, Japan, covering 44 fisheries cooperatives, 13 taxonomic categories, and 11 years (1962-1972), immediately preceding major coastal modifications associated with the Lake Biwa Comprehensive Development Project. We assessed whether non-negative matrix factorization (NMF), with and without spatial smoothing based on port coordinates, provided a stable representation of port-year catch composition beyond direct summaries. Candidate ranks Q = 1-8 were evaluated using bi-cross-validation, 30 random starts, consensus diagnostics, port-block bootstrap resampling, exclusion analyses, and sensitivity analyses. Bi-cross-validation reached its minimum at Q = 8, with the one-standard-error rule selecting Q = 7, whereas component correspondence across random starts deteriorated sharply at Q ≥ 6. Because these criteria did not agree, Q = 4 was used as an operational reference under a study-specific stability rule rather than as a uniquely selected optimum. At Q = 4, three components dominated by Crucian carp, Freshwater clam, and Landlocked Ayu were reproducible and closely tracked the corresponding observed shares, whereas a mixed fourth component was less stable. Repeating the stability analyses at Q = 5 produced the same qualitative pattern of a reproducible core and less stable additional structure. Component correspondence also depended on data representation. Some observed shares and component scores showed spatial autocorrelation among reporting ports, whereas reconstruction error did not. NMF therefore identified a reproducible core representation of recorded catch composition without supporting a unique and uniformly stable latent structure. These patterns describe recorded catch composition rather than stock abundance and provide a historical reference for future comparison.

title: Geochronology and geochemistry of granitic dikes in the Xiaogushan gold deposit NE China and implications for gold mineralization.
abstract: The Xiaogushan cryptoexplosive breccia-type gold deposit is located within the eastern Hebei-western Liaoning gold belt along the northern margin of the North China Craton. The mining area contains multiple episodes of subvolcanic dikes, among which the granite porphyry and granitic aplite dikes show close temporal and spatial relationship with gold mineralization. To constrain their emplacement age, petrogenesis, tectonic setting, and metallogenic significance, integrated zircon U-Pb-Hf isotopic and whole‑rock geochemical analyses were carried out on these dikes. Zircon U-Pb dating yields emplacement ages of 163.9 ± 2.0 Ma for the granite porphyry and 162.2 ± 4.9 Ma for the granitic aplite, indicating Late Jurassic magmatism in the region. The rocks are enriched in SiO2, K2O, and LILEs, depleted in HFSEs, and classified as strongly peraluminous, high‑K calc‑alkaline S‑type granites. The primary magma, derived from Paleoproterozoic lower crust (εHf(t) = -17.7 to -13.5; TDM2 = 2.29 to 2.07 Ga), and the geochemical variations are consistent with fractional crystallization of K‑feldspar and plagioclase. Regional tectonic evidence indicates that these dikes were emplaced in a continental collisional setting related to the closure of the Mongol‑Okhotsk Ocean. This collision caused crustal thickening, deformation, and subsequent extension, which promoted mineralization. These dikes characterized by high oxygen fugacity, alkali enrichment, and moderate evolution, may facilitate metal transport and remobilize pre‑existing mineralization via associated hydrothermal systems. Their clustered occurrence thus serves as a potential indicator for deep‑seated hydrothermal activity and gold mineralization, reflecting the intense Mesozoic tectono-magmatic-metallogenic event in the northern North China Craton.

title: Investigating the transfer of physical stimuli to the dreamed body: A comparative study of muscular, vestibular, and haptic stimulation on dream incorporation.
abstract: The relationship between the dreamed body and the physical body remains an open question in sleep and dream research. This study examined whether somatosensory stimulation applied during REM sleep modulates the corresponding dream content under controlled conditions. Using a within-subject design, we compared three stimulation modalities-electrical muscular, galvanic vestibular, and haptic vibration-each paired with a modality-specific sham stimulation. Twenty-four participants completed one adaptation night followed by three consecutive experimental nights in the sleep laboratory. Dream reports were collected following rapid eye movement sleep awakenings after stimulation or sham periods, yielding a total of 120 reports. Dream incorporation of bodily sensations and actions was observed across all conditions; however, generalized linear mixed-effects analyses revealed no statistically significant differences between stimulation and sham conditions for any modality. No evidence for reliable modality-specific dream incorporation was observed under rigorous sham-controlled conditions. Rather than demonstrating robust stimulation-specific effects, these findings suggest that contextual and expectancy-related influences substantially contribute to bodily dream content under laboratory conditions while highlighting methodological challenges in dream incorporation research. By combining multiple somatosensory stimulation modalities with rigorous sham-controlled procedures, the present study provides a methodological benchmark for future investigations of dream incorporation and dream engineering.

title: Study on radiation damage of tungsten-based targets induced by deuterium ions.
abstract: The effects of homogeneously doped phases on the primary radiation damage of W-based targets were investigated by the Monte Carlo method in this paper. The results show that introducing homogeneously doped phases into W effectively reduces the energy localization of deuterium ions within the targets. Meanwhile, Under 100 keV deuterium ion irradiation, the ballistic distribution, the number of displacement collisions, and the vacancies of deuterium ions in homogeneously doped W targets are all lower than those in pure W. And longitudinal analysis along the depth of all homogeneously doped specimens confirms that homogeneously TiC-doped W offers the strongest suppression of primary radiation damage in the near-surface region. Under 200 keV deuterium ion irradiation, the governing effects of various dopant species and dopant contents on primary radiation damage are summarized as follows: increasing dopant content leads to an approximately linear reduction in vacancies, with Ti dopant showing the strongest vacancy inhibition effect, while the ion range rises linearly and W-TiC possesses the most significant range variation. Large sampling fluctuations of sputtering yield make it an unreliable indicator for evaluating doping performance. Overall, dopants effectively mitigate primary irradiation damage in tungsten. These volume-averaged primary irradiation damage results derived from SRIM simulation are expected to offer reference insights into improving the irradiation tolerance of W by optimizing their compositional design, while microstructural interface effects need further multi-scale modeling for quantitative analysis.

title: Personalized genomic landscape of prostate cancer in African American men reveals novel drivers and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: African American (AA) men experience disproportionately high prostate cancer incidence and mortality. Despite this disparity, current genomic repositories are predominantly derived from European populations, and studies using archived tissues are often limited by stromal contamination. We sought to characterize the high-resolution somatic mutational landscape of AA prostate cancer using a high-fidelity, patient-matched model system to identify population-specific drivers and therapeutic targets. We performed whole-genome sequencing (WGS) on 10 matched pairs of primary cell cultures derived from prostate tumors and adjacent non-malignant tissues of AA patients. Our analyses revealed a complex, heterogeneous landscape characterized by significant genomic instability, including frequent chromothripsis and kataegis signatures. Mutation hotspots were concentrated on chromosomes 1, 2, 3, and X, with the highest mutation density on chromosome 17. Functionally impactful mutations were identified in critical oncogenic pathways, including chromatin remodeling (CHD1, ARID1A, ATRX, KDM6A) and DNA damage response (ATM, BRCA1/2, RAD51). Additionally, we identified potentially novel candidate mutations unique to this AA cohort, distinct from those in European-centric datasets. This study provides a foundational, patient-specific WGS dataset derived from African American prostate cancer cell models. The identification of high-frequency actionable alterations in epigenetic and DNA repair pathways highlights the utility of this renewable resource for developing tailored therapeutic interventions and addressing racial disparities in prostate cancer outcomes.

title: Low diet quality increases the genetic risk of high blood cholesterol levels in Asian Indian adults [CURES - 165].
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asian Indians face an increased burden of cardiometabolic diseases, yet the interplay between genetic predisposition and diet quality in this population remains underexplored. This study aimed to examine their interaction on cardiometabolic traits in this population.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 1,020 adults (452 men, 568 women; aged 25-80 years) from the Chennai Urban Rural Epidemiology Study (CURES). A genetic risk score (GRS) of three variants: TCF7L2 rs7903146, FTO rs8050136, and FTO rs1588413 was constructed. Diet quality was evaluated using the Indian Diet Quality Score, based on the intake of eight food groups. Associations between the GRS and cardiometabolic traits, as well as the interactions between the GRS and diet quality score, were assessed.
RESULTS: A high GRS was significantly associated with higher fasting plasma glucose (p = 0.005) and glycated haemoglobin (p = 0.006). Significant interactions between the GRS and the diet quality score were observed on total cholesterol (Pinteraction = 0.003) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (Pinteraction = 0.005) concentrations, after correction for multiple testing. At the low diet quality score level, individuals with a high GRS had significantly higher total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol concentrations than those with a low GRS (p < 0.001, for all comparisons).
CONCLUSION: This study provides novel evidence for the effect of gene-diet quality interactions on lipid outcomes in Asian Indians. Individuals with higher genetic risk may be more vulnerable to lipid abnormalities when adhering to a low-quality diet, emphasising the value of integrating genetic and dietary data into personalised nutrition strategies for lipid-related cardiometabolic risk prevention.

title: Developing students' reading competence in an EFL context through annotated reading: A blended instructional design.
abstract: Annotated reading is generally believed an effective way to improve learners' reading competence. However, most existing studies focus on online annotated reading while neglecting to scaffold students throughout the entire learning process. To address the gap, this study proposed a four-stage annotated reading framework and employed a quasi-experimental design to evaluate its effectiveness in developing students' reading competence. Concurrently, students' perceptions and actualization of this pedagogy were also investigated. Results demonstrated that this framework had potential in cultivating students' reading competence, it was perceived as offering substantially more benefits than difficulties, and students who yielded greater gains exhibited higher engagement levels. Furthermore, modes of learning were not the decisive factor in learning outcomes, and students' engagement proved equally critical. The findings can facilitate the field's re-examination of technology use and shifting more focus to students' individual differences and the holistic teaching-learning process. Targeted pedagogical suggestions were presented based on the findings.

title: Real-world before-and-after evaluation of AI support for lung cancer diagnosis at three US lung nodule clinics.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health systems and payers require evidence that artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support improves care delivery. Integrating AI into lung nodule management pathways may streamline workflows, improve identification and triage of patients with pulmonary nodules, and enable earlier lung cancer diagnosis. Yet real-world evidence of clinical utility remains limited. This study evaluated the impact of implementing commercially available AI software to support the lung nodule and lung cancer care pathway across three US health systems.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A real-world before-and-after study compared clinic activity during matched 12.5-month pre-implementation and post-implementation periods at three US lung nodule clinics. Primary outcomes were the number of new patients and the number of patients undergoing at least one invasive procedure. Secondary outcomes were numbers of lung cancers and early-stage (stages I-II) lung cancers, and time from baseline CT to diagnosis. Analyses used Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U tests, with medians and interquartile ranges (IQRs) reported for continuous measures.
RESULTS: Across sites, new patients increased from 138 before to 232 after implementation, equivalent to 11.0 to 18.6 patients per month (p = 0.0002), with the median rising from 9 (IQR 7-14) to 16 (IQR 13-21) patients. Monthly patients undergoing at least one invasive procedure increased from 4.9 to 8.0 (p = 0.0085). Monthly cancers increased from 3.0 to 3.8 (p = 0.3242), while monthly early-stage cancers rose from 1.4 to 2.4 (p = 0.125). Median time to diagnosis was 58 days (IQR 33-158) before and 57 days (IQR 27-85) after implementation (p = 0.26), with IQR narrowing from 125 days to 58 days.
CONCLUSION: Implementation of the AI-enabled software was associated with significantly increased throughput of lung nodule patients and procedural volume. These results, observed prospectively post-implementation, suggest AI-assisted identification and triage can expand access to timely specialist review.

title: Hidden in historical sources: Rediscovering the thorny oyster (Spondylus gaederopus Linnaeus, 1758) in art, archives, and cultural knowledge.
abstract: The thorny oyster (Spondylus gaederopus), a Mediterranean bivalve prised during prehistoric times for its distinctive spiny purple shell, has since been overlooked in cultural and scientific records. Frequently depicted in Early Modern still-life paintings, particularly in Italian works of the seventeenth century, its representations were historically misidentified as scallops or common oysters. This participated in obscuring the visual evidence of occurrence and human use of this species during this period. Here, we adopt an interdisciplinary approach combining art historical analysis, taxonomic verification, archival research, and ethnobiological investigation to reconstruct the cultural and ecological history of S. gaederopus in Italy. We identify the species in 43 paintings dated between 1635 and 1750, predominantly by members of the Neapolitan Recco family, revealing its former abundance in coastal markets. Complementary historical documents, local knowledge, and oral testimonies confirm its culinary and cultural significance across Italy from the Early Modern period to the twentieth and twentieth-first century. Comparative measurements indicate a decline in average shell size since the seventeenth century, consistent with a potential harvesting pressure. Our findings demonstrate that unconventional sources including visual art, archival records, and oral testimonies can provide rich ecological and cultural insights, recovering lost biodiversity references and revealing human-marine interactions over centuries. Integrating such interdisciplinary evidence not only sheds light on the forgotten history of S. gaederopus but also highlights the potential of combining cultural heritage and scientific research to inform contemporary conservation strategies.

title: Redefining creativity in AI era: Bloom's taxonomy framework and peer interaction elevate higher-order thinking skills.
abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming cognitive learning by reshaping pedagogical models and raising questions about its impact on higher-order thinking. AI-driven personalized learning improves knowledge acquisition, but its effect on creativity remains largely unexplored. Most research emphasizes content delivery over cognitive engagement, which leaves gaps in understanding how AI influences deeper learning processes. This study investigates how ChatGPT-enabled personalized learning, framed through Bloom's Taxonomy, influences creative thinking among Indonesian higher education students, considering the moderating role of peer interaction. Using SEM via Smart-PLS 4.1, data from 533 Indonesian students reveal that personalized learning strengthens both lower-order cognitive skills-such as remembering, understanding, and applying-and higher-order functions, including analyzing, evaluating, and creating, which are essential for creativity. Among these, analyzing and creating have the strongest impact on creative thinking. Peer interaction selectively moderates this relationship, significantly enhancing creativity in tasks involving creation, while its effect on other cognitive functions remains limited. This study introduces a dynamic framework that integrates personalized learning, Bloom's Taxonomy, and peer collaboration, offering new insights into how tailored cognitive processes and selective peer engagement drive creativity in learning environments.

title: Evolutionary constraint on a core winter proteome across independently cold-adapted PACMAD grasses.
abstract: Grasses in the Panicoideae, Aristidoideae, Chloridoideae, Micrairoideae, Arundinoideae, and Danthonioideae (PACMAD) clade independently colonized cold environments from warm-climate ancestors, but whether their molecular responses to freezing reflect shared evolutionary solutions or lineage-specific innovations remains poorly understood at the protein level. We used comparative proteomics to test whether protein-level cold responses show stronger cross-species conservation than previously observed at the transcript level. We quantified seasonal rhizome proteomes (winter vs summer) from five PACMAD species grown in a common-garden experiment exposed to sustained sub-zero temperatures, identified differentially abundant proteins, and compared fold-change magnitudes across species using orthogroup-based correlation analyses. We further examined LEA3 protein structure through hydropathy profiling and motif analysis. Shared cold-responsive proteins showed higher cross-species fold-change correlation (ρ = 0.80) than background proteins (ρ = 0.45), despite greater divergence in baseline abundance. This correlation advantage persisted (Δρ = 0.27) after controlling for effect-size selection by comparing shared cold-responsive proteins against magnitude-matched single-species responses. LEA3 was the only ortholog elevated across all five species, with cold-tolerant species containing more tandem 11-mer repeats than the cold-sensitive maize. Two species accumulated multiple LEA3 paralogs, increasing total LEA3 abundance. Independent evolution of freezing tolerance in PACMAD grasses is consistent with evolutionary constraints on protein-level response magnitude, reflecting the retention of an ancestral protective capacity. Structural divergence of LEA3 in maize suggests that transcriptional induction alone does not ensure freezing tolerance; functional protection likely requires intact motif architecture.

title: Age-related differences in the clinical and microbiological profile of pediatric microbial keratitis in Eastern India.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the demographics, predisposing factors, microbiological profile, management, and outcomes of pediatric microbial keratitis in Eastern India, with particular emphasis on age-related differences.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective study included children with clinically diagnosed microbial keratitis between April 2024 and September 2025. Clinical, microbiological, nutritional, treatment, and outcome data were recorded. Children were categorized into two age groups: ≤ 5 years and >5 years for comparative analysis.
RESULTS: Ninety-nine eyes of 86 children were analyzed. The mean age was 5.9 ± 4.8 years, and 42 of 86 children were aged ≤5 years. Bilateral keratitis was observed exclusively in children ≤5 years (p < 0.05). Systemic risk factors such as undernutrition and vitamin A deficiency, diarrhea, and fever were significantly more common in children ≤5 years; in contrast, corneal injury was the predominant risk factor in children >5 years. Mean duration of presentation, ulcer size, and ulcer severity did not differ significantly between the two age groups, although perforation at presentation was more frequent in children >5 years. Fungal keratitis was significantly more common in children >5 years, whereas unidentified cases were more frequent in ≤5 years. Corneal ulcers resolved with medical therapy alone in 59.6% of eyes. Surgery was required in 40.4% of eyes overall, including 18.2% of eyes in children ≤5 years and 22.2% in children >5 years. At 3 months, corneal opacity was the most common outcome.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric microbial keratitis showed clear age-related differences. Younger children were more often affected by systemic and nutritional vulnerability with predominantly sterile or bacterial keratitis, whereas older children had more trauma-related and fungal disease. Early referral, improved nutritional support, and timely globe-preserving management may reduce visual loss.
CONFERENCE PRESENTATION: This research work has been selected for presentation at ARVO 2026, Denver, Colo. May 3 - 7.

title: Quality of recovery (QoR-15) after patient-controlled sedation during venous port implantation: A prespecified substudy of the PACSPI-2 randomised clinical trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative recovery after subcutaneous venous port implantation is generally considered uncomplicated; however, patient-reported recovery outcomes in patients with cancer remain poorly characterized. The impact of patient-controlled sedation (PCS) on postoperative recovery has not been established.
OBJECTIVE: To assess early postoperative recovery using the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) questionnaire in a prespecified substudy of the PACSPI-2 randomised clinical trial and to compare recovery between patients receiving local anaesthesia alone and those receiving local anaesthesia combined with patient-controlled sedation.
DESIGN AND SETTING: Prespecified substudy of a randomised, open-label clinical trial conducted at two Swedish anaesthesia departments.
PATIENTS: Three hundred thirty-four adult patients with cancer.
INTERVENTIONS: Local anaesthesia (LA) alone or LA combined with propofol-alfentanil PCS during SVP implantation.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcome was difference of postoperative total QoR-15 scores between groups. The primary endpoint of the parent PACSPI-2 trial was maximal intraprocedural pain.
RESULTS: There was no overall difference in total postoperative QoR-15 scores between the treatment groups (P = 0.61). Total QoR-15 scores changed significantly over time (P < 0.001) in both groups. By postoperative day 1 (POD 1), mean QoR-15 scores had increased from baseline in both groups (mean difference 2.9 and 3.1, respectively; P = 0.02 for both), although these changes were below the published minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 6. Before discharge, the LA + PCS group showed its largest within-group improvement in QoR-15 (mean difference 5.6, P < 0.001), primarily driven by the "Emotional state" and "Psychological support" dimensions, however no significant between group differences were observed. Median pain scores on POD 1 were 3 (IQR 2-5) in both groups, with NRS ≥ 4 reported by 49% in the LA and 48% in the LA + PCS group.
CONCLUSIONS: Early postoperative recovery after subcutaneous venous port implantation was generally good and did not differ between the LA and LA + PCS group. A transient within-group improvement in emotional and psychological recovery domains was observed before discharge in the LA + PCS group. Pain on POD 1 remained common in both groups. These findings were based on secondary analyses and should therefore be considered exploratory.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: European Union Clinical Trials Registry: EudraCT: 2021-003821-31, ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05688384.

title: Talca no es Santiago: Moral geography, rurality, and infrastructure of possibility in LGBTIQA+ violence and survival.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Violence against LGBTIQA+ individuals is not limited to discrete acts of aggression. It also constitutes a territorial ecology that unevenly distributes habitability, safety, and recognition. This study examines how the statement "Talca is not Santiago" works as more than a comment on city size: it names a moral geography where reputation, social surveillance, and uneven access to infrastructure produce distinct thresholds of visibility, risk, and agency.
METHODS: We used Reflexive Thematic Analysis (RTA) following Braun and Clarke to analyze a subcorpus of seven individual interviews and one focus group (n = 7) conducted in Talca and one focus group (n = 5) conducted in Santiago, drawn from a broader research project according to predefined criteria (density of territorial references and representation of both study sites). Reporting follows COREQ guidelines (S1 Checklist). We recruited participants through LGBTIQA+ organizations and social networks; participants self-identified with non-hegemonic sexual-gender identities, were over 18, and reported subjective experiences of violence. The analytical sample is composed predominantly of young (19-35 years) university-educated participants, with representation of cisgender, transmasculine, and non-binary identities and no trans women. We calibrate the scope of our conclusions accordingly.
RESULTS: We constructed three themes: (1) Infrastructure of possibility-LGBTIQA+ life becomes practicable or precarious depending on available circuits of information, networks, and spaces; (2) Surveillance and reputation-in medium-sized cities and rural environments, social legibility intensifies daily control and shrinks the margin to maneuver, which also affects the possibility of leaving violent relationships; (3) Mobility and education as partial territorial rupture-moving for studies and traveling through urban circuits reconfigures future horizons without erasing access asymmetries.
CONCLUSIONS: Within the scope of a young, predominantly cisgender, university-educated sample, territorial scale operates as a constitutive condition of violence and survival, not as a backdrop. Interventions on LGBTIQA+ violence therefore need to address territorial conditions: connectivity, information circulation, community spaces, and confidentiality safeguards adapted to medium-sized cities and ruralities.

title: Methodological drivers, reporting completeness, and transferability in HPV vaccination economic evaluations: A scoping review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is widely reported as cost-effective, but reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) are shaped by model structure, assumptions, comparator choice, vaccine price, threshold selection, and local screening context. Previous reviews have summarized cost-effectiveness findings but have less often examined why conclusions differ across settings.
OBJECTIVE: To map methodological evolution, drivers of variation, reporting completeness, methodological credibility, and transferability in HPV vaccination economic evaluations.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted using the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley, refined by Levac et al., and informed by JBI guidance for scoping reviews. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR, and the protocol was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (OSF). PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025, with a final search conducted on January 2, 2026. Forty-four records were mapped. Thirty-three full comparative economic evaluations formed the primary synthesis; 11 partial or non-standard economic evidence records were retained as contextual evidence. The Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) checklist was applied retrospectively to assess reporting completeness, and a descriptive structured appraisal was used to examine methodological credibility across six health-economic domains. A Welte-informed assessment was used to examine target-context contextualization.
RESULTS: The evidence base evolved from early static cohort models to dynamic transmission and individual-based approaches, while static models remained common in LMIC-focused standardized-tool analyses. The main drivers of variation were vaccine price, discounting, herd-immunity assumptions, cross-protection assumptions, and threshold selection. Reporting completeness varied and did not necessarily correspond to methodological credibility. Relevance to a study's own decision setting did not imply that its ICER could be transferred to other countries. Eleven contextual records showed emerging policy questions around delivery costs, fiscal consequences, uptake, risk-benefit framing, and non-ICER-based decision support.
CONCLUSION: The economic value reported for HPV vaccination depends on the assumptions, comparators, vaccine prices, thresholds, and local screening contexts used in each evaluation rather than on the vaccine alone. Future evaluations should explicitly justify the choice of comparator, model structure, vaccine-price assumptions, discount rates, thresholds, uncertainty analysis, and transferability assumptions. Although formal cost-effectiveness analyses of single-dose HPV vaccination have begun to emerge, evidence remains limited, particularly regarding durability, waning, delivery feasibility, gender-neutral vaccination in LMICs, and country-specific evaluations in underrepresented regions.

title: Who votes when? Midterm and presidential voters differ primarily by age.
abstract: Voters in American congressional midterm elections are widely viewed as demographically less representative than those in presidential elections - older, whiter, wealthier, and more educated. Using Current Population Survey data from 1994 through 2024 as well as voter-file data, we test this conventional wisdom and show that it is partly right but too broad. The key difference between midterm and presidential electorates is age: midterms sharply underrepresent young citizens and overrepresent older citizens compared to presidential elections, while differences between the elections by race, income, and education are much smaller. Midterm voters are, above all, older voters.

title: Protection of beta-blocker and 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A receptor agonist on myocardial ischemia injury in rats by regulating the NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the effects and related mechanisms of a β-blocker combined with a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A receptor (5-HT1AR) agonist on MI injuries in rats.
METHODS: TTC/Evans blue, H&E, Masson, and TUNEL staining were used to assess infarction area, pathological damage, fibrosis, and apoptosis in myocardial tissue. The ELISA kits were used to detect IL-1β and IL-18 levels. The immunohistochemical (IHC) staining was used in conjunction with qRT-PCR and Western blot to determine IL-1β, IL-18, NLRP3, pro Caspase-1, cleaved Caspase-1, GSDMD-FL, and GSDMD-N expression levels.
RESULTS: In myocardial tissue, the β-blocker combined with the 5-HT1AR agonist effectively reduced infarction size, mitigated pathological injury, alleviated fibrosis, and prevented apoptosis. Meanwhile, the β-blocker combined with the 5-HT1AR agonist downregulated IL-1β and IL-18 levels in serum and myocardial tissue. Notably, although it barely altered the expression of the pyroptosis precursor proteins pro Caspase‑1 and GSDMD‑FL, the combined therapy strongly suppressed the mRNA and protein levels of NLRP3, cleaved Caspase‑1, and GSDMD‑N, and reduced the ratios of pro Caspase‑1/cleaved Caspase‑1 and GSDMD-FL/GSDMD-N in myocardial tissue.
CONCLUSION: β-blocker combined with the 5-HT1AR agonist relieves MI injuries by suppressing the NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway.

title: Alterations of SLC14A1 mRNA structure are frequently detected in weak Jka presenting donors.
abstract: RNA structural changes caused by mis-splicing or transcription errors may affect antigenic features of cell surface proteins. They are especially noteworthy in the field of blood transfusion where the discrepancy between DNA-based molecular testing and serological blood typing are often encountered in clinical practice and lead to mismatched blood transfusion. In the Kidd (JK) blood group system weak Jka (Jk(a + w)) phenotype is usually missed in routine serological tests and causes delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions. However molecular bases underlying Jk(a + w) phenotype are still not clear although plentiful genomic DNA-based studies have been conducted. In this study, we used PacBio long-read sequencing to characterize open reading frame (ORF) region of SLC14A1 mRNA obtained from reticulocytes of 18 blood donors possessing JK*A alleles. Among them, 8 donors were determined as normal Jka antigen presentation and 10 donors showed Jk(a + w) phenotype in routine serological tests. We found that Jk(a + w) subjects demonstrated different exon combination patterns compared to those individuals presenting normal Jka antigens, implying the resulted SLC14A1 protein isoforms could make different contributions to the formation of the JK antigenicity. Moreover, exon skipping and exon inclusion that were frequently found in Jk(a + w) individuals could induce frameshift mutations. In addition, high levels of nucleotide insertions or deletions (indels) at 130A position were detected in the transcripts of Jk(a + w) individuals. Technical artifacts were examined using synthesized RNA templates and the results suggested that artifacts generated in reverse transcription and PCR amplification (RT-PCR) processes were unlikely the causes of these observations. All the results indicate that SLC14A1 RNA splicing and transcription fidelity play crucial roles in determining Jka antigen presentation.

title: Smoke characteristics of conveyor-belt fires in U-shaped belt-conveyor roadways under different ventilation velocities.
abstract: To elucidate the smoke characteristics of conveyor-belt fires in U-shaped belt-conveyor roadways under different ventilation velocities, small-scale combustion experiments were conducted using PVG1250S flame-retardant conveyor-belt specimens. A PyroSim model of a U-shaped roadway was subsequently developed to examine smoke transport under different ventilation velocities and prescribed thermal-source intensities. The results show that, as the ventilation velocity increased from 0.4 to 1.6 m/s, the peak CO concentration at the monitoring point decreased from 453 to 175 ppm, whereas the peak flow-rate-corrected CO transport index increased by 54.43%. The fixed-point temperature response was non-monotonic and reflected the combined effects of combustion fluctuation, smoke-layer position, buoyancy, and convective transport. Numerical simulations further reveal that buoyancy dominates smoke movement under low-velocity ventilation, promoting upstream back-layering of hot smoke along the roof and local accumulation of heat and CO near the fire source. As the ventilation velocity increases, the longitudinal airflow increasingly suppresses and entrains the fire plume, thereby weakening upstream back-layering while enhancing smoke transport toward the downstream roadway, working face and connecting roadway. Based on the composite smoke-response index, the scenario-specific characteristic transition velocity associated with a marked reduction in long-distance upstream smoke back-layering was approximately 2.24 m/s, with a transition range of 2.0-2.4 m/s under the prescribed 4800 kW thermal-source sensitivity scenario. The results provide a reference for understanding smoke redistribution and ventilation effects in U-shaped belt-conveyor roadways under comparable source, geometric, and ventilation conditions.
