title: The chytrid fungus threatens the last epidemiologically naive Neotropical montane amphibian biodiversity hotspot.
abstract: The amphibian chytrid fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (B. dendrobatidis) has caused catastrophic biodiversity loss worldwide.1,2,3 Although B. dendrobatidis is now widespread across environmentally suitable regions,4 the absence of amphibian declines in some high-suitability areas suggests the existence of refuges supporting epidemiologically naive communities. Epidemiologically naive refuges have not experienced past B. dendrobatidis epizootics despite suitable environmental conditions and may be B. dendrobatidis-free, harbor less virulent B. dendrobatidis lineages, or contain resistant host communities. As eradication of virulent B. dendrobatidis lineages is rarely successful after establishment, identifying epidemiologically naive refuges is imperative.5,6 Here, following extensive multi-year disease surveillance, we report a major epidemiologically naive refuge in the Neotropical highlands, the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (SNSM) in northern Colombia. We found no evidence for contemporary B. dendrobatidis presence, despite detecting the hypervirulent Global Panzootic Lineage in a neighboring Andean mountain range. Population genomic analyses in SNSM-endemic harlequin toads found no demographic signatures indicative of cryptic epizootic decline. Niche modeling predicted high suitability for B. dendrobatidis occurrence and B. dendrobatidis-induced declines throughout the SNSM, with climatic conditions in lowland regions surrounding the SNSM likely acting as a dispersal barrier and preventing B. dendrobatidis invasion, creating a "sky island." Infection trials using three SNSM-endemic amphibian species revealed tolerant and susceptible species. Together, our results indicate that the SNSM is an epidemiologically naive refuge at risk of invasion by hypervirulent B. dendrobatidis, which could result in the loss of 25 endemic amphibian species. We highlight the urgent need for proactive conservation action and the strict implementation of biosecurity to safeguard the unique and vast amphibian diversity of the SNSM.

title: Dual-mode dynamics in hippocampal populations enable rapid and precise spatial coding.
abstract: Hippocampal spatial representations emerge within minutes of first exposure to novel environments, challenging models based solely on gradual synaptic plasticity. Here, we show that CA1 spatial coding is organized according to a dual-mode architecture comprising a pre-organized backbone and an experience-dependent component. Backbone cells expressing immediately emerging place fields form a stable spatial scaffold and dominate positional decoding from the first traversal, whereas experience-dependent cells bearing gradually emerging fields are progressively incorporated to refine spatial representations. Analyses of ensemble activity further reveal that offline dynamics prospectively organize future spatial coding. In backbone cells, latent tuning aligns with their future place fields prior to task engagement, while in experience-dependent cells this alignment strengthens before overt place-field expression. Together, these findings identify a dual-mode organization of hippocampal populations in which offline dynamics pre-organize network activity to enable rapid and precise spatial coding in novel environments.

title: Endosome-associated Rab GTPases control distinct aspects of neural circuit assembly.
abstract: Neural circuit assembly relies on the precise regulation of cell-surface receptors that mediate signaling and adhesion. Endocytosis controls receptor activity and availability by internalizing and routing proteins through early endosomes to one of two main pathways: recycling back to the cell-surface or delivery to lysosomes for degradation. Rab GTPases direct receptors into these distinct pathways, but their specific contributions to circuit formation remain opaque. Using clonal analyses with null alleles, we dissected the roles of Rab-mediated trafficking to early, late, and recycling endosomes across multiple stages of circuit assembly in vivo. Our approach revealed that Rab5 and Rab11 regulate extensive and largely distinct developmental events, highlighting the pivotal roles of early endosome sorting and recycling pathways in circuit assembly. As neurons mature, both the spatial distribution and abundance of specific endocytic compartments change to reflect evolving trafficking demands. Our findings underscore how distinct post-endocytic trafficking fates are necessary to build neural circuits.

title: Gluconeogenic compensation renders glycogen phosphorylase non-essential as an insecticidal target in Plutella xylostella.
abstract: Glycogen phosphorylase (GP) catalyzes the rate-limiting step of glycogenolysis and supplies precursors for chitin biosynthesis in insects. Acyl urea compounds structurally related to benzoylphenylurea (BPU) insecticides are potent inhibitors of mammalian GP, raising the question of whether insect GP could serve as an independent insecticidal target. Here, we show that a mammalian GP inhibitor (GPI) potently inhibits recombinant Plutella xylostella GP (PxGP; IC50=2.96 nM), while the BPU insecticide diflubenzuron does not. Molecular docking and MM/GBSA analysis predict that this selectivity reflects differential side-chain engagement. Despite potent in vitro inhibition, GPI exhibits no insecticidal activity, and RNAi-mediated knockdown of PxGP does not impair development or survival. We provide evidence that insects compensate through upregulation of gluconeogenic enzymes (PEPCK, G-6-Pase) and protein catabolism, with enzyme activity measurements confirming ~29% reduction in GP-a activity following RNAi. Fitness assessment reveals transient larval weight loss with complete recovery of pupal weight, adult morphology, and fecundity. These findings demonstrate that GP is functionally non-essential under the tested conditions, likely through gluconeogenic compensation and alternative carbon sources, and highlight the importance of metabolic network redundancy in target-based insecticide design.

title: Reduced dorsal CA1 activity limits retention of the temporal component of declarative memory in the Cntnap2 knockout mouse model of autism.
abstract: Growing evidence implicates the hippocampus in the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder, particularly in the domains of social interactions and cognition. Yet, the mechanisms driving the hippocampal-dependent cognitive atypicalities in autism remain poorly defined. Here, we characterized how dysfunction of the CA1 subfield of the dorsal hippocampus drives abnormalities in critical components of declarative memory. Using trace fear conditioning in the Cntnap2 knockout mouse model of autism, we found that capabilities to retain the association of temporally distant stimuli (i.e. temporal binding) were reduced relative to wildtype mice. Fiber photometry and optogenetic experiments demonstrated that reduced CA1 activity during temporal gaps underlies this impairment, linking CA1 dysfunction to a deficit in long-term memory retention in autism. Using a relational/declarative memory task, we also revealed a deficit in flexible spatial memory, and a preferential use of egocentric learning strategy. This inflexible learning strategy resulted from an imbalance between memory system activity, promoting frontostriatal-dependent procedural learning instead of dorsal CA1/hippocampus-dependent relational/declarative memory. Overall, this study establishes dorsal CA1 dysfunction as a circuit-level mechanism underlying cognitive inflexibility in autism, providing a neurobiological framework for hippocampal-dependent memory deficits in the condition.

title: A framework for analyzing global Caenorhabditis elegans neural activity.
abstract: Neurons represent changes in external and internal environments by altering their activity patterns. While coherent brain-wide patterns of neural activity have been observed in neuronal populations, very little is known about their dimensionality, geometry, and how they are correlated with sensory inputs. Here, we recorded the activity of most head neurons in Caenorhabditis elegans experiencing changes in bacterial or control buffer stimuli around their nose. We first classified active neurons into six functional clusters: two sensory neuron clusters (ON and OFF responding to addition and removal of stimuli, respectively) and four motor/command neuron clusters (AVA, RME, SMDD, and SMDV). Next, we estimated stimulus selectivity for each cluster and found that while sensory neurons exhibit their maximal responses within 15 s, changes in bacterial stimuli drive maximal responses in command and motor neuron clusters after tens of seconds. Furthermore, we show that bacterial stimuli induce neural dynamics that are best described by a hyperbolic, not Euclidean, space indicating hierarchical organization in C. elegans neural population dynamics. This space was 8-dimensional, with dimensions that aligned in one sensory direction (ON and OFF neurons), two motor directions (forward-backward and dorsal-ventral), and the rest of dimensions corresponding with unclassified neurons. Collectively, we show that C. elegans neural activity can be effectively represented in low-dimensional hyperbolic space and describe how sensory information is processed by the neural network.

title: Allosteric disulfide control of ligand binding and endocytosis of KIR2DL4, the natural killer cell receptor for HLA-G.
abstract: Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA)-G is selectively expressed by fetal trophoblast cells that encounter maternal natural killer (NK) cells early in pregnancy. In response to HLA-G, the endosomal NK cell receptor KIR2DL4 induces a transcriptional program to support placental development. Structural features of KIR2DL4 that control HLA-G binding and endocytosis are unclear. Random mutagenesis revealed that three cysteines in the first immunoglobulin domain of KIR2DL4 regulate endocytosis and uptake of HLA-G. The atypical Cys10-Cys28 disulfide bond in the KIR2DL4 structure is an allosteric disulfide with potential to switch to a conventional Cys28-Cys74 bond. KIR2DL4 in human cells exists in both disulfide-bonded states, as shown by mass spectrometry analysis. The Cys10-Cys28 bond in a Cys74Ser KIR2DL4 mutant was reduced by protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) in vitro. Inhibition of PDI prevented HLA-G uptake by KIR2DL4 in NK cells. Mutants in the Cys10-Cys28 configuration endocytosed spontaneously but did not bind HLA-G. Conversely, KIR2DL4 with a Cys28-Cys74 bond was detectable at the plasma membrane and internalized soluble HLA-G. A purified Cys10Leu KIR2DL4 mutant bound HLA-G with micromolar affinity in a peptide-dependent manner. Thus, allosteric disulfide-mediated conversion from an inactive to an HLA-G binding form regulates KIR2DL4 trafficking and a functional response that promotes fetal development.

title: JAK-STAT pathway heterogeneity governs immunotherapy response in breast cancer.
abstract: The JAK-STAT pathway (JSP) is a well-known oncogenic cascade; however, recent clinical trials have detected JSP upregulation in breast cancer following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. This paradoxical observation warrants further investigation into JSP's intercellular heterogeneity, tumor dynamics, molecular mechanisms, and clinical implications for immunotherapy. JSP expression showed dynamic shifts during breast cancer progression, with higher levels in T cells and paracancerous epithelial cells. In human breast cancer tumor cells, elevated JSP is highly correlated with malignant phenotypes. JSP-high tumor cells overexpressed oncogenic pathways, while exhibiting increased immunosuppressive signaling via the MIF-CD74 signaling axis. In T cells, higher JSP levels were associated with enhanced cytotoxic activity, improved differentiation, and reduced exhaustion, reflecting robust anti-tumor immunity. Analysis of immunotherapy datasets revealed that higher JSP levels were associated with improved responses toward PD-1 inhibitors, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients, with JSP serving as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy sensitivity. As a key JSP component, STAT4 exerts dual roles in breast cancer: it drives tumorigenesis in malignant cells, sustains breast epithelial cell proliferation, and bolsters T-cell anti-tumor functionality, while also acting as a highly accurate biomarker for predicting immunotherapy response. This indicates that JSP targeting demands a nuanced approach: broad inhibition may impair anti-tumor immunity, and optimized therapeutic strategies paired with precise biomarkers are critical to maximize JSP's utility in breast cancer immunotherapy. Our findings highlight JSP's functional heterogeneity in epithelial, tumor, and T cells, with high JSP activity correlating with enhanced immunotherapy efficacy in breast cancer.

title: Anatomy and mechanics of tsetse fly blood feeding.
abstract: Human African trypanosomiasis (HAT) is a neglected tropical disease transmitted by infected tsetse flies (Glossina spp.) in sub-Saharan Africa. Infected tsetse flies can transmit trypanosomes, including Trypanosoma brucei subspecies that cause HAT in humans, as well as other trypanosome species that cause animal African trypanosomiasis in domestic animals and infect wildlife. Tsetse flies feed on a broad spectrum of hosts, including humans, elephants, buffaloes, rhinos, hippos, turtles, and monitor lizards. To understand how the insects can penetrate such diverse skin types, we detailed the anatomical structures involved in tsetse blood feeding, their mechanical properties, and the forces exerted by the fly during probing. We found that the tsetse fly's feeding apparatus does not rely on exceptionally unique structures or extraordinary forces. Instead, the tsetse fly has evolved subtle yet highly efficient adaptations, which include a labellum equipped with arrays of small teeth. When combined with a robust retraction movement of the proboscis, these structures create lesions on various types of skin, thus facilitating blood pool feeding on a broad host spectrum.

title: Eye movements reflect capacity-dependent organization of working memory.
abstract: Human cognition is capacity-limited, requiring strategies to actively structure information. Eye movements offer a natural mechanism for sequential sampling, but whether such sequences reflect memory organization is unknown. We developed a working-memory task where color-frequency pairings created a latent ordinal structure to optimally reduce memory load. Across two experiments, gaze patterns spontaneously aligned with this structure. Participants sampled items following this sequence during encoding and revisited them during maintenance. Critically, the expression of this structure depended on cognitive demand. In a 3-item task, high performers showed robust sequential sampling during encoding, whereas lower performers compensated with replay-like revisitation during maintenance. Under higher demand (4 items), encoding-based organization was disrupted, and structured revisitation emerged primarily during maintenance. These findings suggest that eye movements provide an overt expression of an internally generated organizational process that flexibly adapts to cognitive demands, revealing a behavioral analogue to neural replay when encoding resources are strained.

title: PrimeStack editors enable efficient and site-specific integration of large multigene cargos in plants.
abstract: Precise, site-specific integration of large DNA sequences into plant genomes is a long-standing goal of crop biotechnology and synthetic biology, yet remains constrained by random insertion, inefficient homologous recombination, and gene targeting. Here, we present PrimeStack, a DSB-independent platform that integrates PE with the unidirectional large serine integrase Bxb1, leveraging evolved variants for enhanced activity, to achieve the programmable insertion of multigene, multikilobase cargos at predefined genomic safe harbors (GSH) in rice (Oryza sativa). Optimized prime editors first install attP landing sites with high fidelity and heritability followed by Bxb1-mediated recombination that generates irreversible integration of genetic information. PrimeStack enabled targeted large-cargo integration in regenerated rice plants with efficiencies of up to 45%, as determined by junction-specific PCR analyses. No obvious morphological differences from WT plants were observed at 5 weeks after transfer to soil under the evaluated conditions. We validate its utility by achieving targeted insertion of a carotenoid cassette at an experimentally confirmed genomic safe harbor. PrimeStack delivers a modular, site-specific gene stacking platform that enables predictable, multigene trait pyramiding and pathway construction at GSH, thereby accelerating the development of improved and resilient crop varieties, as well as scalable plant-based biomanufacturing and a powerful chassis for synthetic biology.

title: An inositol receptor Itr4 coordinates carbon catabolite regulation and virulence in Cryptococcus neoformans.
abstract: Nutrient sensing and utilization are critical for microbes to adapt to their environment and evade predators. The encapsuled yeast Cryptococcus neoformans has a unique ability to sense and utilize the sugar inositol as both a signaling molecule and as a carbon source. This trait is advantageous not only in the natural environment but also to promote its pathogenesis, including invasion of the central nervous system. In this study, we have identified a novel inositol transporter-like receptor (transceptor) Itr4 that coordinates inositol and glucose metabolism by regulating inositol transporters (ITRs) and glucose sensor Hxs1. Itr4 binds inositol and regulates the function of other ITRs and its loss leads to a significant decrease in inositol uptake activity, resulting in a lack of mating, reduced capsule size, reduced blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, and virulence attenuation. Mutagenesis analysis of Itr4 protein identified an essential N-terminal tail and two amino acids, Q388 and Q389, as sites of functional importance. The ITR4Q388A, Q389A allele showed a dominant phenotype with increased inositol uptake, enlarged capsule and significantly attenuated virulence. In summary, we identify a new C. neoformans inositol transceptor, Itr4, the first such example in eukaryotes, with novel regulatory roles in both inositol and glucose metabolism and fungal virulence.

title: Bridging energy and proteome allocation models allows prediction of the resource cost of traits across environments.
abstract: Many traits divert resources from reproduction and are costly due to the physiological trade-offs organisms face. These traits might require the allocation of different resources, e.g., energy expenditure or production of macromolecules, and it is unclear how their costs can be compared given their different units. Moreover, the effect of environmental conditions and genetic background on the cost of traits is not well understood. Two different frameworks have been proposed to quantify the resource costs of traits, focusing on either energy allocation or proteome allocation. These frameworks implicitly assume energy provisioning or protein production limits growth, respectively, but the connection between the two limitations has been underexplored. To better connect these frameworks, we develop a framework that considers limitations in energy provisioning and macromolecule biosynthesis simultaneously to quantify and compare the cost of traits that require different resources. Using this model, we explore how environmental quality and genetic background affect the cost of traits. Notably, our model predicts that increasing food quality increases the cost of traits that require the production of new structures, while decreasing the cost of traits requiring energy expenditure. Moreover, our model makes novel predictions about the effect of degradation, recycling, and energetic demands for maintenance on the relationship between the macromolecular composition of the cells and growth rate (also known as bacterial growth laws).

title: Interindividual vocal tract diversity influences the phonetic diversification of spoken languages.
abstract: Human vocal tracts, like other physical traits, exhibit extensive interindividual variation. However, little is known about how this variation translates into phonetic diversity between speakers, and ultimately, across languages. Here we develop a biocultural model of phonetic evolution, analogous to Russell Lande's model of multivariate phenotypic evolution. We show that individual vocal tract morphologies and associated articulatory strategies leave consistent acoustic signatures, resulting in a characteristic pattern of phonetic variation within speaker groups that correlates with the pattern observed between groups. Recalling a central tenet of evolutionary biology-that within-group variation feeds between-group diversification-our findings suggest that phonologically similar vowel systems can attain phonetically diverse realizations according to a neutral-like evolutionary process. Our model serves as a null hypothesis for disentangling the biological versus cultural mechanisms underlying phonetic diversification, where deviations from the neutral expectation may indicate culturally mediated language change.

title: Interpretable neural networks prioritize cancer driver genes from genome-wide dependency landscapes.
abstract: Identifying cancer driver genes and their therapeutic impact remains a core challenge in computational cancer biology. We introduce xNNDriver and xAEDriver, two interpretable neural network frameworks that connect cancer mutations with genome-wide DepMap gene dependencies, pathway activity, and drug-response patterns. xNNDriver is a supervised pathway-guided model that evaluates whether a gene's mutation status is encoded in the genome-wide dependency landscape; we interpret model fitness as a driver potential score, which quantifies the strength of this mutation-dependency signal and prioritizes genes with broad functional footprints. Across 3,008 candidate genes, xNNDriver recovers major established drivers and highlights literature-supported candidates, while pathway analyses reveal biologically coherent programs related to metabolism, growth factor signaling, and immune regulation. To capture combinatorial functional states, xAEDriver uses an unsupervised autoencoder to learn Driver Variant Representations (DVRs), latent binary features guided by the frequency distribution of known driver mutations. DVRs capture cell-line-specific dependency patterns and expression patterns and are associated with drug sensitivity and pathway activity. Together, these interpretable deep learning models demonstrate that gene dependency landscapes encode rich, interpretable signals of oncogenic function and provide a hypothesis-generating framework for prioritizing drivers, pathways, and therapeutic vulnerabilities for further experimental validation.

title: Going around phase defects: Addressing a fundamental flaw of phase singularity detection.
abstract: Phase mapping is a widespread method for identifying rotational electrical activity sustaining cardiac arrhythmias. However, conventional implementations assume that the cardiac phase map is continuous, leading to ill-defined phase indices in regions affected by functional conduction block, fibrosis, or anatomical boundaries. These regions of discontinuous or undefined phase, termed phase defects, lead to both false positive and false negative detections of rotational drivers. This work introduces an improved phase mapping implementation termed extended phase mapping that explicitly detects and accounts for phase defects, enabling robust calculation of the phase index around them. Extended phase mapping is applied to (1) simulated excitation patterns using the Fenton-Karma model, (2) experimental optical mapping data of rat ventricular fibrillation, and (3) a clinical CARTO activation map of atrial tachycardia. Across all datasets, the extended approach eliminates erroneous detections and resolves previously missed rotations. Our results demonstrate that proper treatment of phase defects yields a unified and physiologically consistent characterization of all rotational drivers including near-complete and anatomical reentries. Therefore, we propose that explicitly accounting for phase defects, rather than tracking singular points alone, gives a more complete and consistent characterization of rotational dynamics in cardiac tissue.

title: Natural killer cell receptor signaling and activation depend on cell cycle stages.
abstract: Natural Killer (NK) cells are lymphocytes of the innate immunity and provide key protection against infection and cancer. NK cells express a wide array of inhibitory and activating receptors on the cell surface including the activating receptor NKG2D. Receptor signaling in NK cells leads to rapid post-translational modification (e.g., phosphorylation) of sub-cellular signaling proteins within minutes of receptor stimulation that ultimately give rise to diverse effector functions including cell proliferation. Recent single-cell mass cytometry (i.e., CyTOF) experiments in macrophages showed variations of abundances of phosphorylated signaling proteins across cell cycle stages indicating a dependence of cell signaling kinetics on an order of magnitude slower kinetics (~ several hours) of cell cycle transitions. We investigated cell cycle dependence of NKG2D signaling kinetics in NK cells using longitudinal CyTOF measurements up to 256 minutes post stimulation performed on IL-2-treated NKG2D-stimulated primary human CD56dim NK cells. The CyTOF experiments revealed cell stage specific kinetics of signaling proteins such as pVav1, pErk, and pS6, with the degranulation marker CD107a showing its largest upregulation specifically in the G2 + M stage. We developed stochastic minimal computational models coupling signaling and cell cycle processes to investigate the effect of cell cycle transitions on NK cell receptor induced signaling kinetics. These models suggest that the observed cell stage specific NK cell receptor signaling kinetics arise due to active modulation of the receptor signaling kinetics by cell cycle progression. The framework can be extended to study the interplay between receptor signaling and cell cycle progression in other cell types.

title: The influence of cell morphology on the dynamics and stability of model bacterial communities.
abstract: Understanding how structures arise in microbial communities remains an outstanding challenge in bacterial ecology. When replicating within dense and confined environments, bacterial populations may collectively self-organize as a result of mechanical interactions. We previously observed that model dual-populations of bacteria, colonizing open-ended microchannels, either quickly fixate to a single population or segregate into long-lived, coexisting populations. This latter quasi-stability results from the alignment of bacteria into lanes, forcing cells to grow toward the open ends of the channel, with inter-lane invasion events driving the boundary dynamics between populations. Here we apply agent-based (AB) simulations to explore the boundary dynamics between dual-bacterial populations of varying morphology and division rate. We find that the simulated boundary dynamics are well-described by a simple drift-diffusion model, which enables us to estimate the mean time to fixation within competitive scenarios where the fixation time is difficult to access by AB simulations. Coccus-like cells display a competitive advantage over bacillus cells as they can more effectively invade and ultimately fixate, while coexisting populations of bacillus cells are "effectively" stable. And while faster-dividing cells should have a selective advantage, their morphology determines if this advantage drives fixation or acts as a defensive strategy to maintain their population. These findings highlight the critical role that cell morphology and mechanics play in shaping bacterial communities.

title: Forecasting of infectious disease epidemics in sexual networks using attenuated renewal processes.
abstract: Forecasting emerging infectious disease outbreaks is particularly challenging for sexual networks of men who have sex with men (MSM), where transmission can be shaped by heterogeneous and overdispersed contact structures, mixing assortativity, and both one-time and recurrent partnerships. Using stochastic epidemic simulations on synthetic MSM networks and empirical mpox case data from major cities, we systematically evaluated five classes of short-term forecasting models, from random walk approaches to semi-mechanistic attenuated renewal processes. Model performance was assessed using the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS). Across both simulated and empirical epidemics in heterogeneous networks, renewal models attenuated by a reverse-sigmoid curve, to account for early depletion of highly-connected nodes, consistently outperformed alternatives, achieving more balanced and reliable forecasts. Our findings suggest a practical approach for robust forecasting in highly overdispersed networks, where distinguishing network effects from other factors remains challenging and usually requires additional data.

title: DipSkmer: Reference-free population genomics with diploid genome skims.
abstract: Ecologists and conservation biologists rely on genetic diversity as a key essential biodiversity variable (EBV) used to track population health and dynamics, and utilize the population-scaled mutation parameter θ as a key metric of diversity. While whole-genome-sequencing (wgs) is increasingly affordable, it will be considerable time before the full diversity of life is represented by high-quality assembled genomes; even then, constant monitoring will still require repeated sampling across time and space. In contrast, genome skimming (low-coverage, short-read wgs) is highly cost-effective but challenging to analyze because the coverage is too low for assembly and reliable error correction. Mature methods, such as Mash, exist for estimating pairwise genomic distances based on the Jaccard similarity of k-mer sets computed using sketching techniques. Some, such as Skmer, additionally model the impacts of low coverage. These methods have been successfully applied to assembly-free species identification and phylogenetics; however, their use in population genetics has been limited. Among other limitations, these methods implicitly treat genomes as haploid, and heterozygosity confounds estimates of genomic distance for diploid organisms. In this paper, we address this problem through several technical advances. First, we use coalescent theory to mathematically derive how the Jaccard index between the k-mer sets of two diploid samples changes with θ under a neutral Kingman's coalescent model. Next, we model the impact of coverage and sequencing error to derive an estimate of θ from the Jaccard index, in addition to several auxiliary variables, which we also estimate from the genome skims. The resulting method, DipSkmer, enables more accurate estimates of coverage, sequencing error, and θ for diploid samples. Analyses of both simulated and empirical datasets show that for diploids and low distances (e.g., < 2%), DipSkmer's estimate outperforms existing alignment-free methods such as Mash and Skmer, and closely approximates ANGSD, a reference and alignment-based tool.

title: Distinct extracellular architectures shape mechanical persistence in GPVI and CLEC-2 receptor assemblies.
abstract: Glycoprotein VI (GPVI) and C-type lectin-like receptor 2 (CLEC-2) are platelet-activating receptors whose extracellular organization contributes to receptor association and signaling during thrombus formation, yet how alternative receptor architectures influence mechanical persistence remains unclear. We used molecular dynamics to compare a GPVI dimer based on 2GI7, a domain-swapped GPVI assembly derived from 7NMU, and a crystallographic CLEC-2 contact using the same pulling protocol and constant-force conditions. During the first 5 nm of imposed separation, reconstructed GPVI required less force and mechanical work than CLEC-2 and domain-swapped GPVI. Under constant-force loading from 400 to 600 pN, reconstructed GPVI also reached the same extension endpoint markedly earlier than the domain-swapped assembly, with passage times differing by more than an order of magnitude under several conditions. Extended pulling to approximately 10 nm produced complete loss of interreceptor heavy-atom contacts in reconstructed GPVI while local peptide and disulfide connectivity remained intact. In contrast, the domain-swapped preparation retained resistance over a larger part of the separation pathway and showed substantially greater mechanical persistence. These results show that alternative extracellular arrangements of the same receptor are not mechanically equivalent and that uncertainty in GPVI architecture can translate into large differences in force transmission and persistence under load. Such architecture-dependent persistence may influence the stability of extracellular receptor associations during thrombus formation and thereby affect the mechanical lifetime of receptor clusters under load.

title: Practice-based initial teacher education in alternative teaching certification programs: A scoping review protocol.
abstract: Given the shortage of specialized teachers, Initial Teacher Education requires alternative teacher preparation routes, such as Alternative Teaching Certification Programs, that allow the incorporation of professionals who already possess prior work experience into the educational system. However, this situation raises new challenges regarding the design and implementation of the teacher preparation model within these programs. Consequently, this study aims to map and synthesize the existing evidence on the characteristics of practice-based teacher education (PBTE) programs, understood as an approach in which professional learning is constructed through authentic, situated teaching experiences rather than primarily theoretical instruction, designed for individuals who already hold technical, bachelor's, or professional degrees. The review will be conducted following the JBI (Joanna Briggs Institute) methodology for scoping reviews, and will be reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Data extraction and synthesis will be structured around the JBI Participants, Concept, and Context (PCC) analytical framework. Database searches will be conducted in Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus, including studies published between 2009 and 2025 in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. The review will specifically examine program duration, mentoring structures, practicum design, institutional type, teaching strategies, and reported outcomes. This protocol has been registered in the Open Science Framework (OSF) and will be publicly available once approved.

title: Quantitative analysis of China's selenium-enriched policy texts: Based on a three-dimensional framework of "theme-instrument-effectiveness".
abstract: Selenium, as an essential trace element for human health, plays a critical role in antioxidant defense, immune regulation, and disease prevention. With approximately 72% of China's soil area being selenium-deficient, developing the selenium-enriched industry has become a strategic priority for local governments under the "Healthy China" and Rural Revitalization initiatives. While existing research has extensively explored selenium's scientific mechanisms and industrial development pathways, a critical research gap remains in the systematic quantitative evaluation of selenium-enriched policy texts. This study addressed this gap by conducting a comprehensive quantitative analysis of 42 selenium-enriched policy documents issued in China from 2009 to 2025. Employing a three-dimensional analytical framework of "policy theme-policy instrument-policy effectiveness" integrated with Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling, content analysis, and the Policy Modeling Consistency (PMC) index model, this study reveals three key findings: (1) Current policies heavily emphasize industrial cultivation and brand building while paying insufficient attention to long-term selenium resource management and cross-regional coordination; (2) Policy instruments predominantly rely on supply-side inputs and indirect market cultivation, with weak direct stimulation of consumer health demand; (3) While policy design demonstrates good operationality (average PMC index = 6.9), it exhibits deficiencies in long-term strategic planning and national-level top-level design. This study provides actionable insights for policymakers to strengthen national top-level design, balance short-term industrial growth with long-term resilience construction, and optimize policy tool configurations to stimulate endogenous market vitality for the high-quality development of the selenium-enriched industry.

title: Long-term trends of carbon monoxide over the North Pacific upper troposphere from in-situ airplane measurements 1991-2018.
abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) is not a greenhouse gas, but as the dominant sink of the hydroxyl radical it governs the oxidising capacity of the troposphere and so indirectly forces climate. Its trends in the North Pacific upper troposphere matter disproportionately: this is the principal outflow corridor for Asian anthropogenic emissions, the fastest-growing combustion source of the past half-century, yet it has almost no routine ground-based monitoring and satellite retrievals resolve it poorly. We therefore combine in-situ CO measurements from the In-service Aircraft for a Global Observing System (IAGOS; 2012-2018) with earlier in-situ data from NASA/NSF/NOAA campaigns (1991-2019), the Measurements of Pollution in the Troposphere (MOPITT) satellite record, and the Integrated Modelling System (IMS) global chemistry transport model. Trends are computed separately for the monthly maximum, percentile, minimum and mean statistics, using a 10,000-sample perturbation regression framework. Mean CO increases by 0.15 ppb month-1 (18.0 ppb decade-1; 95% CI: -0.02 to 0.32) over 150∘E-140∘W, 45∘N-60∘N and by 0.06 ppb month-1 (7.2 ppb decade-1; 95% CI: -0.04 to 0.16) over 25∘N-45∘N; both intervals include zero but lie predominantly positive. The monthly maximum rises significantly over 25∘N-45∘N, by 0.31 ppb month-1 (37.2 ppb decade-1; 95% CI: 0.06 to 0.57), while the monthly minimum declines weakly. The most polluted air masses over the North Pacific are thus becoming more polluted even as background CO falls. The North Atlantic upper troposphere shows significantly decreasing CO over the same period. The opposing signs track the opposing trajectories of the upwind inventories: Asian emissions rose through most of the record and are lifted efficiently by summertime convection and warm conveyor belts, whereas North American and European emissions fell steadily and the Atlantic receives a larger share of CO-poor stratospheric air.

title: Structure-based discovery of a novel Granzyme A (GZMA) inhibitor for autism spectrum disorder through integrative transcriptomics, virtual screening, and long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations.
abstract: Granzyme A (GZMA) is a trypsin-like serine protease expressed in cytotoxic lymphocytes that cleaves gasdermin B (GSDMB) to release a pore-forming N-terminal fragment, thereby inducing pyroptosis, a lytic and pro-inflammatory form of programmed cell death. This pathway has been implicated in immune dysregulation reported in a subset of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In this study, we reanalyzed the peripheral blood transcriptome dataset GSE26415 using an integrative computational framework comprising outlier-aware quality control, differential expression analysis, functional enrichment profiling, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and protein-protein interaction network centrality scoring. These orthogonal evidence layers were integrated into a composite prioritization score, in which GZMA ranked first among candidate genes, followed by KLRK1 and KLRB1. Querying the Drug-Gene Interaction Database revealed no approved small-molecule inhibitors targeting GZMA, indicating that it remains pharmacologically undrugged. To explore druggability at the structural level, we performed structure-based virtual screening of a ZINC similarity library against the active site of GZMA (PDB ID: 1ORF). This yielded three drug-like candidates (T1, T2, and T3) with docking scores of -9.3, -9.1, and -8.9 kcal/mol, respectively, compared with -7.4 kcal/mol for the co-crystallized reference ligand (0G6). Each drug-protein complex and apo enzyme was studied in 500 ns molecular dynamics to verify the binding stability and conformational persistence compared to the unliganded protein. Among the screening compounds, T2 was able to occupy the catalytic pocket for the entire simulation, with a stable protein-ligand interaction and one low-energy conformational basin. T1, despite a better docking score, was able to detach from the pocket after around 400 ns, while T3 was able to do so in 50 ns. The overall order of binding persistence was T2 > T1 > T3. Collectively, these results prioritize GZMA as a key ASD-associated immune effector candidate and identify T2 as the most credible lead compound. Importantly, the findings underscore the limitation of docking scores alone and demonstrate that long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations and binding free energy are essential for distinguishing kinetically stable binders from transient docking poses. We note that GZMA was transcriptionally downregulated in peripheral blood; its selection rests on network centrality and on the premise that granzyme pathology is governed by enzymatic activity at tissue sites rather than by circulating transcript abundance, a mechanistic hypothesis to be tested at the activity level.

title: Designing a multi-epitope vaccine against La Crosse virus using immunoinformatics approach.
abstract: La Crosse virus (LACV) is a mosquito-borne Orthobunyavirus responsible for pediatric encephalitis, with no currently approved vaccine or targeted antiviral therapy. This study aimed to design a multi-epitope subunit vaccine targeting the conserved nucleoprotein of LACV using an integrated immunoinformatics approach. The nucleoprotein exhibited strong antigenicity and favorable physicochemical properties, including stability and hydrophilicity. Highly conserved CTL, HTL, and B-cell epitopes were initially predicted, from which high-affinity, non-allergenic, and non-toxic epitopes were selected. Population coverage analysis revealed extensive global applicability, with MHC class I and II coverage of 98.55% and 81.81%, respectively. Three vaccine constructs (V1, V2 and V3) were developed, while construct V1 demonstrated superior performance, with the highest antigenicity (0.7846) and solubility (0.709). Structural validation confirmed stability, with over 93% of residues in favored regions of the Ramachandran plot. Molecular docking with the TLR8 receptor revealed strong interactions. This was further supported by MD simulations, DCCM analysis, binding free energy calculations, and PCA, all of which confirmed stable binding between the vaccine construct V1 and TLR8, exhibiting a docking score of -1212.6. Molecular dynamics simulations further confirmed stability, with consistent RMSD, stable radius of gyration, and persistent hydrogen bonding (40-60 bonds). Codon optimization demonstrated favorable translational efficiency and confirmed the suitability of the construct V1 for heterologous expression in E. coli. Immune simulation predicted robust humoral and cellular responses, including elevated IgM, IgG, and cytokines. Overall, the proposed vaccine candidate V1 demonstrates strong immunogenic potential and structural stability, warranting further experimental validation for potential clinical application.

title: FDMSNet: A frequency-decomposed multi-scale hybrid framework for renewable energy power forecasting.
abstract: Accurate renewable energy power forecasting is of great significance for the safe operation, dispatch optimization, and efficient management of modern power systems. However, wind and photovoltaic power generation series usually exhibit significant non-stationarity, volatility, and multi-scale variation characteristics, posing great challenges to medium- and long-term forecasting. To address these issues, this paper proposes FDMSNet, a frequency-decomposed multi-scale hybrid network for renewable energy power forecasting. The model first divides the input sequence into non-stationary and stationary components through a frequency decomposition module. For the non-stationary component, a multilayer perceptron is adopted to extract global nonlinear variation features. For the stationary component, a multi-scale forecasting module is designed based on multi-branch downsampling and cross-scale prediction fusion. Subsequently, the forecasting results of different components are fused to generate the final power prediction. Experiments are conducted on real-world wind farm and photovoltaic power station datasets under multiple prediction horizons. MAE, MSE, and RSE are used as evaluation metrics, and FDMSNet is compared with different types of forecasting models. The experimental results show that FDMSNet achieves strong forecasting accuracy and stability in both wind and photovoltaic power forecasting tasks. Further average ranking analysis, significance testing, ablation experiments, and parameter sensitivity analysis verify the effectiveness and robustness of the frequency decomposition module, the multi-scale modeling structure, and the key parameter settings.

title: Reassessing cardiometabolic health disparities among young adult sexual minority women: Evidence from a population-based cohort.
abstract:
PURPOSE: We compared objective measures of cardiometabolic health (CMH) between women who identify as lesbian/gay or bisexual (LGB) and women who identify as heterosexual. In addition, we aimed to test whether group differences in stress reactivity partially explained disparities in CMH health.
METHODS: Participants from a longitudinal study were identified for enrollment in 2017. The LGB group self-identified as LGB in 2017 (n = 239), and the heterosexual group identified as straight or heterosexual in each year that sexual identity was asked (study years 2010-2017) (n = 160). CMH was assessed via measurements and biomarkers, and stress reactivity via heart rate variability and cortisol levels during a social stress test. Participants also provided self-reports of stress and health. We tested group differences using sexual identity at Study Year 17, at the time of the visit, and as a proportion of years identifying as LGB.
RESULTS: Group differences were tested using t-tests for continuous measures, logistic regression for dichotomous measures, and repeated-measures ANOVA for change over time. There were no significant differences in measures of CMH or stress reactivity by sexual identity group. LGB participants had worse self-reported health and higher levels of stress compared to heterosexual participants.
CONCLUSION: We discuss several frameworks for interpreting the present results of no differences in objective markers of health in the context of the existing literature, including developmental, socio-political, and methodological frameworks, and suggest directions for research to link the previous research with the results of the current study.

title: One dimensional detection for radio signals based on SpecUNeSt-MLP.
abstract: Detecting and precisely localizing multiple radio signals in wideband power spectral density (PSD) vectors under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions remains a fundamental challenge for spectrum monitoring and cognitive radio. Traditional energy detection and threshold-based methods suffer from the SNR-wall effect and poor performance in dense, non-cooperative environments. While deep-learning approaches have advanced the field, most treat spectrum sensing as a binary classification task, discarding the fine-grained frequency-bin information needed for accurate signal boundary and parameter estimation. In this paper, we propose SpecUNeSt-MLP, an one-dimensional semantic segmentation framework built upon the U-Net encoder-decoder architecture. The model directly predicts per-frequency-bin occupancy masks from normalized PSD vectors, thereby simultaneously achieving signal detection and parameter estimation (center frequency and bandwidth). Three key enhancements are introduced: (1) a 1D-adapted Split-Attention mechanism in the encoder that dynamically recalibrates cross-channel features to enhance weak-signal extraction under heavy noise; (2) a Bidirectional Rolling MLP (RMLP) module in the bottleneck that efficiently captures long-range spectral dependencies with linear complexity; and (3) Feature Incentive Blocks that refine feature representations through lightweight channel projection. Extensive experiments on 67,200 synthetic broadband PSDs and 820 real-world UAV PSD samples demonstrate the effectiveness of SpecUNeSt-MLP. Across all tested SNR levels (from -4 dB to 8 dB), SpecUNeSt-MLP consistently outperforms LAD, FCN, SS-CNN, and SS-LSTM in terms of detection probability, false alarm rate, and average localization error. Compared with the recent RMP baseline, SpecUNeSt-MLP achieves better performance under low-SNR conditions while maintaining comparable performance at higher SNR levels, with only one-sixth of the parameter count of RMP. These results demonstrate that SpecUNeSt-MLP provides an effective and computationally efficient solution for fine-grained spectrum sensing in complex electromagnetic environments.

title: Operant House: A versatile open-source platform for automated operant conditioning testing of mice in home cages.
abstract: Operant conditioning is a powerful method for probing cognitive functions, yet its widespread use is constrained by low throughput, labor-intensive procedures, and high costs. Here, we developed "Operant House," a low-cost, programmable device equipped with a touchscreen, retractable levers, and a water-reward port, designed to enable automated operant conditioning with minimal experimenter intervention in individually housed mice within their home cages. Although individual home-cage testing requires careful attention to animal welfare, the system permits continuous monitoring through live camera observation and recorded videos. As proof of concept, we implemented two cognitive protocols: a delayed non-match-to-position (DNMTP) test for assessing working memory and a two-choice spatial discrimination (TCSD) test involving working-memory-related processes and behavioral flexibility. Because working memory impairment is one of the earliest clinical features of Alzheimer's disease (AD), we further applied these protocols to a knock-in mouse model carrying familial AD-associated amyloid precursor protein mutations (AppNL-G-F mice). Using this model, we detected significant working memory deficits as early as 5 months of age. At this age, we also detected subtle and spatially heterogeneous synaptic alterations in the prefrontal cortex, whereas conventional electrophysiological measures were largely preserved. Together, these findings highlight the Operant House as a cost-effective, scalable platform for assessing higher cognitive functions in mice, offering an accessible tool for investigating neurological and neuropsychiatric disease models.

title: Integrating MaxEnt and MaxNet for climate-resilient habitat restoration: Predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in semi-arid landscapes.
abstract: Accurate modeling of species distribution is essential for effective biodiversity conservation, afforestation planning, and land-use management. This study presents a comparative analysis of two prominent presence-only species distribution models Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) and MaxNet to evaluate their efficacy in predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in a semi-arid agro-climatic region. A total of 138 georeferenced occurrence records and 25 pseudo-absence points were used, incorporating key environmental variables such as wind speed, temperature range, precipitation, and root zone soil wetness. Both models were optimized and assessed using metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the Area Under the Curve (AUC). Results indicate that MaxEnt outperformed MaxNet in most metrics, achieving an accuracy of 87.5% and an AUC of 0.956, compared to MaxNet's accuracy of 75% and AUC of 0.926. Environmental variable importance varied by model, with MaxEnt highlighting surface pressure and MaxNet emphasizing wind speed. Probability density plots revealed that MaxEnt distinctly identified high suitability zones, whereas MaxNet offered a more balanced, conservative distribution across the landscape. These differences underscore the influence of algorithm design on ecological inference. This study emphasizes the importance of model selection and tuning in species distribution modeling and suggests that integrating outputs from both models can yield robust insights for habitat suitability assessment. The findings support data-driven afforestation strategies, especially under changing climatic conditions, and provide valuable guidance for sustainable plantation efforts involving Eucalyptus tereticornis in similar agro-ecological zones.

title: Joint optimization of detection, task allocation, and path planning for multi-agent cooperative interception under partial observability.
abstract: Safety-critical autonomous systems often require multiple agents to detect, assign, and intercept non-cooperative mobile targets using only partial observations. These subtasks are tightly coupled because the same agents must balance spatial exploration for detection with goal-directed motion for interception, while target maneuvers remain uncertain. This study develops and validates an integrated multi-agent coordination framework for jointly optimizing distributed detection, dynamic task allocation, and path planning under partial observability. The problem is formulated as a coupled Dec-POMDP made computationally tractable through factored decentralized policies, parameter sharing, and centralized training with decentralized execution, and a Weighted Coordinated Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (W-MAPPO) framework is introduced to adaptively coordinate competing subtasks. W-MAPPO combines an observation-conditioned Policy Ratio Predictor, an LSTM-based history-aware processor for temporal modeling of target maneuvers, and a Voronoi-based collaborative detection module for spatial coverage coordination within a centralized-training decentralized-execution paradigm. Comprehensive simulation experiments across increasing target densities compare W-MAPPO with seven representative MARL baselines and two classical methods, supported by statistical testing, ablation studies, sensitivity analysis, and representative case studies. W-MAPPO achieves a 94% success rate in the 5 vs 5 scenario and maintains stable interception performance as the number of targets increases to 10 and 15. These results demonstrate the technical reliability and practical potential of integrated subtask coordination for partially observable multi-agent systems.

title: Phenotypic and genomic characterization of antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella spp. from livestock in Namibia.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing concern within the One Health framework. This study characterized AMR in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella spp. isolated from livestock fecal samples across commercial and communal farms in Namibia.
METHODS: About 140 fecal samples were collected from cattle, sheep, and chickens on farms in Namibia. Isolates were identified using the VITEK® 2 system and MALDI-ToF mass spectrometry. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method against nine antibiotics. Genomic DNA was extracted and subjected to whole-genome sequencing (WGS) using Illumina NextSeq 2000 platform.
RESULTS: AMR genes were identified using ResFinder and Abricate, plasmid-associated replicons using plasmid analysis tools, and virulence-associated genes using VirulenceFinder. Phenotypic analyses showed resistance to β-lactams, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones among the tested isolates. WGS identified diverse resistance determinants and sequence types, including E. coli ST101 and ST1431, K. oxytoca ST2, and K. pneumoniae ST22. Multiple plasmid replicons were detected; however, their presence alone does not establish that individual resistance genes were plasmid-borne or that horizontal gene transfer occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first genomic evidence of livestock-associated AMR in Namibia, identifying resistance determinants and multidrug-resistant E. coli and Klebsiella spp. in the sampled livestock population. The findings provide baseline genomic data for AMR surveillance and support strengthened antimicrobial stewardship and One Health monitoring. The concurrent detection of chromosomal resistance-associated mutations and diverse plasmid replicons illustrates the complexity of resistance mechanisms, although the present short-read data do not establish the direct physical linkage of individual ARGs to plasmids. These findings highlight the need for coordinated surveillance across animal, human, and environmental health sectors in Namibia.

title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of norovirus and rotavirus among children under five with diarrheal infection in lower-middle-income countries after Rotavirus vaccine introduction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rotavirus and norovirus are the leading viral causes of acute diarrheal disease worldwide. Both viruses encompass multiple genotypes and subgenotypes, and this genetic diversity presents a significant challenge to rotavirus vaccine effectiveness and development. High-quality evidence on the prevalence and circulating genotypes of these enteric viruses among children under five years of age remains limited, particularly following the introduction of rotavirus vaccination in low and middle-income countries (LMICs). Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesizes available evidence on the prevalence and genotype distribution of norovirus and rotavirus in this population.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across five major databases PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Embase, and Web of Science between February 20 and 28, 2026. Duplicate removal, title and abstract screening, full-text review and data extraction were performed independently by two investigators using the Rayyan web-based platform. STATA version 17 software was used for statistical analysis. A random-effects model was applied to estimate pooled prevalence and effect sizes. Heterogeneity was evaluated using Cochran's Q statistic, the I2 statistic, forest plots, and Galbraith plots. Publication bias was assessed using both graphical (funnel plots) and statistical methods.
RESULTS: A total of 35,704 children under five years with diarrheal infection from LMICs were included across eligible studies. The overall pooled prevalence of norovirus and rotavirus combined was 18% (95% CI: 15-21%). Rotavirus had a higher pooled prevalence than norovirus, at 24% (95% CI: 19.6-28.3%) and 13% (95% CI: 11-15%), respectively. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies (I2 = 98.72%, p < 0.001). Among norovirus genotypes, GII was predominant (76%), with subgenotype GII.4 accounting for 53% of cases, followed by GI (23%). The most frequently identified rotavirus genotypes were G3[P8] (39%) and G1[P8] (17%).
CONCLUSIONS: Norovirus and rotavirus remain significant causes of diarrheal disease among children under five in LMICs, even after the introduction of rotavirus vaccination. Approximately one in five children with diarrheal illness were infected with at least one of these virusesGII, particularly subgenotype GII.4, was the dominant norovirus strain, while G3[P8] and G1[P8] were the most prevalent rotavirus genotypes. These findings underscore the need to strengthen surveillance systems, consider circulating genotypes in vaccine formulation, and continuously monitor genotype shifts within the population.

title: Task-aware conformal power envelopes for multi-horizon spacecraft monitoring.
abstract: Reliable spacecraft power monitoring requires uncertainty estimates across forecast horizons and consistency between primitive electrical states and derived power. We present a task-aware conformal framework that selects joint residual geometry according to downstream power-envelope efficiency. A residual iTransformer produced point centres for five primitive electrical states at 1, 5, and 15 min. Candidate geometries were fitted, selected, and calibrated on chronologically separated complete-orbit blocks, and the final evaluation comprised 25,278 forecast origins from the chronologically subsequent July 2023 telemetry. Across three random-seed runs, the task-aware selector chose a joint box, whereas a residual-volume control selected the sample-covariance ellipsoid. Orbit-balanced primitive-state joint coverage was 0.892 (95% complete-orbit bootstrap confidence interval [CI], 0.883-0.899) at the 90% nominal level and 0.947 (95% CI, 0.943-0.952) at the 95% nominal level. At 90% and 95%, simultaneous coverage of both power channels across all horizons was 0.913 and 0.957. Relative to residual-volume selection, the task-aware method reduced normalized power interval score by 34.3% and 30.3%; the paired absolute reductions were 1.522 (95% CI, 1.505-1.540) and 1.552 (95% CI, 1.534-1.570). Power envelopes were computed from synchronized primitive current and bus-voltage sets. For the selected non-negative box, zero algebraic gap and full interval-image containment follow by construction; the empirical analyses quantify coverage and sharpness. The results demonstrate task-aware geometry selection for BUPT-1 multi-horizon power monitoring.

title: Toward understanding the role of visual hierarchy in flicker-induced time dilation: A preregistered study.
abstract: When a temporal interval is marked by flickering stimuli, its subjective duration is overestimated. The cortical origin of this temporal illusion, termed flicker-induced time dilation (FITD), is not yet well understood. In this pre-registered study, we aimed to explore whether the higher-level regions of ventral visual stream contribute to FITD. By using the semantic wavelet-induced frequency tagging (SWIFT) technique, four experimental conditions were created. Luminance and semantic flickers were created to selectively target the lower- and higher-level regions of the visual hierarchy, respectively. A combined luminance and semantic flicker condition was additionally created to probe the effect of simultaneous entrainment of lower- and higher-level visual regions on FITD. Lastly, to account for the single-pixel modulations and ripple-like motions induced by SWIFT, a control scramble condition was included. The phase-clustering analysis (N = 20) confirmed that the control scramble condition did not result in neural entrainment, whereas the flicker conditions showed entrainment whose magnitude and topography were consistent with their respective experimental manipulations. Nonetheless, the behavioral results indicated that the time dilation effect was not modulated by the flickering conditions neither was its magnitude correlated with the size of entrained oscillations. Moreover, the SWIFT scrambles led to a time dilation effect which was comparable to the flickering conditions. We discussed that while our results are not in agreement with neural entrainment account of FITD, they are not in agreement with the processing principles definition of salience either. Based on the putative shared cortical sources of SWIFT scrambles and luminance-modulated flickers, we conjectured that FITD, and motion-induced time dilation may rely on the same mechanism based on activation of motion sensitive regions. Finally, our results indicated that, at least at the presence of steadily activated lower-level visual and/or motion sensitive areas, periodic activation of ventral stream does not contribute to FITD.

title: Investigation on the use of ceftazidime-avibactam at a national hospital in Vietnam.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the utilization of ceftazidime-avibactam at Thong Nhat Hospital, a national hospital in Vietnam.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted using retrospective data from medical records of inpatients aged ≥ 18 years who received ceftazidime-avibactam for at least 2 days between January 2023 and March 2025 at Thong Nhat Hospital, Vietnam. The appropriateness of ceftazidime-avibactam use was evaluated based on Thong Nhat Hospital's antibiotic use guideline. The backward conditional method was used to identify factors associated with patient treatment outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 101 patients were included, with a median age of 78 years (68-86). Respiratory and bloodstream infections were the most common types, accounting for 84.15% and 44.55% of cases, respectively. Gram-negative bacteria comprised 76.05% of isolates, with Klebsiella pneumoniae (26.47%), Klebsiella aerogenes (18.50%) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (10.50%) being the most frequent. The susceptibility rate to ceftazidime-avibactam was 71.43% for Klebsiella pneumoniae, 95.65% for Klebsiella aerogenes and 42.86% for Pseudomonas aeruginosa. OXA-48 was the most detected carbapenemase gene (37.84%). The overall appropriateness rate of ceftazidime-avibactam use was 70.30%. The treatment success rate was 39.60%. Treatment in the intensive care unit was associated with decreased treatment success, while comorbid heart failure showed a potential association.
CONCLUSIONS: The treatment success rate with ceftazidime-avibactam in this study was relatively low. Continuous surveillance of microbiological profiles and antibiotic resistance, particularly to ceftazidime-avibactam, is essential to better guide the management of drug-resistant Gram-negative infections at the hospital.

title: Psychological interventions for mental health in adults with multiple long-term conditions: A scoping review and evolution of the evidence base.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Managing multiple long-term conditions (MLTCs) within individuals is a key global public health priority. Psychological interventions are effective in improving mental health outcomes in single-condition populations, yet the evidence for adults with MLTCs remains scarce. This scoping review aimed to map existing evidence on psychological interventions for people with MLTCs, highlight literature gaps and offer recommendations for future research, practice, and policy.
METHODS: The pre-registered review follows Arksey & O'Malley's (2005) framework and is reported in line with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. We searched six databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane, PsycNET, Web of Science) up to January 2025, including reference screening and a grey literature search. After screening 124 full texts, 54 studies were included. Eligible studies evaluated any psychological intervention in adults with two or more long-term health conditions and included a validated psychological health outcome.
RESULTS: Existing research primarily focusses on a handful of chronic conditions (diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic pain), often alongside comorbid depression. Cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) and behavioural activation (BA) are the most frequently evaluated interventions, generally demonstrating positive effects on mental health and acceptability to patients. The evidence base has progressed from early-stage development and feasibility studies to effectiveness trials, though economic evaluations and implementation research are still scarce. Notable gaps include limited research on transdiagnostic approaches, underserved populations and studies involving healthcare providers and carers. Most studies are concentrated in Western countries, highlighting a need for broader geographic representation, particularly in the global South.
CONCLUSIONS: Psychological interventions such as CBT and BA show promise for individuals with MLTCs, but significant gaps remain. Future research should i) prioritise inclusive, transdiagnostic approaches to MLTC management, ii) expand geographic diversity, iii) use data-driven approaches to identify and intervene on common MLTC clusters and iv) incorporate health economic and implementation considerations to support more effective and equitable mental health care for those living with MLTCs.

title: Modeling and experimental validation of dynamic defocusing effects in femtosecond laser ablation of complex gear surfaces.
abstract: Femtosecond (fs) laser ablation has emerged as a disruptive technology for the ultra-precision finishing of aerospace face gears. However, its application to complex 3D curved topologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by spatially varying nonlinear laser-material interactions. In this study, we propose a comprehensive 3D nonlinear mathematical model for the fs laser ablation of 18Cr2Ni4WA alloy steel to reveal the mechanism of spatial light field distortion. By discretizing the involute face gear topology, the model explicitly couples the localized incidence angle with dynamic defocusing, elliptical beam stretching, and incidence-dependent Fresnel reflection. Theoretical analyses demonstrate that geometrical variations severely distort the energy-coupling efficiency, with the dynamic defocusing distance being directly proportional to the tangent of the incidence angle (tanθ), drastically attenuating the absorbed volumetric energy density in highly inclined regions. Comparison with CNC gear-center measurements yielded descriptive model-measurement differences with a whole-grid MAE of 0.131μm, an RMSE of 0.137μm, and a maximum absolute difference of 0.255μm (6.53% relative difference). These differences were below the expanded measurement uncertainty and therefore are not interpreted as metrological proof of submicrometer resolution. The spatial error pattern is consistent with, but does not directly prove, enhanced plasma-plume shielding within geometrically confined concave valleys. This study provides a model-based foundation for adaptive multi-axis parameter compensation in advanced aerospace manufacturing.

title: Barriers and facilitators to using an app-based tool for suicide safety planning in a psychiatric emergency department: A qualitative descriptive study using the Theoretical Domains Framework and COM-B model.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency departments (EDs) play a crucial role in suicide prevention, with evidenced-based safety planning interventions (SPI) playing an important role. Traditional safety plans, which are often paper based, come with challenges (i.e., not easily accessible, or easy to misplace). Digital safety planning tools offer an alternative mode of intervention delivery, but clinical implementation remains limited. Using behavioural change frameworks, we aim to provide insights into the factors influencing app adoption. These insights will be used as a knowledge base to design behavior change strategies to promote the implementation of a SPI app in a psychiatric ED.
METHODS: We used a qualitative descriptive design to conduct semi-structured interviews with clinicians in a psychiatric ED in Toronto, Canada. Participants encompassed all ED staff, irrespective of their SPI app usage. The semi-structured interview guide was developed using the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF) and the capability (C), opportunity (O), motivation (M) and behavior (B) (COM-B) model. We then used directed content analysis, identifying findings within the TDF and COM-B domains as barriers, facilitators, or both.
FINDINGS: A total of 29 ED clinicians were interviewed, including nurses, psychiatrists, social workers, program assistants, and a pharmacist. The majority had not used the app. We observed strong motivation among clinicians across all disciplines to use the app, and they considered SPI as a high-priority ED care strategy closely linked to their professional identity and responsibility. Anticipated barriers regarding the app as a new mode of SPI delivery in routine practice included: documentation, communication, care efficiency, and patient access to smartphones. Some barriers were attributable to the lack of interoperability between the app and the electronic health record and documentation infrastructure for the app.
CONCLUSION: We identified key behavioral factors influencing the implementation of the SPI app in the psychiatric ED. As such, we found that tailored strategies that can mitigate barriers by targeting capability, motivation, and opportunity are essential, while facilitators that can sustain implementation should be leveraged. Additionally, ongoing monitoring and adaptation of strategies are necessary, as new barriers may arise or facilitators may weaken over time, impacting the sustained use of the app in the ED. We will use these findings to inform the next phase of this work, which involves co-designing targeted and tailored implementation strategies.

title: Temporal shifts in insect cuticular hydrocarbons in response to experimental desiccation.
abstract: Insects are vulnerable to desiccation as they are small and have a high surface area-to-volume ratios. Over 80% of their body water is lost through the cuticle, but insects possess specialised cells that synthesize cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs) to form a hydrophobic waxy barrier that reduces water loss. However, how rapidly CHCs are synthesized and transported across the cuticle under desiccating conditions remains poorly understood. To examine this, we exposed male Drosophila melanogaster to varying desiccation durations (2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 h) and compared CHC profiles for each of these time-points to an experimental control (no desiccation: 0 h). We found a rapid, time-dependent shift in CHC composition, marked by an early increase in short-chain hydrocarbons followed by enrichment of longer chain, methyl-branched CHCs over longer periods of desiccation exposure. Cumulative water loss increased most sharply within the first 2 h of desiccation and then progressed more slowly from 2 to 8 h before rising again at 10 h. These changes were closely mirrored by temporal shifts in CHC composition, suggesting that CHCs are dynamic and respond rapidly to desiccation stress.

title: Cost comparison of the ShangRing device versus Mogen clamp for early infant male circumcision in Sub-Saharan Africa.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The World Health Organization (WHO) endorses male circumcision as an effective human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) prevention intervention in settings where the expected impact is greatest, including Sub-Saharan Africa. Data on cost implications of early infant male circumcision (EIMC) are limited. The ShangRing (SR) is a WHO pre-qualified device for circumcision. We sought to perform a comprehensive cost assessment alongside a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of the SR versus the standard of care Mogen clamp (MoC) for EIMC to enable future scale-up towards a cost-effective HIV prevention strategy.
METHODS: We collected resource utilization and economic data as part of an RCT of infants aged 0-60 days old undergoing EIMC in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda. Cost data for both the SR and MoC included baseline facility costs, direct costs, and indirect costs. The Decision Makers Program Planning Tool v1.0 was used to perform a direct cost comparison of these two devices. The Goals model was used to compare the costs of EIMC in 2023 using the present value of money to circumcise an adolescent male 15 years from now.
RESULTS: A total of 1,378 infant males underwent circumcision, 689 via SR and 689 via MoC. The overall cost of a single EIMC in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda were 61.30 United States Dollars ($), $47.14, and $64.59 respectively for the SR, and $56.38, $50.43, and $58.57 respectively for the MoC. In Kenya, EIMC would be less expensive based on nominal present costs in 2023 compared to waiting for adolescent circumcision at age 15 years in 2038. This finding is reversed in Tanzania and Uganda.
CONCLUSIONS: The overall cost of EIMC via SR versus MoC is comparable in an RCT. With scale-up utilizing lower level personnel, the cost of SR may be further reduced. The SR is an attractive alternative for future EIMC initiatives in Sub-Saharan Africa to further reduce HIV burden.

title: Impact of chemical and herbal pre-treatments on shelf life and quality characteristics of dried mango (Mangifera Indica L.) slices.
abstract: The present research was carried out to study and determine the effects of chemical and herbal pre-treatments on dried mango slices stored for 180 days under ambient conditions. Discoloration, antioxidants, loss of nutrients, off-flavour, and microbial growth during storage were reported to be concerning parameters. The parameters included in the study were proximate composition, physicochemical analysis, antioxidant analysis, microbial analysis, and color analysis. Score for vitamin C content, antioxidants, and color analysis, was better in pre-treated samples as compared to untreated dried mango samples, but showed a decreasing trend with an increase in storage interval. The analysis conducted at various intervals of storage depicted that the herbal pre-treatments preserved the vitamin C and antioxidant content, and comparable results were recorded. The microbial population in untreated dried mango slices was recorded as more than pre-treated, but was under the permissible limit. Overall, it was concluded that the use of herbal pre-treatments in comparison to chemicals was also effective for the preservation of nutritionally good quality dried fruit.
