title: Investigation of salivary microRNAs as non-invasive biomarkers for weaning stress in piglets: A preliminary study.
abstract: Weaning exposes piglets to abrupt nutritional and environmental changes that induce physiological stress. Saliva, unlike serum or tissue samples, enables repeated and stress-free sampling, making it a practical biological matrix for monitoring early-life adaptation. To evaluate whether salivary microRNAs (miRNAs) can serve as non-invasive indicators of these responses, we profiled miRNA expression in saliva collected from suckling and weaning piglets. Small RNA sequencing was conducted to detect salivary miRNAs and a total of 41 differentially expressed miRNAs (DEMs) were detected between the two groups, with 20 showing highly expression and 21 showing lowly expression in weaning piglets. Several of these DEMs have been previously associated with immune activity, inflammatory regulation, oxidative stress responses, and disease processes, highlighting their biological relevance during the weaning transition. Functional annotation of predicted target genes revealed enrichment in pathways such as TGF-beta, HIF-1, and AMPK signaling, as well as autophagy-related processes. These pathways are known to play key roles in stress adaptation, cellular metabolism, and immune modulation. These findings suggest that salivary miRNA profiles may reflect molecular changes associated with the weaning transition and may serve as candidate non-invasive indicators of physiological stress and health status in piglets. This approach may provide a basis for future development of saliva-based monitoring strategies after validation in larger cohorts and cost-effective targeted assays.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and coupling of "Forest-Cropland-Water" ecosystem vulnerability in the Yangtze River Economic Belt.
abstract: The Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB), China's "golden waterway" and "green barrier", relies on its "Forest-Cropland-Water" system for carbon sequestration, grain production, and water conservation. Tracking its vulnerability and coordination on a spatiotemporal scale reveals barriers to balancing ecological security with sustainable growth. Our study innovatively proposes a multi-system coupling evaluation framework. We integrate the Order relation (G1) method, the CRiteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC) method, and a game theory combination weighting to assess the ecological vulnerability of the "Forest-Cropland-Water" system across YREB. Using coupling coordination and spatial autocorrelation models, we then map the spatiotemporal pattern and spatial clustering characteristics of ecosystems interactions. Finally, geodetector method is employed to identify the principal drivers of coupling coordination. In 2000-2023, the ecological vulnerability of each ecosystem and the overall system exhibited a fluctuating downward trend. Spatial clustering of coupling coordination gradually weakened, and coupling types shifted from mild imbalance toward mild coordination. Concurrently, high vulnerability areas progressively transitioned to moderate and low vulnerability. Among the driving factors, Land use intensity and aerosol optical depth consistently exhibited the strongest explanatory power for the coupling coordination degree of the "Forest-Cropland-Water" system, whereas the influence of extreme high-temperature days markedly declined over time and the remaining selected factors played only subsidiary roles. This work provides a systematic framework for assessing future multi-system ecological vulnerability and coupling relationship, offering scientific guidance for promoting sustainable natural-resource management and inter-basin development.

title: Cross-omics mapping of the human HIV restrictome across clinical states, immune-cell compartments, and protein responses.
abstract: Host restriction factors can block HIV at multiple stages, but they are often studied as individual genes or within a single molecular layer. I performed an evidence-structured computational reanalysis of three independent public datasets to determine how the human HIV restrictome varies across clinical states, immune-cell compartments, and protein responses. The analysis used bulk monocyte RNA sequencing (GSE157198), PBMC single-cell/CITE-seq data (GSE256089), and primary CD4 T-cell proteomics (PXD012263) within a prespecified restrictome-immunometabolism framework. In GSE157198, ART-naive monocytes had higher core-restrictome activity than healthy controls (difference = 1.154, p = 0.000746), and core scores were strongly correlated with interferon/innate-sensing scores (Spearman r = 0.800, p = 7.47 × 10^-11). Core-lipid/cholesterol correlation was weaker and was not independent of interferon after conditional analysis. In GSE256089, participant-paired core-restrictome scores were enriched in NK cells relative to B cells, monocytes, and T cells, and matched random-gene-set analyses supported enrichment beyond background expression structure. FCGR3A monocytes also had higher participant-paired core scores than CD14 monocytes. Exploratory sensing/death-gene analysis identified cell-type-specific expression patterns but did not establish pathway activation, pyroptosis, or apoptosis. In PXD012263, the historical q < 0.05 proteomic selection contained 19 curated genes and retained mixed response polarity; sensitivity thresholds q < 0.01 and q < 0.10 selected 10 and 25 genes, respectively. Together, the results show that HIV restrictome activity varies across clinical and immune-cell contexts and is embedded within broader interferon-linked and immunometabolic states. Because the datasets are independent and not subject matched, the findings are observational and hypothesis-generating rather than causal.

title: A study on the status quo and influencing factors of science identity in physics among junior high school students.
abstract: This study examines the status of science identity of physics among middle school students, adopting a mixed-methods approach combining survey data and qualitative interviews, thereby addressing a gap in research on science identity in physics within the transitional context from integrated to discipline-specific curricula in early middle school. Quantitative analyses, including descriptive statistics, cluster analysis, correlation analysis, t-tests, and MANOVA, examined students' science identity status, patterns, and gender differences. Qualitative interviews were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis to explore underlying factors. The findings indicate that students' science identity is moderately positive overall but characterized by an internal imbalance. While interest in science classes emerges as the strongest dimension, science role recognition remains notably weak, revealing an interest-recognition gap. A substantial proportion of students cluster within a neutral identity category, suggesting that the transition from integrated science to subject-based curricula represents a critical and malleable stage in identity development. Gender differences are significant across all dimensions of science identity and become more pronounced at higher grade levels, particularly in learning competence, practical performance, and career interest. Qualitative evidence suggests that these patterns may be associated with increasing academic demands following the transition to discipline-specific curricula, shifts in evaluation approaches, and internalized gender stereotypes. Additionally, limited peer discourse, low perceived proximity to the scientist role, and insufficient exposure to authentic scientific practices further constrain identity formation. Teacher recognition is a critical factor, with female students showing heightened sensitivity to it.

title: Study on the spatiotemporal distribution of Neolithic settlement clusters based on complex social evolution: Evidence from the Dongting Lake Basin.
abstract: Settlement aggregation has been a fundamental feature of human sedentary societies and provides important evidence for understanding changes in prehistoric social organization. However, previous studies of prehistoric settlement clusters have focused predominantly on spatial division and morphological structure, while comparatively little attention has been paid to their long-term spatiotemporal evolution at the watershed scale. This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of Neolithic settlement clusters in the Dongting Lake Basin and its implications for the development of social complexity. A total of 1,101 Neolithic settlement sites analyzed using Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm, Arc Geographic Information Systems (ArcGIS), and a Spatiotemporal Object Model. The findings reveal that settlement clusters were initially concentrated primarily in the northwestern part of the Dongting Lake basin and subsequently expanded toward the areas surrounding Dongting Lake. Their spatial organization of settlement clusters gradually evolved from a pattern characterized by "small settlements and loose clustering" into a multi-level hierarchical structure consisting of "large central settlements-medium-sized secondary settlements-small local settlements." The spatial center of the settlement clusters shifted southward at a relatively rapid pace, whereas its shifts toward the northwestern part and peripheral areas of Dongting Lake occurred more slowly. producing an overall V-shaped trajectory. The warm and humid climatic conditions, together with proximity to rivers and lakeside plains, provided favorable environmental settings for settlement development. Over time, settlement sizes generally increased, and the clusters underwent migration and differentiation, indicating increased social complexity. These findings provide new insights into the long-term spatiotemporal organization of Neolithic settlement systems in the middle Yangtze River region and contribute to a better understanding of interactions among environmental change, settlement dynamics, and the development of prehistoric social complexity.

title: The dual burden of disease: Depression among patients with multidrug resistance tuberculosis in low-income and lower- middle-income countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) continues to pose a serious global health challenge, particularly in low-income and lower-middle-income countries where the disease burden, fragile health systems, and socioeconomic hardships are most pronounced. These conditions not only complicate treatment but also worsen patients' vulnerability to depression. Although numerous primary studies have investigated the prevalence of depression among individuals with MDR-TB, their findings have been inconsistent. To address this gap, the present study seeks to estimate the pooled prevalence of depression and identify its associated factors among MDR-TB patients in low- and lower-middle-income countries.
METHODS: Relevant studies were sourced from Google Scholar, Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science. Additionally, the reference lists of selected articles were manually reviewed to identify further eligible publications. A random-effects model was employed to calculate the pooled prevalence of depression among MDR-TB patients in low- and lower-middle-income countries.
RESULTS: The meta-analysis incorporated 23 primary studies with a combined sample of 5,734 MDR-TB patients. The pooled prevalence of depression among this population was 41.89% (95% CI: 32.63-51.15; I² = 98.51%, P < 0.001). Several factors were significantly linked to depression, including female gender (AOR = 2.00, 95% CI: 1.66-2.41), financial hardship (AOR = 2.56, 95% CI: 1.44-4.55), presence of comorbidities (AOR = 3.72, 95% CI: 2.11-5.38), greater disease severity (AOR = 2.13, 95% CI: 1.42-3.12), medication-related side effects (AOR = 2.77, 95% CI: 2.20-3.48), and perceived stigma (AOR = 3.58, 95% CI: 2.13-6.02).
CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of depression among MDR-TB patients in low- and lower-middle-income countries was found to be notably high. These findings emphasize the importance of implementing routine depression screening and integrating psychosocial support into patient care.

title: Assessing primary health care facilities in six prioritized Nigerian states: Linking facility readiness with service availability.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nigeria's poor health indicators have been linked to its dysfunctional Primary Health Care (PHC) facilities. Policy gaps remain in achieving sustainable and equitable provision of PHC for Nigerians. Therefore, this study examined the relationship between health facilities' readiness and service provision in Nigeria.
METHODS: This was a cross-sectional assessment of 204 PHC facilities enrolled under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund program, in six prioritized states in Nigeria. The facilities were assessed for the provision of ≥80% of the three levels of primary healthcare services-Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3-as the outcome variables. The three tiers represent the minimum, intermediate, and comprehensive levels of essential PHC services, respectively, defined under Nigeria's Minimum Service Package. Health Facility (HF) readiness (explanatory variable) was assessed across six domains, with five of the domains disaggregated into 3 levels (poor, fair, and good). Data were analysed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and multivariable logistic regression model (alpha = 0.05).
RESULTS: The majority (81.9%) of the HFs have a functional management committee, 54.4% have an updated BHCPF annual quality improvement plan, 81.9% have standard operating procedures. While 16.2% met the World Health Organization standard ≥2.3 Health Care Workers (HCWs)/1000 population, none met the Minimum Service Package standard for HCWs across all cadres. The proportion of facilities with good readiness in each domain was: management and finance (42.6%); Health Management Information System tools/registers, supply chain tools/registers, and guidelines (40.2%); infrastructure and utility (33.3%); tracer equipment (34.8%); and tracer drugs (29.9%). The percentage of HF that provided ≥80% services was: Tier 1 (65.2%), Tier 2 (46.6%), and Tier 3 (35.8%); while 31.9% met ≥ 80% across all the service Tiers. Common predictors of providing ≥80% across the service Tiers were tracer drugs and equipment availability. The likelihood of delivering all Tiers of services was higher in HF with fair (aOR=2.38, 95% CI = 1.92-11.14, p < 0.05) and good (aOR=3.93, 95% CI = 1.96-8.49) levels of tracer equipment readiness compared to the poor.
CONCLUSION: Good PHC facility readiness supports the provision of health care services in Nigeria. Availability of tracer drugs and equipment predicts the provision of healthcare services in PHC facilities. Investment in PHC facility functionality and prioritization of funds for tracer drugs and equipment will therefore improve service availability and delivery in Nigerian public PHC facilities.

title: Integrating Quantum Machine Learning and Ontology Matching for Efficient Semantic Web Services discovery.
abstract: Existing Semantic Web Service (SWS) discovery approaches based on classical machine learning suffer from limited representational capacity in high-dimensional semantic feature spaces and fail to fully exploit structured ontological knowledge for semantic alignment. This paper addresses these gaps by proposing a hybrid framework that integrates Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models with multi-type Ontology Matching to improve both the accuracy and semantic coverage of SWS discovery. In this paper, we discuss the use of quantum machine learning models and ontological matching techniques for the discovery of Semantic Web Services (SWS) in the Semantic Web. We contrast the effectiveness of different quantum machine learning models with their classical counterparts, including Quantum k-Nearest Neighbors (QkNN), Quantum Decision Trees, Quantum Random Forest, and Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVM). Our experiments on the OWLS-TC v4 benchmark demonstrate that QSVM achieved the highest post-integration accuracy of 95.1% when paired with graph-based ontology matching, while Quantum Random Forest achieved the highest standalone accuracy of 92.2% without ontology matching. QSVM's standalone accuracy was 63.0%, reflecting its sensitivity to noisy feature representations in the absence of semantic enrichment; ontology matching consistently recovered and surpassed its performance. Tables 7 through 10 report post-integration results per matching method. Table 13 reports standalone baseline accuracy. These two result sets are distinct and complementary, not contradictory. The application of ontological matching techniques to SWS discovery made the accuracy of SWS discovering much better in both quantum and classical machine learning models. QkNN was the one with the greatest accuracy improvement of 2.8% after adding ontological matching in the mix. Our results indicate that quantum machine learning models, for example Quantum Random Forest (QRF) and Quantum k-Nearest Neighbors (QkNN), are the best candidates for the discovery of SWS. The application of ontological matching methods together with machine learning models is advisable for the improvement of the accuracy of the SWS discovery process. Nevertheless, it should be mentioned that the efficiency of these methods may be different depending on the accuracy and the completeness of the ontologies that are the basis. This research gives a useful information about the possible of quantum machine learning models and ontological matching techniques for enhancing the SWS finding accuracy.

title: Integration of transplanted chemically induced liver progenitor cells into recipient bile ducts in a rat bile duct transection model.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chemically induced liver progenitor cells (CLiPs) generated from mature hepatocytes are bipotent and represent a promising source for biliary repair. However, their therapeutic potential in cholangiopathy models remains unclear. In this study, we investigated rat CLiPs using a rat bile duct transection (BDT) model.
METHODS: Rat CLiPs were induced using the Y-27632/A-83-01/CHIR99021 regimen, resulting in loss of the hepatocyte marker ALB and gain of the progenitor markers CD90 and EpCAM. GFP-labeled CLiPs (1 × 10^7) were transplanted into Sprague-Dawley rats following BDT via portal vein infusion. On postoperative days (POD) 3 and 7, engraftment, proliferation, differentiation, and injury indices were assessed using immunofluorescence, quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), and serum biochemistry.
RESULTS: CLiPs engrafted and survived until POD 7 after portal vein infusion, and proliferative activity was observed by Ki-67 staining. Immunofluorescence revealed GFP + /ALB+ hepatocyte-like cells and GFP + /CK7 + cholangiocyte-like cells integrating near native ducts, indicating bipotential differentiation. qRT-PCR showed that BDT-induced expression of progenitor/ductular markers (Sox9, Epcam, Krt7, and Krt19) was attenuated in CLiP-treated groups compared to untreated BDT rats, although levels remained above those in sham rats. Serum AST, ALT, and ALP levels tended to decrease, and albumin levels increased after CLiP transplantation.
CONCLUSIONS: CLiPs survived and acquired hepatocyte-like and cholangiocyte-like phenotypes during the early phase after portal vein transplantation in a rat BDT model. These findings support the feasibility of CLiP-based hepatobiliary regenerative therapy, although longer-term and functional studies are required to confirm durable biliary repair.

title: Balancing work and health: A cross-sectional study on the relationship between paid employment and treatment adherence in Dutch people with a chronic condition.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: People with a chronic condition struggle with treatment adherence. At the same time, a majority of the working-age population with a chronic condition actively participates in the workforce. Having a paid job might affect the ability of people to incorporate treatments into their daily schedule, but it is currently unclear how and to which extent job-related factors affect treatment adherence.
METHODS: The Nivel Panel Stronger Together was used to collect self-reported data from 309 individuals with one or more chronic illnesses, who have paid work and use medication. Correlation analysis and univariate and multiple logistic regressions were performed to examine the effects of employment type, contract type, hours of work, extent of both physical and psychological demands, limitations at work, inclusion at work and work-related medication self-efficacy on treatment adherence. For this study, treatment adherence was defined as following the treatment plan as agreed with health professionals, and consisted of adherence to both medication and healthcare appointments.
RESULTS: The treatment adherence rate was 56%. Inclusion at work was positively associated with adherence (AOR 1.50, 95% CI 1.00-2.25, p = .049). Also, a relationship between moderate physical job demands and adherence was found (AOR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.92, p = .026). No significant associations were found between adherence and the other studied variables.
CONCLUSIONS: These results imply that the extent to which the working population with a chronic condition is able to adhere to their prescribed treatment, is not affected by practical workplace characteristics. Also, we found no evidence for an effect of self-efficacy, though results warrant further research. Still, working at a workplace where one feels acknowledged and valued improves the likelihood of being adherent, highlighting the importance of fostering an inclusive workforce for individuals with a chronic condition to improve adherence and workability.

title: Mechanical-acoustic-optical response properties in uniaxial compression failure of rock masses with different dissolution degrees.
abstract: To reveal the effects of dissolution cavities on the mechanical properties and failure mechanisms of surrounding rock, uniaxial compression tests were conducted on rock-like specimens with dissolution degrees of 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20%. A mechanical-acoustic-optical integrated system combining acoustic emission (AE) and digital image correlation (DIC) was used to characterize mechanical response, AE activity, strain field evolution, and failure behavior. The results indicate that with increasing dissolution degree, compressive strength, elastic modulus, peak axial strain, and deformation modulus decreased by 36.45%, 27.01%, 17.25%, and 41.28%, respectively. Post-peak failure gradually changed from rapid coalescence of a single dominant crack to progressive failure controlled by multiple defects. AE activity shifted from concentrated release near peak strength to continuous release throughout loading, accompanied by earlier crack initiation and an expanded pre-peak damage interval. Crack activity evolved from small scale microcracking to the propagation and coalescence of larger scale cracks. Combined AE and DIC results further showed a transition from axial tensile splitting failure to progressive mixed tensile-shear failure with multiple shear strain concentration zones and coordinated crack coalescence. These findings provide experimental evidence for stability assessment and disaster mitigation of dissolution voided surrounding rock in karst underground engineering.

title: Addressing gender bias in sexual and reproductive health care: A scoping review of training tools and interventions.
abstract: Gender norms and bias influence how health workers interpret and deliver sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) services, contributing to stigma, discrimination, and inequities in care. This scoping review aimed to map training tools and educational interventions designed to strengthen health workers' competencies and address gender bias in SRHR care. This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were conducted across multiple databases and organizational websites for literature published between 2000 and November, 2025. Eligible records included manuals, curricula, toolkits, and educational interventions targeting health workers and addressing gender norms, bias, values, or stigma in SRHR care. Data were extracted and synthesized using descriptive and narrative approaches. A total of 128 sources were included, comprising 25 toolkits/manuals and 103 intervention reports representing 100 unique intervention approaches. Together, they covered diverse SRHR domains and used multi-component pedagogical approaches, including didactic instruction (98.4%), reflective or values-based learning (83.2%), and experiential methods such as role-play, simulation, and case-based learning (92%). Most interventions emphasized equitable, person-centered care (98.4%) and 68.8% incorporated gender-transformative elements, while 74.4% included system-level components. Across the mapped literature, gender-transformative and system-level approaches were incorporated to varying degrees, reflecting variability in their integration across educational interventions. Overall, the review highlights the breadth and characteristics of existing training approaches and identifies opportunities for greater integration of gender-transformative and system-level strategies in future SRHR training and evaluation.

title: Antimicrobial resistance and molecular characterization of blaCTX-M-producing Escherichia coli isolated from broiler chickens in Peru.
abstract: The misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in humans and animals contribute to the selection and dissemination of antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) bacteria. In animal production systems, antimicrobial use is a key driver of the emergence and spread of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria across humans, animals, and the environment within a One Health framework. A total of 300 cloacal swabs were collected from apparently healthy broiler chickens at two poultry collection centers in Lima, Peru. ESBL-producing Escherichia coli were isolated on CHROMagar™ ESBL and identified by conventional biochemical tests. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines, and ESBL production was phenotypically confirmed. CTX-M groups were detected by qPCR, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on selected isolates. Seventy-nine ESBL-producing E. coli isolates were recovered (26.3%; 95% CI: 21.4-31.6). All isolates exhibited multidrug-resistant phenotypes. CTX-M group 1 was detected in 87.3% of isolates and group 9 in 12.7%. WGS analysis identified blaCTX-M-55, blaCTX-M-65, and blaCTX-M-3 distributed across multiple sequence types. Phylogenetic analysis revealed the presence of both closely related clonal clusters and genetically diverse isolates. These findings suggest that poultry production systems may serve as potential reservoirs of multidrug-resistant ESBL-producing E. coli in Peru. Given the study design and limited genomic sampling, the results should be interpreted as preliminary and highlight the need for expanded surveillance within a One Health framework.

title: USB-powered vs. self-heating warm compresses for meibomian gland dysfunction: A prospective randomized crossover clinical trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dry eye syndrome (DES) is a prevalent multifactorial condition characterized by tear film instability and meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD). Warm compress therapy remains a cornerstone for improving lipid layer function. However, very limited comparative data exist on newer USB-powered devices vs. self-heating masks in Middle Eastern populations.
METHODS: This randomized crossover clinical trial compared USB-powered and self-heating masks in 15 participants aged 18-40 years with meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD) associated eye (tear break-up time ≤10 s). Each intervention was scheduled for five consecutive days, separated by a two-week washout. The prespecified primary outcome was non-invasive TBUT measured with the OCULUS Keratograph 4M; tear meniscus height (TMH) and symptom scores were secondary outcomes. A two-way ANOVA and Post-hoc Bonferroni tests adjusted for multiple comparisons were used for analysis. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07618169).
RESULTS: All 15 participants contributed data to both intervention phases. Across observed visits, the USB-powered device was associated with higher TBUT (likelihood-ratio χ2(1) = 7.43, p = 0.006) and TMH (χ2(1) = 4.49, p = 0.034). Day 5 descriptive means with USB-Powered compress and self-heating mask were 9.53 ± 2.18 s versus 7.21 ± 2.90 s for TBUT, and 0.200 ± 0.020 mm versus 0.188 ± 0.016 mm for TMH, respectively. No significant between-device difference was observed in SPEED scores, although mean scores showed a mild improvement, and no adverse events were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: USB-powered warm compresses provided superior outcomes in enhancing tear film stability and volume compared to self-heating masks. Consistent temperature control and reusability make them a promising at-home therapy for patients with MGD. USB-powered devices may be preferred for patients requiring sustained thermal therapy, particularly in arid climates with variable indoor cooling. Further large-scale trials are warranted to confirm these findings.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov under registration number: NCT07618169.

title: Vigorous physical activity and physical function are strongly associated with better health in patients with long-standing radiographic axial spondyloarthritis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of physical function and level of physical activity on health status and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with long-standing radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA).
METHODS: In total, 141 patients with long-standing r-axSpA were included in this cross-sectional cohort study. Assessments included physical function (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI)), spinal mobility (modified Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Metrology Index (BASMI)), muscle function for leg strength (Timed Stands Test (TST)) and handgrip force (Grippit), amount of self-reported physical activity (vigorous physical activity, moderate physical activity, sedentary behavior), health status by ASAS Health Index (ASAS HI) and HRQoL with Short Form Survey Instrument 36-Item. Multivariable linear regression was used to analyze associations between health status, HRQoL, physical activity, muscle function, and physical function.
RESULTS: The mean (SD) age was 60 (12) years, diagnosis duration was 25 (10) years, and 57% were male. Physical function and vigorous physical activity were the strongest determinants of health status and HRQoL. The models explained approximately 50% of the variation in ASAS HI and the physical aspects of HRQoL and 21% of the mental aspects of HRQoL. Participants displayed good health status (62%) by ASAS HI ≤ 5, reached the recommended level of health-enhancing physical activity (77%), had normal muscle function (TST 82% and Grippit 91%), and demonstrated physical function (55%), and spinal mobility (45%) within reference values.
CONCLUSION: This study highlights the importance of regular vigorous physical activity in older individuals living with long-standing r-axSpA since it was strongly associated with health status and HRQoL.

title: First responders' experiences and training needs at the scene of a suspected suicide in Ireland: A mixed methods study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: First responders are categorised as those who are the first to respond to emergency calls and attend the site of an emergency. They include, but are not limited to police, emergency medical technicians, firefighters, and water safety personnel. First responders play a critical role in suicide postvention, supporting those bereaved by suicide and preventing adverse outcomes. However, many responders feel uncertain about how to effectively support those bereaved by suicide and often lack formal postvention training. This study aimed to explore and understand the experiences and training needs of first responders when attending the scene of a suspected suicide.
METHODS: A mixed-method approach was adopted. A national quantitative survey with first responders was conducted. The impact of previous suicide-related training on suicide literacy, attitudes, and postvention knowledge was analysed using multivariate ANOVA, adjusting for sociodemographic factors. Qualitative data were collected through focus groups and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 1587 first responders completed surveys. Participants demonstrated positive and non-stigmatising attitudes towards suicide prevention and suicidal individuals, though lower scores were achieved for suicide literacy, postvention knowledge, organisation support, and preparedness. Previous suicide-related training was significantly associated with higher literacy, attitudes, and postvention knowledge, although effect-sizes were small. Qualitative findings from 10 focus groups revealed substantial gaps in training and confidence when responding to suspected suicides. Participants also described the considerable emotional toll of attending the scene and emphasised the need for support in the aftermath.
CONCLUSION: Attending the scene of a suspected suicide has an impact on first responders. Limited suicide prevention and postvention training creates challenges, particularly in communicating with the bereaved. These findings underscore the need for comprehensive suicide prevention and postvention training and the allocation of adequate support.

title: Modelling the impact of migration on FGM/C prevalence and risk in immigrant and diaspora populations.
abstract: Previous estimates of the number of women and girls impacted by female genital mutilation and cutting (FGM/C) in the United States (US) failed to account for the impact of migration and acculturation. Similar studies in Europe applied a standard factor to estimate the impact across the entire immigrant population. Several of the resultant European estimates offered two scenarios: no impact, in which prevalence remained unaffected by migration and acculturation, and partial impact, in which risk was assumed to drop by 50% for native-born children. Each of these previous studies was based on adaptations of the extrapolation method, which produces estimates based on the product of three input variables: the immigrant population in the country of residence, the prevalence in the country of origin, and the mitigating impact of migration and acculturation. This paper offers several methodological innovations to better estimate the impact of migration and applies the results to the US. It develops methods to account for selective migration, the mitigating impact of legislation and law enforcement, and it considers the age of migration and the age of cutting to estimate the impact of migration timing on the likelihood that individuals were cut prior to migration. Using these innovations to model the impact of migration on the population in the US suggested that previous studies had underestimated the number of women living with FGM/C, while overestimating the number of girls who were at risk.

title: Personalized assessment of high-definition slow-oscillatory transcranial direct current stimulation (so-tDCS) in older adults with sleep and subjective cognitive complaints: A study protocol for a randomized clinical trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) is increasingly recognized as an early and potentially modifiable stage in the trajectory of neurodegenerative diseases. In older adults with SCD, untreated sleep disturbances may accelerate the neurodegenerative process, potentially via mechanisms involving amyloid-beta accumulation, and contribute to more rapid cognitive deterioration. Currently, non-pharmacological treatment options that concurrently manage SCD and sleep disturbances remain scarce. High-definition slow-oscillatory transcranial direct current stimulation (so-tDCS) is an emerging, frequency-specific neuromodulation technique designed to enhance brain health and cognition.
METHODS AND DESIGN: This is a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial. Right-handed Chinese older adults with SCD and sleep disturbances will be randomly assigned to receive either high-definition 0.75 Hz so-tDCS or sham stimulation over a 4-week intervention period, with 40 participants per group. Outcome measures, including galvanic skin response, subjective cognitive complaints, sleep quality, salivary amyloid-beta levels, and domain-specific cognitive performance, will be evaluated at four time points: baseline, week 4 (immediately post‑intervention), and follow‑up at weeks 8 and 12.
CONCLUSIONS: Personalized neurophysiological signals, namely electrode-skin impedance, will be monitored using state-of-the-art measurement during so-tDCS. The successful implement of this signal will provide researchers with access to an "add-on" setting that enables them to easily, quickly and quantitatively evaluate real-time neurophysiological signals, thereby facilitating the incorporation of transcranial brain stimulation into clinical practice.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07433738.

title: Application of a concise video to improve patient understanding of tumor genomic testing in community and academic practice settings.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Tumor genomic testing (TGT) is standard-of-care for most patients with advanced/metastatic cancer. Despite established guidelines, patient education prior to TGT is frequently omitted. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the impact and durability of a concise 3-4 minute video for patient education prior to TGT in community versus academic sites and across cancer types.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients undergoing standard-of-care TGT were enrolled at a tertiary academic institution in three cohorts: Cohort 1-breast cancer; Cohort 2-lung cancer; Cohort 3-other cancers. Cohort 4 consisted of patients with any cancer type similarly undergoing SOC TGT at one of three community cancer centers. Participants completed survey measures prior to video viewing (T1), immediately post-viewing (T2), and after return of TGT results (T3). Outcome measures included: 1) 10-question objective genomic knowledge/understanding (GKU); 2) 10-question video message-specific knowledge (VMSK); 3) 11-question Trust in Physician/Provider (TIPP); 4) perceptions regarding TGT.
RESULTS: A total of 203 participants completed all survey timepoints. Higher baseline GKU and VMSK scores were significantly associated with higher income and greater years of education. For the primary objective, there was a significant and sustained improvement in VMSK from T1:T2:T3 (Poverall p < 0.0001), with no significant change in GKU (p = 0.41) or TIPP (p = 0.73). This trend was consistent within each cohort (all p ≤ 0.0001). Results for four VMSK questions significantly improved, including impact on treatment decisions, incidental germline findings, and insurance coverage of testing.
CONCLUSIONS: A concise, 3-4 minute, broadly applicable educational video administered prior to TGT significantly and sustainably improved video message-specific knowledge in diverse cancer types and in academic and community settings. This resource is publicly available at http://www.tumor-testing.com, with a goal to efficiently educate and empower patients regarding TGT while addressing guidelines within the flow of clinical practice.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05215769.

title: Promoting good and equal health by advancing vulnerable students' employment and income opportunities: Protocol for a multiple method research program leveraging student and school staff perspectives.
abstract: School-level social determinants of health (SDOH) account for a large share of variation in students' health behaviors. Because educational attainment is itself a key social determinant of health-shaping later employment, income, and health-efforts to promote equitable health must include understanding and improving school climate as a mechanism influencing academic achievement and wellbeing. This project examines how school-level SDOH develop and how they relate to later employment, income, and health outcomes in a representative sample of Swedish young people. It also investigates how school staff and students perceive the school's ability to address school-level SDOH and develops and pilots an intervention aimed at strengthening these determinants. This multi-method, multi-informant study uses a large longitudinal dataset following a representative cohort from ages 12-20. Additional primary data will be collected from school staff and students to assess perceptions of school-level SDOH. The project will also design and test an intervention intended to improve students' academic achievement, a central pathway influencing later employment, income, and health. Combining longitudinal data with new qualitative and quantitative materials allows the project to examine the development of school-level SDOH and the mechanisms through which they shape long-term outcomes. Education is essential for strengthening skills, economic opportunities, and health equity. Strong links exist between education level, employment, income, and health, making this project relevant for students, families, school personnel, and broader policy development. Findings may guide schools and policymakers in improving school environments to support achievement and long-term health equity. The project involves extensive data collection and collaboration across disciplines and universities. By integrating multiple methods, it aims to advance knowledge on how education influences employment, income, and health while informing school-level and policy-level strategies to support academic achievement and wellbeing.

title: Geologically-inspired and mutation-aware driven well log density reconstruction method for complex heterogeneous formations.
abstract: To address the issue of data distortion in traditional well log density reconstruction methods caused by harsh borehole environments in complex heterogeneous formations, and the challenge for general machine learning models to capture high-frequency abrupt change features due to the lack of geophysical constraints, this paper proposes a density curve reconstruction framework integrating geologically-inspired feature engineering and a mutation-aware mechanism. The method first constructs a multi-dimensional enhanced feature space covering sedimentary cycle characteristics and fluid properties through multi-scale geologically-inspired analysis, utilizing robust range normalization to eliminate interference from outliers. Subsequently, a mutation-aware driven algorithm based on the gradient change rate is innovatively designed. By dynamically adjusting loss weights, it resolves the drawback where traditional smoothing algorithms tend to erase formation interface information. Finally, geological prior constraint terms are embedded into the XGBoost architecture to achieve multi-objective optimization that balances data-driven accuracy with consistency in geological laws. Under leave-one-well-out cross-validation over ten wells, the proposed method achieves a mean R² of 0.98, an RMSE of 0.029, and an MAE of 0.022. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method not only improves reconstruction accuracy but also significantly enhances the physical consistency of the results. Furthermore, it precisely identifies thin interbedded boundaries, providing highly reliable basic data support for the refined evaluation of oil and gas reservoirs.

title: Experiences of palliative care for patients with pulmonary fibrosis: A qualitative exploration of patients and partners perspectives.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary fibrosis is often a progressive disease associated with reduced life expectancy and quality of life. Palliative care aims to optimize quality of life for both patients and their informal caregivers. So far, multiple studies have shown unmet palliative care needs in patients with pulmonary fibrosis. This study explores the experiences and needs of patients with pulmonary fibrosis and their partners to identify opportunities for improving palliative care.
METHODS: A qualitative study was performed with focus groups and individual semi-structured interviews with patients and their informal caregivers. Data collection and analysis were performed iteratively. A reflexive thematic analysis was performed, following the methods of Braun and Clarke.
RESULTS: In total, fifteen patients and 10 informal caregivers participated. One focus group, 13 individual interviews, and 5 dyadic interviews were performed. Two themes were generated: 'See me as a person', and 'Guide me through the trajectory' with both two subthemes, reflecting the patient and partner perspectives. Patients seek recognition beyond their disease, valuing empathy, open communication, and holistic care. At the same time, both patients and partners express the need for clear guidance and support throughout the medical journey, from diagnosis to end of life care, including emotional, practical, and logistical aspects.
CONCLUSIONS/DISCUSSION: Patients and partners experience a 'one-size-fits-all' approach to care and reveal several gaps that can be improved. Patients expressed the importance of being acknowledged as a person beyond the disease and being supported in navigating care and anticipating future needs. Partners highlighted the need to be valued and to receive information that enables them to provide care and maintain a sense of control and security.

title: Bowel sound in predicting the severity of acute pancreatitis: Protocol of a prospective, multi-center study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is a common condition, with approximately 20% of patients developing severe acute pancreatitis (SAP), which is associated with a poor prognosis. Early identification and timely intervention for SAP patients are essential for improving clinical outcomes. This study aims to investigate whether bowel sound (BS) monitoring could facilitate the early recognition of SAP in AP patients.
METHODS: This study is a prospective, multi-center prognostic study. We will consecutively recruit newly diagnosed AP patients within 48h of disease onset who have not developed SAP at enrollment from the emergency departments of three centers from 01/04/2024. Upon enrollment, each patient will undergo continuous bowel sound monitoring for at least 48 hours using standardized equipment and procedures. The primary outcome is the occurrence of SAP within the first 7 days of hospitalization. Collected bowel sound data will be analyzed using an automated algorithm to derive five bowel sound acoustic parameters: bowel sound occurrence rate, dominant frequency, duration, amplitude, and inter-bowel-sound interval. These parameters will be used as predictors of SAP. Bowel sound analysts will be blinded to patients' clinical information and outcomes, and treating clinicians will not have access to the bowel sound analysis results during the study. We will calculate the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and area under the curve (AUC) to evaluate their predictive performance.
DISCUSSION: This study explores bowel sound monitoring as a non-invasive, real-time tool for assessing AP severity. Early BS changes correlate with prognosis, offering continuous physiological insights complementary to traditional scores. Despite confounders like clinical interventions, preliminary data show BS attenuation in SAP. Standardized protocols and noise-cancellation algorithms enhance reliability. Mechanistically, BS reflects intestinal dysmotility, aiding early deterioration detection. Future work will validate BS-guided interventions to optimize AP management.

title: Adult-sourced fecal microbiota transplantation ameliorates early-life antibiotic-induced intestinal immune stress in juvenile mice associated with the modulation of the TLR4/MyD88 signaling pathway.
abstract: Early-life antibiotic (ABX) exposure profoundly disrupts gut microbiota assembly, triggering long-lasting intestinal immune stress. While fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) is a promising intervention, its immunological and ecological mechanisms in the juvenile gut remain underexplored. In this study, juvenile mice were subjected to a broad-spectrum ABX cocktail for 8 days followed by 4 days of adult-sourced FMT. 16S rRNA sequencing (n = 6/group) revealed that ABX drastically altered the microbial landscape, causing a severe relative reduction of core commensals and an opportunistic expansion of Bacteroides. Subsequent molecular analyses on day 13 (n = 3/group) demonstrated that this dysbiosis significantly upregulated the mucosal TLR4/MyD88 signaling axis and effector cytokines IL-17 and IL-22. Strikingly, adult FMT administration effectively attenuated the TLR4 cascade and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine transcript levels while immunoregulatory IL-10 transcripts remained partially elevated. Ecologically, FMT did not merely revert the gut to its naive juvenile baseline. Instead, it suppressed Bacteroides overgrowth and established a distinctly new, highly complex community enriched with putative mature, adult-signature taxa such as Parabacteroides, Tannerellaceae, and Desulfobacterota. Interestingly, the downregulation of TLR4 occurred concurrently with the engraftment of these Gram-negative, LPS-bearing taxa. Collectively, adult-sourced FMT ameliorates ABX-induced immune stress not by restoring the original microbiota, but by driving the juvenile gut towards a putatively mature, structurally distinct, and potentially immunologically tolerant ecological state.

title: Psychological distress among women with abnormal cervical cancer screening results in Poland: Validation of the Polish version of the Cervical Dysplasia Distress Questionnaire (CDDQ-PL).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated the validity and reliability of the Polish version of the Cervical Dysplasia Distress Questionnaire (CDDQ-PL) in women with abnormal cervical cancer screening results.
METHODS: A cross-sectional validation study was conducted among 285 women referred to a colposcopy unit following an abnormal cervical cancer screening result. Psychometric evaluation included language and content validity, item analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, internal consistency, and concurrent and convergent validity. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the CDDQ, an anxiety scale, and the Short Form Health Survey (SF-36).
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 38.69 years (SD = 10.77). The mean total CDDQ-PL score was 2.21, with the highest distress observed for health consequences (3.02) and the lowest for embarrassment (1.47). Anxiety significantly decreased after the visit (6.51 ± 2.73 vs. 4.87 ± 2.95). Internal consistency was good, with Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranging from 0.830 to 0.919 across subscales. Total CDDQ-PL scores showed moderate positive correlations with anxiety before (r = 0.378, p < 0.001) and after the visit (r = 0.381, p < 0.001). Higher distress was associated with poorer quality of life, particularly in emotional well-being, pain, and energy/fatigue domains of the SF-36.
CONCLUSIONS: The Polish version of the CDDQ demonstrated satisfactory validity and good internal consistency for assessing psychological distress in women with abnormal cervical cancer screening results. Its temporal stability requires confirmation in future test-retest studies.

title: Deep learning-based virtual perturbation reveals increasing heterogeneity of gene regulatory responses with aging
abstract: A central hypothesis in aging biology proposes that the gradual accumulation of stochastic molecular damage drives transcriptional deregulation (TD), ultimately leading to functional decline. However, existing single-cell analyses largely rely on static expression measurements and provide limited resolution of how regulatory responses change at the level of individual cells. Here, we leverage DKO, a deep learning framework that predicts cell-specific virtual gene perturbation effects from unperturbed transcriptomes, capturing cell-to-cell differences in regulatory context without requiring a reconstructed gene regulatory network or matched perturbation data. Applying DKO to single-cell transcriptomic datasets from humans, mice, Drosophila, and C. elegans revealed that the transcriptional consequences of perturbing the same gene became increasingly heterogeneous across cells with age, indicating that gene regulatory responses become less consistent and more dependent on cellular context. Furthermore, we find that cells with higher somatic mutation burdens have greater knockout-response variability, linking accumulated molecular damage to regulatory inconsistency. Within the same cellular populations, higher impact variability was also associated with higher senescence scores, linking transcriptional dysregulation to senescence-associated states. Our findings identify a progressive loss of regulatory robustness at both the gene and cell levels as a conserved feature of aging, linking stochastic molecular damage to increasing heterogeneity in cellular regulatory responses.

title: The influence of decay in dynamic models of gene regulatory networks
abstract: We investigate the influence of decay rates on the dynamics of three-dimensional gene regulatory networks modeled by nonlinear differential equations with logistic sigmoidal regulatory functions. Particular attention is paid to the existence, location, and stability of equilibrium points in systems involving numerous interacting parameters. An explicit analytical representation of a central equilibrium is obtained under suitable relations between the regulatory weights, thresholds, and decay coefficients, allowing its location to be determined without solving the corresponding nonlinear algebraic system numerically. General formulas for the characteristic polynomial of the linearized system are derived, and spectral conditions for instability are established for several classes of regulatory interactions. We demonstrate how variations in decay rates can change the number and stability of equilibria, transform oscillatory dynamics, and influence the emergence or suppression of complicated attractors. The possibility of chaotic behavior is investigated through eigenvalue configurations, Lyapunov exponents, and the Kaplan-Yorke dimension. Numerical examples illustrate the sensitivity of the dynamics to decay parameters, including the suppression of previously observed chaotic behavior. The results provide an analytical framework for investigating equilibrium configurations, stability transitions, and complex dynamics in parametrized gene regulatory networks.

title: An Open-Source Web-Based Viewer for Disseminating Image-Derived Models
abstract: Patient-specific 3-dimensional (3D) models are increasingly central to planning surgery and catheter-based intervention in children with congenital heart disease (CHD), whose anatomy is often atypical and variable. These models inform care only when the surgeons and interventional cardiologists who make treatment decisions can rotate, crop, and measure them directly. Desktop modeling applications require local installation, capable hardware, and training. Commercial web-based viewers are portable but closed, and, in our experience, cannot display volume rendering, time-resolved (e.g., 4-dimensional) data, or the custom workflows centers build for CHD. Because CHD populations are small and heterogeneous, such workflows are unlikely to be prioritized commercially, and end users have no means to add them. To address these limitations, we developed the SlicerHeart Viewer, an open-source module that presents a simplified interface to a complete 3D Slicer/SlicerHeart session running on a server. Clinicians access models created by clinical modeling services from any device through a web browser. Because 3D Slicer runs underneath, volume rendering, time-resolved data, and any SlicerHeart workflow, including those developed for CHD, are available without modification. The module is independent of the hosting environment; we chose internal servers behind institutional single sign-on, and a cloud-hosted option is in development. Over one year at a single pediatric center, nearly all of 82 modeled cases were shared through the Viewer with clinicians from five specialties, with cases loading in 5 to 10 seconds. The approach is not specific to CHD and is deployable at other centers.

title: PMO-Dock: Benchmarking Docking, Specificity, and Generalization in Molecular Optimization
abstract: The Practical Molecular Optimization (PMO) benchmark standardized evaluation in molecular optimization, but it is built on simple property-based oracles that do not capture structure-based drug design. As the field has moved to docking-based objectives, evaluation practice has become unstandardized, and different methods report results on different docking tasks, often without a shared protocol for fair comparison or sample-efficiency constraints. To address this, we introduce Practical Molecular Optimization for Docking (PMO-Dock), a benchmark and protocol for docking-based optimization consisting of 25 tasks covering hit generation, lead optimization, and a new specificity task requiring strong on-target binding while penalizing off-target interactions. The protocol separates model development from final evaluation: validation tasks are used for hyperparameter tuning, and test tasks are held out for final evaluation and are not used during development. Evaluation on the test tasks is done under a strict oracle budget to reflect realistic drug-discovery settings. We benchmark four diverse high-performing methods spanning different optimization paradigms, Saturn (reinforcement learning), GenMol (discrete diffusion), Genetic-guided GFlowNet, and ChemLlama (LLM-based evolutionary search). Our results show no universally best method across tasks, additional analyses of hyperparameter transfer (cross-task and cross-category) and sensitivity show that transfer is often limited and varies by method, motivating method-dependent selection strategies. This benchmark provides a concrete standard for evaluating generalization to unseen tasks and sample efficiency under a limited test-time oracle budget.

title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
abstract: Multi-objective molecular optimization is a critical process in drug discovery that aims to modify a given molecule to simultaneously improve multiple properties while maintaining a similar overall structure. This process often requires iterative modifications guided by computational or experimental feedback. Recent large language model (LLM)-based methods have begun to explore this iterative approach; however, these methods are not explicitly trained to leverage such feedback, while existing approaches primarily focus on single-turn molecular optimization. To address this gap, we introduce Multi-turn Feedback Guided (MFG) molecular optimization, a reinforcement learning framework that trains an LLM to progressively optimize molecules using feedback from previous turns. MFG introduces a feedback vector capturing both property improvements and source molecule similarity, alongside a feedback-aligned reward function that promotes progressive improvement across turns. We apply MFG over $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$, a state-of-the-art LLM model for multi-objective molecular optimization, evaluate $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ on ten multi-objective molecular optimization tasks. The results demonstrate that $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ achieves the highest average similarity-constrained success rate ($81.50%$), outperforming the base model $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$ ($70.81%$).

title: Brain Age Gap Progression in Individuals at Risk for Neurodegeneration
abstract: Neuroimaging is a widely used modality for characterizing neurodegeneration in various health conditions. Brain age gap has emerged as a promising biomarker for monitoring brain health from neuroimaging data using machine learning algorithms. Recent studies have leveraged coVariance neural networks (VNN)-driven pipelines based on the advancements in graph signal processing for relatively transparent construction of brain age gap from neuroimaging data. In this paper, we focus on a longitudinal study of VNN-based brain age gap in conjunction with Alzheimer's Progression Score (APS) in individuals that are at a higher risk of neurodegeneration due to family history of Alzheimer's disease. APS is a multimodal marker of disease progression. The longitudinal analysis of APS and VNN-derived brain age gap metrics revealed that a higher risk of disease progression at baseline predicted a larger rate of increase in brain age gap in follow-up visits. Thus, our findings revealed potential stratification in the brain age gap modulated by clinical/biological risks of AD in the at-risk population.

title: STAMP as a topology-aware molecular language for fragment-level learning and editing
abstract: Molecular fragments provide chemically meaningful units, but existing molecular languages rarely make their locations and connections explicit for editing. Here we introduce STAMP (Sequential Tree Attachment-based Motif-Preserving representation), a topology-aware molecular language that connects fragment-level representation learning with precise structural editing. STAMP separately encodes motif identity, attachment sites and tree topology, making fragments reusable across contexts and subtrees directly accessible. Learned representations capture motif similarity and recurring transformations, and lower activity-cliff prediction error on 23 of 30 targets versus a matched SMILES encoder. Compatible subtree operations support scaffold-preserving optimization, ranking first among six methods on 15 of 23 benchmark objectives. A deterministic compiler enables frozen language models to act on indexed fragments, improving molecular editing, optimization, transformation transfer and change identification by 9 to 56 percentage points over plain SMILES. Together, these results establish an executable molecular language in which learned chemical units remain directly operable during design.

title: An efficient and flexible generalization of transit compartment models for delayed biological processes
abstract: Transit compartment models are widely used in pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics to represent delayed biological processes such as absorption, maturation, cellular proliferation, and treatment-induced toxicity. This transit compartment formulation imposes an artificial relationship between the mean and variance of the delay distribution, as the number of transit compartment must be integer-valued number of transit compartments. Consequently, estimating the number of compartments from experimental data leads to mixed-integer optimization problems that artificially constrain model dynamics and bias parameter inference. However, these transit compartment models are mathematically equivalent to distributed delay differential equations with Erlang delay kernels. We leverage a hypoexponential generalization of these distributed delay differential equations that preserves the familiar ordinary differential equation structure while allowing the mean and variance of the delay distribution to be estimated directly as real-valued parameters. This approach does not increase the number of inferred parameters and can be immediately implemented as a straightforward modification of existing transit compartment models. We demonstrate the approach using models of viral eclipse phases, lymphocyte proliferation, and chemotherapy-induced neutropenia. Across these examples, the hypoexponential formulation provides comparable or improved fits relative to Erlang transit models and substantially reduces computational cost by avoiding grid search over compartment numbers. This framework provides a practical approach to estimate biologically meaningful delay distributions in quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models.

title: ECG-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Targeted Electrocardiogram Waveform Evolution
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) models need supervision that targets evolving weaknesses and remains faithful to waveform evidence. We introduce ECG-RSI, a recursive self-improvement framework combining verified waveform synthesis with feedback-guided intervention search. Signal remeasurement verifies waveform edits; construction errors guide generator repair, while learner errors motivate interventions compared on a separate selection set. Across seven benchmarks, three rounds raise Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's mean question-answering accuracy from 34.57% to 56.04% and mean classification F1 from 24.27 to 34.03. Across the retained trajectory, the preferred supervision shifts from direct reinforcement to confusion-focused contrasts. Continued feedback correction yields diminishing external gains. These results motivate separating error diagnosis from intervention selection and checking whether gains on the feedback set transfer to independent benchmarks.

title: MedEvo: Medical Reasoning Evolution through Knowledge Navigation
abstract: Medical multimodal reasoning models are typically trained on teacher-generated rationales, discarding the valid reasoning in students' own failed trajectories, while general-domain correction methods offer little guidance for errors in image reading, anatomical context, or differential diagnosis. We propose MedEvo, which uses medical knowledge, namely a tag taxonomy and error-type diagnosis, to navigate both trajectory repair and data selection. For each failed rollout, a gold-blind auditor locates the first consequential error and provides a minimal, answer-free hint; the same student retains the valid prefix and regenerates the erroneous suffix. After each round, MedEvo identifies capability gaps across medical tags on a held-out feedback set and prioritizes related questions for new rollouts and repairs. With supervised fine-tuning (SFT) alone, MedEvo raises Qwen3.5-9B mean accuracy across seven benchmarks from 65.57% to 69.12% (47.40% to 54.50% on the multimodal track of MedXpertQA (MedXpertQA-MM)), surpassing teacher-distillation SFT (66.93%). It also raises Qwen3.5-35B and Qwen3.5-397B mean accuracy from 67.91% to 73.04% and from 71.83% to 74.95%, respectively. Our analyses show that failed trajectories contain reasoning worth preserving, that repair success does not imply learning value, and that independent feedback is key to sustained improvement.

title: Effects of cortisol time-scales in a model of emotion regulation
abstract: Stress reshapes cortico-limbic dynamics across multiple timescales, with important consequences for healthy and pathological arousal responses. We develop and analyze a Wilson-Cowan model of prefrontal-amygdala circuitry, incorporating excitatory and inhibitory populations involved in emotional regulation. The effects of stress cortisol are represented as history-dependent modulations of two stress-sensitive interactions: recurrent prefrontal excitation and inhibition of basolateral amygdala principal cells. Using numerical simulations and bifurcation analysis, we examine how this self-interacting system organizes transitions between stable activity and infra-slow oscillations, and how this structure changes with cortisol-related temporal memory. To distinguish the effects of memory temporal distribution from those of its timescale, we compare weak and strong Gamma kernels with a discrete-delay limit, representing progressively different ways in which past activity can influence current coupling. Introducing temporal memory reshapes the parameter region supporting oscillations and alters their persistence. Weak and strong Gamma kernels produce remarkably similar global dynamics, whereas the discrete-delay limit generates a substantially richer bifurcation structure, including quasiperiodic activity. Together, these results suggest that the dynamical effects of cortisol depend not only on the characteristic timescale of its action, but also on the shape of the temporal memory through which past neural activity influences the present. Different forms of temporal integration may provide a mechanism by which neural systems implement distinct functional dynamics, while changes in this integration could promote atypical or pathological rhythmic regimes.

title: Simulating Alzheimer's amyloid-like pathology on a fly central nervous system connectome
abstract: In Alzheimer's disease, the amount of pathology in the brain is an imperfect predictor of how much function is lost. Pathology leads to that loss through neural circuits, but these cannot be observed neuron by neuron in patients. This study therefore simulated the central nervous system of the adult male Drosophila melanogaster: 166,700 integrate-and-fire neurons wired by the MaleCNS connectome. The simulator reproduced a published fly brain model (rate correlation 0.9997). Three kinds of damage reported in amyloid-$β$ flies, a lowered spike threshold, synapse loss and neuron loss, were imposed with assumed magnitudes, and circuit responses were measured in 1,424 simulated flies. The number of neurons lost was a poor guide to the deficit, which depended partly on how many synaptic contacts went with them and whether they included input neurons or one command neuron. With the same 12% of neurons removed, odour-evoked whole-brain activity was 93%, 47% or 31% of the healthy value when damage fell on poorly connected, random or highly connected neurons; these flies lost 20%, 35% and 48% of contacts. When the contacts lost were equalised, the three groups differed less; whether the remaining difference reflects where the damage fell could not be established. In 48 flies, restoring only the contacts that surviving neurons had lost recovered 62% of the whole-brain deficit, and restoring the removed neurons 39%. In flies that had lost neurons delivering the odour, these accounted for about half the deficit due to neuron loss. One neuron could decide an outcome: all 66 flies that lost the giant fibre on the stimulated side, which commands escape, had a giant fibre rate below 100 Hz, against 1 of 254 that kept it. Whole-brain activity revealed damage at milder severity than the learning index, because it changed much relative to its variation between trials.

title: Two Routes to Interoceptive Prioritisation: Dissociating Likelihood Precision and Preference Reweighting in Active Inference
abstract: An embodied agent must prioritise among competing bodily needs. In active inference, it can respond to an urgent need by increasing the precision of information about that need or by increasing its preference for outcomes that relieve it. We compare these two interventions, separately and together, in a foraging gridworld with three lethal needs, and ask how each changes survival, perception and the body model the agent learns. Precision sharpens interoceptive posteriors and improves survival. Preference reweighting keeps bodily states further from their lethal boundaries and changes the states from which the agent learns, so its learned model covers fewer need levels, with lower quality across all levels but slightly higher quality on the levels it visits. An experiment on 72 further layouts does not establish the predicted preference benefit on difficult layouts, but both interventions improve average survival there and their interaction is positive. Survival alone therefore gives an incomplete account of how a model prioritises needs and learns about its body.
