title: Texture-aware diffusion modelling for severity-conditioned synthetic progression-like visualization of diabetic foot ulcers from single images.
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are serious complications of diabetes associated with delayed healing, infection, and limb amputation. Modelling DFU progression remains challenging because publicly available image datasets generally contain independent single-timepoint images rather than longitudinal follow-up sequences. This study proposes a texture-aware conditional diffusion framework for generating severity-conditioned, progression-like synthetic DFU images from a single RGB input. Instead of claiming patient-specific temporal prediction, the framework models plausible population-level visual transitions across ordinal pseudo-stages derived from clinically relevant severity cues. The full model achieved an SSIM of 0.851 ± 0.020, PSNR of 24.76 ± 1.12 dB, and FID of 44.33 ± 5.02, with higher observed SSIM and PSNR and lower FID values than the evaluated GAN and VAE baselines across structural fidelity and distributional realism. The GAN baseline achieved SSIM 0.782 ± 0.031, PSNR 21.98 ± 1.56 dB, and FID 59.13 ± 6.59, while the VAE baseline achieved SSIM 0.738 ± 0.038, PSNR 19.63 ± 1.83 dB, and FID 69.77 ± 7.44. The framework also obtained a Texture Consistency Score of 0.79 ± 0.04 and a Granulation Tissue Fidelity Score of 0.76 ± 0.05, indicating preservation of fine-grained texture and granulation-related appearance patterns. Ablation results confirmed the contribution of texture conditioning and cross-attention to image fidelity. Advanced severity-state analysis produced SSIM values of 0.674, 0.804, and 0.726 across three pseudo-stages, supporting severity-aligned structural consistency. Since true longitudinal future-state images were unavailable, these metrics indicate synthetic image fidelity and distributional realism, not longitudinal progression accuracy. Longitudinal DFU cohorts and larger clinician-centred validation remain necessary before clinical decision-support use or temporal progression claims can be justified. To assess generalization beyond the primary 493-image dataset, external validation was additionally performed on an independent DFU dataset under a zero-shot setting, demonstrating stable cross-dataset performance with only modest degradation in image fidelity and texture consistency. Therefore, the proposed framework should be interpreted as modelling cross-sectional severity-conditioned appearance interpolation across independent cases, rather than true patient-specific future progression prediction.

title: Rabbit distal femoral critical size bone defect model: Vascular anatomy, surgical technique, peri-operative husbandry and biological response of empty and autograft-filled defects.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Critical size bone defects do not heal spontaneously and are often used preclinically to evaluate the in vivo response to materials, devices or bone graft substitutes. Results may inform product development or satisfy regulatory body requirements, whilst also, providing clinically relevant information that cannot be obtained by in vitro or in silico experimentation. The New Zealand White (NZW) Rabbit distal femoral condylar defect in skeletally mature animals is a common model used in the development and evaluation of bone graft materials. When performed with appropriate consideration of the many pre, peri and post-operative factors the morbidity with this model is low. We present our experience with this model to provide a technical reference including the local vascular anatomy, surgical technique, peri-operative husbandry in large series between 2017-2022. The typical healing responses of empty and autogenous corticocancellous bone-filled defects is provided to assist in illustrating the model.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The local vascular anatomy was characterised ex vivo with anatomical dissection and intra-vascular injection of methylene blue, and an iohexol contrast study with micro-computed tomography. The in vivo animal model is described, highlighting the surgical approach, technique for defect creation and perioperative animal husbandry considerations. Examining outcomes from animals operated on over a 5-year period between 2017 and 2022 at our institution, the biological response following defect creation is also described qualitatively for empty defects (negative control) and autograft-filled defects (positive control) at 6 and 12-weeks post-operatively, with paraffin and polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) histology and micro-computed tomography (µCT) endpoints.
RESULTS: 2040 individual defects were created in 1020 rabbits confirmed to be skeletally mature with radiographs. Anaesthetic and intra-operative complications occurred with a very low incidence (1/ 1020 animals {0.1%}and 1/ 2040 defects {0.05%}, respectively). No post-operative complications impacting the healing outcomes or necessitating removal from the study occurred. Empty defects functioned as critically sized defects over a 12-week period, whilst autograft implanted into defects had incorporated into the surrounding cancellous architecture at 12 weeks. Closure of the cortical bone surface on the medial aspect of the femur was restored at 12 weeks, but not 6 weeks.
CONCLUSION: In vivo models provide invaluable, irreplaceable preclinical data; however, such high-impact studies must have a sound ethical basis and be conducted with animal welfare and scientific rigour at the forefront of study design and execution.

title: Assessing cultural awareness and competency in nursing education: A cross-sectional study of undergraduate nursing students in Ireland.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a growing imperative for nurses to navigate multicultural healthcare systems and deliver quality, responsive, safe, person-centred care. Accordingly, undergraduate nursing education must be relevant and innovative to provide undergraduate nursing students with meaningful learning opportunities to develop cultural competence. This study aims to assess undergraduate nursing students' cultural awareness and examine how these perceptions vary according to socio-demographic characteristics.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted utilising a valid and standardised tool, the cultural awareness scale (CAS). "One hundred and sixteen" undergraduate nursing students from a higher education institution participated in the study. The Mann-Whitney U test and the Kruskal-Wallis test were used to examine differences in CAS scores across subscales and total scores according to participants' socio-demographic characteristics.
RESULTS: Overall, the CAS results showed students' level of cultural awareness was moderately high, with slight variations across the four CAS subscales. Participants born in Ireland had higher scores on all subscales compared to participants born outside Ireland, although these differences were not statistically significant. Participants who identified as White scored highest on General Education Experience (64.54 vs 42.66, U = 837, p = 0.002, r = -0.29), and Total Awareness (63.32 vs 45.86, U = 939.5, p = 0.012, r = -0.23) compared with participants who were categorised as people of colour.
CONCLUSIONS: The cultural awareness scores in this study were moderately high among undergraduate nursing students, consistent with previous research using the CAS instrument. The findings suggest an association between ethnic background and perceptions of culturally inclusive educational practices and highlight the need for further research to explore these patterns and inform the development of culturally responsive nursing education.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics and machine learning characterize LTA4H-linked lipid metabolism and inflammatory signatures in the knee osteoarthritis IPFP/synovium compartment.
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a whole-joint disease characterized by inflammation, immune dysregulation, and metabolic imbalance. To define lipid metabolism-related transcriptional heterogeneity within the infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP)/synovium compartment, we integrated publicly available single-cell transcriptomic data from IPFP/synovium-derived joint cells with bulk synovial transcriptomic datasets from patients with KOA and controls. Lipid metabolism-related scores were derived using multiple single-cell scoring algorithms, and candidate genes were identified through score-associated analyses, differential expression, protein-protein interaction analysis, and five machine-learning approaches, followed by external bulk validation and single-cell characterization. Myeloid cells showed the most consistent KOA-associated increases in lipid metabolism-related transcriptional scores. Fifty composite-score-associated genes were identified and were enriched in lipid metabolic, lysosomal, and PPAR-related pathways. Cross-screening prioritized PLIN2, LTA4H, and PPT1, with LTA4H showing the strongest association with lipid metabolism-related transcriptional scores. LTA4H was predominantly enriched in myeloid cells, particularly monocytes and inflammatory macrophages, and was increased in KOA myeloid cells and high-score cells. Cell-cell communication, myeloid subclustering, and pseudotime analyses linked LTA4H-positive myeloid cells to inflammatory signaling and the transition from monocytes toward inflammatory macrophages. In silico knockout analysis further implicated LTA4H in regulatory programs related to leukocyte migration, chemotaxis, phagocytosis, and cytokine receptor binding. In a rat KOA model, LTA4H protein expression was increased in knee synovial tissues and spatially colocalized with CD68-positive macrophages. These findings define a myeloid-cell-centered context for LTA4H in KOA and link its expression to lipid metabolism-related transcriptional features and inflammatory myeloid-cell states.

title: Maize (zea mays l.) yield, and selected chemical properties of soils as influenced by lime and manure application in acid soils of Meket District, northeastern Ethiopia.
abstract: Acid affected soils have been expanding in the Ethiopian highlands, and caused serious yield decline. Organic amendments and lime have been used to manage soil acidity. However, the rate and the right combinations have not been sufficiently documented for various crops and locations. This study aimed at investigating the effects of four manure rates (0, 4, 8, and 12 t ha-1), with three lime rates (0, 1.5 and 3 t ha-1 CaCO3) on maize yield, and selected soil chemical properties. The experiment was arranged in factorial combinations using randomized complete block design (RCBD) with three replications. The result showed that significant variations were obtained for yield, and yield components of maize where maximum grain yield (4087.0 kg ha-1) was harvested from the combination of 8 t manure ha-1 with 1.5 t lime ha-1. However, significantly (P < 0.01) highest stalk yield (11155.0 kg ha-1) and yield of dry aboveground biomass (14803.7 kg ha-1) were achieved from the integrations of 3 t lime with 12 t manure ha-1. The plots that received 12 t ha-1 manure only had the highest OC content (1.96%), with an increase of 54%. Following 3 t ha-1 lime plus 12 t ha-1 manure applications, the available P content was found to be significantly (P < 0.01) the highest (14.41 mg kg-1). The present experiment indicated that integrated application of 3 t ha-1 lime with 8 t ha-1 manure could help increase maize yield and profitability while maintaining fertility of soils in acid affected soils of Meket area and similar other locations.

title: Barriers and enablers shaping kidney transplant care delivery: Insights from Iraqi pharmacists.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney transplant care in low-resource countries is often affected by multiple factors, including workforce constraints, fragmented communication, and medication access challenges. Given pharmacists' involvement in medication management and regular patient follow-up, this study was designed to explore transplant care delivery in Iraq from pharmacists' perspectives.
METHOD: Qualitative data were collected using face-to-face, semi-structured interviews with all eligible pharmacists from the two major governmental hospitals in Baghdad caring for kidney transplant recipients. Afterwards, data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis approach.
RESULTS: This study included 13 pharmacists, 5 of whom were working in the clinical transplant wards, whereas the remaining 8 were working in the outpatient consultation setting. Four descriptive themes were identified: Dispensing-centered practice within a constrained and evolving pharmacist role, fragmented yet adaptive interprofessional collaboration, patient education as an informal and inconsistently delivered practice, and medication availability within a constrained and variably regulated supply system.
CONCLUSION: This study highlights the adaptive approaches used by pharmacists in an attempt to maintain medication access and patient support with the available resources. However, the study findings also highlight challenges that extend beyond the capacity of individual pharmacists to resolve and suggest the need for more structured organizational support, clearer communication pathways, and an integrated system to strengthen Iraqi transplant care practices within comparable governmental settings.

title: Effectiveness of a self-management intervention on clinical outcomes among patients with type 2 diabetes at high risk for Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a common complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and a leading cause of end-stage renal disease, posing substantial health and economic burdens. Early self-management interventions targeting modifiable risk factors are crucial to prevent or slow DKD progression. However, most studies focus on later stages of DKD, leaving a gap in early prevention for high risk of DKD individuals.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of a structured self-management intervention on clinical outcomes among T2DM patients at high risk of DKD.
DESIGN: A prospective, two-arm, randomized controlled trial.
SETTING: A tertiary hospital in Shandong Province, China.
PARTICIPANTS: 134 patients with T2DM who were classified as being at high risk of DKD using a validated DKD risk prediction model.
METHODS: 134 participants were randomized 1:1 to the intervention or control group. The intervention group received a 12-week a structured self-management program and 12-week follow-up. The control group received usual care. Clinical outcomes included hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), systolic blood pressure (SBP), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC) were collected at baseline (T0), after the 12-week intervention (T1), and at 24 weeks (T2). Generalized estimating equations and intention-to-treat analyses were performed. Sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation were conducted.
RESULTS: All participants completed the intervention phase. During the follow-up visits period, 7 participants in the intervention group and 9 participants in the control group were lost to follow-up at T1 (attrition rate: 11.94%), while 5 participants in the intervention group and 4 participants in the control group were lost to follow-up at T2 (attrition rate: 6.71%). No significant differences in baseline sociodemographic or clinical indicators between participants retained and those lost to follow-up (p > 0.05), suggesting data were missing at random. Baseline comparisons between the intervention and control groups revealed no significant differences in demographic or clinical indicators (p > 0.05). Compared with the control group, the intervention group demonstrated significant improvements in HbA1c, eGFR, SBP, and LDL-C, while no significant differences were observed for UACR, BMI, or WC. Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results.
CONCLUSIONS: The self-management intervention effectively improved HbA1c, eGFR, SBP and LDL-C among T2DM patients at high risk of DKD. These findings suggest that integrating structured self-management into routine diabetes care may help improve modifiable risk factors and support early DKD prevention.
REGISTRATION: China Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400092745; registered on 22 November 2024).

title: Dietary intake patterns and KDOQI guideline compliance among hemodialysis patients in Bangladesh: Gaps, misreporting, and clinical implications.
abstract: Optimal nutrition is a central to the care of people receiving maintenance hemodialysis, yet dietary intake in these patients is usually measured by self-report, and self-report is known to be unreliable. Evidence from resource-limited dialysis settings is scarce. This cross-sectional study assessed dietary intake among 181 adults receiving maintenance hemodialysis at four hospital-based units in Bangladesh, and examined how screening reported intake for plausibility changes conclusions about guideline adherence. Intake was measured by three non-consecutive 24-hour recalls and compared with the Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (KDOQI) recommendations. Reporting plausibility was classified from the ratio of energy intake to estimated basal metabolic rate. Appetite was assessed using the Appetite and Diet Assessment Tool. Of 178 participants with complete data, 65.2% reported acceptable, 32.0% under-reported and 2.8% over-reported energy intake. In the cohort as a whole, only 20 of 176 (11.4%) met the energy target of 30-35 kcal/kg/day and 58 (33.0%) met the protein target of at least 1.0 g/kg/day. Screening changed these estimates in opposite directions according to the type of target. For intake targets, adherence rose once implausible reports were excluded: energy from 11.4% to 15.5% and protein from 33.0% to 47.4%. For restriction targets the reverse occurred: apparent adherence to the sodium limit fell from 73.6% to 65.5% and to the phosphorus limit from 88.2% to 84.5%. The phosphorus-to-protein ratio exceeded 12 mg/g in all but five participants. Poor appetite was common (42.0%) but did not correspond to lower measured intake, and was instead associated with reporting plausibility (p = 0.024). Unscreened self-reported intake simultaneously overstates dietary inadequacy and understates dietary excess, and should not be used unfiltered to guide nutritional decisions in this population.

title: Niallia Circulans mediated Bio-fabrication of ZnO nanoparticles: Synthesis, characterization, and multifunctional applications.
abstract: The current study addresses increasing global problems (agricultural sustainability, environmental contamination, and antimicrobial resistance) by means of sustainable and multifunctional biosynthesized Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). The study utilized a cell-free supernatant of a novel endophytic bacterial strain (Niallia Circulans) to synthesize ZnO NPs. Biosynthesized NPs were evaluated by using various techniques of characterization. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was revealed by UV-Visible spectral peak for ZnO NPs at 355 nm. A X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed a crystallite size of 90.64 nm, while scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX) demonstrated the predominance of hexagonal-structured zinc, carbon, and oxygen elements. The functional groups in Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) confirm the presence of biomolecules. The evaluated multifunctional application of biosynthesized ZnO NPs exhibits an enhanced early seedling growth rate and increased seed germination (100% in 12 h) on cowpea (Vigna unguiculata L.) compared to the control groups. Also shows excellent antibacterial activity against test bacterial strains. Additionally, a high removal efficiency of 97.85% was achieved within 110 min for 10 ppm methylene blue dye solution at pH 9. This study highlights the endophytic bacteria-mediated successful synthesis of ZnO NPs, with potential multifunctional applications in agriculture, antimicrobial treatments, and environmental remediation.

title: Menstrual health challenges and associated barriers among tribal adolescent girls in India: A systematic review.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Menstrual health is a critical yet neglected public health issue among tribal adolescent girls in India, influenced by socio-cultural, economic, and infrastructural determinants. This review aimed to explore the key menstrual health challenges, barriers, and associated outcomes among tribal adolescent girls in India.
METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed across PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar for studies published between January 2015 and March 2026. Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies focusing on menstrual health among tribal adolescent girls in India were included. Study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal were conducted independently by multiple reviewers. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tools. Due to heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis approach was adopted.
RESULTS: Out of 197 identified records, 28 studies met the inclusion criteria. The findings reveal significant disparities in menstrual health management driven by socioeconomic status, education, cultural taboos, and infrastructural limitations. Key challenges included limited access to sanitary products, inadequate WASH facilities, and poor awareness. Cultural stigma and restrictive practices contributed to psychological distress and unsafe hygiene behaviours. These barriers were associated with adverse outcomes such as reproductive tract infections and increased school absenteeism. The quality appraisal indicated overall moderate to high methodological rigour, with most studies demonstrating acceptable quality despite some limitations related to study design and reporting.
CONCLUSION: Menstrual health among tribal adolescent girls remains a significant public health concern in India. Addressing these challenges requires integrated, culturally sensitive interventions focusing on education, improved infrastructure, and equitable access to menstrual health services to enhance health outcomes and well-being.

title: Interactive effects of seed rate, sowing method, and variety on Teff (Eragrostis tef) yield, yield components, and lodging trait performance in the central highlands of Ethiopia.
abstract: Teff (Eragrostis tef) occupies close to three million hectares of agricultural land in Ethiopia, nonetheless, realized yields remain substantially below the crop's inherent genetic yield potential. Thus, this study aimed to examine how different sowing rates and methods impacted productivity of teff varieties in Mojana Wodera Woreda. The treatments included three varieties of teff (namely, Quncho, Kora and Abolse (local variety), three sowing rates (10, 15 and 20 kg ha -1), and three sowing methods (15 cm and 20 cm spacing between rows and broad casting). The interaction effect of seed rate, sowing method and variety significantly affected crop growth and yield parameters (P < 0.01). The tallest plant (128.33 cm) was achieved from variety Quncho combined with 20 cm row spacing and at a seed rate of 10 kg ha-1. Quncho sown at a rate of 10 kg ha-1 with a row spacing of 15 cm produced the maximum amount of aboveground biomass yield (10.76 t ha-1). Furthermore, the highest lodging index (44%) was recorded when variety Quncho was sown with a broadcasting method at the highest seed rate of 20 kg ha-1. The main effect of seed rate, sowing method and variety significantly affected days to 50% heading (P < 0.05), panicle length and grain yield (P < 0.01). Variety Kora significantly took longer time (59.18) to reach 50% heading than variety Quncho and Abolse. Increasing row spacing to 20 cm prolong the time for 50% heading of teff varieties, while sowing teff variety at a a rate of 15 kg ha-1 also significantly increased the days to heading. Quncho produced the largest panicle length (45.14 cm) and yield (2.47 t ha-1) which is 15.96% higher than variety Kora and 26.67% higher than the grain yield obtained from the local Abolse variety. Furthermore, sowing teff at a row spacing of 20 cm produced the maximum panicle length (44.46 cm) and yield (2.32 t ha-1). As to the seed rate, thhe highest grain yield and largest panicle were when teff was seeded at 10 kg ha-1.

title: Integrated bioinformatics analysis identifies an immune-related gene signature associated with non-obstructive azoospermia.
abstract: Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) is a severe male infertility disorder. This study aims to identify immune-related biomarkers for explore immune-related molecular signatures associated with NOA. Here, we integrated transcriptomic data from four independent cohorts (GSE145467, GSE45885, GSE45887, GSE9210) using an integrative pipeline combining differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and consensus-based multi-machine learning to identify an immune-related gene signature associated with NOA. We identified 16 immune-related differentially expressed genes through WGCNA, which were refined into a 12-gene panel-Hub NOA.Sig (CD14, CD19, CMTM2, CXCL16, HSPA1L, HSPA2, IGF1, IL13, POMC, RBP1, STAB2, TYROBP)-using five feature selection algorithms (Bagged Trees, Bayesian, Boruta, LASSO, LVQ). A Random Forest classifier based on Hub NOA.Sig yielded good classification performance with an AUC of 0.87. This signature offers a transcriptomic reference for characterizing NOA heterogeneity and exploring immune-related molecular features. Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) revealed significant alterations in six immune cell populations-including effector memory CD4 ⁺ /CD8 ⁺ T cells, regulatory T cells, and plasmacytoid dendritic cells-and demonstrated strong correlations between hub genes and specific immune infiltrates. Furthermore, drug-gene interaction screening and molecular docking predicted loperamide-POMC, acitretin-RBP1, and retinol-RBP1 as candidate drug-gene pairs for subsequent experimental validation. This work provides transcriptomic clues and candidate molecular targets for future mechanistic investigations into NOA-related male infertility.

title: Exploration of treatment burden during transition onto kidney replacement therapy: A longitudinal qualitative study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: People with kidney disease who need to transition onto kidney replacement therapy (KRT) face a life-changing diagnosis. This process involves complex decisions about treatment and a high volume of healthcare work. Little work has been done looking at KRT transition through the lens of treatment burden. This study aims to explore how treatment burden evolves during KRT transition in a population recruited from a large nephrology and kidney transplant unit in Glasgow, Scotland.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: Serial in-depth qualitative interviews were conducted with 30 participants across up to three time points, generating 76 interviews. We used a framework analysis informed by Normalisation Process Theory (NPT), Theory of Patient Capacity (TPC) and Burden of Treatment Theory (BoTT) to explore the interaction between workload, capacity, and the system. Five main themes affecting treatment burden arose: engaging personal and social resources to navigate KRT transition, being able to meet the challenges, preparing to enact the healthcare workload, undertaking KRT transition related workload, and the evolution of burden over time.
CONCLUSION: Transitioning onto KRT is a process that entails a high volume of healthcare workload and significant treatment burden. Experiences of treatment burden are influenced by the nature of the work required; the patient's capacity including physical, psychological, financial and cognitive factors; the capacity of their social network; and the functioning of the healthcare system. Particular focus should be placed on understanding the impact of the healthcare system on experiences of burden, as it represents a potentially modifiable driver of treatment burden that clinicians and healthcare policy-makers can directly influence.

title: Omicron SARS-CoV-2 shows NRP1-linked susceptibility in adipose-derived MSCs and alters primitive cord blood CD34⁺ HSPCs.
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 infection is linked to hematologic abnormalities, but whether early hematopoietic compartments and their stromal niche are directly engaged remains unclear. We used in vitro exposure models to compare variant-associated responses of adult mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and umbilical cord blood (UCB) CD34 ⁺ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). Adipose-derived (AD) and bone marrow-derived (BM) MSCs exposed to wild-type, Delta, or Omicron showed source- and variant-dependent nucleocapsid protein (NP) positivity, highest with Omicron in AD-MSCs; infectious virus in supernatants was undetectable. AD-MSCs expressed higher neuropilin-1 (NRP1) than BM-MSCs, and NRP1 knockdown reduced Omicron-associated NP signal, implicating an NRP1-linked entry process. SARS-CoV-2 exposure induced indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), most prominently in AD-MSCs. In UCB CD34 ⁺ HSPCs, Omicron increased NP positivity enriched in long-term HSCs, reduced primitive fraction frequencies, increased colony formation, and promoted early erythroid progenitor accumulation; heat-inactivated virus did not. NanoString profiling revealed host-response activation and altered cell-cycle/differentiation programs. These data indicate Omicron can engage stromal and early hematopoietic compartments and remodel stress-responsive hematopoiesis.

title: Explainable spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks: Multi-City PM2.5 forecasting in Bangladesh with geographic graph topology validation.
abstract: Accurate forecasting of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is critical for mitigating severe health risks in South Asia, yet it remains challenging in data-scarce regions like Bangladesh. While spatiotemporal graph neural networks (GNNs) offer a promising solution by capturing atmospheric transport, their effectiveness and the physical validity of their assumed spatial graphs have rarely been rigorously tested in such constrained settings. This study addresses this gap by evaluating a graph diffusion gated recurrent unit (GD-GRU) model using four years of daily, multi-source environmental data across a 12-city network. For forecasts up to three days ahead, the GD-GRU achieves an overall mean absolute error of 8.853 µg/m3 and an R2 of 0.666, significantly outperforming non-graph baselines under FDR-corrected Diebold-Mariano testing (p < 0.001). Furthermore, the model significantly outperforms DCRNN when pooled across all forecast horizons (p < 0.001), while remaining closely matched at individual lead times. Crucially, empirical validation of the model's underlying spatial assumptions demonstrates that occlusion-based spatial influence closely tracks the fixed geographic adjacency (r = 0.928, p < 0.001), and this simple distance-based graph outperforms unconstrained adaptive, wind-informed, and hybrid alternatives. Finally, a multi-method explainability framework shows strong rank convergence (Spearman ρ = 0.590 to 0.783), identifying the Green Leaf Index, wind speed, atmospheric pressure, and seasonal encoding as the dominant predictors of PM2.5. These findings confirm that carefully validated, interpretable static graph models can deliver robust air quality forecasts without requiring dense sensor networks, offering a practical template for environmental monitoring in data-limited regions.

title: Experiences and perspectives of Ayurvedic practitioners on non-communicable disease management in the UK: A qualitative study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a major public health challenge in the United Kingdom (UK), placing strain on the National Health Service (NHS). While Western medicine dominates NCD care, the use of complementary and alternative medicine (CAM), such as Ayurveda, is increasing. The objective of this study was to explore the experiences and perspectives of Ayurvedic practitioners in the UK regarding the use of Ayurveda for managing NCDs.
METHODS: Seventeen UK-based Ayurvedic practitioners participated in semi-structured qualitative interviews that were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically.
FINDINGS: Three key themes were identified. First, Ayurvedic practitioners viewed their role as complementary to Western medicine, providing holistic, individualised, and patient-centred care to support NCD management. Second, they faced multiple barriers in the UK, including structural challenges (limited integration, poor institutional support, and restricted patient access) and financial constraints (high treatment costs, lack of NHS coverage, and import regulations). Finally, professional associations played a vital role in providing legal and regulatory guidance, promoting continuous professional development, and supporting research to strengthen evidence and legitimacy.
CONCLUSION: Although Ayurvedic practitioners face considerable challenges in the UK, they play a unique role in negotiating legitimacy, professional recognition, and the epistemological challenges of practising within a Western-dominated healthcare system. Professional associations help legitimise and advance their practice, supporting culturally congruent, patient-centred care that complements conventional NCD management. Despite structural barriers, Ayurvedic practitioners have maintained their presence and have navigated a complex, structurally Western-centric healthcare landscape, offering insights into integrative approaches to NCD care.

title: Adaptation of the Quiet Quitting Scale into Turkish: A methodological study.
abstract: Quiet quitting has emerged as a contemporary work behavior associated with reduced organizational engagement and increased work-related stress, particularly among healthcare professionals. This study aimed to adapt the Quiet Quitting Scale into Turkish and evaluate its validity and reliability among healthcare workers. This methodological study was conducted online between February and April 2025. The sample included 298 healthcare professionals currently working in Turkey. Data were collected using the "Personal Information Form" and the "Quiet Quitting Scale." Content validity analysis showed item-level I-CVI values ranging from 0.83 to 1.00, with a total scale S-CVI of 0.97. Factor loadings for individual items ranged from 0.510 to 0.890. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) confirmed that the proposed factor structure fitted the data well, with model fit indices as follows: χ² = 64.31; df = 21; p < 0.05; χ²/df = 3.06; RMSEA = 0.083; CFI = 0.97; SRMR = 0.052; TLI = 0.95; RMR = 0.069; AIC = 112.31. These findings provide strong support for the structural validity of the scale. The Turkish version of the Quiet Quitting Scale demonstrates both validity and reliability, making it a suitable tool for evaluating quiet quitting tendencies among healthcare workers.

title: Evaluating the effectiveness and cost-benefit of a worksite mental health program among manufacturing workers: A study protocol for a quasi-experimental study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health problems lead to the loss of about 12 billion workdays worldwide each year. This creates a major economic burden. In food manufacturing, workers often face various psychosocial stressors. These include high workload, time constraint, repetitive tasks, and low autonomy. These conditions can affect both mental health and work performance. Workplace mental health interventions have shown promising results in mental health improvement. However, most studies come from high-income countries and service sectors. There is still limited evidence from industrial settings in middle-income countries. To address this gap, a structured Worksite Mental Health Program (WMHP) was developed.
METHOD: This study will employ a quasi-experimental two arm repeated measures design among workers from food manufacturing factories in Malaysia. The intervention group will receive an eight week WMHP including psychoeducation, mindfulness practices, progressive muscle relaxation, and breathing exercises. The comparison group will continue with routine workplace practices and receive a general mental health information pamphlet. Assessments will be carried out at baseline, one month post intervention, and at three months follow up. Primary outcomes include depression, anxiety, stress, and burnout. Secondary outcomes include job satisfaction, absenteeism, presenteeism, and economic outcomes. Changes over time will be analysed using Generalised Estimating Equations (GEE). A cost-benefit analysis (CBA) will also be conducted to assess economic impact.
ANTICIPATED RESULTS: The program is expected to improve mental health and work performance, while simultaneously reducing absenteeism and presenteeism. The economic evaluation is expected to demonstrate positive productivity gains associated with the program.
CONCLUSION: This study will provide evidence on the effectiveness and economic value of a workplace mental health intervention in an industrial setting, informing workplace health strategies in Malaysia and similar contexts.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR): TCTR20241217003.

title: TAL-CGBR: A class-guided boundary regression approach for Temporal Action Localization.
abstract: Temporal Action Localization (TAL) aims to identify all action categories along with their precise temporal boundaries in untrimmed videos. It serves as a fundamental task supporting various downstream applications, including intelligent video editing, automatic summarization, anomaly detection, and human-computer interaction. Despite significant progress, TAL in real-world scenarios remains challenging due to two critical factors: substantial intra-class variations in action duration, ranging from a few seconds to several minutes, and severe degradation of boundary localization accuracy caused by variations in illumination, background clutter, and camera viewpoints. To address these issues, this paper presents a Temporal Action Localization with Class-Guided Boundary Regression (TAL-CGBR) framework, which incorporates semantic information from the classification branch into the regression network to enhance boundary precision. In addition, a window-based attention mechanism and a temporal hierarchical feature structure are introduced to improve computational efficiency while maintaining high localization accuracy. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed TAL-CGBR achieves competitive performance, attaining 68.5% average mAP on THUMOS14 and 36.7% average mAP on ActivityNet v1.3, ranking second among recent methods and demonstrating a favorable balance between accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Low peak expiratory flow and subsequent first self-report of recognized lung disease: Person-disjoint replication and spirometric benchmarking in HRS and ELSA.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low peak expiratory flow (PEF) may precede the first self-report of recognized lung disease, but cross-cohort consistency and incremental value are uncertain.
METHODS: We analysed Health and Retirement Study (HRS) discovery and prespecified person-disjoint replication samples and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA). The estimand linked baseline PEF to the first subsequently observed self-report of recognized lung disease, not biological onset. HRS used a prespecified nominal lower-decile z score and ELSA an empirical lower decile. Participant-clustered models adjusted for demographic, clinical and functional factors. Weighting and a stroke comparator were sensitivity analyses. Post-hoc ELSA benchmarking compared PEF with FEV1 and FVC using person-disjoint cross-validation and full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity.
RESULTS: Models included 18,510 HRS discovery windows (320 reports), 11,424 replication windows (188), and 8,634 ELSA person-waves (95). Low PEF was associated with first report in discovery (odds ratio [OR] 3.36, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.54-4.45), replication (3.14, 2.19-4.49), and ELSA (3.77, 2.36-6.01). Weighted estimates were similar; stroke associations were weaker or null. After adjustment for separate FEV1 and FVC indices, the continuous-PEF OR was 1.04 (0.90-1.20). In 1,584 fixed-horizon participants (95 events), AUCs were 0.650 for covariates, 0.684 with PEF, 0.745 with FEV1 and FVC, and 0.739 with all three. Full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity found no clear incremental evidence beyond FEV1 and FVC. Across differing horizons, low-PEF rules identified fewer than one-third of reports in HRS replication and ELSA.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower PEF was associated with a subsequent first observed lung-disease report; cohort-specific low-PEF rules identified fewer than one-third. In exploratory fixed out-of-fold predictions, PEF improved average precision and prediction error over covariates; no clear incremental evidence remained after FEV1 and FVC. Same-protocol collection does not establish a peak-flow-only pathway.

title: Knowledge, willingness, and self-efficacy in CPR: A two-phase study of prevalence and preliminary peer-led workshop in a Malaysian tertiary institution.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest remains a major public health concern, and early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) by bystanders is crucial for improving survival outcomes. University students represent an important target population for CPR education because they are socially active, highly accessible, and capable of disseminating lifesaving knowledge within the wider community. However, inadequate CPR knowledge, low willingness to perform CPR, and poor self-efficacy remain common among university students in Malaysia.
OBJECTIVES: This two-phase study aims to determine the prevalence of self-reported CPR-related knowledge, willingness, and self-efficacy among students in a Malaysian tertiary institution (Phase 1) and to explore the preliminary changes in these outcomes following a peer-led CPR workshop (Phase 2).
METHODS: In Phase 1, a cross-sectional survey was conducted at a tertiary institute in Selangor, Malaysia using a validated questionnaire on knowledge, attitudes, behavioral intention, and self-efficacy (KABSE) (N = 431). In Phase 2, a two-hour peer-led workshop, delivered by medical students, targeted students without CPR training in the past two years, and pre-post KABSE changes were measured (N = 33).
RESULTS: Phase 1 baseline findings revealed CPR knowledge and self-efficacy levels were relatively lower than attitudes and willingness to perform CPR. Females showed higher knowledge and attitudes, while males reported greater self-efficacy. Older and married participants demonstrated better attitudes, and those with a healthcare-related background had higher knowledge, attitudes, and self-efficacy, though similar behavioral intention. Higher scores were also linked to AED awareness, AED usage capability, and recent CPR training. Statistical analysis revealed significant associations among the KABSE domains. Following the peer-led workshop, the participants showed significant gains in self-reported knowledge (p < 0.001), attitude (p < 0.001), behavioral intention (p < 0.01), and self-efficacy (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Although participants displayed positive attitudes toward CPR, baseline knowledge and self-efficacy were limited. The peer-led workshop demonstrated feasibility as a proof-of-concept intervention, generating significant short-term gains in self-reported knowledge and confidence.

title: Justice under tourism pressure: Governance fairness, emotional solidarity, and residents' co-governance participation intention in tourism-affected communities.
abstract: Amid growing tourism pressure in communities surrounding major attractions, questions of governance legitimacy, fairness, and resident engagement have become increasingly salient. This study examines how residents' perceptions of distributive, procedural, and interactional justice are associated with emotional solidarity with tourists and co-governance participation intention. Survey data from 308 residents living near major attractions in Wuxi, China, were analyzed using structural equation modeling, mediation analysis, and hierarchical regression analysis. The results show that all three dimensions of perceived justice are positively associated with emotional solidarity and co-governance participation intention, with procedural and interactional justice showing particularly strong associations. The mediation results indicate a significant indirect association between governance fairness and participation intention through emotional solidarity. The moderation results show that perceived tourism pressure is significant only for the association between interactional justice and emotional solidarity, while its moderating role is not significant for distributive or procedural justice. These findings suggest that residents' willingness to engage in co-governance is associated not only with how tourism is managed institutionally, but also with their relational orientation toward tourists. The study highlights the importance of transparent procedures, meaningful resident voice, and respectful everyday interactions for understanding collaborative governance in urban destinations under sustained tourism pressure.

title: Ca2+-dependent exocytosis of parasperm globular bodies in the strawberry conch gastropod Conomurex luhuanus.
abstract: Several animal groups produce two morphologically distinct types of sperm in the testis, including fertilizing eusperm and non-fertilizing parasperm. This phenomenon, termed sperm dimorphism, is considered to play a role in reproductive strategies such as sperm competition. In the marine gastropod Conomurex luhuanus, parasperm possess numerous globular bodies and the cilia-based undulating membranes. However, the function of the globular bodies and the motility of the undulating membranes remain unclear. Here, we describe the process and regulation of globular body exocytosis in parasperm. Upon dilution in artificial seawater, exocytosis occurs via membrane fusion between globular body membrane and the plasma membrane, followed by the release of globular body contents. Exocytosis was markedly suppressed under Ca2+ -deficient conditions but was enhanced by increases in intracellular Ca2+ induced by an ionophore A23187. In contrast, both the absence of extracellular K⁺ and high extracellular K⁺ concentrations enhanced exocytosis. On the other hand, the direction of wave propagation of the undulating membrane was reversed by high extracellular Ca2+ concentrations or by treatment with A23187, whereas it was suppressed under high extracellular K⁺ conditions. Together, these findings indicate that globular body exocytosis and changes in swimming direction are regulated by different mechanisms. This study provides novel insight into the post-ejaculatory behavior and potential function of parasperm within the female reproductive tract of gastropods.

title: Enforcing Thermodynamic Consistency in Parameter Optimization and Bayesian Inference of Biochemical Reaction Networks
abstract: Subcellular signaling pathways regulating, e.g., cell division or synaptic plasticity, are often modeled as dynamical networks of reactions satisfying the law of mass action. To remain physically grounded, these models must satisfy different physical conservation laws, such as conservation of energy. This gives rise to thermodynamic constraints formalized by the Wegscheider conditions, which ensure that the system is in detailed balance at thermodynamic equilibrium. Explicitly imposing Wegscheider conditions requires identifying cycles in the reaction network. This can become computationally cumbersome, especially in large, complex systems. Furthermore, even when these constraints are explicitly available, enforcing them requires choosing a reparameterization of the network, which may introduce asymmetries among the parameters and affect numerical conditioning. Moreover, this approach often causes inverse uncertainty quantification methods like Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) to struggle. Instead of imposing Wegscheider conditions directly in the parameter space, we propose an approach for promoting physical consistency by penalizing parameters that violate detailed balance. We first illustrate the approach on a simple reaction network containing a single cycle. We show that parameter values inferred without thermodynamic constraints can reproduce the experimental data seemingly accurately, while substantially violating the Wegscheider condition. In contrast, the proposed approach preserves the agreement with the observed dynamics while yielding posterior samples that approximately satisfy the thermodynamic constraint. We further apply the approach to a model of PKA-calcineurin signaling in synaptic long-term depression, demonstrating its applicability to a more complex biochemical reaction network.

title: Calibrating AlphaFold confidence scores for interface quality
abstract: AlphaFold confidence scores are widely used to rank protein complex predictions and to select subsets of models for downstream applications. Although these scores provide strong discriminatory power for distinguishing prediction quality, their numerical values were never intended to represent the probability that a prediction satisfies a given structural quality criterion. In this work, we calibrate commonly used confidence scores to estimate the probability that a predicted complex exceeds a chosen threshold of DockQ, an established measure of interface quality. On antibody-antigen and general multimer datasets, post-hoc isotonic calibration consistently improves agreement between predicted probabilities and observed DockQ success rates while preserving the underlying score ordering. The calibrated probabilities also provide more accurate estimates of the fraction of selected models expected to pass a given structural quality threshold. Although the mapping is fitted within a given prediction distribution and therefore transfers imperfectly across prediction domains, we show that reliable estimates are recovered from a small number of labeled target-domain samples. Because the calibration is entirely post hoc and requires no underlying AlphaFold model fine-tuning, it provides a straightforward and customizable way to convert existing model quality rankings into calibrated probabilities of passing a chosen structural quality threshold.

title: Physiology-Informed Sparse Identification of Dynamic Crop Models
abstract: Developing resilient crops requires models that accurately capture how plant growth dynamics emerge from the continuous interplay between genetic and environmental factors. While high-throughput phenotyping platforms generate data for dynamic growth models, current modelling approaches show limitations: process-based crop growth models (CGMs) capture environmental dynamics but are difficult to scale across many genotypes because they require calibration of many parameters, while quantitative genetic models allow modelling many genotypes but often summarise time-varying environments using static covariates. To address this gap, we propose a data-driven framework to identify reduced systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) describing crop growth dynamics as functions of environmental variables and a controllable number of genotype-specific coefficients (GSCs). Using the Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) method, we infer model structure directly from data via sparse regression on a physiologically informed library of candidate functions. In this framework, GSCs parameterise cultivar-specific differences in response to environmental conditions. The resulting models are linear in these GSCs, making them compatible with mixed-model and genomic prediction approaches. We evaluate the approach on an in silico dataset generated with WOFOST for five potato cultivars across twelve growing seasons. Our identified ODEs generalise to held-out years and achieve $R^2 > 0.9$ for end-of-season yield prediction across held-out years when compared to full-scale WOFOST simulations. These results provide a proof of concept for SINDy-based identification of parsimonious dynamic crop models from longitudinal crop-growth data.

title: Probability generating functions for epidemiological time series
abstract: Probability generating functions (PGFs) are a fundamental tool in mathematical epidemiology to characterize the stochastic evolution of epidemics via branching process theory. However, they are rarely used as operational tools in real-time during an outbreak, the main barrier being a lack of a systematic, computational methodology to describe epidemiological time series, such as cases or hospital admissions over time. Here, we introduce a general and computationally efficient framework for outbreak analytics based on PGFs. We first develop a method to encode joint distributions of incidences and their noisy measurements by realistic surveillance systems. Then, by transforming PGFs to cumulant generating functions (CGFs), we enable efficient evaluation of these joint distributions. We demonstrate the practicality of our approach for Bayesian inference and short-term forecasts, offering a significant computational advantage over simulation-based methods. Altogether, our framework operationalizes generating functions and paves the way for their broader adoption in computational epidemiology.

title: From Simulated Fluids to Living Tissue: Zero-Shot Foundation Model Transfer to Perturbed Embryos
abstract: Morphogenesis is driven by the interplay of genetic regulation and tissue mechanics. In vivo video data is limited, particularly under genetic mutations and environmental perturbations, making generalization beyond the most representative conditions in the dataset challenging. However, at tissue scales, the dynamics of Drosophila can be described as a continuum flow, motivating the usage of representations learned across other physical systems as priors for developmental dynamics. We investigate finetuning Walrus, a Continuum Dynamics Foundation Model pretrained across a broad set of simulated continuous systems, on tissue velocity fields from only 12 wild-type Drosophila blastoderm videos. We evaluate autoregressive prediction both in-distribution and zero-shot under unseen temperature and genetic perturbations. Zero-shot refers to evaluation on perturbation conditions never seen during wild-type finetuning, without any additional training. In-distribution, a Fourier Neural Operator model trained from scratch achieves best performance on VRMSE. However, Walrus (CRPS) is the strongest model under the most severe distribution shift of unseen samples of mutated embryos and temperature conditions. Interestingly, predictions capture the shape of the mean surface tissue velocity trajectory and its separation between 17°C and 27°C, including the timing of the peak at Germ Band Extension onset, a biologically meaningful milestone of embryo development. Our results provide preliminary support that representations learned from different dynamical systems can transfer to experimental morphogenesis in developmental regimes, provided they admit a continuum description. More broadly, our results motivate further study of physics foundation models as a new complementary tool for the simulation of morphogenesis in low-data regimes.

title: AutoNovo: Agentic Program Search Discovers Transferable Nucleic Acid Design Algorithms
abstract: In-silico optimization of nucleic acids relies on predictive oracles that imperfectly capture biological function, so sequences optimized against one model may exploit model-specific artifacts and fail to generalize to independent models. Recent studies have shown that not all designers generalize equally well to independent models. In this work, we use agentic program search to iteratively propose, execute, evaluate, and revise code for nucleic-acid designers. We describe the successful strategies used to prompt the search. AutoNovo designers achieved the best observed mean among the evaluated methods on 3/3 DNA-design tasks in terms of in-silico performance, and 6/6 transfer tasks in terms of independent models. The designers come from a family of discovered nucleic acid designers rather than a single universal best designer. We plan to release the resulting designers. These results are the first steps in creating nucleic acid designers that maximize cross-model generalization, and thus improving the odds that in-silico designed sequences reflect real biology.

title: Beyond Successful Play: Diagnosing Opponent Modeling in Large Language Models
abstract: Language-model agents are expected to adapt to others whose behavior changes through interaction. Yet adaptation may rely on learned behavioral patterns rather than theory of mind (ToM): the ability to infer others' mental states, including beliefs and intentions. We introduce a benchmark and diagnostic framework for repeated hide-and-seek against algorithmic opponents with explicitly defined recursive belief updates. Their ground-truth beliefs and action probabilities let us distinguish adaptive play, action prediction, and belief tracking through live interaction, fixed-history evaluation, and controlled information interventions. With structured elicitation and behavioral supervised fine-tuning (SFT), we find improved play in several tested settings, but diagnostics reveal limitations in opponent prediction and belief tracking. We test whether supervising opponent action probabilities can address this predictive deficit in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Predictions improve when the model is told the opponent's type and parameter settings, but become less accurate when it must infer the opponent from history without this information. Training on examples that also omit these details reduces the gap, although improvements vary across opponents. Is this limitation specific to smaller open-weight models, or does it also appear in a frontier model? GPT-5.4 also benefits from correct opponent beliefs: supplying them improves its predictions and choices, whereas deeper explicit belief reports and self-generated memory do not consistently improve forecasting from interaction history. This contrast suggests that using useful belief information is easier than inferring it autonomously, even for a frontier model. Together, our findings distinguish improved play and action prediction from reliable belief tracking, providing a framework for evaluating mentalizing and testing targeted improvements.

title: Learning Perceptual Geometry of Natural Odor Mixtures from LLM-Derived Descriptors
abstract: The relationship between odor chemistry and perception remains incompletely understood. Many existing studies focus on the perception of single molecules, whereas natural odors contain tens to hundreds of components, adding extra layer of complexity to percept formation. Here, we explore the relationship between molecular composition and perceived similarity in natural odor objects. We study this using a database of more than 1,200 volatile-compound-in-food mixtures containing more than 8,000 molecular components, and use large language models (LLMs) as a scalable surrogate for deriving mixture-level perceptual descriptions. We find that language-derived representations provide useful supervision for predicting held-out mixture similarities from molecular composition. The prediction was consistently strongest when perceptual targets were derived from chemosensory prompts than from other sensory prompts. Further, during the mixture-level training, we learned low-rank molecular embeddings that enabled better prediction of held-out mixture similarities than component-overlap metrics, even for mixture pairs with no shared molecules. Although no single-molecule labels were used during training, the learned molecular geometry showed significant alignment with the independent human odor-descriptor space. Finally, we explored the use of external molecular features in our mixture-similarity prediction task. These features showed modest zero-shot alignment with mixture-level perceptual similarity. They improved prediction under limited supervision but offered little additional predictive benefit with the full training set. Together, these results show that language-derived descriptions can provide scalable supervision for predicting the perceptual organization of complex natural mixtures, contributing to a quantitative understanding of how molecular composition gives rise to odor perception.

title: MP-MNCA: Morphology-Prior Masked Neighbor Cross-Attention for Efficient Spatial Domain Identification
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics jointly captures molecular state, tissue morphology, and spatial organization, yet spatial-domain methods are typically compared only at late training checkpoints, obscuring differences in convergence efficiency. We introduce MP-MNCA, a morphology-prior masked neighbor cross-attention framework that preserves the full 3,000 dimensional highly-variable-gene representation while selectively routing molecular information across spatial neighbors, with histological similarity incorporated as a continuous attention prior under a self-supervised masked neighbor-contrastive objective. Across 12 heterogeneous human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) sections, MP-MNCA is evaluated against established spatial-domain baselines using both convergence trajectories and epoch-wise spatial-domain visualizations. Our results show that MP-MNCA (i) reaches coherent spatial-domain structure in substantially fewer training epochs, as reflected quantitatively by convergence curves and qualitatively by progressive spatial grids, and (ii) maintains strong clustering quality, achieving a mean peak refined ARI of 0.546 versus 0.549 for the strongest baseline (STAIG), while attaining the highest mean refined NMI of 0.657 versus 0.640. Moreover, MP-MNCA outperforms STAIG on 7 of 12 sections in ARI and 11 of 12 in NMI, demonstrating faster convergence without sacrificing spatial-domain quality.

title: Hybrid Context Forests and Bilateral Viterbi Matching for 3D Rib Centerline Tracing in CT
abstract: Automatic extraction and anatomical numbering (R01-R12, L01-L12) of all 24 rib centerlines in thoracic CT is essential for unfolded rib visualization, fracture detection, and surgical navigation, but remains challenging due to adjacent-bone confluence, calcified costal cartilage bridges, kyphotic pose variation, and partial visibility of terminal ribs. We present ribline, an open-source three-stage framework combining: (1) an automatically detected lung-apex and vertebral-midline coordinate frame with a kyphosis-aware azimuthal angle for point ordering along each rib; (2) a hybrid voxel detector fusing an anatomically anchored Semantic Context Forest (SCF) with a lightweight 3D U-Net; and (3) a global stage that decomposes the probability skeleton into candidate curves, assigns rib indices via a bilateral Viterbi dynamic program coupled across both hemithoraces, and refines curves via template recovery and normal-plane centering (RibSnake). On the Siemens Corporate Research 2 mm thoracic CT benchmark (47 training and 12 evaluation scans), our pipeline achieves a labeled Chamfer distance of 2.05 mm, labeled clDice of 0.886 (3 mm) and 0.945 (4 mm), 97.2% labeling accuracy (278/286 ribs), and zero false-positive curves on the evaluation split, and 3.64 mm (median 2.39 mm) with 91.8% labeling accuracy across all 59 annotated scans (1,402 ribs) in 5-fold cross-validation. title: Probing the role of sequential sampling and integration in decisions about protracted, noiseless stimuli
abstract: Perceptual decision behaviour is known to be well-captured by models based on sequential sampling and temporal integration, but doubts have been raised about the generality and identifiability of these operations. Here we used neurally-constrained modelling to probe their role and temporal extent in the uncertain case of perceptual judgments about long-duration stimuli with no physical noise but weak evidence. We found that accuracy steadily improved across four covertly-manipulated evidence durations, indicating protracted sampling, but these delayed behavioural reports alone were insufficient to establish the operation of integration or of a decision-terminating bound. We then elaborated the models to prescribe how they would generate decision variable signals as well as choices, and fit them additionally to the average dynamics of a centroparietal electroencephalographic signal (CPP) that traces decision formation. This established the setting of a bound and ruled out some non-integration mechanisms. However, one extrema detection model, which evokes a stereotyped signal "flagging" the first bound-exceeding sample, rivalled the integration model in reproducing the evidence-dependent buildup dynamics of the CPP, alongside behavioural data. Moreover, the two models captured different features of neural motor preparation signals but neither captured all of them. We discuss the implications for the generality of integration and the technical challenges of neurally-informed modelling given limited behavioural data.

title: Neural prediction decorrelation reveals that adversarial robustness substantially improves DNN prediction accuracy across the entire human auditory cortex
abstract: Sensory neuroscientists seek to model the neural computations that encode complex stimuli. Distinct encoding models often make similar predictions for natural stimuli such as speech, posing a challenge for model comparison. We developed a method to synthesize stimuli that decorrelate model predictions across a neural population, termed neural prediction decorrelation (NPD). Using fMRI responses to NPD sounds, we compared standard and adversarially robust deep neural network models of human auditory cortex. Prediction accuracy for NPD sounds was substantially better for the adversarially robust model in every region tested, an effect completely masked with natural sounds. Population responses to natural and synthesized NPD sounds shared an interpretable low-dimensional organization that was reproduced by the robust encoding model. NPD provides a general approach for comparing encoding models and reveals that adversarial robustness expands the predictive power of DNNs beyond natural stimuli, which is likely critical for targeting population activity through stimulus synthesis.

title: NeuroGraphBench: Interacting with Drosophila Connectomes at Scale for Exploring the Functional Logic of Neural Circuits
abstract: Drosophila connectomic datasets provide increasingly comprehensive maps of neuronal morphology and synaptic connectivity, offering an unprecedented opportunity to explore the structural organization of its neural circuits. This calls for designing automated tools to interact with connectomic datasets at scale for efficiently exploring structural features embedded in the vast amounts of data. Yet the central challenge remains the understanding of the functional logic of neural circuits. In order to formulate a connectome-grounded hypothesis for what a circuit computes, it is critical to (i) characterize the objects in the natural environment in which brain circuits operate, and (ii) formulate how brain circuits represent and process the defined objects. To develop and demonstrate a methodology for these requirements, we focus on the Drosophila looming-evoked escape pathway. We modeled the trajectory of looming objects that are on a collision course (direct-hits) or pass by the fly (near-misses): their projected images on the retina can be characterized by the subtended solid angle and center elevation. By analyzing the sub-neuronal structure and retinotopic organization of the looming pathway embedded in connectomic datasets, we devised a pathway abstraction, and mapped each of its structural elements to a processing block to construct an executable circuit model. We demonstrate that this connectome-grounded functional model separates direct-hits from near-misses well before the trajectories can be distinguished based on the subtended solid angle alone. To accelerate the connectomic analysis step, we developed a Python toolset with an agentic, code-free workspace interface called NeuroGraphBench (NGB). NGB provides four composable morphology-analysis primitives and an AI Agent that composes them to interactively respond to natural-language queries aided by visualization on an interactive 3D canvas. Thus, NGB automates tedious and repetitive tasks to enable faster and scalable connectomic exploration, keeping human reasoning, instead of writing code, at the center of an open-ended research inquiry.

title: Linear NeuroPaint: An Efficient Baseline for Cross-Session Neural Alignment and Inpainting
abstract: Large-scale Neuropixels recordings sample many brain areas, but no single experimental session records every area of interest. NeuroPaint, a transformer-based autoencoder, integrates such recordings by aligning area-specific latent dynamics across sessions and "inpainting" activity in unrecorded areas. Could a linear model, which would be computationally efficient and potentially more interpretable, suffice to achieve this? To address this question, we introduce Linear NeuroPaint, a linear variant of NeuroPaint, and evaluate it on two multi-area Neuropixels datasets. Linear NeuroPaint achieves strong predictive performance on recorded areas, however, it is less accurate than nonlinear models at cross-area inpainting, despite extensive hyperparameter optimization. Moreover, its parameters are not readily interpretable: incomplete cross-session alignment leads parameter-defined neuron clusters to exhibit heterogeneous response profiles. Together, these results show that linear transformations are insufficient for cross-session alignment and cross-area prediction. Nevertheless, Linear NeuroPaint provides a computationally efficient baseline for benchmarking multi-session neural models.

title: Subtype-Selective Neuronal Vulnerability and Compensatory Neuroglial Remodeling in Human Cortical Dementia
abstract: Whether the nodal vulnerability in dementia is solely represented by changes in cellular abundance or attrition of cellular transcriptomic landscape attribute to that transition in aging brain is yet to uncover with minutiae. To understand this complication, we have analyzed two snRNA-seq data specific to (I) dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC): A comprehensive study of cellular profiling among cognitively normal and pathological ageing and dementia (AD) brain, (II) occipital cortex (OC) in the context of Nasu-Hakola disease along with a tissue level bulk RNA-seq data corresponds to temporal cortex. We pinpoint cellular subpopulations their proportional changes within the nodal points and their transcriptomic profiling. In DLPFC we observed alteration of mitochondrial and synaptic maintenance program in the pathological manifestation of disease. In OC we noticed depleted upper layer CUX2 neuron, PVALB and SST neurons on the contrary an enrichment of RORB and LAMP5 neurons with compromised metabolic states in the disease context. Glial populations are marked by representation of fibrous astrocyte, neuronal-supporting subpopulations associated with extracellular matrix remodeling programs. Proportional increment of intermediate myelinating oligodendrocyte and a decrease in mature myelinating subpopulation highlighted a compromised myelin repair attempt. In temporal cortex at tissue level we observed transcriptomic landscape adopted a neuroglial phenotypes in dementia brain. Cell-Chat analysis demonstrated a shift in cellular coordination towards glial population from neuron in NHD brain. A single cell-based drug reprofiling approach identified efatutazone and balaglitazone as broad-spectrum candidates for major cell types in occipital cortex, whereas major actionable biological targets belong to CDK subtypes and proteasome subunits. Overall, our findings imply cellular persistence do not necessarily substantiate molecular preservation, also the coexistence of cellular vulnerability alongside selective remodeling features, present a cellular framework on how to cope up with degenerative changes.

title: Continuous amyloid staging complements global amyloid burden in early Alzheimer's disease
authors: For the Alzheimers Disease Neuroimaging Initiative,
abstract: Introduction: Early Alzheimer's disease (AD) staging remains challenging because clinical categories and global amyloid PET measures provide only coarse characterization of disease progression. We developed a continuous amyloid staging score from regional amyloid PET to complement global amyloid burden. Methods: Using longitudinal florbetapir PET from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), we trained an end-to-end deep learning model to directly estimate a continuous amyloid staging score. We evaluated longitudinal consistency, its relationship with global amyloid burden, regional contributors to early-stage variation, and whether the staging score stratified subsequent memory decline among participants matched for baseline global amyloid burden. Cognitive analyses were replicated in A4+LEARN. Results: The staging score better preserved longitudinal visit order than existing amyloid staging approaches. During early disease stages, it captured regional amyloid variation despite relatively stable global amyloid burden. Among participants with similar baseline global amyloid burden, higher staging scores were associated with faster subsequent memory decline in both ADNI and A4+LEARN. Discussion: A continuous amyloid staging score complements global amyloid burden for early AD staging and cognitive risk stratification. Keywords: Alzheimer's disease; amyloid PET; disease staging; cognitive decline

title: Simultaneous recordings link intracranial and scalp correlates of somatosensory awareness in humans
abstract: The electrophysiological events underlying the conscious perception of touch in humans remain elusive. Scalp-EEG studies have identified a negative deflection peaking 120-200 ms after stimulus onset, known as the N140. This component, recently reinterpreted as the somatosensory awareness negativity (N140/SAN), has been proposed as a putative marker of tactile awareness, but its underlying neuronal dynamics are still unknown. Intracranial studies have shown that responses to median nerve stimulation include, after an initial phasic activation mainly localized to primary somatosensory cortices, a predominantly insulo-opercular tonic broadband high-frequency activity (BHA; 50-150 Hz) that has been linked to tactile awareness. Yet these scalp and intracranial signatures have never been directly linked. Using simultaneous high-density scalp EEG and intracranial EEG recordings, we show that the N140/SAN is the scalp manifestation of the insulo-opercular local field potential that follows the BHA response to stimulation. By bridging invasive and non-invasive recordings our results identify the neural origins of the N140/SAN and connect scalp and intracranial correlates of somatosensory awareness.

title: Identification of surface colors across environmental illuminations
abstract: When objects are embedded in a complex lighting environment, the illumination they receive depends on their geometric relationship to the environment. We measured performance in an odd-one-out color constancy task, with objects rendered in complex lighting environments. Observers identified the odd object among four objects, with two rendered under each of two lighting environments, sampled from a wide range of object orientations and camera positions. Constancy was high. The presence of a surrounding context increased accuracy. Gloss provided no measurable benefit. We also tested a condition in which the global color impression provided misleading information about the lighting environment, but this impaired performance only slightly. These findings suggest that human color constancy remains robust even under complex lighting environments, contrary to predictions of many simple models of illuminant discounting.
